qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts spouses and financially dependent children of fallen State or local public safety employees from out-of-state or out-of-county tuition. Subjects Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor memorial scholarship awards to State budget availability. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to allocate scholarship funds to postsecondary institutions through a formula. Directs postsecondary institutions to prioritize eligible renewal recipients before awarding scholarship funds to new applicants. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Spouses and financially dependent children of State or local public safety employees killed in the line of duty; eligible postsecondary institutions; recipients and applicants of the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and the Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant decrease in State general fund expenditures by capping total scholarship awards to amounts provided in the State budget rather than funding all verified eligible recipients. Postsecondary institutions, including community colleges, experience a corresponding decrease in scholarship revenues and expenditures. The out-of-state and out-of-county tuition exemption is anticipated to have a minimal fiscal impact on public higher education institutions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with establishing the allocation formula for the Conroy and Cryor scholarship programs, administering the scholarship fund, and adopting necessary regulations and guidelines.

The Commission is directly charged with administering the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund, developing fund distribution formulas for postsecondary institutions, and promulgating regulations for nonresident tuition exemptions.

USM institutions are directly impacted by the requirement to provide out-of-state and out-of-county tuition exemptions to eligible surviving dependents and by changes to how Conroy and Cryor scholarship funds are allocated and awarded to students.

As an independent public university, Morgan State University must implement the in-state tuition exemptions for eligible dependents and will determine eligibility and award Conroy and Cryor scholarships under the new funding allocation formula.

As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland must grant in-state tuition exemptions to eligible surviving dependents and award Conroy and Cryor scholarships subject to the new state funding allocations.
The bill explicitly designates that the Comptroller shall account for the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund.
The bill explicitly designates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund and receive deposits of gifts or grants for the fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to collect student-level parental status data from public institutions of higher education. Excludes the University of Maryland Global Campus from the parental status data collection mandate. Directs community colleges to adopt a support plan for pregnant and parenting students. Requires public senior higher education institutions and community colleges to post their plans by October 1, 2026. Adds parental status to the Maryland Longitudinal Data System while explicitly excluding pregnancy status. Mandates annual summary reports to specified legislative committees beginning September 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: pregnant and parenting students; students with caregiving responsibilities; Maryland public senior higher education institutions; Maryland community colleges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $51,857 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Higher Education Commission to hire a half-time staff specialist. Public four-year institutions and community colleges face minimal operational costs to collect data and adopt required plans. Medicaid and related public assistance expenditures may increase if referrals lead to higher program enrollment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing demographic questions in consultation with institutions, adopting regulations, collecting parental status data from public institutions, and submitting annual summary reports to the General Assembly.

As the state's higher education regulatory body (listed alongside Maryland Higher Education Commission), the agency is directly responsible for administering the bill's data collection, regulation adoption, and annual legislative reporting requirements.

Constituent institutions of USM (excluding UMGC) are required to add parental status questions to student demographic forms, report data to MHEC, and post a plan supporting pregnant and parenting students on their websites.

Morgan State University is a public senior higher education institution required to collect parental status data on demographic forms, submit data to MHEC, and maintain and post an institutional plan for pregnant and parenting students.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the bill's requirements to collect student parental demographic data, report findings to MHEC, and post an institutional plan for pregnant and parenting students.
The bill amends the definition of 'student data' in the MLDS statute to include parental status and exclude pregnancy status, authorizing MHEC to share parental status data with the MLDS Center.

The fiscal note indicates that required institutional referrals to public assistance programs like Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), administered by MDH, may increase program participation and state expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech–Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists to issue limited licenses. Permits eligible applicants to practice music therapy under the supervision of a fully licensed music therapist. Requires applicants to meet all full licensure qualifications except for the examination. Establishes that a limited license expires after one year and allows a single one-year renewal. Mandates a one-year waiting period before reapplying if the licensee fails to obtain full licensure within two years.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech–Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants seeking licensure to practice music therapy, fully licensed music therapists providing supervision, and clients receiving music therapy services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures are not meaningfully impacted. The board can implement and issue limited licenses using existing budgeted resources, and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists is a health occupations licensing board operating under the Maryland Department of Health, which regulates health care professionals in the state and will administer the new limited license.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County to appoint three majors. Establishes that the appointed majors serve at the pleasure of the Sheriff. Requires the majors to receive a salary as provided by the County Council of Anne Arundel County. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Sheriff of Anne Arundel County; County Council of Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Anne Arundel County; newly appointed majors in the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office; Anne Arundel County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Anne Arundel County expenditures may increase by up to $822,300 in FY 2027 and by at least $730,000 annually thereafter for salaries, fringe benefits, and operating equipment if all three majors are appointed. Local revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the standard bullying reporting form to identify motivating actual or perceived personal characteristics. Requires county boards of education to report investigated incidents motivated in whole or in substantial part by actual personal characteristics. Requires the State Department of Education to establish standards for reporting conditions by July 1, 2027. Mandates each county board make disaggregated incident information available upon request by January 31 each year. Prohibits county boards from publishing any information that could be used to identify an individual student. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: public school students, parents and guardians, public school staff, and county boards of education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems can implement reporting updates and information disclosures using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education is the primary implementing agency tasked with updating the statewide standard bullying report form, establishing standards for reporting motivated incidents by July 1, 2027, and submitting annual summary reports to legislative committees.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education focused on school safety protocols, school climate, and anonymous safety reporting mechanisms, the center is impacted by changes to reporting standards and tracking of bullying, harassment, and intimidation in public schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies criteria for determining county venue for administrative or judicial probate of decedents not domiciled in the United States. Authorizes venue where the decedent previously resided or where related property, representatives, or beneficiaries are located. Authorizes the register or orphans' court to determine venue if specified statutory criteria do not apply. Establishes that the taxable situs of intangible personal property for inheritance tax is the decedent's domicile. Repeals a reciprocal inheritance tax exemption for personal property passing from nonresident decedents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Registers of Wills; Orphans' Courts; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Personal representatives, heirs, legatees, and beneficiaries of estates of nonresident decedents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 due to changes in the taxable situs of intangible personal property. State expenditures are unaffected. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the venue criteria for administrative probate administered by the Registers of Wills and alters the application and situs rules of the Maryland inheritance tax, which the Registers of Wills are responsible for assessing and collecting.

The bill alters statutory standards for determining venue in judicial probate proceedings before the Orphans' Courts and Circuit Courts, which are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

As the State's chief financial officer overseeing tax collections and state general fund revenues, the Comptroller is impacted by statutory modifications to the inheritance tax and its potential effect on state revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes a related event promoter’s permit issued by the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City. Authorizes the Board to issue permits for events coordinated with third-party promoters during the CIAA Basketball Tournament. Requires applicants to obtain written consent from Visit Baltimore at least 30 days before the event. Requires holders of a State caterer's license to obtain a Class C per diem license before participating. Establishes a $50 application fee and a permit fee of $500 or $1,500 based on venue capacity. Imposes fines between $1,000 and $3,000 for operating without a required permit or license.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Related event promoters, participating alcoholic beverages license holders in Baltimore City, and State caterer's license holders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2029 from application and permit fees, while monitoring and enforcement can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates alcoholic beverages licensing, enforcement, and State caterer's licenses for events in Baltimore City. While local licensing boards and the state alcohol regulatory authorities oversee enforcement, the Comptroller is responsible for broad alcohol industry regulation and collection of state alcoholic beverages and sales taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands Department of State Police regulation of police-initiated towing to include light-duty vehicles. Requires the Department to establish approved rates for light-duty towing and recovery based on committee recommendations. Prohibits approved light-duty towing rates from exceeding 80% of maximum approved medium-duty towing rates. Renames the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery. Requires the committee to examine insurance issues concerning out-of-state vehicles and cargo debris cleanup costs. Establishes an effective date of October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery
qa_results.stakeholders: Authorized towing companies performing police-initiated towing; owners and operators of motor vehicles requiring police-initiated towing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Department of State Police can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland State Police is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing approved rates for light-duty police-initiated towing, maintaining the authorized tow list, adjudicating complaints, and providing administrative and staff support to the advisory committee.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner appoints a member to the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery, and the committee is statutorily charged with examining and reporting on insurance matters regarding out-of-state vehicles and cargo/debris cleanup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames and directly alters the statutory duties and scope of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery, requiring it to recommend light-duty rates and examine specific insurance matters.

The Administrator of the State Highway Administration is statutorily required to appoint a representative to serve on the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.
A representative of the Maryland Transportation Authority Police serves on the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.
The Secretary of Transportation appoints a representative of the MDTA Police to the committee, and MDOT oversees the State Highway Administration which is also represented on the committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a county or municipality to regulate listed invasive trees and trees of heaven by ordinance. Permits local ordinances to prohibit selling, planting, or allowing trees of heaven or listed invasive trees to grow on property. Allows local governments to enforce ordinances by establishing civil fines and requiring damage mitigation. Authorizes counties and municipalities to establish bounty or native tree replacement programs to incentivize tree eradication. Requires incentive programs to follow University of Maryland Agriculture Extension identification and removal standards. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipalities; Maryland Department of Agriculture; University of Maryland Agriculture Extension
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, nurseries, plant dealers, and landscaping businesses in Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Local expenditures may increase if local governments choose to establish bounty or native tree replacement programs. Local revenues may increase from civil fines under adopted ordinances, though specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the Department of Agriculture by defining 'listed invasive trees' according to the Maryland Prohibited Invasive Plant List posted and maintained by the department.

The bill mandates that local bounty or native tree replacement programs identify species and utilize removal methodology consistent with the species pages published by the University of Maryland Agriculture Extension, a unit of the University of Maryland within the University System of Maryland.
The Department of Natural Resources oversees state forestry, natural resource conservation, and invasive plant management programs, and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands licensing provisions for affiliated insurance producer–mortgage loan originators to include originators for approved single mortgage lenders. Requires the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to approve qualifying mortgage lenders who meet good standing and compliance standards. Authorizes licensees to act only on behalf of an identified sponsor that is a mortgage lender or exempt person. Requires sponsoring mortgage lenders to supervise licensees, assume joint and several liability, and meet surety bond requirements. Prohibits licensees from aiding borrowers with unauthorized lenders or handling borrower funds in connection with loan originations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Affiliated insurance producer–mortgage loan originators, mortgage lenders, financial institutions, and mortgage borrowers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in special fund revenues from licensing fees beginning in fiscal 2027. The Office of Financial Regulation can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local governments are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters licensing and sponsorship requirements for affiliated insurance producer–mortgage loan originators under the regulatory authority of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, an office housed within the Maryland Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals registered by the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to continue practicing beyond October 31, 2026. Establishes educational and contact hour qualification standards for applicants who graduated from out-of-state massage therapy programs. Permits out-of-state applicants to supplement deficient contact hours through board-approved education or recent hands-on experience. Repeals the hearing requirement before the Board may impose a $100 administrative penalty for address notification failures. Requires licensees and registered practitioners on inactive status to submit to a criminal history records check to reactivate. Conditions reinstatement or reactivation after five years for registered massage practitioners on meeting current licensing requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: registered massage practitioners, licensed massage therapists, and out-of-state massage therapy applicants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters the licensing, registration, educational qualifications, penalty procedures, and reinstatement requirements administered and enforced by the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program to recognize the civic readiness and civic engagement of public high school students. Requires the State Board of Education to adopt criteria for awarding a Seal of Civic Excellence by the 2027–2028 school year. Requires the criteria to include a capstone project focused on State, county, or local government civic service. Authorizes each local school system to choose whether to participate in the program. Prohibits public high schools within a participating local school system from opting out. Requires participating local school systems to award the seal with a cord, medal, or diploma insignia.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; State Board of Education; local school systems
qa_results.stakeholders: public high school students in participating local school systems, public high schools, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact, as the State Board of Education can adopt regulations with existing resources. Potential discretionary increase in local school system expenditures for staff and operational costs if a system elects to participate. No effect on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program within the Department of Education (MSDE) and requires the State Board of Education to adopt regulations establishing program criteria, capstone project guidelines, and requirements for awarding the Seal of Civic Excellence, as well as receiving annual reporting from participating school systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that communications between an attorney and a fiduciary client are subject to attorney-client privilege. Protects these communications even when fiduciary funds compensate the attorney for legal services rendered. Clarifies that the existence of a fiduciary relationship with a beneficiary does not waive attorney-client privilege. Defines fiduciary to include an agent granted authority under a power of attorney. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Fiduciaries including personal representatives, trustees, and agents under powers of attorney; attorneys representing fiduciaries; and estate and trust beneficiaries.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies a rule of evidence regarding attorney-client privilege between attorneys and fiduciaries in legal and judicial proceedings, which directly affects civil litigation, evidence admissibility, and court procedures administered by the judicial branch.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration, personal representatives, and acts as clerk to the Orphans' Court, where matters involving fiduciary administration and fees are routinely handled.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a Maryland nonstock corporation to convert to a cooperative limited equity housing corporation upon acquiring a residential rental facility. Requires converting corporations to submit formation documents to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation following an affirmative member vote. Mandates offering cooperative membership to existing eligible residential tenants and reimbursing certain low-income households for moving expenses. Caps cooperative interest appreciation at initial purchase cost adjusted for inflation plus approved improvements. Restricts cooperative membership primarily to low-income households and moderate-income households. Authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide grants promoting cooperative limited equity housing corporations.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: low-income and moderate-income households, tenants residing in converting residential rental facilities, Maryland nonstock corporations, and cooperative limited equity housing corporations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in Department of Housing and Community Development general fund expenditures beginning as early as fiscal 2027 to administer the program and award grants, accompanied by a potential minimal increase in State Department of Assessments and Taxation corporate filing fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) with adopting regulations, establishing additional rights and requirements for cooperative limited equity housing corporations and their members, and authorizing DHCD to establish a grant program to support their formation.

The bill creates statutory requirements, minimum timeframes, and protections regarding notices to vacate and occupancy agreements during cooperative conversions, which intersect with landlord-tenant and summary ejectment matters adjudicated in the state court system.
The Office of the Attorney General acts as legal counsel to state agencies, including reviewing DHCD's implementing regulations and advising on statutory preemption of local ordinances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes alternative expiration and renewal periods for handgun permits issued to qualifying retired law enforcement officers. Applies to officers who retired in good standing from a State, county, or municipal law enforcement agency. Sets permit expiration to the last day of the holder's birth month five years after issuance. Authorizes permit renewal for successive five-year periods if the applicant maintains required qualifications. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: retired law enforcement officers who retired in good standing from a State, county, or municipal law enforcement agency in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $170,000 in FY 2027 only for computer programming modifications to the automated handgun permit system. State revenues are not affected because qualifying retired officers are exempt from permit fees. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of State Police is the issuing and regulatory authority for Maryland handgun permits under Title 5, Subtitle 3 of the Public Safety Article. MSP will incur approximately $170,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2027 to reprogram its automated handgun permit system to accommodate the new 5-year expiration and renewal schedule for retired law enforcement officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the membership of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission from 19 to 21 members. Adds one member appointed by the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees Local 3, Council 434. Adds one member appointed by the Citizens Advisory Council for Gifted and Talented Education. Updates the appointing authority from the Baltimore County Chamber of Commerce to the Greater Baltimore Chamber of Commerce. Establishes staggered termination dates for specified commission member terms ending in 2028 and 2030. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and appointing organizations of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, including AFSCME Local 3, Council 434, the Citizens Advisory Council for Gifted and Talented Education, the Greater Baltimore Chamber of Commerce, and Baltimore County public school candidates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Adding members to the commission does not materially affect Baltimore County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor appoints eight members of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission and receives lists of nominees from the Commission to appoint members to the Baltimore County Board of Education.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and executing gubernatorial appointments to boards and commissions, which includes the gubernatorial appointees to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission.

Towson University, an institution within the University System of Maryland, is statutorily designated to appoint a member to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, and the bill staggers the term for Towson University's appointee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires county superintendents of schools to establish a remote registration process for advance enrollment of active service members' dependent children. Prohibits charging a fee or requiring physical appearance at any county location during advance enrollment. Mandates remote registration procedures allowing parents to note existing individualized education programs or 504 plans. Requires county boards of education to provide appropriate education to students with disabilities without undue delay. Allows enrolled dependent children to complete the school year even if residency requirements are no longer met. Directs the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to publish and maintain military school enrollment information.
qa_results.responsible_party: County superintendents of schools; county boards of education; Secretary of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Active service members relocating to Maryland, dependent children of active service members, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances; the Department of Veterans and Military Families and local school systems can implement the bill's requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families, in consultation with specified entities, to publish and maintain information regarding advance enrollment procedures, the Purple Star Schools Program, the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children, and services for active-duty military families.

The bill establishes mandatory remote advance enrollment and special education transfer procedures across local public school systems, which are overseen and guided by the Maryland State Department of Education, including the Purple Star Schools Program administered by MSDE.

The bill explicitly requires the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council, which are units within the Department of Commerce, to be consulted regarding published information and resources on school enrollment procedures for military families.

The bill directly references and requires publication of information on the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children and coordination with its military family education liaison.

qa_results.bill_summary: Declares void any consumer contract provision that waives, limits, impairs, or disclaims certain remedies authorized by federal or State law. Applies this prohibition to statutory damages, punitive damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief. Prohibits consumer contracts from setting a shorter limitation period than required by State law. Authorizes contracts to limit statutory or punitive damages to the extent of applicable insurance coverage limits. Establishes that violations are unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under Maryland consumer protection law. Exempts self-service storage facilities, certain regulated utility and communication services, and licensed security system services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: consumers entering into consumer contracts in Maryland, businesses offering consumer goods and services, and self-service storage facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces the Maryland Consumer Protection Act through its Consumer Protection Division. The bill establishes that a violation of the prohibited contract terms constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article, subjecting violators to enforcement and civil penalties by the office.

The bill directly impacts the judicial system by declaring certain consumer contract clauses void and unenforceable, instructing courts on how to handle contracts containing illegal provisions, and creating a private right of action for declaratory relief and injunctions.
The bill explicitly mentions the Maryland Public Service Commission, establishing an exemption from the bill's provisions for consumer contracts involving services regulated by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program within the Motor Vehicle Administration by October 1, 2027. Requires drivers facing license suspension or revocation for specific speed-related offenses to participate for one year. Directs the Administration to issue restrictive licenses requiring aftermarket devices that actively prevent vehicles from speeding. Establishes certification standards for service providers and requires destruction of collected driver data within 90 days. Requires the District Court to establish separate fine schedule entries for distinct reckless driving offenses. Terminates the pilot program on June 30, 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers facing license suspension or revocation for point accumulation from speeding or reckless driving, intelligent speed assistance system manufacturers, and certified service providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase by up to $61,020 annually from fiscal 2028 through 2031 through program participation and licensing fees. The Motor Vehicle Administration can likely implement the program with existing resources, although consultant costs to develop program parameters could reach $100,000 annually. District Court fine schedule modifications can be absorbed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and regulating the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program, issuing restrictive licenses, certifying service providers, monitoring participants, setting fees, and reporting to the General Assembly and Governor.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund, which will receive program participation fee revenues, and may receive data collected under the program.

The bill mandates that the District Court include separate entries in its traffic fine schedule for specific reckless driving violations and permits the sharing of program data with courts exercising jurisdiction over participants.
The bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to submit a comprehensive implementation report on the pilot program to the Governor by December 30, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Volunteer Services Program in the Division of Correction to assist incarcerated individuals with release preparation. Requires the Division of Correction to establish a protocol registering volunteers, including formerly incarcerated individuals and organizations led by formerly incarcerated individuals. Requires the Division of Correction to submit the registration protocol to the Office of the Attorney General for approval. Grants volunteers the right to elect public disclosure of their names, requiring written consent for disclosure. Prohibits the Division from denying a volunteer's facility access schedule unless it interferes with normal correctional facility operations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Correction; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in State correctional facilities, formerly incarcerated individuals, and volunteer organizations led by formerly incarcerated individuals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the program using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Release Preparation Volunteer Services Program directly within the Division of Correction, a principal unit of DPSCS, requiring the department to establish registration protocols, maintain volunteer records, manage access schedules, and handle public disclosures.
The bill specifically requires the Division of Correction to submit the newly established volunteer registration protocol to the Office of the Attorney General for review and approval.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes automatic voter registration restoration for individuals released from State correctional facilities. Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to transmit monthly release records to the State Board of Elections. Requires the State Board to promptly restore active voter registration for previously registered individuals residing in Maryland. Requires local election directors to enclose explanatory notices and declination options with voter notification cards. Mandates that both agencies jointly develop procedures and an electronic transmission process by January 1, 2028. Prohibits public disclosure of the agency identity through which a formerly incarcerated voter is registered.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals released from incarceration at State correctional facilities who were registered to vote in Maryland before incarceration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Local government expenditures increase collectively by $400,000 in FY 2027 for one-time statewide voter registration system development costs billed to local boards of elections. State finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is directly tasked with jointly developing and implementing procedures and an electronic transmission system with the State Board of Elections, and must transmit monthly lists of individuals released from State correctional facilities to SBE.

SBE is the primary agency responsible for jointly developing the transmission process, receiving monthly release data from DPSCS, matching records to identify eligible individuals previously registered to vote in Maryland, and restoring their active voter registration status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes certain agents providing payroll processing services from the definition of money transmitter under the Maryland Money Transmission Act. Applies the exclusion when a written agreement directs the agent to provide payroll processing services on the payor's behalf. Requires the payor to hold the agent out to employees and other payees as providing those payroll processing services. Specifies that the payor's obligation to a payee is not extinguished if the agent fails to remit the funds. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation, Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Payroll processing service providers, employers and payors using payroll agents, and employees or payees receiving payroll funds
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor decrease by $6,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to lost money transmitter licensing fees. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor's Office of Financial Regulation regulates money transmitters and oversees the licensing requirements under the Maryland Money Transmission Act. The bill excludes certain payroll processors from the definition of money transmitter, resulting in an estimated reduction of $6,000 annually in special fund licensing fee revenue for the department beginning in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes qualifying Class B and Class D licensees in Baltimore County to sell mixed drinks or cocktails for off-premises consumption. Applies only if the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County adopts regulations after considering public health impacts. Requires drinks to be purchased with prepared food other than prepackaged snacks and sold not later than 11 p.m. Requires purchasers to be at least 21 years old and provide valid identification as proof of age. Prohibits the Board from charging a license holder an additional fee for these off-premises sales. Authorizes the Board to limit the quantity of alcoholic beverages sold to an individual in a single transaction.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages licenses operating restaurants or bars in Baltimore County, and alcoholic beverage consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Local finances and operations in Baltimore County are not expected to be materially affected because the board is prohibited from charging an additional fee for the permit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and administers state sales and excise taxes. While implementation and permitting under this bill are handled locally by the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal effect, the bill governs retail alcoholic beverage sales and off-premises consumption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud to examine deed fraud incidents across Maryland. Requires the task force to examine complaint numbers, case resolutions, restitution awards, and perpetrator patterns. Directs the task force to evaluate victim demographics, economic impacts, and anti-fraud practices in other states. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to provide staff for the task force. Requires the task force to report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; Task Force to Study Deed Fraud
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland property owners, victims of deed fraud, title insurance industry professionals, and notaries public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are minimally affected, as the Department of Legislative Services can staff the task force and absorb any travel reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud, a temporary executive advisory body tasked with studying incidents of deed fraud and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or the Secretary's designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud.

The Governor is responsible for designating the chair of the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud and appointing two members (a representative of the land title insurance industry and an individual with notary public experience).

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees to state boards, commissions, and task forces, which applies to the two appointed members of the Task Force.

The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland designates a representative of the Judiciary to serve on the Task Force, and the Task Force will analyze court data regarding deed fraud cases and restitution.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a political subdivision to designate a noncontiguous blighted area as a development district. Extends this specific designation authority under the Tax Increment Financing Act to Baltimore City. Defines a blighted area as one where a majority of buildings declined in productivity to an extent that no longer justifies maintenance. Allows political subdivisions to issue tax increment financing bonds for these designated noncontiguous districts. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland political subdivisions
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, property owners and businesses in blighted areas, and construction contractors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances. Local revenues and expenditures increase beginning as early as fiscal 2027 from tax increment financing bond proceeds, debt service, and redevelopment spending, though specific dollar figures are unavailable. The bill has no fiscal impact on Baltimore City because its city charter already permits noncontiguous districts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 135 amends the Economic Development Article regarding Tax Increment Financing (TIF) authority and development districts. While implementation is carried out by local political subdivisions, the Department of Commerce serves as the state's lead economic development agency and tracks municipal and county economic development financing tools and policies.

Under Maryland's Tax Increment Financing Act framework, local tax increment revenues may be pledged to debt issued by MEDCO for economic development projects. Expanding development districts to include noncontiguous blighted areas may affect projects or debt structures facilitated by MEDCO.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes collective bargaining for graduate assistants at the University of Maryland, College Park and University of Maryland, Baltimore County. Defines graduate assistants to include teaching, administrative, or research assistants, fellows, and postdoctoral interns. Establishes a separate collective bargaining unit at each institution for eligible graduate assistants. Maintains existing collective bargaining exclusions for positions funded through research grants, service contracts, or clinical revenues. Takes effect July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board; University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Graduate assistants, teaching assistants, research assistants, administrative assistants, fellows, and postdoctoral interns at the University of Maryland, College Park and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County; University System of Maryland administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase minimally beginning in FY 2029 for UMCP and UMBC to reimburse the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) for election and bargaining costs, with corresponding minimal increases in PERB reimbursable revenues and expenditures. UMCP and UMBC administrative, salary, and benefit costs may also increase depending on future collective bargaining negotiations. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) to administer and oversee collective bargaining, union elections, unit certifications, and dispute resolutions for the newly authorized graduate assistant bargaining units, which will result in reimbursable expenditures and revenues.

The legislation directly impacts two constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland—the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP) and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC)—by extending collective bargaining rights to eligible graduate assistants, leading to administrative, personnel, and negotiation costs.

Morgan State University is explicitly referenced in the statutory sections amended by the bill regarding higher education collective bargaining units, but it is not directly impacted as the definition of eligible graduate assistants is limited to UMCP and UMBC.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly referenced in the amended statutory sections governing higher education bargaining units, though it experiences no operational or fiscal impact because the definition of graduate assistants applies only to UMCP and UMBC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county or municipal corporation to designate an assistant State fire marshal with the State Fire Marshal's approval. Requires the State Fire Marshal to adopt regulations establishing minimum qualification, training, and certification standards for assistant fire marshals. Mandates automatic fire sprinklers and specific fire safety features in residential rental high-rise buildings undergoing substantial renovations. Defines substantial renovations as permanent alterations costing at least 40% of the building's assessed value intended to enhance property value. Requires the State Fire Prevention Commission to adopt regulations establishing a licensing and regulatory program for fire alarm system technicians.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal; State Fire Prevention Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Fire alarm system technicians and companies; owners and tenants of residential rental high-rise buildings; local fire departments and assistant State fire marshals; county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $311,100 in FY 2027 and between $231,400 and $264,500 annually thereafter for staff, IT licensing system upgrades, and staff certifications. General fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount from new licensing fees as early as FY 2027. Local government expenditures increase to cover training and certification costs for assistant State fire marshals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission are agencies within the Maryland Department of State Police. The bill tasks the State Fire Prevention Commission with establishing a licensing and regulatory program for fire alarm system technicians and requires the State Fire Marshal to set qualification standards and regulations for assistant fire marshals, resulting in direct operational and budgetary impacts for the department.

USM institutions own and manage residential high-rise housing facilities (such as student residence halls) that are subject to the bill's requirement to install automatic fire sprinkler systems and life safety features if they undergo substantial renovations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant a local property tax credit for converted retail service stations. Applies to real property converted from a service station to residential, mixed retail and residential, or other retail use. Excludes conversions to discount stores, self-service storage facilities, alcohol retailers, and licensed tobacco or vape retailers. Prohibits granting the credit unless underground storage tanks are permanently closed under Department of the Environment regulations. Permits local governing bodies to establish the amount, duration, and additional eligibility criteria for the credit. Takes effect June 1, 2026, for taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; county governing bodies; municipal corporation governing bodies; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and developers converting retail service stations to retail, residential, or mixed-use properties; local governments in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent local jurisdictions enact and grant the tax credit; specific revenue impact figures are unavailable. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly conditions eligibility for the local property tax credit on underground storage tanks being permanently closed in accordance with Department of the Environment (MDE) regulations, directly aligning with MDE's regulatory oversight of underground storage tanks and contamination remediation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county board of education to consider the provision of educator workforce housing as a school purpose. Defines educator workforce housing as affordable housing reserved for non-administrative local school system employees. Expands the Housing Innovation Fund and Housing Innovation Pilot Program to include municipal corporations and county boards of education. Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to prioritize funding for pilot program projects that include educator workforce housing. Adds educator workforce housing to qualifying projects under the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Teachers and non-administrative employees of local school systems; county boards of education; municipal corporations; housing developers; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Housing and Community Development can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, and State revenues are unaffected. Local school boards and municipal corporations become eligible for State financial assistance to support educator workforce housing development, with no other material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Housing Innovation Fund, the Housing Innovation Pilot Program, and the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program, all of which are directly amended by the bill to incorporate and prioritize educator workforce housing.

The bill amends the Education Article to allow county boards of education to classify educator workforce housing as a 'school purpose' when acquiring, maintaining, or determining whether to dispose of school land and buildings, an area overseen with the approval of the State Superintendent of Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes sole owners or specified co-owners of marine vessels to designate a transfer-on-death beneficiary. Expands existing law to allow specified co-owners of motor vehicles to designate a transfer-on-death beneficiary. Restricts eligible co-ownership to joint tenants with right of survivorship or tenants by the entirety. Transfers vehicle or vessel ownership to surviving beneficiaries outside probate administration upon the last owner's death. Requires surviving beneficiaries to apply for a new certificate of title with required documentation and fees. Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources and the Motor Vehicle Administration to establish fees covering costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Sole owners and co-owners of marine vessels, co-owners of motor vehicles, and designated transfer-on-death beneficiaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Department of Natural Resources (State Boat Act Fund) and the Transportation Trust Fund may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 from certificate of title fees. General fund revenues may experience a minimal decrease from reduced probate fees and inheritance tax collections. State expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for vessel transfer-on-death (TOD) designations, tasked with processing applications, issuing new certificates of title, adopting regulations, and collecting associated fees deposited into the State Boat Act Fund.

MVA is the primary implementing agency for motor vehicle transfer-on-death (TOD) designations, responsible for processing applications from co-owners, updating certificates of title, and adopting regulations.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and manages the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will see an increase in revenues from motor vehicle title application fees.

The bill allows qualifying vessels and motor vehicles to transfer directly to beneficiaries outside of probate estate administration, which directly impacts the estate assets handled by the Registers of Wills and may reduce probate fees and inheritance tax collections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the annual cap on venison donation State income tax credits an individual may claim. Authorizes a credit of up to $75 for qualified butchering and processing expenses per antlerless deer. Requires donating the meat to an eligible tax-exempt venison donation program. Prohibits carrying over unused credit amounts to any other taxable year. Takes effect July 1, 2026, for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Abrogates when the termination provision in Chapters 769 and 770 of 2024 takes effect.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals who hunt, harvest, and donate antlerless deer; charitable venison donation programs; deer meat butchers and processors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $125,000 annually in FY 2027 through FY 2029 due to additional tax credits claimed against the personal income tax. The Comptroller of Maryland can administer the changes using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering state tax credits and collecting income taxes. Under the bill, venison donation programs must report annual donor and donation information directly to the Comptroller, and the bill impacts state income tax revenues collected by the office.

The Department of Natural Resources oversees state wildlife management, regulates deer hunting compliance required to qualify for the tax credit, and administers the complementary Venison Donation Grant Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires political parties and unaffiliated presidential candidates to submit elector nominees and alternate elector nominees with executed voting pledges. Designates the State Administrator of Elections to preside and serve as secretary at the presidential electors meeting. Establishes vacancy replacement procedures using alternate presidential electors or appointments by remaining electors. Prohibits the State Administrator from accepting ballots marked in violation of an elector's pledge. Vacates the office of any elector who refuses to vote or votes contrary to their pledge. Directs the State Administrator and Governor to prepare and transmit amended certificates of ascertainment if electors change.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections; State Board of Elections; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: presidential electors, alternate presidential elector nominees, political parties in Maryland, and unaffiliated presidential candidates
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill can be implemented with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns substantial administrative and oversight duties to the State Board and the State Administrator of Elections, including receiving presidential elector nominations and pledges, presiding over the electors' meeting, verifying ballots, administering substitute elector appointments, and preparing certificates of vote.

The bill mandates specific certification requirements for the Governor when submitting the State's certificate of ascertainment under federal law and requires the Governor to sign and deliver an amended certificate of ascertainment if substitute electors are appointed.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a person to file an expungement petition for specified criminal offenses under certain disposition conditions. Applies when a remaining charge was disposed of by a court with a no finding designation. Applies also when a remaining charge was included in a case designated as terminated without finding. Covers listed misdemeanors, listed felonies, and attempts, conspiracies, or solicitations of those offenses. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals seeking expungement of criminal records for cases with charges disposed of with a no finding designation or terminated without finding
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $11,740 in FY 2027 only for the Judiciary to update expungement-related brochures, forms, and instructional videos. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary by expanding eligibility for petitions for expungement under Criminal Procedure § 10-110, requiring revisions to court forms, brochures, and instructional videos, as well as operational adjustments in court case management systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), which serves as the central repository for criminal records and is responsible for processing and complying with court-ordered expungements.
As the primary state law enforcement agency and a keeper of police records, MSP must comply with court orders to expunge police records covered under the expanded expungement criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits merchants from refusing cash payments for in-person purchases of essential consumer goods totaling less than $300. Applies to sales between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., banning surcharges on cash transactions and mandatory card use. Defines essential goods to include food, water and beverages, personal hygiene items, health products, and fuel. Exempts remote transactions, vending machines, on-premises food consumption, specialty gourmet shops, and membership fuel sales. Authorizes merchants to refuse denominations over $20 or offer fee-free prepaid card conversion machines on site. Establishes civil fines up to $1,000 enforced by the Consumer Protection Division after two compliance warnings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Retail merchants selling essential consumer goods to the public, consumers purchasing essential goods with cash, and retail establishments operating in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can enforce the provisions using existing resources, and civil penalty revenues are not expected to be material.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to enforce the new cash acceptance requirements, mandate compliance opportunities, and assess civil penalties for violations under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires State procurement officers to debrief unsuccessful offerors upon request before contract awards receive final approval. Mandates contract clauses authorizing contractor requests for equitable adjustments caused by changes in State law. Exempts individuals who provide information from solicitation drafting conflict-of-interest prohibitions if no unfair competitive advantage occurs. Extends dispute and claim resolution procedures beyond construction contracts to all State procurement contracts. Lengthens the deadline for contractors to file written notices of contract claims to 60 days. Requires contractors to certify claim accuracy and good faith before receiving payment on a contract claim.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of State Procurement; State procurement units
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement contractors, subcontractors, bidders, and offerors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may experience indeterminate increases from potential contract award delays and bid protests, but implementation can be handled with existing agency resources and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of State Procurement, which is housed within the Department of General Services as the state's central procurement authority, with establishing statewide guidelines and procedures for procurement debriefings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the procedures, timelines, default denial determinations, and appeal mechanisms for bid protests and contract claims appealed to the Board.
The bill explicitly mandates that procurement officers seek the advice of the Office of the Attorney General on any legal issues raised in timely bid protests and contract claims.

As the state's highest procurement review body, the Board of Public Works is directly referenced regarding the requirement that debriefings for unsuccessful offerors occur before contract awards are presented to the Board for approval.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to publish a real property flood risk disclosure form by June 1, 2027. Applies to residential real property improved by four or fewer single-family units, subject to specified exemptions. Requires vendors, beginning July 1, 2027, to provide purchasers a completed form before entering into a contract of sale. Requires vendors to provide a copy of any available FEMA elevation certificate for the property. Mandates disclosures on flood hazard zones, insurance, federal disaster aid, and past property flood damage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of residential real property improved by four or fewer single-family units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled by the Maryland Department of the Environment using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of the Environment to develop, publish, and maintain the real property flood risk disclosure statement form required for residential property sales by June 1, 2027.

The Department of Labor regulates and licenses real estate brokers, salespersons, and industry professionals through the Maryland Real Estate Commission, who must incorporate the new disclosure requirement into residential real estate transaction practices.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees consumer protection in real estate transactions and may handle enforcement or inquiries regarding deceptive practices or failure to provide mandatory property disclosures.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial system, which may hear civil disputes and litigation arising from real estate contract disputes or noncompliance with statutory disclosure mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Baltimore County to grant a property tax credit against county property taxes. Covers real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 located at 730 Wampler Road. Requires the property tax credit to equal 100% of the property tax imposed on the property. Takes effect June 1, 2026. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 and Baltimore County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $9,600 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 if the credit is granted. County expenditures and State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes an optional local property tax credit on a specific parcel in Baltimore County. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is responsible for hearing appeals concerning real property valuations, exemptions, and property tax credits, giving it low administrative relevance in the event of an eligibility or application dispute.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including appeals arising from local taxing authority decisions and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property taxes and credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting, or obtaining an individual through deception, coercion, exploitation, or isolation to appropriate government benefits. Prohibits knowingly benefiting from or aiding, abetting, or conspiring in benefits exploitation ventures. Establishes graduated penalties ranging from a misdemeanor to felonies based on aggregate benefit values. Subjects offenses involving $100,000 or more to imprisonment up to 20 years and fines up to $25,000. Treats each violation as a separate offense that may run concurrently or consecutively with related sentences.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Recipients of government assistance programs, elderly or disabled adults, and individuals accused of benefits exploitation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,600 in FY 2027 only for one-time computer programming by the Judiciary. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal offenses and graduated penalties for benefits exploitation, requiring the Judiciary to implement one-time computer programming changes in FY 2027 costing approximately $1,600 and adjudicate new cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor and felony offenses, which will generate additional caseloads for the Office of the Public Defender to provide legal representation to indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes prison terms ranging from up to 1 year for misdemeanors to up to 20 years for felonies, which impacts correctional facility operations and community supervision under DPSCS.

The Office of the Attorney General houses specialized units, such as the Senior and Vulnerable Adult Asset Recovery Unit and Medicaid Fraud Division, tasked with addressing the financial exploitation of vulnerable individuals and benefit fraud.

The bill specifically protects government assistance programs administered by DHS, including TANF, SNAP, TDAP, and Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), and aligns with DHS's role in protecting vulnerable adults and low-income individuals from economic abuse.

The bill defines government benefits to include Medicaid, which is administered by MDH, and addresses coercion involving the denial of medical care or improper provision of controlled dangerous substances.

The bill addresses coercion and financial control exerted over elderly adults, directly touching on the Department of Aging's mission to protect the rights, safety, and well-being of older Marylanders from exploitation.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating criminal violations, including trafficking-like recruitment, harboring, and exploitation of individuals for benefit theft.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual reporting deadline for the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit from November 30 to October 1. Requires the Attorney General to submit the report annually to the Governor and the General Assembly. Specifies that the report must cover the activities of the Unit during the previous fiscal year. Requires reporting on actions taken by the Department of the Environment or the Department of Natural Resources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland Department of the Environment, and Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. The bill has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the annual reporting date and reporting period for the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit, which operates within the Office of the Attorney General.

The required annual report documents actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations of the Unit, and the date change aligns with MDE's enforcement reporting timeline.
The annual report explicitly includes actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to the Unit's findings and recommendations.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the annual report submitted by the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes owners, operators, managers, contractors, and local housing authorities to install individual water submeters in apartment houses and mobile home parks. Prohibits charging units more than actual water provider charges, allocated in proportion to actual usage. Restricts charges for common area usage, leaks, poor maintenance, and nonresidential areas, while permitting a one-dollar monthly administrative fee. Requires owners to maintain adequate records and permits estimated billing if a submeter fails. Prohibits billing occupants after two consecutive billing cycles if an inaccurate submeter remains unreplaced or unrepaired. Requires landlords mandating third-party water payments to use written leases and provide advance bill notices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Housing and Community Development; Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division); Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, operators, managers, and contractors of apartment houses and mobile home parks; residential tenants and occupants; local housing authorities; water service providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agency operations and requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory agency tasked with adopting standards and regulations for the accuracy, testing, and recordkeeping of individual water submeters in consultation with DHCD.
DHCD is required to consult with MDE on the development of regulations and standards for water submeters, and must approve the installation of submeters by local housing authorities.

The Consumer Protection Division within the OAG is authorized to handle consumer complaints against apartment and mobile home park owners/operators regarding water submeter billing when local enforcement bodies are unavailable.
The Board of Public Works (or equivalent local authority) must approve the installation of individual submeters by local housing authorities.
The bill creates private causes of action for occupants and specifies that unpaid water bills under submetering may not be treated as unpaid rent in court eviction proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland Horse Industry Board by 10 years to July 1, 2036. Continues the board's statutory and regulatory authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the licensing and inspection of horse stables throughout the State. Preserves the Maryland Horse Industry Fund to support equine research, education, and promotion. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Horse Industry Board; Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed horse stable operators, commercial equine feed purchasers and distributors, and the Maryland equine industry
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the board from FY 2027 through FY 2036. The FY 2027 budget includes $435,471 in special funds and $12,298 in federal funds for board operations. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board (MHIB) is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. The bill directly extends the board's statutory authority, operations, licensing functions, and associated special funds through July 1, 2036.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board is a statutory state regulatory and advisory board whose operational termination date is extended by 10 years under this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Disabilities to oversee and administer affordable and accessible housing programs. Authorizes the department to establish one or more affiliated foundations to support specified departmental programs and units. Prohibits an affiliated foundation from making or influencing policy decisions, program standards, or eligibility determinations.
