Permits department officials and employees to serve without compensation as directors or officials of an affiliated foundation. Requires the department to hire an independent certified public accountant annually to audit each affiliated foundation. Requires the Secretary of Disabilities to deposit contributions from an affiliated foundation into a separate special fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities; Office of the Attorney General; State Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with disabilities, Maryland Department of Disabilities personnel, affiliated foundations, and private or public donors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Department of Disabilities special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount from foundation contributions. State general fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate, minimal amount for required annual independent audits if costs cannot be absorbed with existing resources. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOD is the primary subject and implementing agency of the bill, which requires the department to administer affordable and accessible housing programs and authorizes it to establish and oversee affiliated foundations.

The bill explicitly tasks the State Ethics Commission with reviewing and approving foundation operating policies regarding conflicts of interest, evaluating notices of MDOD employees serving on foundation boards, and receiving annual implementation reports.
The bill requires the Office of the Attorney General to review and approve the operating policies developed by MDOD for form and legal sufficiency.
The bill requires MDOD to submit an annual report to the Governor by September 1 detailing the personnel serving in affiliated foundations and the implementation of operational policies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the authority of the Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service to delegate financial functions to the Deputy Treasurer. Increases the maximum expenditure threshold for small procurements by the Service from $25,000 to $50,000. Requires the Service to notify service district residents at least 60 days before establishing or adjusting district charges. Alters newspaper notice formatting for proposed charges and requires placement with legal notices. Requires the Service to provide supplemental notice via website posting, electronic messaging, or mail. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Service
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Environmental Service contractors and vendors, and residents, property owners, and ratepayers in Maryland Environmental Service service districts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on Maryland Environmental Service finances, though the Service may experience administrative efficiencies from procuring more goods and services under small procurement procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 227 is a departmental bill specifically governing the Maryland Environmental Service (MES). It expands the financial functions the MES Treasurer may delegate to the Deputy Treasurer, raises MES's small procurement expenditure threshold from $25,000 to $50,000, and updates public notice requirements for rate changes in MES service districts.

The bill references the State Treasurer's role in determining the type and coverage amount of the surety bond or insurance policy required for the Deputy Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits slaughtering or causing the slaughter of a racehorse in the State for any commercial purpose. Bans purchasing, selling, transferring, offering for sale, importing, or transporting racehorses known to face commercial slaughter. Establishes misdemeanor criminal penalties and fines up to $5,000 for individual and entity violations. Authorizes the State Racing Commission and State Department of Agriculture to suspend or revoke violators' licenses. Distributes all fine revenue collected under the Act to the racing Special Fund. Permits humane euthanasia performed by a licensed veterinarian for reasons unrelated to commercial purposes.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Racing Commission; State Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Racehorse owners, breeders, trainers, equine dealers, commercial transporters, and State Racing Commission licensees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 from fines collected from violators, but the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Labor. Its unit, the Maryland Racing Commission, is tasked with adopting implementing regulations (in consultation with the Department of Agriculture), authorized to suspend or revoke licenses for violations, and directs collected fine revenue into the horse racing Special Fund.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture to revoke or suspend licenses it has issued upon finding a violation, and requires the Maryland Racing Commission to consult with the department when adopting implementing regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum allowable outstanding principal balance of Maryland Transportation Authority revenue bonds from $4.0 billion to $5.0 billion. Applies this debt limit to revenue bonds secured by toll revenue as of June 30 each year. Requires the maximum aggregate amount to be reduced by certain federal transportation loans or drawn credit lines. Authorizes the Authority to issue bonds to refinance prior transportation facility projects without General Assembly approval. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists and commercial drivers using Maryland toll facilities, bondholders, and transportation construction contractors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MDTA nonbudgeted revenues increase significantly, potentially beginning in fiscal 2029, from proceeds of additional bond issuances. Nonbudgeted expenditures increase correspondingly to pay related debt service. Local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly increases the Maryland Transportation Authority's statutory cap on outstanding toll revenue-backed debt from $4.0 billion to $5.0 billion to finance capital projects and bridge reconstruction.
MDOT is the parent department of MDTA that requested this departmental legislation and coordinates overall state transportation capital programming and federal reimbursement tracking.
The State Treasurer acts as Maryland's chief financial officer overseeing state debt and bond activity, and served as an information source for the fiscal evaluation of this debt capacity increase.
DBM oversees statewide fiscal planning and capital budget evaluations, and was consulted as an information source regarding the fiscal impacts of adjusting authority debt limits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Delays the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029–2030 financial aid award year. Maintains central award notification and issuance by the Office of Student Financial Assistance through fiscal 2029. Postpones requirements for institutions of higher education to determine and offer grant awards using certified need rankings. Defers mandatory institutional reporting of award recipients and subsequent State reimbursements until the 2029–2030 award year. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for and recipients of Guaranteed Access Grants, Maryland public four-year institutions, locally funded community colleges, and participating nonpublic institutions of higher education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Delays State and local higher education administrative expenditures associated with institutional grant processing until fiscal 2029. Any potential general fund appropriations intended to offset institutional costs are likewise postponed. Specific cost figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC requested this departmental legislation and oversees the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA), which administers the Guaranteed Access Grant Program. The bill directly delays the transfer of grant notification and awarding responsibilities from MHEC to higher education institutions until the 2029–2030 award year.

This departmental bill directly impacts the commission's operational timeline and administrative responsibilities by delaying the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029–2030 financial aid award year.

USM constituent institutions are directly impacted by the delayed transfer of administrative responsibilities, operational costs, and corresponding state revenues associated with notifying applicants and issuing Guaranteed Access Grant awards until FY 2029.

As an independent public institution of higher education, MSU's financial aid office is impacted by the postponement of responsibilities and funding related to the decentralization of Guaranteed Access Grant notifications and awards.

As a public four-year higher education institution, the college's financial aid operations and associated administrative costs are affected by the delayed transition of Guaranteed Access Grant responsibilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands tuition assistance provided by the Maryland Military Department for eligible active Maryland National Guard members. Authorizes assistance covering up to 100% of training assistance expenses directly related to required professional development resources. Adds private postsecondary vocational-technical, trade, or career schools recognized by designated State education and apprenticeship bodies. Repeals the requirement that private postsecondary vocational-technical schools provide a tuition waiver of at least 50%. Requires members who receive assistance for career courses to remain active for at least 2 years after completion.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Military Department
qa_results.stakeholders: Active members of the Maryland National Guard and private postsecondary vocational-technical, trade, and career schools.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. Assistance is authorized only to the extent funds are provided in the State budget, which included $600,000 annually in fiscal 2025 through 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is the primary official responsible for certifying the eligibility of National Guard service members to receive tuition and training assistance and enforcing subsequent active service commitments.

Active members of the Maryland National Guard are the direct beneficiaries of the expanded tuition and training assistance for trade and career courses, and are subject to the associated mandatory service obligations.

The bill expands eligible institutions to include private postsecondary trade or career schools recognized and approved by MHEC, without requiring private schools to offer a minimum 50% tuition waiver.

The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC) and oversees workforce development programs; schools and training recognized by MATC are newly incorporated into the tuition and training assistance program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals a restriction on promotion pay rates for Department of State Police police employees and deputy State fire marshals. Removes an exception that reduced an employee's pay step upon promotion based on another employee's service time. Entitles promoted police employees and deputy State fire marshals to their prior pay step in the new rank without exception. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: police employees and deputy State fire marshals in the Department of State Police
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No current State fiscal impact because the Department of State Police has not used the pay restriction on prior promotions. Future promotional costs are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing agency resources. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the promotional pay rates and step placements for police employees and deputy State fire marshals within the Department of State Police, and was introduced as a departmental request by the agency.
As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM reviews and approves State Police pay plans and oversees state compensation and personnel classifications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces from 45 days to 15 days the time a political subdivision has to respond to project notices. Applies to financial assistance applications submitted under the Neighborhood Business Development Program. Authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to approve applications if no local response arrives within 15 days. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Small businesses, nonprofit organizations, and microenterprises applying for Neighborhood Business Development Program financing, and local political subdivisions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected because the Department of Housing and Community Development can handle administrative changes with existing resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) altering the local approval timeframe for financial assistance applications under DHCD's Neighborhood Business Development Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the window for required contestant blood testing from 30 days to 90 days before licensing or participation. Applies to applicants and licensed contestants in boxing, kick boxing, wrestling, and mixed martial arts contests. Requires documentary evidence of negative test results for HIV antibodies, hepatitis B virus antigen, and hepatitis C antibodies. Mandates contestants present these negative results when applying for a license or whenever directed by the Commission. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Athletic Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants and licensed contestants in boxing, kick boxing, wrestling, and mixed martial arts contests, as well as combat sports promoters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Labor. The State Athletic Commission, which administers and enforces the licensing and blood testing requirements for combat sports contestants modified by the bill, is housed within the Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Maryland Heritage Area Authority and increases its quorum from nine to ten voting members. Adds the Secretary of Agriculture and the State Superintendent of Schools to the Authority. Replaces a Maryland Greenways Commission appointee with an expert in natural resource stewardship or climate resiliency. Authorizes the Authority to establish terms, conditions, and matching fund proportions for grants and loans. Repeals statutory 50% matching fund caps on grants for management plans, acquisition, development, and programming. Repeals requirements to send boundary maps to county clerks and to submit interagency program statements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Heritage Area Authority; Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: Local jurisdictions, heritage area management entities, and applicants for Maryland Heritage Areas Program grants and loans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Overall funding under the Maryland Heritage Areas Program remains unchanged, though local jurisdictions may experience greater access to grants and loans due to the Authority's discretion to adjust matching fund requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA) is an independent unit within the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) and is staffed by the Maryland Historical Trust. MDP requested this departmental legislation to update the authority's membership, grant-making flexibility, and statutory requirements.

The bill adds the Secretary of Agriculture as a voting member of the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority and establishes a statutory responsibility for the Secretary to support and assist activities regarding agricultural resources within certified heritage areas.

The bill adds the State Superintendent of Schools as a voting member of the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority and assigns the Superintendent responsibilities regarding educational resources and their interpretation within certified heritage areas.

The Secretary of Commerce is a voting member of the Authority, and the bill modifies the statutory requirement for the Secretary regarding supporting tourism, economic development, and job creation in certified heritage areas.

The Secretary of Natural Resources is a voting member of the Authority and provides support for outdoor recreation and natural resources. The bill also alters an appointed seat previously tied to the Maryland Greenways Commission.
The Secretary of Transportation is a voting member of the Authority, and the bill updates requirements regarding transportation access, scenic byways, and signage within certified heritage areas.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development serves as a voting member of the Authority with statutory responsibilities regarding housing and neighborhood revitalization in certified heritage areas.
The Secretary of Higher Education serves as a voting member of the Authority and carries duties related to educational resources and their interpretation.
The Secretary of General Services has statutory duties under the bill to support and assist certified heritage area activities regarding the management and disposition of State property.
The Governor appoints ten public and local government members to the Authority with the advice and consent of the Senate, and the bill alters the qualifications for one of the appointed seats.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for appointed boards and commissions, including the modified public appointment for a member with expertise in natural resource stewardship or climate resiliency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local planning commissions to notify the Maryland Department of Planning when beginning a 10-year comprehensive plan review. Requires the Department to provide guidance materials within 60 days after receiving notification. Specifies that guidance materials must address State laws, best practices, and resources supporting plan review or amendment. Directs the Department to develop and maintain guidance materials in consultation with other State agencies and offices. Replaces statutory references to "visions" with "planning principles" in local comprehensive planning and reporting laws.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: local planning commissions, county governments, and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Planning can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 240 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP). The bill requires local planning commissions to notify MDP when initiating a 10-year review of their comprehensive plans, mandates that MDP provide guidance materials to local jurisdictions within 60 days of notification, and directs MDP to develop and maintain these guidance materials in consultation with other state entities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory authority for five State licensing entities through July 1, 2032. Reauthorizes the State Board of Barbers and the State Board of Cosmetologists. Reauthorizes the State Board for Professional Land Surveyors and the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers. Reauthorizes the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to report on each entity by July 1, 2030. Mandates submission of information determined by the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee to that committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; State Board of Barbers; State Board of Cosmetologists; State Board for Professional Land Surveyors; State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors; State Board of Individual Tax Preparers; Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed barbers, cosmetologists, professional land surveyors, real estate appraisers, appraisal management companies, home inspectors, and individual tax preparers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained through fiscal 2032 for the affected boards and commission. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee can handle the reporting requirement with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 241 directly extends the statutory termination dates for five professional licensing boards and commissions operating within the Maryland Department of Labor and requires the Department to submit evaluation reports to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2030.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reauthorizes and extends the statutory sunset dates through July 1, 2032, for multiple ongoing regulatory boards and commissions, including the State Board of Barbers, the State Board of Cosmetologists, the State Board for Professional Land Surveyors, the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors, and the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters confidentiality requirements for unemployment insurance records to ensure compliance with federal law and regulations. Defines confidential unemployment insurance information and establishes standards for safeguarding disclosed records. Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to disclose confidential information under specified circumstances, including to public officials and authorized representatives. Prohibits elected officials from using confidential unemployment insurance data to solicit campaign contributions or expenditures. Expands misdemeanor penalties for unauthorized disclosure or redisclosure of protected information to include former department employees and third-party recipients.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: unemployment insurance claimants, Maryland employers, current and former employees of the Maryland Department of Labor, public officials, third-party data recipients, and child support enforcement units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill from the Maryland Department of Labor that directly governs its administration of the Unemployment Insurance program, updates confidentiality standards for UI information to conform to federal law, and establishes disclosure protocols and penalties for departmental employees and third-party recipients.

The Department of Human Services administers Maryland's child support enforcement program. The bill directly alters and establishes data safeguarding and redisclosure requirements governing how child support enforcement units and their agents access and use confidential unemployment insurance information to enforce child support obligations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reorganizes and modifies the required elements of comprehensive and general plans across Maryland local jurisdictions. Establishes eight standardized plan elements: land, transportation, housing, economy, equity, resilience, place, and ecology. Incorporates prior standalone elements like water resources, sensitive areas, and municipal growth as required subelements. Directs the Maryland Department of Planning and other State agencies to provide local jurisdictions with data and technical assistance. Applies prospectively to local jurisdictions initiating plan amendments, revisions, or readoptions on or after October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Commerce; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Charter counties, code counties, commission counties, and municipal corporations; local planning commissions; commercial watermen; property owners and developers; residents of overburdened and underserved communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the data, technical assistance, and review requirements using existing resources with no effect on state revenues. Local government expenditures may increase for certain jurisdictions that rely on contractual services or supplemental staff to conduct comprehensive plan reviews.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the requesting agency for this departmental legislation, MDP is the primary state entity tasked with implementing the bill. MDP must develop guidelines and best practices, coordinate state agency data and analysis, provide demographic and land use data, and provide technical assistance to local jurisdictions across the comprehensive plan elements.

MDE is directly assigned statutory duties to provide environmental justice data for the equity element, review mineral resources and sensitive areas subelements for consistency with department goals, and provide data, technical assistance, and plan reviews for the water resources subelement.

DNR is statutorily required to supply a statewide forest resource inventory every five years, coordinate with MDP and SHA on wildlife crossings and habitat connectivity, and review local jurisdictions' sensitive areas subelements.

MDOT is statutorily mandated to provide charter counties and local jurisdictions with the best available state-level transportation data and facilitate relevant data sharing from other state and federal agencies to inform the required transportation elements.

DHCD is required to provide local jurisdictions with the best available state-level housing data and collaborate with MDP to provide technical assistance regarding housing elements and fair housing assessments.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of Commerce to supply local jurisdictions with the best available state-level economic development data to inform the newly established economy element.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to provide local jurisdictions with the best available state-level labor force data to inform the newly established economy element.
SHA is specifically named in statute to coordinate with MDP and DNR to supply local jurisdictions with updated data on habitat connectivity concerns and planned wildlife crossings.

The bill requires local resilience elements to align with and be informed by the State Resilience Strategy and the State of Maryland Hazard Mitigation Plan, core plans overseen and administered by MDEM.

The bill incorporates optional priority preservation area subelements under the Land element referencing § 2-518 of the Agriculture Article and addresses prime agricultural land preservation policies.

The municipal growth subelement requires local jurisdictions to plan for public school capacity consistent with State rated capacity standards established by the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes liability for video tolls on the registered owner of a Class G (trailer) vehicle. Applies this liability when the registered owner of the towing motor vehicle cannot be determined. Extends video toll notice, citation, civil penalty, and collection procedures to Class G trailer owners. Authorizes trailer owners to transfer liability under specified circumstances, including vehicle theft or documented third-party towing. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to refuse or suspend vehicle registrations for unpaid toll violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered owners of Class G (trailer) vehicles, operators of motor vehicles towing trailers, and toll facility users
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues for the Maryland Transportation Authority increase significantly beginning in fiscal 2027, potentially by millions of dollars annually, from additional video toll and civil penalty collections. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Central Collection Unit and general fund revenues also increase to the extent delinquent accounts are referred for collection.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDTA is the primary implementing agency of the bill. It assesses video tolls and civil penalties, issues notices of toll due and citations, handles transfers of liability, and refers delinquent accounts to the Central Collection Unit, resulting in a significant increase in nonbudgeted toll revenues.

MVA is responsible for vehicle and trailer registrations and must provide registration and address records to MDTA, as well as enforce registration suspensions or refusals for delinquent Class G vehicle toll violators.
MDOT requested this departmental legislation and serves as the parent agency overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and coordinating transportation facilities and financing alongside MDTA.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), an operational unit within DBM, receives delinquent toll violation accounts referred by MDTA for collection, which impacts CCU special fund revenues, operating expenditures, and general fund fee reversions.
AOC supports the District Court, which has jurisdiction over individuals electing to stand trial to contest video toll citations and civil penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters standards and requirements for granting variances under the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program. Prohibits local jurisdictions from accepting variance applications to authorize unallowed uses or adjust required mitigation. Establishes a rebuttable presumption that existing accessory structures demonstrate reasonable and significant use, excluding accessory dwelling units. Requires applicants to demonstrate substantial need and prove development cannot be located outside a habitat protection area. Requires local boards of appeals to hear variance appeals on the record and defer to administrative factual findings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners and developers seeking variances in the Critical Area, as well as local boards of appeals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 247 is a departmental bill submitted on behalf of the Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays, which is housed within the Department of Natural Resources. The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to alter standards and requirements for local critical area land use variances overseen by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory requirement that photographs on identification cards, driver's licenses, and moped operator's permits be in color. Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to produce these credentials using non-color photographs. Maintains all existing identity, residency, and documentation verification standards for card applicants. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for and holders of Maryland identification cards, driver's licenses, and moped operator's permits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures decrease by approximately $114,000 in FY 2027 and by $152,000 annually thereafter due to reduced printing and cartridge costs. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the direct implementing agency responsible for issuing driver's licenses, identification cards, and moped operator's permits. The bill eliminates the statutory requirement for color photographs on these credentials, reducing MVA's annual printing and materials expenditures by approximately $152,000.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation. The bill results in an expenditure reduction for MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment to impose administrative penalties for violations concerning water appropriation, use, and dam safety. Caps administrative penalties at $5,000 per violation and $100,000 in total. Requires the department to provide written notice and offer an informal settlement meeting before seeking penalty recovery. Expands the department's authority to issue corrective orders and notices across all subtitle provisions. Directs collected administrative penalties to the Maryland Clean Water Fund or the Private Dam Repair Fund. Establishes that unpaid penalties become liens against the violator's real and personal property.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: dam owners, water appropriation and use permit holders, municipal water systems, local governments, and businesses subject to state water and dam safety regulations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Clean Water Fund and Private Dam Repair Fund increase by at least $50,000 in FY 2027 from new penalty collections. Special fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2027 with a matching $250,000 decrease in general fund expenditures to satisfy contingent budget provisions. Local governments and regulated entities experience no material fiscal impact assuming compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill directly granting the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) expanded enforcement authority, including the ability to issue orders and impose administrative penalties up to $5,000 per violation for water appropriation, use, and dam safety violations, with funds deposited into the Maryland Clean Water Fund and the Private Dam Repair Fund.

The bill standardizes administrative notice and hearing procedures under the Administrative Procedure Act for orders and penalties related to water use and dam safety, potentially involving administrative law judges to adjudicate contested cases.

Circuit courts may receive petitions from the Department of the Environment to compel obedience to subpoenas or enforce contempt orders, and clerks of the circuit court are responsible for recording liens on real property for unpaid penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement to submit a notarized bill of sale to the Motor Vehicle Administration when transferring certain used vehicles. Applies to used vehicle sales by persons other than licensed dealers. Sets fair market value at the national publication valuation when the purchase price is at least $500 below retail value. Authorizes the Administration to require alternative purchase documentation, including canceled checks, money order receipts, and loan records. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of used vehicles in private transactions (non-dealer sales)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the vehicle titling and excise tax valuation process administered by the Motor Vehicle Administration, repealing the requirement to submit a notarized bill of sale for private used vehicle transfers.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation to streamline vehicle titling operations and transition to electronic titling.
As the state's chief tax agency, the Comptroller was consulted on the legislation regarding vehicle excise tax provisions, though primary administration remains with MDOT MVA.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of the Environment to require accredited lead paint abatement service providers to carry financial coverage. Permits regulations to mandate coverage by a reasonable performance bond or reasonable liability insurance. Applies to any person accredited by the Department to provide lead paint abatement services. Excludes individuals who act only as workers or project designers from accreditation requirements. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: accredited lead paint abatement contractors, supervisors, and inspectors; residential and commercial property owners; tenants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances. The Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Insurance Administration can implement regulatory updates, outreach, and rate reviews using existing resources. Special fund revenues to the Lead Accreditation Fund may increase minimally from penalties applied under existing law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental request from the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) authorizing it to adopt regulations requiring accredited lead paint abatement contractors, inspectors, and supervisors to maintain reasonable performance bonds or liability insurance.
The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating insurance products and reviewing rates and policy forms developed by insurers offering the liability coverage required by the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to MDE, assists in drafting regulatory changes, and handles enforcement actions and criminal or civil litigation involving lead paint abatement violations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters regulatory requirements for issuing heavy weight port corridor permits for vehicles carrying sealed international freight. Repeals the requirement that travel routes be established by regulation and designated as heavy weight port corridors. Requires the Secretary of Transportation to adopt regulations establishing authorized destinations from the Seagirt Marine Terminal. Requires permitted vehicles to travel only on specific routes identified on the permit without deviation. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial motor carriers and drayage operators transporting international freight from the Seagirt Marine Terminal
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected as the Maryland Department of Transportation can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local operations are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative of MDOT. The Secretary of Transportation is granted statutory authority to adopt regulations setting permit criteria and establishing authorized destinations for heavy weight port corridor permits.
MDOT SHA oversees highway hauling permits and manages the Maryland One Permit Routing System, into which these heavy weight port corridor permits and route assignments will be integrated.
The bill directly governs the transport of international containerized freight originating from the Port of Baltimore's Seagirt Marine Terminal to authorized destinations like Tradepoint Atlantic.
Listed as an information source for the legislation, the Maryland State Police enforces vehicle weight limits, traffic laws, and commercial hauling permit compliance on state highways.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to facilitate community participation in project planning and development. Establishes the Resilience Through Restoration Capital Grant Fund to provide grants for nature-based climate resilience projects. Directs the department to provide planning tools, guidance, and training for local jurisdictions by October 1, 2027. Requires the department to evaluate climate risks on two coastal and two inland department properties by December 31, 2035. Modifies the Shore Erosion Control Construction Loan Fund by removing loan percentage limits and authorizing partial loan forgiveness.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, nonprofit organizations, waterfront property owners, and communities facing climate and flood hazards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2029 due to interest earnings crediting directly to the Shore Erosion Control Construction Loan Fund. Special fund revenues from loan repayments may decrease depending on the extent of partial loan forgiveness granted. State PAYGO general fund expenditures may increase in future years to support the grant fund. Local governments benefit through grant eligibility, technical planning assistance, and expanded shore erosion control financing.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to facilitate community participation in project planning, administer the newly established Resilience Through Restoration Capital Grant Fund, provide resilience tools and training to local jurisdictions, evaluate climate vulnerabilities on department lands, and administer the Shore Erosion Control Construction Loan Fund.

The bill explicitly mandates the State Treasurer to hold and invest the moneys of the newly created Resilience Through Restoration Capital Grant Fund separately, credit interest earnings back to the fund, and manage interest allocations pursuant to exemptions under Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article for both this fund and the Shore Erosion Control Construction Loan Fund.

The bill specifically requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created Resilience Through Restoration Capital Grant Fund and track interest allocation exemptions under Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

DBM oversees the state budget and special funds. The bill restricts General Fund appropriations to the new grant fund in FY 2027 and may impact future PAYGO general fund expenditures and state budget planning.

The bill requires DNR to develop guidance and training to assist local jurisdictions in incorporating climate adaptation planning into local comprehensive plans and other planning documents, which directly intersects with the Department of Planning's role in guiding local comprehensive planning.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the purpose of the Pamela J. Kelly Tree-Mendous Maryland Program in the Department of Natural Resources. Expands the program to promote community participation in tree planting and stewardship. Authorizes the planting and maintaining of native trees and shrubs through community forestry activities. Covers activities on public lands, community open spaces, school grounds, and rights-of-way. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Community members, volunteers, local groups, and schools engaging in tree planting, maintenance, and stewardship on public lands and community spaces
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances, as the bill only broadens the authorized uses of existing donated and grant funds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 255 is a departmental bill that directly modifies the statutory purpose of the Pamela J. Kelly Tree-Mendous Maryland Program, which is administered by the Department of Natural Resources and its Maryland Forest Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates standards and procedures under the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program. Requires the Critical Area Commission to adopt and amend regulations by an affirmative vote. Extends the required comprehensive review cycle for local critical area programs from 6 years to 10 years. Bases Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area mapping mistake corrections on land uses existing on June 1, 2002. Expands the qualified professionals who may prepare, oversee, and approve tree replanting plans after illegal tree clearing. Directs court damages assessed for illegal tree clearing to the applicable local jurisdiction rather than the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays; Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: local jurisdictions within the Critical Area, property owners in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area, licensed foresters, and licensed landscape architects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to directly affect State or local finances because the statutory changes reflect current administrative practice, including the existing local receipt of damages assessed for illegal tree cutting.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative on behalf of the Critical Area Commission, which is housed within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It modifies standards, procedures, and timelines for the Critical Area Protection Program, addresses duties of the State Forester regarding tree replanting plans, and redirects court-assessed damages for illegal tree cutting from DNR to local jurisdictions.

The bill maintains and references statutory procedures under which the chair of the Critical Area Commission may refer violations concerning illegal tree cutting or clearing to the Attorney General to initiate legal action in court.
The bill impacts circuit court actions regarding civil remedies and the assessment of damages for tree cutting violations within the Critical Area, specifying where assessed damages must be paid.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund and alters regulatory requirements for State-chartered financial institutions. Extends the Commissioner of Financial Regulation's authority to match venture fund investments through June 30, 2030. Establishes the venture fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the State Treasurer. Authorizes annual assessment offset credits for qualifying institutions that offer Maryland Opportunity Accounts. Adds cybersecurity incidents necessitating bank closures to the statutory definition of an emergency. Repeals obsolete charter certificate and charter amendment filing fees for banking institutions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: State-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and consumers and businesses in low- to moderate-income census tracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues decrease by an estimated $25,000 in FY 2027 and at least $52,000 annually by FY 2031 due to new assessment offset credits. Special fund expenditures increase by approximately $14,000 annually in FY 2029 and FY 2030 to match venture fund investments. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of Financial Regulation (housed within the Department of Labor), which regulates State-chartered banks and credit unions, oversees the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, establishes deposit growth caps, and administers the annual assessment offset credits.
The bill explicitly designates the State Treasurer as the custodian of the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund and directs the Treasurer to invest the fund's moneys.

The bill amends statutory emergency powers under which the Governor may proclaim an emergency necessitating the closure of banking institutions or branches, expanding the definition to include cybersecurity incidents.
The bill amends § 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding fund interest accrual and exemptions accounted for by the Comptroller of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the earliest date for distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund to participating gubernatorial tickets. Authorizes distributions to begin on July 1 of the year before the election instead of January 1. Changes the annual January campaign finance reporting deadline for campaign finance entities and continuing political committees. Moves the filing deadline from the third Wednesday in January to the fourth Wednesday in January. Requires the January report to cover the period through and including the 14th day before the due date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, campaign finance entities, and continuing political committees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill sponsored at the request of the State Board of Elections. It alters campaign finance reporting deadlines and shifts the earliest date the Board can authorize distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund to eligible gubernatorial tickets.

The Comptroller of Maryland administers the Fair Campaign Financing Fund and is responsible for making distributions to candidates upon authorization by the State Board of Elections, which may now begin earlier in the election cycle.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes competitive proof of concept procurements as an authorized source selection method for State procurement. Expands the scope of these procurements to include subsequent phases through full implementation or deployment. Requires State units to obtain approval from the Chief Procurement Officer before conducting such procurements. Requires approval from the Secretary of Information Technology if the procurement involves information technology. Authorizes units to issue contracts for product samples or demonstrations to offerors reasonably susceptible of selection. Requires the Department of General Services, in consultation with the Department of Information Technology, to adopt regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Department of Information Technology; Chief Procurement Officer
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement units and commercial vendors competing for State contracts for goods, services, and information technology
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances. The bill may create operational efficiencies for State agencies that choose to use competitive proof of concept procurements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS requested this departmental legislation. The bill establishes competitive proof of concept procurements as an authorized method of procurement, requires units to obtain approval from the Chief Procurement Officer (housed within DGS) before conducting such procurements, and mandates that DGS adopt implementing regulations, policies, and procedures.

The bill requires State units to obtain approval from the Secretary of Information Technology prior to conducting competitive proof of concept procurements for information technology, requires units to enter into memoranda of understanding with DoIT, and requires DGS to consult with DoIT when adopting regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office oversees the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) and Small Business Reserve programs. The bill amends provisions under Title 14 regarding how MBE and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise participation goals are established across phases of competitive proof of concept procurements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Council on Open Data to the Council for Open Data. Reduces the Council's membership from 37 to 11 members. Designates the State Chief Data Officer as the Council chair. Expands the Council's responsibilities to include advising on data initiatives and exploring community partnerships. Modifies the statutory definition of data by removing the restriction to final versions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Council for Open Data; Department of Information Technology; State Chief Data Officer
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland state agencies, local governments, academic institutions, private sector entities, nonprofit organizations, and users of Maryland open data
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary agency responsible for the bill, as it requested the departmental legislation. The bill establishes the State Chief Data Officer (within DoIT) as the Chair of the Council for Open Data and tasks DoIT with primary staffing responsibilities for the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council for Open Data is an executive council whose statutory name, membership composition (reducing from 37 to 11 members), member terms, and advisory responsibilities are directly modified by this bill.
The bill directly eliminates the Director of GOPI's statutory role as Vice Chair of the Council, removes GOPI from shared staffing responsibilities, and removes the agency from council membership.

The Governor appoints eight members to the restructured Council (local entity officials and private/academic/nonprofit representatives), holds removal authority, may designate additional staff, and receives the Council's annual report and legislative recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointments for the eight non-legislative positions on the reconstituted Council for Open Data.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain county- or municipality-funded fixed local bus routes to serve early voting centers located within one-half mile. Mandates that buses allow passengers to embark and disembark at center entrances on days early voting occurs. Directs compliance to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with accessibility requirements. Excludes express or commuter routes with limited stops, Maryland Transit Administration routes, and Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority routes. Directs the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations and guidelines for the conduct of early voting.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Voters utilizing early voting centers, county and municipal transit agencies, transit contractors, and public bus passengers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Local government expenditures increase indeterminately beginning in fiscal 2028 for jurisdictions modifying local bus routes, driven by additional operating mileage, driver hours, temporary bus stop signage, and accessibility compliance. Costs may be partially offset by bus fare revenue in jurisdictions with non-free service.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the State Board of Elections. The bill amends Maryland Election Law regarding early voting centers, requires SBE to adopt regulations and guidelines to implement the requirements, and mandates that SBE and local election boards inform the public about early voting centers.
The bill explicitly references the Maryland Transit Administration to exempt all bus routes operated by the administration from the requirement to stop at early voting centers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits personal information collected, processed, and retained by State government units to the minimum necessary for legitimate purposes. Requires personal records to be securely deleted or de-identified when no longer needed. Requires each State government unit to designate a Privacy Officer and post a website privacy notice. Directs the Department of Information Technology to establish privacy and data collection requirements for applicable procurement contracts. Expands the statutory definition of personal information to include email account credentials, health data, and sensitive demographic data.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; units of State government; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents; State government agencies and employees; third-party government contractors handling State data or information technology systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase for certain agencies needing additional personnel to fulfill compliance requirements, though most agencies are expected to implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and local government operations and finances experience no material impact. Specific cost estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency and departmental sponsor of the bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations, guidelines, model templates, and standard privacy and security contract requirements for all third-party state IT contracts.

State units maintaining personal records must submit annual reports to the Secretary of General Services, and DGS is explicitly tasked with adopting regulations to govern the form and method of this reporting.

The bill mandates that designated agency Privacy Officers across state government coordinate directly with the Office of the Attorney General to oversee compliance with data privacy and protection requirements.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is granted explicit statutory authority to adopt regulations exempting certain personal records based on recommendations from the Secretary of Information Technology, and DBM advises on statewide personnel and fiscal impacts.

The fiscal note specifically highlights that the Comptroller's Office anticipates an increased workload requiring additional staffing to implement the statutory data privacy and protection mandates, as it was previously exempt from the Governor's data privacy executive order.

MDOT is explicitly noted in the fiscal note as anticipating operational impacts and an increased workload that may exceed existing staff capacity to comply with the bill's data collection, retention, and privacy requirements.

The Department of Disabilities is specifically cited in the fiscal note as projecting an increased workload requiring additional staff resources to meet the new privacy officer, notice, and data handling requirements.
The legislation codifies and expands upon standards originally enacted by the Executive Department under Executive Order 01.01.2021.10 establishing the State Chief Privacy Officer.
The bill explicitly references public records accepted by the State Archivist for deposit in the Maryland Hall of Records as an exempt category from certain personal record requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person for the Address Confidentiality Program. Mandates that the contact person handle inquiries about the program from local election boards and program participants. Specifies that local boards of elections must use a participant's actual address for absentee ballots. Authorizes the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations to administer these requirements. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Address Confidentiality Program participants, survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, harassment, or human trafficking, and local election officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Elections can implement the requirements using existing resources with no effect on state revenues. Local election board operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person for the Address Confidentiality Program to handle inquiries from local boards and participants, and authorizes SBE to adopt regulations.
The Secretary of State administers the Address Confidentiality Program and requested this departmental legislation to facilitate coordination with election officials regarding program participants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes money in the Information Technology Investment Fund to support State-owned communication sites, communications facilities, and telecommunications equipment. Limits this permissive spending to facilities and equipment used in connection with State information technology agreements. Permits using these funds for program management at the discretion of the Secretary of Information Technology. Requires the Secretary to submit an annual allocation report to the General Assembly by January 15 each year. Terminates the expanded fund uses on June 30, 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Secretary of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies operating telecommunications infrastructure and private telecommunications companies entering into resource sharing agreements with the State
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on overall State revenues or expenditures, though the internal distribution of Information Technology Investment Fund monies may change from FY 2027 through FY 2031. The Department of Information Technology can complete required annual reports using existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a departmental bill requested by the Department of Information Technology (DoIT), this legislation directly affects DoIT's operations and statutory authorities. It grants the Secretary of Information Technology discretion to use Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF) revenues from resource sharing agreements (RSAs) to support State-owned communication sites, facilities, telecommunications equipment, and program management, while also requiring DoIT to submit an annual allocation report to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Administrative Office of the Courts to administer financial disclosure requirements for Judicial Branch officials and candidates. Authorizes the Supreme Court of Maryland to designate another entity to carry out these administrative duties. Directs the administering body to maintain financial disclosure statements and make them publicly available for examination and copying. Limits the Commission on Judicial Disabilities and Judicial Ethics Committee to administering conflict of interest provisions. Repeals the mandate that the Supreme Court of Maryland transmit judicial disclosure statements to the State Ethics Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: Administrative Office of the Courts; Supreme Court of Maryland; State Ethics Commission; Commission on Judicial Disabilities; Judicial Ethics Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: State officials of the Judicial Branch, candidates for judicial office, and members of the public seeking access to judicial financial disclosure statements
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Judiciary and the State Ethics Commission can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly designates the Administrative Office of the Courts (or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland) to administer and implement financial disclosure provisions under the Maryland Public Ethics Law for judicial branch officials and candidates, including maintaining records and making them available for public inspection.

The bill was requested by the State Ethics Commission and directly alters its duties by repealing the requirement that copies of judicial financial disclosure statements be transmitted to and maintained by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of several State boards and commissions to include military-connected individuals and families. Adds a family caregiver of a service-disabled veteran to the Maryland Commission on Caregiving. Designates the General Assembly members on the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees as ex officio trustees. Adds an organization representing military families to the Maryland Veterans Commission while repealing the veteran-status requirement for all members. Adds a youth with an immediate family member who is a service member to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families; Department of Human Services; Governor's Office for Children
qa_results.stakeholders: Military families, family caregivers of service-disabled veterans, military-connected youth, and veterans organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Altering the composition of the specified entities does not materially affect State government operations or finances. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Veterans and Military Families to update governance, membership, and removal procedures for the Maryland Veterans Commission, the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees, and the Veterans' Home Commission.

The bill alters the composition of the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which is housed and staffed within the Department of Human Services, by adding a family caregiver of a service-disabled veteran.
The bill specifically directs the Governor's Office for Children to appoint an additional member to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council who has an immediate family member who is a service member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition, membership criteria, and operating structures of several state advisory boards and commissions, including the Maryland Veterans Commission, the Commission on Caregiving, the Maryland Youth Advisory Council, and the Maryland Veterans Trust Board.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, and will oversee candidate selection under the updated criteria for the Maryland Veterans Commission and the Commission on Caregiving.

The bill alters gubernatorial appointment requirements and eligibility criteria for seats on the Maryland Veterans Commission, the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees, and the Maryland Commission on Caregiving.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the lavatory requirement for agritourism businesses, Class 4 limited wineries, and Class 8 farm breweries to allow any portable toilet. Establishes a one-year on-farm food service facility license and repeals the previous 30-day operating limit. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to set the license fee based on regulatory costs, not to exceed $100. Requires the Department to adopt regulations in consultation with specified state departments and key stakeholders. Prohibits construing the licensing provisions to limit local building codes, zoning, land use designations, or health regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of the Environment; Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: agritourism businesses, Class 4 limited wineries, Class 8 farm breweries, on-farm food service facility operators, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate minimal increase in Maryland Department of Health general fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 from license fees capped at $100. Local health departments can absorb inspection and enforcement duties using existing budgeted resources, though regulatory costs may exceed license fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency responsible for setting the on-farm food service facility license fee, determining allowable foods, issuing licenses, and adopting regulations governing sanitation, toileting, food preparation, and public health requirements.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to consult with the Department of Agriculture when adopting regulations governing on-farm food service facilities, particularly regarding agricultural operations and structures.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health consult with the Department of the Environment to develop regulations concerning water access, wastewater management, and toileting facilities for on-farm food service facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters coverage effective dates for individuals enrolling in Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Exchange plans during specified special enrollment periods. Sets coverage to begin the first day of the month following receipt of plan selection for court-ordered dependents, if allowed and selected. Repeals provisions delaying effective dates to the second month for selections submitted after the fifteenth day. Establishes coverage effective dates on the first day of the month following plan selection for special enrollment periods involving death, divorce, or legal separation. Aligns Maryland health insurance statutory provisions with existing federal regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Small employers, eligible employees, and dependents enrolled in Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Exchange plans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies existing exchange operations that align with federal regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 273 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) to update and align the Maryland Insurance Article with federal regulations regarding SHOP special enrollment period effective dates.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange operates the Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Exchange in Maryland, directly administering the special enrollment periods and coverage effective dates modified by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory termination date for the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists by five years. Continues the board and its adopted regulations through July 1, 2032. Subjects the continuation to the evaluation and reestablishment provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the board's authority to license and discipline environmental health specialists. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed environmental health specialists and applicants for licensure in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists through fiscal 2032. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This departmental bill extends the Board's statutory authority and termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act through July 1, 2032, allowing the department to continue regulating and licensing environmental health specialists.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the termination date and statutory operating authority of the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists by five years to July 1, 2032.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires carriers issuing Medicare supplement policies in the State to offer coverage under two new special enrollment periods. Mandates policy issuance to individuals losing Maryland Medical Assistance Program coverage who apply within 63 days. Applies to individuals enrolled in Medicare Part B for at least six months before Medicaid termination. Requires carriers to issue open policies to individuals eligible for Medicare before January 1, 2020. Eligible applicants must qualify under a federal special enrollment period and apply within 63 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Carriers issuing Medicare supplement policies in Maryland, individuals transitioning off the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, and Medicare beneficiaries eligible before January 1, 2020 who qualify for a federal special enrollment period
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational impact is minimal and absorbable within existing Maryland Insurance Administration budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulator of private health insurance carriers and Medicare supplement policies in Maryland and requested this departmental legislation. The agency will enforce carrier compliance with the new guaranteed issue special enrollment periods.

MDH administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill creates a special enrollment period for individuals disenrolling or terminating from Medicaid, requiring applicants to submit evidence of termination from the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program administered by the State Emergency Medical Services Board. Exempts law enforcement agencies from obtaining a certificate for an automated external defibrillator deployed in a patrol vehicle. Defines and establishes duties for automated external defibrillator coordinators designated by registered entities. Establishes specific certification qualifications for grocery stores and restaurants participating in the program. Repeals statutory provisions regarding regional councils and regional council automated external defibrillator committees.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Emergency Medical Services Board; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Entities registered in the Public Access AED Program, owners and operators of grocery stores and restaurants, and law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the statutory changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS requested this departmental legislation and, alongside the State Emergency Medical Services Board, directly administers and oversees the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program governed by the bill.

The bill amends Section 21-330.3 of the Health - General Article regarding AED requirements for grocery stores and restaurants, which fall under the public health regulatory purview of the Department of Health.

The bill explicitly exempts law enforcement agencies from the requirement to obtain a certificate for an AED deployed in a patrol vehicle, directly affecting state and local police vehicle equipment protocols.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands enforcement authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner over third party administrators. Authorizes the Commissioner to deny, suspend, revoke, or refuse registration for violations of state insurance laws. Authorizes registration actions when an applicant or registrant knowingly violates a Commissioner regulation or order. Authorizes civil penalties of up to $10,000 for each violation of the Insurance Article. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Third party administrators (TPAs), applicants for TPA registration, and plan sponsors, participants, and beneficiaries covered under plans administered by TPAs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State revenues or expenditures; the Maryland Insurance Administration can handle the enforcement requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration. It directly expands the enforcement and regulatory authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the administration over third-party administrators (TPAs), authorizing civil penalties and registration denials, revocations, or suspensions for violations of the Insurance Article or state insurance laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of Aging to lead implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan. Directs the Secretary to submit an updated comprehensive plan every four years beginning July 1, 2029. Mandates an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on plan progress and activity center funding. Alters the membership, appointment process, and advisory duties of the Commission on Aging. Requires the Department of Aging to provide staff for the Commission.
