qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Commission on Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: older adults, family caregivers, area agencies on aging, and organizations advocating for older adults
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill generally codifies existing policies and procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Aging by requiring the Secretary of Aging to lead the implementation and reporting of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, updating the Secretary's powers and duties, and requiring the department to staff and support the restructured Commission on Aging.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the membership composition, meeting rules, attendance requirements, and advisory duties of the Commission on Aging in relation to the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan.

The bill modifies the gubernatorial appointment requirements for the Commission on Aging, establishing specific categories and qualifications for members that the Office of Appointments must vet and process.

The bill requires annual reporting and four-year comprehensive updates on the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan to be submitted to the Governor, and establishes appointments to the Commission on Aging to be made by the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Codifies federal mental health parity standards into State health insurance law. Requires health insurance carriers to collect and evaluate data assessing how nonquantitative treatment limitations impact benefit access. Establishes that material differences in access serve as a strong indicator of noncompliance with parity requirements. Requires carriers to provide meaningful benefits and coverage for core treatments across all applicable benefit classifications. Requires carriers to submit comparative analyses and documentation of remedial actions upon request by the Commissioner. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to review compliance reports and issue administrative orders against noncompliant carriers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers operating in Maryland and individuals receiving or seeking coverage for mental health and substance use disorders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill and promulgate regulations using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) and directly strengthens MIA's authority to enforce mental health and substance use disorder parity requirements, review carrier comparative analyses and data reports, adopt regulations, and issue administrative orders or penalties.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note specifically evaluated the bill's requirements against state employee health plans and concluded there is no fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters provisions governing criminal background investigations for individuals who care for or supervise children. Requires the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository to send State records to applicants and national records to authorized agencies. Mandates criminal history records checks for non-relative adults agreeing to provide care due to the sudden unavailability of a primary caretaker. Authorizes local departments to request national name-based checks by State or local law enforcement agencies for emergency out-of-home placements. Requires local departments to submit fingerprints within 15 calendar days after law enforcement conducts the name-based check.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Child care facilities, child care employees and volunteers, non-relative emergency caregivers, and children in out-of-home placements
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures likely increase minimally beginning as early as fiscal 2026 for background check fees and potential temporary foster care placements. Local expenditures may experience a minimal increase to process background checks. Revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS requested this departmental legislation. Its Criminal Justice Information System - Central Repository (CJIS-CR) is directly responsible for collecting fingerprints, processing fees, and conducting and disseminating State and national criminal history records checks (CHRC) in compliance with updated FBI standards.

DHS oversees child welfare, foster care, and local departments of social services. The bill alters requirements for background checks and emergency out-of-home placements (including safety plans involving non-relative caregivers), which carries direct operational and fiscal impacts for DHS when covering CHRC costs or placing children in foster care.

MSDE regulates and licenses child care centers, family child care homes, and informal child care subsidy providers, and receives criminal history record information from CJIS-CR for covered child care personnel and adult residents.

MDH licenses home health agencies and residential service agencies authorized to provide home- or community-based health services for minors, which are among the facilities required to obtain criminal history records checks under the bill.
DJS operates juvenile detention, correction, and treatment facilities, whose employees and employers are among the covered entities mandated to obtain criminal history records checks.
As the primary State law enforcement agency, MSP is authorized to conduct preliminary national name-based checks for emergency out-of-home child placements at the request of local departments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters provisions governing the reporting and investigation of vulnerable adult abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and exploitation. Expands the definition of abuse to include psychological harm and sexual abuse by an individual in a relationship of trust. Authorizes mandated reporters to submit reports of suspected maltreatment through an online reporting portal. Requires local departments of social services to determine whether an alleged vulnerable adult is at risk of harm. Mandates that local departments complete investigations within 60 days and make an indicated, not indicated, or undetermined finding. Repeals the 10-day investigation completion deadline for cases involving an emergency.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services; local departments of social services
qa_results.stakeholders: Vulnerable adults, individuals in relationships of trust with vulnerable adults, and mandated reporters including health practitioners, police officers, and human service workers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or expenditures, and it may help protect federal funding by ensuring compliance with federal Adult Protective Services standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 282 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services (DHS) to align Maryland's Adult Protective Services (APS) statutory definitions, reporting, and investigation standards with a federal 2024 rule, directly impacting DHS and local departments of social services.

The bill impacts the protection of vulnerable older adults, explicitly addresses long-term care ombudsman reporting requirements, and maintains statutory provisions allowing the Department of Aging to assist local departments in adult protective investigations.

State police officers are designated mandatory reporters of vulnerable adult abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and exploitation, and law enforcement agencies are statutorily called upon to assist local departments with adult protective investigations.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for operational impacts regarding vulnerable adult protective proceedings, guardianship reviews, and related judicial matters governed under the Family Law Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a licensed firearms dealer to notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours of discovering specified compromising events. Applies when a burglary, attempted burglary, robbery, or theft involving a firearm or ammunition occurs at dealer premises. Applies when required security features fail, including video equipment, entry barriers, alarm monitoring, or physical breach barriers. Clarifies that this notification is in addition to any report made to local law enforcement or federal authorities. Establishes a civil penalty not exceeding $250 for a first violation and $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed firearms dealers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Civil penalty alterations are not anticipated to materially affect State revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 284 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Police. It requires licensed firearms dealers to notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours of specific criminal events or security feature compromises, and authorizes the Secretary to impose updated civil penalties and enforce licensing compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an individual to participate in the Ignition Interlock System Program to modify a license suspension or revocation. Applies this requirement to any driver who violates an alcohol restriction imposed under the Transportation Article. Mandates participation for individuals under age 21 who violate drug and alcohol impairment driving prohibitions. Directs the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a restricted license to an otherwise eligible required participant. Requires the Administration to impose a one-year license suspension if a required participant fails to complete the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: drivers subject to license suspensions or revocations for alcohol restriction violations, including drivers age 21 and older
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations; hearing requests before the Office of Administrative Hearings are anticipated to decrease. No effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) establishes and administers the Ignition Interlock System Program (IISP) and driver's license suspensions, revocations, restrictions, and modifications. Under the bill, MVA directly implements the requirement that any individual who violates an alcohol restriction participate in the IISP as a condition of license modification or restricted license issuance.

The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and sponsored this departmental legislation to streamline participation in the Ignition Interlock System Program.

The bill allows individuals age 21 and older who violate alcohol restrictions to enroll directly in the Ignition Interlock System Program without appearing before an Administrative Law Judge, which is expected to decrease hearing requests before the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Superintendent of Schools to declare a prolonged state of emergency preventing in-person school attendance. Applies to emergencies lasting at least 14 consecutive school days due to disasters, health emergencies, or security threats. Requires the State Superintendent to consult the Governor and specified state agencies before issuing the written declaration. Authorizes a county board of education to transition affected public schools to virtual education under an approved plan. Allows the General Assembly, the State Board of Education, or the State Superintendent to terminate the emergency declaration.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Superintendent of Schools; State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, teachers, county boards of education, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The State Superintendent of Schools and local school systems can implement the bill's provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill directly concerns the State Superintendent of Schools and the State Board of Education, authorizing the State Superintendent to declare a prolonged state of emergency for public schools and oversee virtual education transitions.

The bill shifts the declaration authority for school-specific prolonged states of emergency from the Governor to the State Superintendent of Schools, while mandating that the State Superintendent consult with the Governor before making a declaration.

The bill identifies MDH as an agency the State Superintendent must consult if appropriate when declaring an emergency, and explicitly clarifies that the bill does not limit or interfere with the powers of the Secretary of Health during public health emergencies.

The bill explicitly lists the Maryland Department of Emergency Management as an entity the State Superintendent must consult, if appropriate, prior to issuing a declaration of a prolonged state of emergency.
The bill explicitly identifies the Department of State Police as an agency to be consulted by the State Superintendent if appropriate, particularly when emergencies involve specific security threats.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Central Collection Unit to certify debts owed to the State to video lottery operators for prize interception. Requires video lottery operators to withhold prize payouts requiring federal form W-2G from certified debtors. Authorizes the Child Support Administration and Central Collection Unit to certify child support and restitution obligors directly to operators. Establishes an order of priority for honoring child support, restitution, and State debt interception requests. Allows debtors 15 days after notice to appeal a proposed prize transfer under the Administrative Procedure Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Central Collection Unit; Child Support Administration; State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: video lottery facility operators; individuals winning casino prizes who owe child support, court-ordered restitution, or State debts; recipients of child support and restitution payments; State agencies and community colleges collecting delinquent debts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues increase annually across all funds by at least $3.0 million beginning in FY 2027 from intercepted casino prizes. Central Collection Fund special fund revenues increase by at least $510,000 annually from collection fees. Local community college revenues may increase from collections on delinquent debts referred to the Central Collection Unit. State expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the authority of the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is housed within DBM, authorizing it to certify debts and claims owed to the State to video lottery operators for prize interception. Furthermore, the Secretary of DBM may jointly adopt implementing regulations with the Director of the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, and CCU's dedicated special fund will receive increased fee revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SLGCA regulates video lottery operators and facilities across Maryland, requested this departmental bill, must establish and honor prize interception priority orders, and its Director is authorized to jointly adopt regulations with DBM.
The Child Support Administration (CSA) within DHS is authorized by the bill to certify child support obligors directly to video lottery operators for prize intercept enforcement.

OAH is responsible for adjudicating appeals from individuals disputing intercepted lottery facility winnings under the Administrative Procedure Act and will train administrative law judges on the provisions of the bill.

DJS refers overdue juvenile restitution accounts to the Central Collection Unit for collection, which can now be satisfied through video lottery prize interceptions under the specified statutory priorities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of Parole and Probation within DPSCS refers overdue criminal restitution accounts to the Central Collection Unit for interception and collection under the bill's framework.
AOC was consulted regarding court-ordered restitution and judicial enforcement of debt/restitution collections, though the bill is anticipated to have minimal operational impact on court operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to share data with third-party data centers. Limits data sharing to one third-party data center at a time for multistate research on student outcomes. Requires the data center to be FedRAMP-certified and maintain security standards at least as rigorous as the Center. Requires the Center to execute written data sharing agreements and submit reports to specified legislative committees. Repeals the Governing Board's authority to send student information to the United States Census Bureau.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland students and workforce participants whose records are maintained in the Maryland Longitudinal Data System; third-party data centers and researchers conducting multistate student outcome research
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources by the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 293 is a departmental bill directly governing the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center. It authorizes the MLDS Center and its Governing Board to share individual-level student and workforce data with a qualified third-party data center for multistate research and reporting, establishes data privacy and security criteria, requires written data-sharing agreements, mandates annual reviews and legislative reporting, and repeals previous authorization to share data with the U.S. Census Bureau.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the MDiplomaWorks pathway as an alternative method to earn a Maryland high school diploma. Bases diploma achievement on demonstrated academic and career competencies, including workforce experience. Restricts eligibility to Maryland residents without diplomas who have withdrawn from regular schooling and compulsory attendance. Requires participants to complete approved combinations of credentials, assessments, career coursework, and on-the-job training. Directs the Maryland Department of Labor to publicize the pathway in calendar years 2027 and 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents without a high school diploma who have withdrawn from regular schooling and are exempt from compulsory attendance
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the pathway, publicize it, and adopt regulations using existing resources. State education aid and revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which was submitted as a departmental bill. It oversees the establishment and approval of the MDiplomaWorks pathway, adopts implementing regulations jointly with the State Board of Education, and is required to publicize information about the pathway.

The State Board of Education, supported by the Maryland State Department of Education, is required to jointly adopt regulations with the Secretary of Labor to govern the awarding of high school diplomas through the MDiplomaWorks pathway.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade from statutory prohibitions on contract terms. Applies the exemption to contracts relating to the development of international business activities and opportunities. Relieves qualifying international trade agreements from prohibitions against indemnification clauses, binding arbitration, and out-of-state venues. Allows these contracts to include liability limits, automatic renewal terms, and non-State legal counsel provisions. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Office of International Trade
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of International Trade; international contractors, vendors, and business entities contracting with the State
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill codifies existing contracting practices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill specifically exempts contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade within the Department of Commerce from certain prohibited state contract provisions, allowing the department to continue executing international business agreements and event contracts without violating state procurement statutes.

As the State of Maryland's central procurement authority overseeing state contracting rules and procedures under the State Finance and Procurement Article, DGS has an operational interest in statutory exemptions to standard contract requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Places members of the Maryland Military Department on State active duty under the operational command of the Adjutant General. Authorizes the Adjutant General to designate a National Guard officer to exercise operational command and control. Applies this command structure whether the commander is in State active duty or certain federal status. Expands coverage to all department units, including the National Guard, the Maryland Defense Force, and State operations. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Military Department; Adjutant General
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Military Department, including the Maryland National Guard, the Maryland Defense Force, and State operations personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill codifies existing operational practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 301 is a departmental bill requested by the Military Department that explicitly establishes that members of the Department on State active duty are under the operational command and control of the Adjutant General or an officer designated by the Adjutant General.
The bill directly governs the command structure and operational control of Maryland National Guard members and designated officers during mobilizations and State active duty.

The Governor serves as Commander-in-Chief of the State militia with statutory authority to order personnel into State active duty, and the command authority in the bill applies in situations where the Governor is Commander-in-Chief.
The statute amended includes provisions regarding coordination with and emergency command authority over the Department of State Police when the militia is called into State active duty.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a vehicle manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch from taking adverse action against a dealer for specific website price disclosures. Protects dealers who disclose that an advertised vehicle price is the manufacturer's minimum allowable advertised price. Protects dealers who disclose on their website that they may offer a lower price for the vehicle. Applies these protections unless the dealer violates false advertising laws or public protection laws.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration licenses and regulates motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and vehicle dealers under Title 15 of the Transportation Article, which governs the dealer-manufacturer relations and vehicle advertising standards amended by this bill.
The Department of Transportation oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and administers the Maryland Transportation Article amended by the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes business entities in Maryland to designate an address supplied by a commercial mail receiving agency as their principal office. Applies to Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, and limited partnerships. Requires the entity to maintain a valid commercial mail receiving agreement under U.S. Postal Service regulations. Defines a commercial mail receiving agency as a person authorized by the postal service to accept mail deliveries. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, limited partnerships, and commercial mail receiving agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase minimally in fiscal 2027 from filing fees when existing entities change their principal office address. There is no material impact on State Department of Assessments and Taxation operations or finances, and local government finances are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each local school system to identify and develop solutions for accessibility issues for individuals with disabilities during regular safety evaluations. Mandates reporting of instances where a public school facility became inaccessible for a student with a disability in a manner that could impede emergencies. Directs local school systems to submit these reports annually to the Maryland Center for School Safety. Establishes that the submitted safety reports are confidential and exempt from inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act. Authorizes disclosure of the reports to members of the General Assembly upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety; local school systems
qa_results.stakeholders: students and individuals with disabilities in public schools, public school personnel, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Center for School Safety can implement the bill using existing resources. Local school system finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) is the primary state entity tasked with receiving, reviewing, and consulting on the local school systems' safety evaluations, updated emergency plans, and annual incident reports detailing school accessibility issues during emergencies.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public school systems statewide, houses the Maryland Center for School Safety, and maintains the Emergency Planning Guidelines for Local School Systems regarding accommodations for individuals with disabilities.

The bill's statutory framework requires local school safety coordinators to coordinate safety evaluations and public school facility assessments with the Interagency Commission on School Construction's facility assessment process.

As the state agency responsible for coordinating policies and improving services and accessibility for Maryland residents with disabilities, the bill's focus on school facility accessibility and emergency evacuation accommodations directly aligns with the department's mission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits residential landlords from denying housing to prospective tenants using income-based housing subsidies based on income or credit. Designates violations as discriminatory housing practices enforceable by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights. Authorizes landlords to verify a tenant has sufficient income to pay the tenant's portion of rent. Requires landlords owning six or more residential units to offer tenants optional positive rental payment history reporting. Authorizes landlords to charge electing tenants a fee capped at actual costs or $10 monthly. Requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations implementing the reporting requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: residential landlords, prospective and current residential tenants, recipients of income-based housing vouchers and subsidies, and consumer reporting agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Housing and Community Development can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly expands the definition of discriminatory housing practices to include certain refusals to rent to prospective tenants who pay rent using income-based housing subsidies, making these violations subject to investigation and enforcement by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Housing and Community Development adopt regulations specifying the form and requirements for the mandatory offer of positive rental payment history reporting provided to tenants.

The Judiciary may adjudicate civil actions authorized under the state's fair housing laws for alleged discriminatory housing practices, though any impact on court workloads is projected to be negligible.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts contested case hearings for administrative complaints referred by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights regarding discriminatory housing practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the termination date of provisions authorizing county boards of education to transport certain students using alternative vehicles. Authorizes county boards of education to permanently use vehicles other than Type I and Type II school vehicles when appropriate. Requires the State Department of Education to review regulations governing alternative student transportation vehicles and drivers. Mandates consultation with county boards of education and the Motor Vehicle Administration during the regulatory review. Requires the Department to report its findings to specified legislative committees on or before January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Motor Vehicle Administration; County Boards of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: public school students receiving transportation, county boards of education, and commercial student transportation contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State implementation costs can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Local school system transportation expenditures may decrease or avoid future increases beyond fiscal 2026 by continuing the use of alternative vehicles.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for reviewing regulations regarding alternative school vehicles and drivers, consulting with stakeholders, and reporting findings to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027.

MVA is explicitly required by the bill to be consulted by the Maryland State Department of Education in reviewing the regulations for alternative student transportation vehicles and driver requirements.
The bill specifically directs MSDE to examine the Public Service Commission's regulations for transportation network operators to assess if school transportation regulations can be aligned with them.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is statutorily required to participate in the regulatory review of alternative school transportation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to grant, by law, a county property tax credit. Applies the credit to real property located in a designated Rural Legacy Area. Requires that the property owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: governing body of Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: owners of real property located in a Rural Legacy Area in Anne Arundel County who have sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Anne Arundel County property tax revenues decrease by approximately $27,800 annually beginning in FY 2027 to the extent the credit is granted, with no effect on county expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a local property tax credit for landowners who have sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program, which is a state conservation program established under Title 5, Subtitle 9A of the Natural Resources Article and administered by the Department of Natural Resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the deadline for the Department of the Environment to submit a synthetic turf study report to January 15, 2027. Moves the previous reporting deadline from July 1, 2026. Directs the department to submit findings to the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment and the House Environment and Transportation Committee. Requires the study to examine synthetic turf, existing synthetic turf fields, and the synthetic turf industry in the State. Mandates consultation with industry representatives, environmental and community stakeholders, and synthetic turf users. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Synthetic turf industry representatives, the Synthetic Turf Council, synthetic turf producers, retailers, and users including local governments, county school systems, higher education facilities, and professional sports organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the reporting deadline does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the statutory deadline from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027, for the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to complete its study and submit a comprehensive report on the synthetic turf industry and disposal to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership composition of the Maryland Health Care Commission. Reduces the number of members unconnected to health care provider or payor management from nine to eight. Adds one hospital administrator to the Commission. Decreases the required number of members residing in counties with 300,000 or more residents from five to four. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospital administrators, Maryland Health Care Commission members, health care providers, and health care payors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as altering Commission membership does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership composition of the Maryland Health Care Commission by adding a hospital administrator and modifying the ratio of consumer/unaffiliated members and geographic representation requirements.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent regulatory agency operating within the Maryland Department of Health, which provided information on the bill.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Maryland Health Care Commission and must adhere to the bill's updated composition and geographic distribution criteria.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointees for state commissions, including identifying qualified hospital administrators and candidates meeting geographic requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board. Removes the board seat for a certified nonpublic school classroom teacher nominated by the Association of Independent Schools. Increases the representation of the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities from one member to two. Requires the Governor to appoint one licensed special education teacher currently providing classroom instruction from association nominees. Requires the Governor to appoint one administrator or supervisory staff member from association nominees. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Association of Independent Schools; Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities; nonpublic school teachers and administrators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the State Board of Education provide administrative and staffing support for the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, and the State Superintendent serves as an ex officio member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory membership composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, a state regulatory board governing teacher education and certification standards.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing nominations and appointments to state boards, including the revised seats on the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board.

The Governor is statutory authority responsible for appointing the members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, subject to Senate advice and consent, following the altered composition criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system. Directs the system to coordinate receipt of school safety concerns while maintaining reporter anonymity. Requires the Center to develop operational guidelines and provide navigation training for school personnel. Requires each local school system to participate in the reporting system beginning July 1, 2027. Authorizes a local school system to opt out by December 1, 2026, if it operates a substantially similar system. Requires public records custodians to deny inspection of materials related to the reporting system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, public school personnel, local school systems, parents, and emergency response personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill codifies existing practice, and local school systems already comply with the requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 326 directly mandates the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop, administer, and establish operational guidelines and training for a statewide anonymous school safety reporting system.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, and the bill impacts safety reporting and compliance across Maryland's public school systems overseen by the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the membership of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County from 15 to 11 members. Increases the number of at-large members from one to two. Allocates one member to each of nine Baltimore County councilmanic districts instead of two from seven districts. Terminates the terms of specified current trustees on June 30, 2026. Reassigns continuing trustees to newly structured districts and establishes staggered terms for new appointments beginning July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Senate; Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, the Community College of Baltimore County, and Baltimore County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Minimal decrease in local reimbursement expenditures for trustee members begins in fiscal 2027 due to the smaller board size. Baltimore County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, which consists of members appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and managing appointments to state boards and commissions, and will need to implement the transition, seat redistricting, and new appointment schedule for the Baltimore County Community College Trustees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers certain bicounty commission financial disclosure responsibilities to the Prince George’s County Office of Ethics and Accountability. Requires applicants seeking appointment from Prince George’s County to submit paper financial disclosure statements to the Office. Directs the county chief administrative officer to transmit statements of commissioners and appointed applicants to the Office. Requires the Office to retain statements, return unappointed applicants' statements, and notify the State Ethics Commission. Mandates that the Office maintain disclosure statements for public inspection and record examining individuals' identifying information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George’s County Office of Ethics and Accountability; State Ethics Commission; Prince George’s County Chief Administrative Officer
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for appointment and appointed commissioners of bicounty commissions from Prince George’s County, and members of the public examining financial disclosure statements.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions of the Maryland Public Ethics Law governing financial disclosure statements for bicounty commissions filed electronically with the State Ethics Commission, including requirements for the Commission to delete electronic filings when notified that an applicant was not appointed.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a law enforcement officer from engaging in sexual contact, vaginal intercourse, or a sexual act with a student. Applies this restriction to students enrolled in a school where the officer serves as a school resource officer. Classifies a violation as a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment up to three years, a fine up to $3,000, or both. Authorizes courts to impose sentences consecutive to or concurrent with sentences for other specified sexual crimes. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State's Attorneys; State and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement officers assigned as school resource officers, Baltimore City school police officers, and students enrolled in schools with assigned resource officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS), an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, coordinates statewide school safety and oversees standards, training, and policy regarding School Resource Officers (SROs) pursuant to Title 7, Subtitle 15 of the Education Article, which is directly referenced in the bill.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and local school policies where School Resource Officers are deployed, and was consulted for the fiscal and policy note.

The Maryland State Police is the primary statewide law enforcement agency and employs law enforcement officers who may serve in roles subject to statutory standards of conduct and criminal prohibitions governing law enforcement officers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a misdemeanor offense punishable by up to three years of imprisonment and/or fines, impacting correctional operations and supervision overseen by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense with potential terms of incarceration, requiring OPD representation for indigent defendants charged under the statute.
The Maryland Judiciary is responsible for the trial and adjudication of individuals charged with misdemeanor offenses under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the voting membership of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12. Requires the Governor to appoint the additional members with the advice and consent of the Senate. Expands the required number of lawyer board members from five to seven. Increases the required number of nonlawyer board members from four to five. Raises the vote threshold required to remove a voting member from seven to nine members.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Appointees and members of the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation from 9 to 12 voting members, all of whom are appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. The Governor also fills any vacancies on the Board.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages the recruitment and appointment process for gubernatorial appointments to state boards, commissions, and councils, which will include identifying candidates for the three additional board positions created by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the jurisdiction of the Maryland Capitol Police and the Department of General Services statewide. Increases the surrounding enforcement area around State-owned or State-leased buildings from 1,000 feet to 2,000 feet. Authorizes Maryland Capitol Police officers to investigate and enforce statewide criminal, asset forfeiture, and motor vehicle laws. Requires advance notification to the Secretary of State Police before conducting an investigation or enforcement action, absent an emergency. Requires the Maryland Capitol Police to enter a memorandum of understanding with the Baltimore Police Department before operating in Baltimore City.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Capitol Police; Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Capitol Police officers, state and local law enforcement agencies, and individuals subject to law enforcement actions on or near State property or statewide
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Altering and expanding the jurisdiction of the Department of General Services and the Maryland Capitol Police is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of General Services (DGS) by expanding the statutory jurisdiction and police powers of the Maryland Capitol Police (MCP), a division within DGS, granting them statewide jurisdiction.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Capitol Police to provide notification to the Secretary of State Police in advance of exercising statewide investigative and enforcement powers (absent emergency/exigency) and post-action notification to local barrack commanders.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Capitol Police notify the Superintendent of the Natural Resources Police (or designee) after exercising statewide enforcement and investigative powers.
The bill requires post-enforcement notification to the Chief of Police of the Maryland Department of Health Secured Transport and Investigation Unit when Capitol Police exercise statewide authority.

The bill specifically identifies the Chief of Police of the Maryland Transit Administration Police Force as a recipient of notifications following investigations and enforcement actions conducted by the Capitol Police.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration (whose police force must be notified under the bill) and the manager of extensive state transportation facilities, MDOT is affected by expanded interagency police coordination.
The bill references the Board of Public Works' authority to designate other public improvements or grounds over which DGS and Capitol Police maintain jurisdiction and police authority.

The bill repeals an outdated, specific statutory reference to properties administered by the Maryland Department of Labor on June 30, 2019, replacing it with generalized statewide coverage for state-owned and leased facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enters Maryland into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact to facilitate interstate practice for qualified school psychologists. Requires member states to grant equivalent licenses to eligible individuals holding an active home state license. Establishes qualifications for licensure, including completing graduate education, supervised internship hours, and a qualifying national examination. Creates the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission to administer the compact and promulgate binding rules. Mandates that applicants seeking an equivalent license undergo a criminal background check.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed school psychologists, local school systems, public and nonpublic school students, and military families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $37,000 in FY 2027, reflecting $30,000 in one-time licensure system IT modifications and a $7,000 annual compact participation fee recurring thereafter. Potential minimal increase in State license fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the state licensing authority responsible for credentialing school psychologists. MSDE will implement the compact, serve as Maryland's representative commissioner on the interstate commission, adapt its educator licensing systems, and pay annual compact participation fees.

The bill formally enters Maryland into a new multistate compact and establishes membership in the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission to facilitate interstate practice and regulation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Applicants seeking licensure under the compact must undergo state and national criminal history records checks, which are processed through the department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR).

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters educational qualifications for individuals applying for a forestry license from the State Board of Foresters. Requires applicants to graduate from a four-year forestry curriculum approved by the Board. Requires the institution to be accredited by the Society of American Foresters or an equivalent accrediting entity. Authorizes an applicant to qualify if the Board determines the applicant's education is substantially equivalent. Specifies that qualifying education may include a comparable graduate degree or international degree. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Foresters
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for a forestry license in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Foresters can implement the changes with existing resources. There is no material effect on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the occupational and professional licensing boards, including the State Board of Foresters, which is directly responsible for administering and implementing the altered educational and licensing requirements established by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires recipients of certain Department of Housing and Community Development funds to provide information on federal housing counseling services. Applies this condition to projects funded by the Strategic Demolition Fund or the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative. Mandates providing the information to prospective residents before executing a contract to purchase single-family residential property. Requires certified counselors employed by an approved housing counseling agency to provide the counseling services. Requires the Governor to appropriate $90,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2028 for community development organization partnerships.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Recipients of Strategic Demolition Fund or Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative funding, prospective single-family homebuyers, community development organizations, and HUD-approved housing counseling agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2028 due to a mandated appropriation for community development organizations. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency. The bill conditions funding from DHCD's Strategic Demolition Fund and the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative on providing housing counseling information, and DHCD will administer and disburse the annual $90,000 appropriation to community development organizations.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning, which includes implementing the bill's statutory mandated appropriation of $90,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2028.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to appropriate $90,000 in the annual state budget beginning in fiscal year 2028 for community development organizations to partner with approved housing counseling agencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a workers' compensation occupational disease and disablement presumption for specified paid public safety employees diagnosed with hypertension. Applies to paid firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, and State Fire Marshal members. Requires an authorized provider diagnosis, 90 consecutive days of prescribed medication, and two years of cumulative Maryland service. Disqualifies individuals from receiving disability retirement benefits for the same condition, unless authorized under a collective bargaining agreement. Prohibits claimants from receiving duplicative benefits for the same condition under multiple statutory provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Paid firefighters, paid firefighting instructors, paid rescue squad members, paid advanced life support unit members, and sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal employed by airport authorities, counties, fire control districts, municipalities, or the State; local governments and workers' compensation insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State, Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, and local government expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 due to expanded occupational disease presumptions and additional workers' compensation benefit payments. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the primary regulatory and adjudicative body administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law. The bill directly impacts the Commission by establishing a new compensability presumption for hypertension and requiring the Commission to adopt regulations defining an 'authorized provider.'

As the third-party administrator handling workers' compensation claims on behalf of the State of Maryland, the Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (operating through Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) would directly handle any additional workers' compensation claims and benefit payments resulting from the expanded hypertension presumption.

The bill explicitly covers sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, which operates within the Department of State Police, making its employees eligible for the occupational disease presumption.

The bill specifies that individuals who qualify for compensation under the new presumption generally may not receive disability retirement benefits for the same condition, which directly affects the administration and coordination of disability retirement benefits managed by the Agency.

The bill covers firefighters and emergency personnel employed by airport authorities or the State, which includes personnel at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport operated under MDOT.
The MAA employs airport firefighters and rescue personnel who would be covered under the bill's expanded occupational disease presumption for airport authority or State employees.

The Subsequent Injury Fund investigates and pays liabilities for workers' compensation claims involving preexisting health conditions combined with workplace conditions; expanded occupational disease claims can impact potential fund assessments and liabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the expiration date of a racetrack alcoholic beverages license in Baltimore City until July 1, 2029. Applies to a license issued for premises in the 5200 block of Park Heights Avenue. Specifies that the license remains unexpired to complete a transfer of ownership and renewal at that location. Specifies that the license also remains unexpired to complete renovations at the same location. Takes effect July 1, 2026, and terminates at the end of July 31, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of a racetrack alcoholic beverages license located in the 5200 block of Park Heights Avenue in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. Baltimore City expenditures and revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for regulating the state's alcoholic beverage industry and collecting related excise and sales taxes. Although the racetrack alcoholic beverages license in question is administered locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, the bill touches on state alcohol statutes and industry operations under the Comptroller's general regulatory purview.

The authority oversees community revitalization and projects surrounding the Pimlico Race Course in the Park Heights corridor. The bill directly accommodates the ongoing major redevelopment and renovation closure of Pimlico Race Course by preserving its alcoholic beverages license through 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an aggrieved party or the Office of the Attorney General to sue certain judicial officers for constitutional deprivations. Authorizes plaintiffs in an action to seek damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief. Permits courts to award reasonable fees and costs, including attorney's fees and expert witness fees, to prevailing plaintiffs. Requires filing an action within five years after the cause of action accrues. Authorizes prosecutors to direct law enforcement agencies to gather and retain identifying digital data upon receiving misconduct complaints. Restricts a plaintiff to obtaining that identifying digital data only under a court order.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; State Prosecutor; State's Attorney
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals deprived of constitutional or legal rights by federal officers; federal law enforcement officers authorized to carry firearms and make arrests; State and local law enforcement agencies; civil rights attorneys and law firms
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase if the Office of the Attorney General is awarded damages or recovers fees and costs. No impact on State expenditures is expected because existing budgeted resources are sufficient. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly empowers the Office of the Attorney General to initiate civil actions for damages and injunctive relief against judicial officers who violate constitutional and legal rights, and authorizes the office to direct state and local law enforcement agencies to gather and securely retain identifying digital data upon receiving a complaint.

The bill directly names the State Prosecutor as an authority empowered to receive complaints of judicial officer misconduct and direct appropriate state and local law enforcement agencies to collect and retain identifying digital data.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article for constitutional rights violations and requires court orders issued by state courts to release identifying digital data to plaintiffs.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be directed by the Attorney General, State Prosecutor, or State's Attorneys to gather and securely retain specified identifying digital data (such as license plate, GPS, and cell data) pursuant to complaints under the bill.

The State Treasurer's Office administers the Maryland Tort Claims Act and State Insurance Trust Fund; the fiscal note evaluates the potential impact on the office regarding claim investigations, state liability, and insurance adjusting workload.

The Department operates the Natural Resources Police, a state law enforcement agency that could potentially be directed to gather and retain digital data under the bill's provisions, and was consulted as an information source in the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each municipality to report the date and offices for its next regular election when submitting certified election results. Mandates that the State Board of Elections prominently display reported upcoming municipal elections on its website. Directs the State Board of Elections to publish a list of municipalities that have not yet reported upcoming elections. Requires each municipality maintaining a website to prominently display upcoming regular and special elections, dates, and offices. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities; municipal election officials; municipal voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 357 directly tasks the State Board of Elections with receiving reports from municipalities regarding upcoming municipal election dates and offices to be voted on, and requires SBE to prominently display this information as well as a list of nonreporting municipalities on its website.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts sales made at in-person elementary or secondary school book fairs from the State sales and use tax. Applies to sales by an elementary or secondary school, nonprofit parent–teacher organization, or other in-school nonprofit organization. Requires the book fair to take place in-person on school premises. Requires net proceeds to be used solely for the educational benefit of the school or its students. Covers sales where students, teachers, staff, or organization members manage the fair for a third-party vendor. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland elementary and secondary schools, students, teachers, school staff, nonprofit parent–teacher organizations, and third-party book fair vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State sales and use tax revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2027, potentially totaling approximately $150,000 annually. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for administering and enforcing sales and use tax regulations, including the implementation of this new tax exemption for school book fairs.

The bill directly impacts fundraising activities and book fairs conducted at public elementary and secondary schools and by affiliated parent-teacher organizations across the State's school systems overseen by MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters eligibility for the local option property tax credit on urban agricultural property. Defines eligible property as real property used for urban agricultural purposes and not assessed as agricultural land. Expands qualifying urban agricultural purposes to include hydroponics, beekeeping, livestock raising, composting, and agritourism activities. Removes acreage restrictions, priority funding area location requirements, and the restriction that produce stands be temporary. Requires jurisdictions terminating the credit to provide the public one year advance notice and opportunities for comment and appeal. Authorizes jurisdictions to prioritize credit renewals based on specific local priorities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of urban agricultural properties, urban farmers, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. County and municipal property tax revenues may decrease by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent jurisdictions grant the credit and expanded eligibility allows additional recipients. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly touches agricultural policy by expanding the statutory definitions of urban agricultural property and purposes to include indoor/outdoor crop production, value-added products, beekeeping, raising livestock, composting, controlled-environment agriculture, and agritourism.

The bill eliminates the requirement that urban agricultural property be located within a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which is a key land-use planning designation administered and tracked by the Department of Planning.

The agency hears administrative appeals regarding real property tax valuations, exemptions, and credits; the bill modifies eligibility criteria for this local property tax credit and explicitly guarantees an opportunity for appeal if a local government moves to terminate the credit.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments and local property tax credit determinations.
Responsible for executive policy coordination, intergovernmental relations with local governments, and final enactment/approval of legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county to establish a local grant for recipients of the State child tax credit. Limits eligibility to resident taxpayers with federal adjusted gross income below $15,000. Reduces the grant by 10% for each $1,000 or fraction thereof exceeding $15,000. Requires participating counties to reimburse the Comptroller for reasonable expenses incurred in sharing necessary information. Permits non-filing individuals to file an income tax return to claim the State child tax credit refund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; County governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income taxpayers with dependent children under age 6 or under age 17 with disabilities; Maryland county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local expenditures may increase beginning as early as fiscal 2027 to the extent counties elect to establish grant programs and reimburse the Comptroller for administrative costs; specific estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires counties establishing a child grant program to reimburse the Comptroller for reasonable expenses incurred in providing tax return and eligibility information necessary to implement the grants. The Comptroller also administers the underlying State Child Tax Credit upon which the local grant program is based.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Veterans and Military Families to provide an outer burial receptacle or a columbarium niche and marker. Mandates these items be provided at no cost for each interment location allotted to eligible decedents. Defines 'interment' and 'interment location' within provisions governing State veterans' cemeteries and related death-care services. Replaces statutory references to grave liners and burial plots with outer burial receptacles and interment locations. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: military veterans, qualified reserve members, and their eligible spouses and dependents in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Veterans and Military Families, which manages Maryland's state veterans' cemeteries. The legislation requires the department to provide an outer burial receptacle or columbarium niche and marker at no cost with each interment location.

The bill amends provisions in the Business Regulation Article governing cemeteries and the handling/transfer of unclaimed cremains and remains by regulated entities under the department's licensing oversight.

The bill updates definitions and reporting/transfer procedures under the Health Occupations Article governing licensed funeral establishments, crematories, and morticians regulated under boards within the department.
The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the implementing agencies and is referenced in the fiscal note and enforcement provisions of the amended subtitle.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals with emergency departments to provide stabilizing treatment or an appropriate transfer for emergency pregnancy-related medical conditions. Requires hospitals to allow pregnancy terminations when a treating practitioner determines the procedure is medically necessary to stabilize a patient. Prohibits hospitals from transferring an unstabilized patient unless the transfer complies with federal standards. Protects treating providers and reporting hospital employees from adverse employment or credentialing actions. Establishes civil penalties up to $50,000 per negligent violation for larger hospitals and $25,000 for smaller hospitals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: hospitals with emergency departments, pregnant patients seeking emergency care, treating health care practitioners, and hospital employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally from civil penalties in cases heard in the District Court. Local revenues increase minimally from civil penalties in circuit courts. Expenditures are unaffected, as the Maryland Department of Health can implement the requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for the oversight and regulation of hospitals under the Health - General Article, and is specifically tasked under the bill with adjudicating potential violations, imposing civil penalties, and staying or adjusting state fines based on related federal EMTALA investigations.
The court system is impacted by adjudicating civil penalty actions or related legal proceedings arising from violations of the bill in the District Court and circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and coordinates the state's emergency medical services and emergency patient transfer network, which intersects directly with the bill's standards governing the transfer of patients with unstabilized emergency conditions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Acupuncture Board to make available proof of renewal instead of issuing a renewal certificate. Prohibits employing an individual to practice acupuncture without a license or aiding or abetting unauthorized practice. Establishes criminal penalties of a misdemeanor for a first offense and a felony for subsequent offenses. Authorizes the Board to assess a civil penalty up to $10,000 for violations. Directs the Board to remit collected penalties into the General Fund of the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Acupuncture Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed acupuncturists, applicants for acupuncture licensure, and employers or individuals involved in the practice of acupuncture
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations; Board workload changes can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, and any civil penalties collected are remitted to the General Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Acupuncture Board is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters board operations regarding renewal proof, establishes new prohibitions on unauthorized practice and employment of unlicensed acupuncturists, and authorizes civil fines assessed by the board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes physician assistants, certified nurse-midwives, and licensed certified midwives to perform various clinical duties alongside other practitioners. Authorizes physician assistants to certify competency in guardianship proceedings and certify patient medical incapacity. Authorizes physician assistants to certify voluntary mental health admissions and petition for emergency evaluations. Requires health maintenance organizations to allow members to select physician assistants, certified nurse-midwives, or licensed certified midwives. Adds a physician assistant to the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study emergency department involuntary admission lengths of stay by November 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: physician assistants, certified nurse-midwives, licensed certified midwives, health maintenance organization members, pregnant incarcerated individuals, and individuals subject to emergency psychiatric evaluations or voluntary mental health admissions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Health Care Commission can complete the required study and report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is heavily impacted as the bill expands physician assistant authority across several MDH-regulated areas, including emergency evaluations, voluntary mental health facility admissions, covering charges for emergency evaluee exams, the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program, and HMO quality of care standards.

The bill explicitly mandates MHCC to review data on emergency department length of stay for individuals subject to an application for involuntary admission and submit a report with findings and recommendations by November 1, 2026.

The bill amends the eligibility certification requirements for the Department of Disabilities' Attendant Care Program, allowing physician assistants to certify that an individual is at risk of institutional placement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the health care practitioners authorized to order that a pregnant incarcerated individual be admitted to the correctional facility's infirmary.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM oversees state employee leave policies, which are impacted by authorizing physician assistants to sign certificates of illness or disability for state employees using sick leave for five or more consecutive workdays.

The bill expands the acceptable medical certifications that can accompany court petitions for guardianship of disabled persons to include physician assistants, impacting judicial filings and proceedings.
The bill amends the Human Services Article regarding financial assistance eligibility certifications for the Attendant Care Program, and DHS was identified as an agency affected by this provision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory membership of the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations to add a physician assistant member from the Maryland Academy of Physician Assistants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies examination requirements for optometrist licensure and license reinstatement under the State Board of Examiners in Optometry. Requires applicants to pass all sections of each part of a required licensure examination. Prohibits the Board from placing a licensee on inactive status for more than six consecutive years.
