Repeals requirements that the Board administer examinations periodically and collect reexamination fees. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners in Optometry
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for optometry licensure or license reinstatement and licensed optometrists in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State special fund expenditures or local finances, as the bill does not substantively change Board operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners in Optometry is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, which is responsible for regulating health care professionals and facilities across the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library to engage in collective bargaining. Establishes no more than two bargaining units: one for supervisory employees and one for nonsupervisory employees. Removes supervisory employees from the exclusions to the statutory definition of library employee. Protects existing bargaining units and collective bargaining agreements recognized or in existence on or before June 30, 2026. Alters criteria for determining when an employee is deemed a management employee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Public Library; Baltimore County Public Library Board of Library Trustees
qa_results.stakeholders: Supervisory and nonsupervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library; Baltimore County Public Library
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Baltimore County Public Library expenditures may increase minimally due to mediator costs and negotiated employee salary increases, though specific amounts depend on collective bargaining outcomes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency provides leadership, funding, and coordination for the state's 24 public library systems, which includes the Baltimore County Public Library system affected by this collective bargaining legislation.

The Public Employee Relations Board administers and standardizes collective bargaining for public sector entities across Maryland and served as an information source regarding the expansion of bargaining units to supervisory employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover scalp cooling systems. Mandates this coverage for entities that provide coverage for chemotherapy to treat cancer. Defines a scalp cooling system as a reusable medical device used to prevent or reduce chemotherapy-related hair loss. Applies to health benefit plans and contracts issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2027. Establishes an effective date of January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount, estimated between $11,600 and $302,800, beginning in FY 2027. Local government expenditures may increase for fully insured health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency responsible for enforcing health insurance mandates, reviewing carrier rate and form filings, and investigating consumer complaints under the Insurance Article.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which typically adopts state-mandated health benefits and expects a fiscal expenditure increase to cover scalp cooling systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement to hold a concentrated animal feeding operation discharge permit before constructing a new facility. Repeals the prohibition on issuing a permit to any person who begins construction without one. Authorizes the Department of the Environment to approve construction when the general discharge permit is administratively extended. Requires applicants to demonstrate compliance with coverage terms under the administratively extended general discharge permit. Requires applicants to comply with all other applicable laws, regulations, and required construction permits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: owners and operators of animal feeding operations and concentrated animal feeding operations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local government finances experience no effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies environmental discharge permitting requirements administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), authorizing MDE to establish an approval process allowing construction on new animal feeding operations while general discharge permits are administratively extended.

The bill impacts agricultural producers and concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) across the state; the Maryland Department of Agriculture provides regulatory oversight, support, and soil conservation coordination for the agricultural community affected by these permitting rules.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the 16-year maximum age cap for children receiving educational support in residential child care programs. Requires program operators to keep children enrolled in their previous school unless social services determines otherwise. Directs operators to provide academic assistance, study time, extracurricular support, and computer access for eligible students. Establishes mandatory training topics for applicants seeking certification as residential child and youth care practitioners. Exempts certified practitioners from new training requirements until their certificate renewal is due.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals; Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.stakeholders: children in residential child care programs, licensed operators of residential child care programs, and residential child and youth care practitioners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in fiscal 2027 for the Department of Human Services to conduct staff training, update regulations, and modify contracts, with indeterminate but minimal ongoing monitoring costs in future years. Other state agencies can implement the bill with existing resources, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS licenses residential child care programs and oversees local departments of social services, which are tasked by the bill with determining whether keeping a child enrolled in their previous school is in their best interest. DHS also incurs a direct fiscal impact ($25,000 in FY 2027) to train staff, update regulations, and modify contracts.

MDH licenses residential child care programs and houses the State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals, which must update and administer the expanded training and certification requirements established in the Health Occupations Article.

DJS licenses residential child care programs and contracts with providers, and will need to ensure that its facilities and contracted operators comply with the updated educational support and practitioner certification standards.

The bill amends the Education Article regarding the enrollment, academic support, individualized education programs (IEPs), behavioral intervention plans, and school-provider coordination for school-aged children placed in residential child care programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the reporting deadline for the workgroup studying member service transfers between State and local retirement and pension systems. Requires the State Retirement Agency to submit the workgroup's findings and recommendations by October 1, 2026. Directs the agency to report to the Governor, Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, House Appropriations Committee, and Joint Committee on Pensions. Extends the termination date of the workgroup and authorizing law to June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: members of Maryland State and local retirement and pension systems, and the State Retirement Agency
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as extending the reporting and termination dates does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary implementing agency tasked with convening and staffing the workgroup to study service transfers between State and local systems and submitting the final report by the extended deadline of October 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the operational life and reporting timeline of a temporary inter-system stakeholder workgroup/advisory body established to examine pension service transfers.
The bill requires the State Retirement Agency to submit the workgroup's report of findings, recommendations, and legislative initiatives directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters statutory terminology by replacing references to State historical parks with State parks. Applies this terminology change to strategic planning and establishment decisions for parks interpreting underrepresented populations. Renames Freedman's State Historical Park in Montgomery County to Freedman's State Park. Renames Port of Deposit State Historical Park in Cecil County to Port Deposit State Park. Preserves the existing statutory historical purposes and educational missions of the affected parks. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland State parks, local governments and nonprofit organizations partnering with the State on partnership parks, and underrepresented communities whose history is interpreted in State parks
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances because signs and publications have not yet been produced for the renamed parks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article governing the Maryland State Park System administered by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR), changing statutory references from 'State historical parks' to 'State parks' and renaming Freedman's State Historical Park and Port of Deposit State Historical Park.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits governing documents of condominiums and homeowners associations from unreasonably restricting installation of electric vehicle recharging equipment. Applies this prohibition to common use and limited common use parking spaces. Subjects equipment installations to ordinary budget processes for similar common area renovations. Requires governing bodies to consider sufficient community parking availability before installing or authorizing equipment. Authorizes governing bodies to grant renewable licenses for up to three years on necessary common elements. Applies retroactively to governing documents recorded or adopted before October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: condominium unit owners, homeowners association lot owners, governing bodies of condominiums and homeowners associations, and electric vehicle owners in common ownership communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state clean energy policies and electric vehicle infrastructure initiatives. While the bill does not establish new grant programs or regulatory mandates for the agency, it directly impacts statewide electric vehicle recharging equipment deployment policies.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division handles inquiries, mediation, and enforcement related to common ownership communities (condominiums and homeowners associations) and consumer rights.

The bill establishes statutory standards rendering certain restrictive covenants void and enforceable in common ownership communities, which may be the subject of civil dispute litigation within the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain Class B licenses from the prohibition against holding multiple alcoholic beverages licenses in Prince George's County. Applies this exemption to Class B (on-sale) beer and wine licenses. Includes Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses under the same exemption. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue multiple qualifying licenses to the same person or premises. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license applicants, restaurant and hotel operators, and license holders in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County revenues increase by $365 per additional Class B beer and wine license and $2,305 per additional Class B beer, wine, and liquor license issued, but total revenue gains are indeterminate because the number of new licenses is unknown. County expenditures are unaffected as enforcement can be handled with existing resources. No state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill pertains to alcoholic beverages licensing. While it specifically alters local licensing restrictions administered by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission by two years to September 30, 2028. Reduces legislative representation to one member of the Senate of Maryland and one member of the House of Delegates. Adds two private sector members appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. Requires the Commission to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly annually each December 1. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission; Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Private sector businesses engaged in bilateral trade with Ireland, the Irish–American community, and members of the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues or local finances. The Department of Commerce can continue to support the Commission using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission is established within the Department of Commerce, which provides staff and operational support for the commission. The Secretary of Commerce or their designee also serves as a member.
The Secretary of State or the Secretary of State's designee serves as an ex officio member of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership structure, reporting timeline, and termination date of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission, an executive advisory commission.

The Governor appoints members to the commission (including two additional private sector members created by the bill), has authority to remove appointed members, and receives the commission's annual report of findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments, which includes the new private sector seats on the commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds bacterial vaginosis to the list of infections eligible for expedited partner therapy. Authorizes licensed certified midwives to prescribe, dispense, or provide antibiotic therapy to partners without personal physical assessments. Replaces the statutory term sexually transmitted infection with an infection transmitted through sexual activity. Requires the Secretary of Health to adopt implementing regulations for public and private health care settings. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis and their sexual partners, licensed certified midwives, authorized prescribing health care practitioners, and licensed pharmacists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The Maryland Department of Health can update regulations and provider materials using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) oversees public health programs, health occupations licensing, and the Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT) program. Under the bill, the Secretary of Health is tasked with adopting updated regulations to implement the inclusion of bacterial vaginosis and licensed certified midwives in EPT protocols.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Prince George’s County Board of Education to require high schools to provide free drink spiking detection products. Requires schools to provide drug detection strips if an incident requiring overdose-reversing medication was reported. Applies these mandates only if the detection products are provided to the schools at no cost. Authorizes schools to make detection products available in school-based health clinics or school libraries. Requires each county public high school to report product distribution quantities annually to Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of Education; Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response
qa_results.stakeholders: public high school students and public high schools in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response can receive annual reports with existing budgeted resources. Prince George's County Public Schools expenditures may increase minimally to install product dispensers in clinics or libraries, while detection product mandates apply only if acquired at no cost.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article to require Prince George's County public high schools to make drink spiking and drug detection strips available to students under certain conditions, referencing overdose incident reporting submitted to the Maryland State Department of Education under existing law.

The bill involves distribution of drug detection strips and reporting to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response. The Maryland Department of Health manages the Overdose Response Program, which supplies free fentanyl test strips to authorized entities that schools may use to satisfy the bill's provisions.

The bill requires high schools to submit annual reports regarding distributed drug detection products directly to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response, an executive entity established within the Governor's coordinating offices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a party to the property guardianship of an alleged disabled person to request a stay of specified civil actions. Covers actions for failure to pay rent, warrants of restitution, wrongful detainer, foreclosures, sheriff's sales, and property actions. Requires the requesting party to give notice of the petition and stay request to all parties. Limits the stay to 90 days after filing the petition, unless extended for good cause. Lifts the stay automatically upon the appointment of a guardian or denial of the petition. Requires serving the appointed property guardian to effectuate service of process for a stayed action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: alleged disabled persons subject to property guardianship petitions, appointed guardians of property, landlords, mortgage lenders, and creditors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented with existing State resources with no material effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact. Small business plaintiffs such as landlords and creditors may experience delayed revenue or proceedings due to court stays.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland court system by authorizing parties to petition for stays in specific civil proceedings (such as failure to pay rent, wrongful detainer, and foreclosure actions) during guardianship proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for implementing these procedural changes and associated court case management programming.

The bill amends the Estates and Trusts Article regarding guardianship proceedings for alleged disabled persons, an area closely related to estate and fiduciary administration overseen in part by the Registers of Wills.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances through December 31, 2027. Adds a representative of a Maryland historically Black college or university to the task force membership. Requires the task force to submit an updated report of findings and recommendations by October 31, 2026. Directs the task force to submit the updated report to the Governor and General Assembly. Continues task force staff support by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration; Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances
qa_results.stakeholders: Historically Black colleges and universities in Maryland, Task Force members, and individuals affected by natural psychedelic substance policies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Maryland Cannabis Administration can provide staff support and absorb minimal travel reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration is mandated to provide staff support for the Task Force, and its Director (or designee) serves as an ex officio member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the operational timeline through 2027 and alters the membership requirements of the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances.
The Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee is a designated member of the Task Force examining psychedelic substances and therapeutic uses.
The Secretary of Disabilities or the Secretary's designee is an ex officio member of the Task Force.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (Department of Veterans and Military Families) or the Secretary's designee serves as a member of the Task Force.
The Governor designates the chair of the Task Force, appoints several members (including the new HBCU representative), and receives the updated findings and recommendations report.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to the Task Force, including the newly added seat for an HBCU representative.

The University System of Maryland is explicitly listed among the entities eligible for a research appointment and also encompasses three state historically Black universities eligible for the new HBCU seat.
As a state agency and historically Black university, Morgan State University representatives are eligible to fill the newly created Task Force seat for an HBCU representative.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program in the Maryland Department of Agriculture starting July 1, 2028. Requires the Department, in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment, to administer the program and seek funding. Directs the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 for the program beginning in fiscal year 2028. Authorizes grants to farmers, soil conservation districts, higher education institutions, nonprofits, partnering businesses, and qualifying consortiums. Supports projects developing or maintaining infrastructure, collection programs, education, or technical assistance for food waste reduction and composting. Requires the Department to submit an annual program report to the General Assembly beginning December 31, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Farmers, urban farmers, urban agricultural producers, soil conservation districts, institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, and partner businesses in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2028 for the mandated appropriation (covering administrative start-up costs), rising to $371,471 in FY 2029 for ongoing grant awards and administrative expenses, and $380,300 by FY 2031. State and local institutions of higher education and local soil conservation districts may receive indeterminate grant revenues and incur corresponding project expenditures beginning as early as FY 2029.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 429 establishes the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA). MDA is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the program, applying for external funding, awarding grants, and reporting annually to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly requires MDA to administer the grant program, identify and apply for funding, and prioritize grant applications in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE).
The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 for the grant program in the State budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2028.

As the State's principal budget agency, DBM is responsible for preparing the Governor's annual budget and incorporating the $250,000 mandated appropriation established by the bill starting in fiscal year 2028.

Institutions of higher education are explicitly designated as eligible grant recipients under the program, potentially receiving funding for research and projects involving organics recycling, compost application, and food waste diversion.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to apply for and receive grant funding under the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program.

As a public four-year higher education institution, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is eligible to receive grant awards under the program for qualifying organics recycling and food waste reduction projects.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a family child care provider who is a reserve component member to designate a substitute provider. Mandates that the substitute provide care during the provider's absence for required training and active service. Authorizes the provider to use the substitute for up to 45 working days in any 12-month period. Preserves the Maryland State Department of Education's authority to establish substitute requirements and necessary qualifications.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Family child care providers who are members of a military reserve component, designated substitute child care providers, and families with children in family child care homes
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill with existing resources; state revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE regulates and registers family child care homes and providers under the Education Article. The bill directly impacts MSDE's regulatory framework by allowing family child care providers who are reserve component members to use a substitute provider for up to 45 working days per year for required training and active service.

The bill provides protections and regulatory flexibilities for reserve component and National Guard members who operate child care businesses, supporting military service members and their families in balancing service obligations with small business ownership.

The legislation directly accommodates National Guard members called for required training and active service duties by expanding the allowed use of substitute child care providers to 45 working days per year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing. Renames the advisory council as the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing. Adds the Secretary of Disabilities or a designee from the Department of Disabilities to the council. Prohibits using new stationery until all printed documents bearing the prior name are fully used. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; Maryland Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland, along with members and staff of the Office and Advisory Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. State expenditures are unchanged because renaming expenses and participation on the advisory council by the Maryland Department of Disabilities can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly renames the agency to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, updating its statutory references and advisory council framework.
The bill explicitly alters the composition of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing by adding the Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) as a statutory member.
The Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing is established directly within the Office of the Governor, and the Governor appoints the members of its advisory council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally renames the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing to the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing and modifies its statutory membership.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives to disclose when they lack professional liability insurance coverage. Mandates written notice to residents, prospective residents, or patients if insurance coverage is not maintained or has lapsed. Directs nursing homes and assisted living programs to notify residents within 30 days after coverage lapses. Requires nurse midwives and licensed certified midwives to provide notice during initial visits and informed consent procedures. Obligates covered providers lacking coverage to post conspicuous notices and retain signed disclosure acknowledgments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Nursing home residents, assisted living program residents, midwifery patients, nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the licensing and regulation of health care facilities (including nursing homes and assisted living programs through the Office of Health Care Quality) and houses the State Board of Nursing, which licenses and regulates nurse midwives and licensed certified midwives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office administers the arbitration system for medical malpractice and professional liability claims in Maryland and served as an information source on the fiscal and policy note.
The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's commercial insurance market, including medical professional liability insurance policies, and served as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class B–SEC (small event center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George’s County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George’s County to issue the license to qualifying small event centers. Requires venues to accommodate between 75 and 110 individuals and meet a $350,000 capital investment or appraised value threshold. Mandates that venues make food available during the hours of operation for an event. Limits license issuance to 24 per license year and three per State legislative district. Sets the annual license fee at $3,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George’s County
qa_results.stakeholders: small event center owners and operators in Prince George’s County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George’s County license fee revenues increase by approximately $10,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees the regulation of the alcoholic beverage industry and the collection of applicable excise and sales taxes in the state. While this bill is localized to Prince George's County and administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal effect, it falls under the broader statutory and regulatory purview of state alcoholic beverages law.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State, units of local government, county sheriffs, and their agents from entering into immigration enforcement agreements. Defines these agreements as contracts or memoranda authorizing state or local entities to enforce federal civil immigration law. Applies to agreements made under 8 U.S.C. § 1103, 8 U.S.C. § 1357, or other federal laws. Requires entities and agents with existing agreements to exercise the agreement's termination provision immediately. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Sheriffs; Maryland Department of State Police; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Immigrants residing in or traveling through Maryland, county sheriffs, local correctional officers, and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly subject to the bill's statutory prohibition against entering into or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements (such as 287(g) agreements) with federal authorities to enforce civil immigration law, and was consulted for the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees state correctional facilities and detention operations whose officers and facilities are prohibited under the bill from participating in civil immigration enforcement agreements or 287(g) jail enforcement/warrant service models, and the department served as an information source for the fiscal note.

The OAG serves as chief legal counsel to state agencies, advises state and local entities on legal standards when interacting or partnering with federal law enforcement, and would handle legal interpretation and defense of the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's coordinating body for criminal justice policy and public safety grant funding, making the statewide ban on intergovernmental immigration enforcement agreements relevant to its policy alignment and oversight responsibilities.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies that must comply with the prohibition and ensure immediate termination of any existing immigration enforcement agreements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and specified health insurance entities to provide annual coverage for orthoses and replacements. Includes in covered benefits all orthoses and prostheses determined medically necessary by a treating provider for physical activities. Prohibits coverage requirements more restrictive than the Medicare Coverage Database. Prohibits separate annual or lifetime dollar maximums and higher cost-sharing than similar medical benefits. Mandates compliance reporting by carriers and Medicaid managed care organizations to state agencies by June 30, 2032.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid enrollees and insured individuals requiring orthoses or prostheses, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and orthotic and prosthetic providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. No impact on the Maryland Medical Assistance Program because the bill codifies existing coverage. Health insurance expenditures for local governments offering fully insured plans may increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is required to cover orthoses under the bill. MDH is also tasked with jointly developing reporting forms, receiving compliance data from Medicaid managed care organizations, and submitting a joint report with the Maryland Insurance Administration to the General Assembly.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs subject to the coverage and provider panel requirements. MIA collects rate and form filings and is responsible for jointly prescribing reporting forms, receiving carrier compliance data, and submitting a joint report to the General Assembly.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which was reviewed for potential fiscal and coverage impacts resulting from the mandated benefits (determined to be negligible as coverage is already provided).

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program in the Maryland Department of Health. Requires the Director of Dementia Services and Brain Health to administer the Program. Directs the Program to staff the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council. Mandates the Department establish a provider resource toolkit for dementia care by October 1, 2027. Requires the Department to review and update the toolkit annually beginning January 1, 2028. Expands Council duties to examine provider readiness and identify methods to assist health care providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council; Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: health care providers, individuals with or at risk for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, and their caregivers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,700 in FY 2027 to hire one program administrator, increasing to $103,500 by FY 2031. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 446 establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and requires MDH to administer the program, oversee the State Plan on Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias, develop and maintain a provider resource toolkit, and hire new staff.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Aging assist in providing staff support for the Council and partner with MDH to develop and maintain the dementia care provider resource toolkit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory duties of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council, expanding its responsibilities to examine health care provider readiness and receive quarterly activity updates from the new Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the termination date for the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council, making it a permanent entity. Alters council membership by adding the Secretary of Agriculture and removing representatives of higher education and retail electric suppliers. Directs the council to identify barriers and recommend policies for integrating electric vehicle charging infrastructure statewide. Requires the council to develop charging solutions for multidwelling units and policies supporting fleet purchases. Mandates that the council submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1 each year. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council; Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: electric vehicle drivers, electric utilities, zero emission vehicle and charging equipment manufacturers, fleet operators, automotive dismantlers and recyclers, and state and local government agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Staffing and reporting requirements continue with existing State resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council, where the Secretary of Transportation is a member and the Maryland Department of Transportation is tasked with providing primary staff support.
The Director of MEA is a designated member of the Council, and MEA is statutorily required to assist MDOT in providing staff support to the Council.
The Executive Director of the Technical Staff of the Public Service Commission is a member of the Council, and the PSC is required to assist MDOT in providing staff support.
The bill explicitly amends the Council's membership to add the Secretary of Agriculture (or designee).
The People's Counsel (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the permanent Council.
The Governor designates the chair or co-chairs of the Council, appoints numerous stakeholder members, and receives annual reports from the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the duties and membership of, and repeals the sunset date for, an executive advisory council (ZEEVIC).
The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is a statutory member of the Council, which addresses state fleet vehicle policies and charging infrastructure.
The Secretary of the Environment (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Council.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the various public and industry stakeholder members to the Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from suspending or revoking a veterinary license solely for specific conduct. Bars the Board from reprimanding, censuring, or placing a licensee on probation on that sole basis. Applies when a licensee discusses or recommends cannabis or a product containing cannabidiol on an animal. Requires the discussion or recommendation to be for potential therapeutic effect or health supplementation purposes. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed veterinarians, veterinary practitioners, and animal owners in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture and regulates veterinarians, veterinary practitioners, and animal health standards. This bill directly amends the grounds upon which the Board may take disciplinary action against licensees.

The bill references statutory definitions under the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article and protects veterinary professionals when discussing or recommending cannabis or CBD products, an area tangentially related to the state's overarching cannabis regulatory framework overseen by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a gift basket permit in Howard County issued by the Board of License Commissioners. Authorizes qualifying florists selling gift baskets to deliver beer, wine, or liquor to of-age county consumers. Limits basket contents to 72 ounces of beer, 2.25 liters of wine, or 2.25 liters of liquor. Requires permit holders to purchase all alcoholic beverages from a retail license holder. Exempts the gift basket permit from public school distance restrictions applicable to other licenses. Sets the annual permit fee at $100.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County florists, gift basket businesses, retail alcohol license holders, and adult consumers in Howard County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Howard County revenues increase by $100 annually for each permit issued, potentially totaling $1,500 per year across an estimated 15 eligible florists. County enforcement and inspection costs are absorbed using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and taxation of the alcoholic beverage industry. Although this bill creates a local permit administered by the Howard County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it pertains to the regulation and retail sale of alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each institution of higher education that provides on-campus housing to provide menstrual hygiene products free of charge. Mandates the provision of these products in all student health centers on or before August 1, 2028. Defines menstrual hygiene products as size-appropriate tampons or sanitary napkins for use in connection with the menstrual cycle. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Institutions of higher education that provide on-campus housing
qa_results.stakeholders: Students attending institutions of higher education with on-campus housing; public four-year universities; community colleges providing on-campus housing; private colleges and universities providing on-campus housing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local higher education expenditures increase, likely minimally, beginning in FY 2029 for public four-year institutions and community colleges providing on-campus housing due to dispenser, supply, and maintenance costs. Specific dollar figures are unavailable. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: USM constituent institutions that offer on-campus housing are directly mandated to provide menstrual hygiene products free of charge in all student health centers, incurring direct operational and supply costs.

Morgan State University provides on-campus housing and is directly required by the bill to provide free menstrual hygiene products in its student health center, leading to an increase in higher education operating expenditures.
As a residential public college providing on-campus housing, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly required to supply free menstrual hygiene products in its student health center.
MHEC is the state's coordinating and regulatory agency for higher education and Title 11 of the Education Article, within which this new mandate for degree-granting institutions is codified.
MHEC coordinates statewide policies and oversees degree-granting higher education institutions subject to this statutory addition to the Education Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Rural Readiness Program administered by the Rural Maryland Council to enhance economic development capacity in rural communities. Requires the Council's Executive Director to certify eligible applicants that successfully complete the program. Requires funding priority for specified rural development funds to be given to entities holding a completion certificate. Establishes the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to provide competitive planning and capacity building grants up to $50,000. Prohibits awarding grants from the fund to eligible applicants that have not completed the Rural Readiness Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Rural Maryland Council; Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Rural communities and eligible applicants, including nonprofit organizations, units of local government, State-recognized tribes, institutions of higher education in the State, regional planning agencies, and economic or workforce development organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly as grants are awarded. Local governments in rural communities may receive grants of up to $50,000 but must provide a 20% match.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Rural Readiness Program and the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to be administered by the Rural Maryland Council.

The Rural Maryland Council is administratively and budgetarily housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture, making the department relevant to the implementation and budget administration of the new program and fund.
The bill designates the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill designates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund.
The Rural Maryland Council is required to submit an annual report to the Governor on the grants awarded under the program and fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Parole Commission from permanently denying parole to an incarcerated individual. Entitles incarcerated individuals to subsequent parole hearings at specified intervals following a parole denial. Requires the Commission to provide copies of parole determination documents to incarcerated individuals and their representatives. Mandates recording each parole hearing and providing redacted recordings to incarcerated individuals at no cost. Prohibits a county from being a party to an administrative proceeding involving an erroneously convicted individual.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals eligible for parole, their legal representatives, crime victims, erroneously convicted individuals seeking state compensation, and county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $346,800 in FY 2027, reflecting four new staff and operational costs for audio recordings, rising to $456,000 by FY 2031. General fund revenues may decrease due to foregone $30 fees for hearing recordings. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Parole Commission and the Division of Correction are housed within DPSCS. The bill establishes major procedural, recording, document disclosure, and reporting mandates on the Maryland Parole Commission, resulting in significant ongoing operational and fiscal impacts including the need for additional staff.

Wrongful conviction compensation claims under Section 10-501 are filed with and adjudicated by Administrative Law Judges at OAH. The bill amends the procedural rules governing parties to these proceedings and applies retroactively to existing proceedings before an ALJ.

The Attorney General is statutorily designated to represent the State as a party in wrongful conviction compensation proceedings under Section 10-501, which are directly amended by the bill regarding party designation.
Under Section 10-501, the Board of Public Works is named as the state respondent entity in wrongful conviction compensation cases and is responsible for disbursing monetary awards ordered by ALJs.
The bill expands the mandated contents of the Maryland Parole Commission's annual report submitted to the Governor, requiring detailed data on parole decisions disaggregated by race.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force. Requires the Task Force to study the expansion of blockchain technology and cryptocurrency in the State. Directs the Task Force to examine associated benefits, privacy and other risks, state revenues, and energy consumption. Requires the Office of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor to provide staff. Mandates submission of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by October 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation, Maryland Department of Labor; Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force
qa_results.stakeholders: cryptocurrency and blockchain businesses, financial services industry representatives, Maryland higher education economics faculty, and state and local government agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $49,400 in FY 2027 and $53,500 in FY 2028 for one contractual staff position in the Maryland Department of Labor. Member travel reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor provide staff support for the Task Force, the Secretary of Labor is an ex officio member, and the agency incurs a direct fiscal impact for contractual staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary body, the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force, to study blockchain and cryptocurrency and submit findings and recommendations.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which evaluates blockchain implementation, privacy risks, and benefits for state government.
The Securities Commissioner (within the Office of the Attorney General's Securities Division) is designated as a member of the Task Force to examine regulatory aspects of digital assets.
The Comptroller (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force, which is charged with assessing the cryptocurrency industry's effect on State revenues.
The State Treasurer (or designee) is named as a member of the Task Force to evaluate the fiscal and financial implications of digital assets.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which examines the economic and business impact of blockchain and cryptocurrency in Maryland.
The Governor is responsible for appointing five members to the Task Force and will receive the final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for the five gubernatorial appointments to the Task Force.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the refundable theatrical production State income tax credit through taxable year 2031. Limits the aggregate credit amount carried forward from all prior fiscal years to $20,000,000. Prohibits the Secretary of Commerce from carrying forward unissued credit amounts exceeding that cap. Maintains the $2,000,000 maximum tax credit certificate limit for a single theatrical production. Abrogates the tax credit program on June 30, 2032.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified theatrical production entities and facilities staging for-profit, national touring or pre-Broadway theatrical productions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $500,000 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2032, with no effect in FY 2027. To the extent credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, Higher Education Investment Fund revenues, Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures, and local highway user revenues also decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for administering the Theatrical Production Tax Credit, including reviewing applications, issuing tax credit certificates, and tracking the new $20 million cap on carry-forward credit amounts under the bill.

As the State's chief tax collection agency, the Comptroller processes the refundable income tax credits claimed by qualified theatrical production entities against personal and corporate income taxes.

To the extent that credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, revenues to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and subsequent TTF expenditures for local highway user revenue grants may decrease.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits operating or towing a vehicle without making reasonable efforts to remove dangerous accumulated snow and ice from exposed surfaces. Excludes situations where compliance would violate workplace safety regulations or threaten the operator's health or safety. Restricts police enforcement to a secondary action unless a violation contributes to property damage, serious bodily injury, or death. Establishes graduated fines for violations, ranging from $25 to $200 for noncommercial vehicles and $75 to $1,000 for commercial vehicles. Imposes fines up to $1,000 for noncommercial and $1,500 for commercial vehicles if a violation contributes to an accident.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and commercial vehicle operators in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from District Court fines. Enforcement can be handled with existing state and local resources, resulting in no material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle and traffic safety laws on state highways, MSP officers are responsible for enforcing the bill's prohibitions and issuing citations for dangerous accumulations of snow and ice.
The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding rules of the road and exposed vehicle surface safety, directly impacting the transportation statutory framework overseen by MDOT.

As the MDOT administration responsible for driver licensing, vehicle regulations, driving records, and traffic safety initiatives, MVA is affected by changes to vehicle operation standards and traffic violation records.
The District Court will process citations, collect fine revenues, and adjudicate contested cases resulting from violations of the new traffic prohibition.
MDTA operates Maryland's toll facilities and employs its own police force, which is empowered to enforce vehicle laws and citations on toll roads and bridges.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for unreimbursed classroom supplies to certain prekindergarten teachers. Includes full-time prekindergarten classroom teachers in publicly funded programs at eligible public providers. Includes full-time lead teachers and consulting teachers in publicly funded programs at eligible private providers. Authorizes a subtraction of up to $250 for unreimbursed classroom supplies used by students or teachers. Excludes expenses subtracted from federal adjusted gross income under the Internal Revenue Code. Applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time prekindergarten teachers at eligible public and private prekindergarten providers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease by approximately $80,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Local income tax revenues may decrease by approximately $50,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. The Comptroller's Office can administer the change using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's tax administration agency, the Comptroller is directly responsible for modifying state income tax forms and administering the expanded subtraction modification for eligible prekindergarten teachers.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees publicly funded prekindergarten programs and eligible providers defined under § 7-1A-01 of the Education Article whose teachers are made eligible by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires transportation network companies to maintain and publish a written plain-language deactivation policy for operators. Prohibits companies from deactivating an operator for violations not reasonably understood to be part of the policy. Restricts companies from relying solely on passenger reports for deactivation except under specified conditions. Mandates written notice of deactivation and allows deactivated operators to withdraw accrued earnings under certain circumstances. Establishes an appeals process allowing operators at least 30 days to appeal a deactivation decision.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Transportation network companies and transportation network operators in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 10 of the Public Utilities Article, which governs Transportation Network Companies (TNCs) and operators regulated and licensed by the Public Service Commission. While the bill places direct operational requirements on TNCs regarding deactivation policies and appeals, it alters the statutory and regulatory framework for for-hire passenger motor carriers under the Commission's jurisdiction.

The bill mandates that a TNC's deactivation policy is legally enforceable as a contractual term between the company and the operator, which may lead to breach of contract actions in the state court system, though it does not materially affect judicial finances or operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the gross income thresholds from charitable contributions that trigger independent CPA audits or reviews for charitable organizations. Raises the contribution threshold requiring an independent certified public accountant audit from $750,000 to $1,000,000. Raises the threshold requiring an independent certified public accountant review from $300,000 to $400,000. Increases the cash receipt limit for submitting an affidavit in place of an audit or review to $400,000. Authorizes the Secretary of State to require an audit or review if gross income is under $1,000,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Charitable organizations soliciting or receiving contributions in Maryland; independent certified public accountants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State implementation and online filing system update costs are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary agency responsible for the registration and oversight of charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill directly alters the statutory thresholds for independent audits and reviews required for charitable organization registration statements filed with the Secretary of State.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects to the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects. Alters experience qualifications for landscape architect Board members and updates institutional accreditation standards for licensure applicants. Authorizes the Board to issue an emeritus status license to eligible professionals with at least 25 years of experience. Establishes a two-year term from issuance for individual licenses and business permits. Repeals the permit exemption for businesses providing landscape architectural services to themselves or affiliated entities. Repeals the requirement for license applicants to pay examination fees directly to the Board.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Landscape Architects; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Professional landscape architects, applicants for landscape architect licensure, business entities offering landscape architectural services, and retired landscape architects seeking emeritus status.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact; the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects can implement the provisions with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Landscape Architects is an occupational licensing unit housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly alters the board's name, composition requirements, exam procedures, licensing terms, and fee structures.

The bill alters the statutory qualification requirements for professional landscape architect members appointed by the Governor to the Board, directly impacting the vetting and candidate recommendation duties of the Office of Appointments.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members of the Board with the advice and consent of the Senate, and the bill modifies the statutory qualifications required for those appointments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to adopt regulations governing investment committee responsibilities. Mandates establishing a process for considering remedies, including divestment, when a business ceases to be a qualified business. Authorizes, rather than requires, the Corporation to divest itself of an equity investment within 15 years. Requires investment committee review and approval before divestment or pursuing another remedy in the Corporation's best interest.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: businesses receiving equity investments from the Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances, though financial investment returns to the Maryland Technology Development Corporation may increase. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), requiring it to adopt regulations regarding investment committee responsibilities and providing flexibility regarding divestment and alternative remedies for its equity investments.

The Department of Commerce is Maryland's primary economic development agency and works closely with TEDCO initiatives, including programs funded through the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account referenced in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a law enforcement agency from requesting a verbal acknowledgement during an interaction with a victim. Applies the prohibition to requests purporting to relieve an agency of an obligation. Prohibits requests purporting to preclude or define investigation scope or limit prosecution. Bars requests purporting to limit a victim's private right of action. Authorizes an affected victim to bring an action seeking injunctive or declaratory relief.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of sexually assaultive behavior and Maryland law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's primary law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police officers and investigators are directly bound by the bill's prohibition on requesting verbal acknowledgments or waivers from victims of sexually assaultive behavior during investigations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which establishes the recommended standards and practices that law enforcement agencies must follow when a victim requests to limit or suspend an investigation. The department was also consulted for the bill's fiscal note.

The bill maintains the statutory provision permitting an affected victim to file a civil action seeking injunctive or declaratory relief in the state court system if a law enforcement agency violates the statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a minimum adequate security standard for courtroom security at all courthouse facilities in the State. Requires court security officers to meet the qualifications for a special police officer. Directs entities responsible for courthouse security to use best efforts to meet specific staffing ratios beginning July 1, 2027. Mandates officers in criminal, family, or juvenile proceedings, custody cases, and across courthouse floors. Expands best-effort staffing requirements to cover all court proceedings beginning July 1, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; local sheriffs' offices
qa_results.stakeholders: Judges, court personnel, litigants, criminal defendants, county sheriffs' offices, and court security officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.6 million in FY 2027 only to provide security enhancement grants to local jurisdictions. Local government expenditures increase, significantly in some jurisdictions, beginning in FY 2027 for sheriffs' offices to hire an estimated 206 additional court security officers, partially offset by $5.6 million in local grant revenues in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly impacts court security operations across all Maryland courthouse facilities. The Administrative Office of the Courts serves as the administrative arm of the Judiciary, which is responsible for court security in the appellate and District courts and will administer state grant funding provided to local jurisdictions to support courtroom security enhancements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of District Court associate judges in District 11 from five to six. Requires three associate judges to be appointed from Washington County instead of two. Maintains the requirement that three associate judges be appointed from Frederick County. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: District Court judges, court personnel, and litigants in Washington County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $423,500 in FY 2027 to fund one new judgeship, one clerk, and two contractual bailiffs, increasing to $571,800 by FY 2031. Revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 493 creates an additional District Court judgeship in Washington County (District 11), along with associated court staff positions (courtroom clerk and contractual bailiffs), directly impacting judicial administration, operations, and general fund expenditures managed under the Judicial Branch.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and processing of candidates to fill judicial vacancies across Maryland, which includes the newly created District Court judgeship.
The Governor holds the constitutional authority to appoint judges to fill newly established judicial seats in the District Court.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the effective duration of temporary protective orders from seven days after service to 14 days after issuance. Requires the court to hold a final protective order hearing no later than 14 days after order issuance. Retains judicial authority to extend a temporary protective order up to six months to effectuate service. Maintains order effectiveness until the second open day if the court is closed on the expiration date. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Petitioners seeking domestic protective orders and respondents named in protective order proceedings
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by altering the effective duration of temporary protective orders issued by courts to 14 days after issuance and adjusting the statutory deadline by which the courts must schedule and conduct final protective order hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts qualifying intermediate care facilities providing medically managed residential substance use disorder treatment from certificate of need requirements. Requires facilities to submit written notice of intent to the Maryland Health Care Commission at least 45 days beforehand. Authorizes the Commission to approve exemptions that align with the State health plan and serve the public interest. Alters conditions under which licensed intermediate care facilities may change bed capacity without a certificate of need. Repeals the prior certificate of need exemption for certain residential or intensive substance-related disorder treatment facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: intermediate care facilities offering substance use disorder treatment services and patients seeking residential substance use disorder treatment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Workload on the Maryland Health Care Commission can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) administers the Certificate of Need (CON) program and is the primary entity responsible for receiving notices and determining whether proposed intermediate care facilities or changes in bed capacity meet the criteria for CON exemptions under the bill.

The Secretary of Health licenses the intermediate care facilities providing substance use disorder treatment affected by the bill, and MHCC is an independent commission housed within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the State sales and use tax exemption for sales of precious metal bullion or coins exceeding $1,000. Repeals the requirement that the transaction must occur at the Baltimore Convention Center to qualify. Alters the definition of refined precious metal to specify that its value primarily depends on precious metal content. Excludes jewelry or a work of art made of precious metal bullion or coins from the exemption. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and vendors of precious metal bullion or coins in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by $2.8 million in FY 2027, including a $2.5 million decrease in general fund revenues and a $0.3 million decrease in Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund revenues. Expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's chief tax collector, the Comptroller of Maryland administers and enforces the state sales and use tax laws and oversees the collection and distribution of sales tax revenues affected by this exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the felony crime of sexual offense by a person in a position of authority involving a child under age 13. Establishes felony penalties for individuals with specified prior convictions who commit sexual offenses while in positions of authority. Designates these felony offenses as qualifying predicate crimes for sexual solicitation of a minor. Requires individuals convicted of these felony offenses to register as Tier III sex offenders. Classifies individuals convicted of misdemeanor sexual offense by a person in a position of authority as Tier I sex offenders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Persons in positions of authority at schools or youth programs, minors, and victims of sexual offenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected, though an unknown number of cases may shift from the District Court to the circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for operating Maryland's state correctional facilities, managing probation and parole, and overseeing sex offender registry requirements. The bill establishes new felony penalties of up to 10 and 20 years of imprisonment and designates offenders under these provisions as Tier III sex offenders.
