The bill establishes new offenses and elevates certain misdemeanor sexual offenses to felonies, shifting caseloads from the District Court to the circuit courts and impacting judicial proceedings, caseload tracking, and sentencing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal cases. The creation of new felony offenses, heightened penalty thresholds, and mandatory lifetime Tier III sex offender registration directly affect defense workload, case exposure, and trial proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands collective bargaining subjects for full-time sworn law enforcement officers and court security officers in Baltimore City. Includes salary, wages, and merit step increases in bargainable compensation alongside city-administered benefits. Requires eligible officers to collectively bargain in good faith jointly with the Sheriff or designee and Baltimore City. Retains collective bargaining over leave, holidays, vacations, hours, working conditions, and job security. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Sheriff's Office; Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time sworn deputy sheriffs at the rank of lieutenant or below and court security officers in the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office, the Baltimore City Sheriff, and Baltimore City government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Baltimore City expenditures may increase if negotiated personnel costs under collective bargaining agreements exceed what would have otherwise been spent; exact amounts cannot be reliably estimated in advance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the minimum annual salaries for members and inspectors of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners. Sets the board chair annual salary at not less than $21,240. Sets the annual salary for each other board member at not less than $17,700. Sets minimum annual salaries of $18,000 for the part-time deputy chief inspector and $8,260 for 18 part-time inspectors. Requires all listed salaries to include any cost-of-living increase available to nonrepresented Anne Arundel County employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County; Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: chair, members, part-time deputy chief inspector, and part-time inspectors of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners; Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County salary expenditures increase by at least $33,716 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 due to mandated salary increases, rising further with future cost-of-living adjustments. State revenues and expenditures are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames and alters entertainment permits for certain alcoholic beverages license holders in Anne Arundel County. Replaces the music permit with a background entertainment permit authorizing televisions and recorded or piped-in background music. Replaces the entertainment permit with a general entertainment permit authorizing background entertainment, trivia games, karaoke, and limited live music. Replaces the dancing permit with a full entertainment permit authorizing general entertainment, a stage area, a permanent dance floor, and floor shows. Requires outdoor entertainment areas under general or full entertainment permits to be at least 100 feet from residentially zoned property. Removes the statutory prohibition against dancing on licensed premises without an entertainment permit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders in Anne Arundel County and residents of nearby residentially zoned properties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this bill strictly modifies local alcoholic beverage entertainment permits administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and operation of licensed alcoholic beverage establishments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the fee structure for Class C per diem alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. Maintains existing flat daily fees for events with an estimated attendance of fewer than 500 individuals. Restructures license fees for events with an estimated attendance of 500 or more individuals. Requires larger events to pay fees per day for each point of sale location serving alcohol. Sets large-event fees at $25 per point of sale for beer or beer and wine licenses. Sets large-event fees at $50 per point of sale for beer, wine, and liquor licenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Clubs and organizations hosting events with Class C per diem alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase by up to $7,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 from per-point-of-sale fees on events with 500 or more attendees. County expenditures and state finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry in the state. While this bill specifically modifies local per diem alcoholic beverages license fees set and collected by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation of alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt a policy prohibiting student electronic communication device use. Mandates implementation not later than the 2027–2028 school year. Requires students to store devices and prohibits accessing social media platforms during the academic school day. Permits device use for disability accommodations, documented health issues, translation tools, or approved caregiving. Prohibits disciplinary suspension or expulsion solely for a violation of the policy. Directs local boards to report policy and enforcement data annually to the Maryland State Department of Education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; County Boards of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students, parents and guardians, public school teachers and administrators, and county boards of education in Maryland (excluding the Maryland School for the Blind and the Maryland School for the Deaf)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems can implement the policy, regulation, and reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary state oversight agency responsible for adopting regulations to implement the act, receiving electronic communication device policies and annual implementation data from local school boards, and publishing compiled reports and policies on its website.
The bill explicitly mentions the Maryland School for the Deaf to exempt it from the requirement to implement the student electronic communication device prohibition policy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Revises, restates, and recodifies State laws governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program. Reorganizes statutory provisions relating to managed care organizations, advisory committees, and the Maryland Children's Health Program. Replaces outdated references regarding substance abuse with modern terminology referring to substance use disorders. Updates cross-references throughout the Health - General Article to reflect renumbered and newly codified sections. Clarifies that the enactment constitutes a nonsubstantive code revision without altering existing legal rights or duties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees, Maryland Children's Health Program enrollees, participating managed care organizations, and Medicaid health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill constitutes a nonsubstantive code revision.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the core subject of this code revision and recodification bill.
MHCC's Executive Director is an ex-officio member of the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee recodified by the bill, and the committee is tasked with reviewing data collected by MHCC.
HSCRC is referenced in provisions governing required hospital discharge data submissions for out-of-state hospitals treating Maryland Medicaid recipients.

The Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex-officio member of the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee, and Medicaid managed care organizations are required to track benefit information from DHS-administered assistance programs.
The Insurance Commissioner is consulted by the Secretary of Health to establish actuarially adjusted capitation payments for Medicaid managed care organizations.
MSDE is consulted by the Department of Health to define school-based clinics that provide care to Medicaid managed care enrollees.
The Department of Aging is designated as an entity from which the Secretary of Health must seek recommendations when appointing consumer members to the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee.
The Department of Disabilities is consulted for recommendations on consumer appointments to the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee.
OAH is designated in statute as the administrative body to hear appeals by managed care organizations regarding penalties imposed by the Department of Health.
The Comptroller receives fines and penalties collected by MDH from managed care organizations that fail to comply with program requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires governmental units employing firefighters to compute overtime wages on hours worked exceeding 168 hours per 28-day period. Requires counties and municipalities to provide pay rate notices and pay period statements of hours, earnings, and deductions. Authorizes firefighters or their exclusive representatives to initiate grievances for missing payroll statements or unpaid wages due. Entitles firefighters to unpaid wages and damages up to three times the missing wage amount. Exempts collective bargaining agreements in effect before the October 1, 2028 effective date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: Firefighters employed by governmental units, Maryland counties and municipalities that employ firefighters, and the Maryland Aviation Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Local government expenditures likely increase, potentially significantly in some jurisdictions, beginning in fiscal 2029 to pay additional overtime wages or hire more firefighters. State expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund are not materially affected, and the Maryland Department of Labor and Office of Administrative Hearings can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Wage and Hour Law under the Labor and Employment Article regarding overtime computation for firefighters employed by governmental units, which the Maryland Department of Labor oversees and enforces.
MAA employs 99 state firefighters at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport who are directly covered by the bill's overtime pay calculation standards.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Aviation Administration, and any operational or overtime expenditure adjustments for state airport firefighters affect the Transportation Trust Fund.
OAH adjudicates contested wage payment cases and state employee grievances referred under labor laws and will need to train its administrative law judges on the bill's provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to expand annual reporting on the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund. Mandates reporting agricultural land transfer tax proceeds from entirely woodland parcels distributed during the preceding fiscal year. Requires the department to explain any uncertainties regarding required distribution amounts and actions necessary to resolve them. Directs the department to submit this report annually by September 30 to two legislative committees. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Private woodland owners participating in the Woodland Incentives Program, students seeking natural resources careers through the Mel Noland Fellowship Program, and the Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Department of Natural Resources can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Natural Resources to expand its annual reporting on the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund to include the amount of agricultural land transfer tax proceeds distributed to the fund and any uncertainties regarding those distributions.

The Comptroller receives remitted agricultural land transfer tax revenues and oversees state fund distributions, making the agency relevant to the accounting and resolution of any uncertainties regarding transfer tax proceeds credited to the fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum annual revenue limit for a cottage food business from $50,000 to $100,000. Allows qualifying residential kitchen operations to generate up to $100,000 annually without obtaining a commercial food manufacturer license. Regulates businesses producing or packaging nonhazardous cottage food products in a residential kitchen. Requires these businesses to continue complying with State labeling rules and food safety course requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: cottage food business owners, home-based food producers, consumers, and retail food stores
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $52,434 in FY 2027 to hire one part-time registered sanitarian, increasing to $67,700 by FY 2031. General fund revenues face a potential minimal decrease starting in FY 2027 if businesses opt out of commercial food manufacturer licensing. Local health departments can handle any workload changes using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary regulatory agency overseeing cottage food businesses, including processing submissions, reviewing labels and food safety certifications, and issuing unique identification numbers under Health - General § 21-301. The bill directly impacts MDH by increasing its general fund expenditures to hire staff to manage the increased volume of cottage food businesses.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture promotes local agricultural products and oversees venues like farmers' markets where cottage food products are commonly sold directly to consumers. MDA was also consulted as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to offer an educator well-being and flourishing course by July 1, 2027. Makes the course available synchronously or asynchronously to all school personnel and administrators. Mandates the course only if the department can provide it at no cost or comparable cost. Requires instruction on eight dimensions of well-being identified by the federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. Sets the course fee at a rate comparable to courses with equivalent professional development points. Terminates the statutory provisions on June 30, 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland school personnel and administrators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland State Department of Education can use existing resources to provide an existing course, and statutory requirements are contingent on no-cost or comparable-cost availability. Local school system finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 546 directly requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to make available a professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing for school personnel and administrators, covering the eight dimensions of well-being.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a refundable $1,000 State income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child. Reduces the credit by $50 per $1,000 of income exceeding $100,000 for individuals or $150,000 for joint filers. Authorizes claiming the credit only for the taxable year in which the stillbirth occurred. Applies the tax credit to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026. Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to report annually to the Governor and General Assembly on additional qualifying agricultural equipment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland income taxpayers who are parents of a stillborn child, agricultural producers, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will decrease beginning in fiscal 2028 due to the refundable income tax credit, but specific estimates are unquantified in the available fiscal note. The Maryland Department of Agriculture can complete annual reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers the state income tax system and is responsible for implementing the new refundable income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child as well as overseeing the subtraction modification for enhanced agricultural management equipment.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Agriculture to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly recommending additional types of equipment that should qualify for the enhanced agricultural management equipment subtraction modification.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the annual report required from the Secretary of Agriculture regarding recommended agricultural equipment qualifying for tax subtractions.

The bill establishes a tax credit contingent upon receiving a Certificate of Birth Resulting in Stillbirth issued under § 4-213.1 of the Health - General Article, which is maintained and issued by the Maryland Department of Health's vital records division.

qa_results.bill_summary: Governs housing development application approvals under local laws and regulations in effect when a complete application is submitted. Requires regulatory authorities to determine whether an application is complete within 30 days of receipt. Grants approved housing development project proponents a vested development right for at least five years. Prohibits local governments from collecting development excise taxes or impact fees until project construction is complete. Exempts taxes or impact fees imposed to finance county debt incurred on or before January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission; local regulatory authorities
qa_results.stakeholders: Housing developers, residential construction businesses, county governments, and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances. Local government revenues from residential development impact fees and excise taxes will be delayed until construction completion. Local government expenditures may increase in certain jurisdictions for personnel and tracking systems to implement required application review timelines and vested right durations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Land Use Article to regulate local land use application procedures, vesting of development rights, and local development impact fees. The Department of Planning provides guidance, technical assistance, and land use policy support to local governments as they implement these changes.

The bill directly impacts the regulatory predictability, timeline, and fee structure of residential housing development projects statewide, aligning with DHCD's core mission to promote housing development and affordability across Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children to research resident deaths and unmarked graves. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to staff the Commission and administer its funding. Authorizes the Commission to conduct archaeological surveys, excavations, disinterments, and forensic DNA analyses without separate agency permits. Grants the Commission and its contractors unrestricted access to sealed juvenile, medical, and administrative records. Requires the Commission to submit an initial progress report by December 31, 2027, and a final report by December 31, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Descendants of deceased children buried at the facility, former residents of the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children, justice-involved youth, and African American communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,050,000 in FY 2027, reflecting funding included in the FY 2027 State budget for the cemetery project, with potential additional indeterminate expenses in FY 2028 and FY 2029. The Office of the Attorney General can provide staff using existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Attorney General as Chair of the newly established Commission, requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide staff, grants the office authority to procure goods and services and administer funding/grants, and authorizes the Attorney General to appoint public members and issue subpoenas.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services is an ex officio member of the Commission. The subject of the investigation, the former House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children, operated on the grounds of what is now DJS's Cheltenham Youth Detention Center, and DJS holds relevant records, historical ties, and related cemetery project funding.
The State Archivist is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission, and the investigation will extensively access and rely upon historical archives and records held by the agency.

The Director of the Maryland Historical Trust (a division of the Department of Planning) is an ex officio member of the Commission, and the Commission is explicitly required to consult with the Trust regarding methods and safety for disinterment and archaeological excavations.

The Commission is mandated to consult with the Maryland Department of Health regarding methods and safety for disinterment and excavation, and the investigation requires access to historical health, vital, and medical records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an executive commission (Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children) operating with a four-year sunset to study historical deaths and abuses and make formal recommendations.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.
MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, whose Chief Archaeologist is mandated to serve on the Commission.
The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.

The State Superintendent of Schools is a member of the Commission, and the Commission is charged with recommending educational initiatives to incorporate this history into the state's school curriculum.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission, and the department collaborates on cemetery conservation planning.
The Executive Director of the Gibson-Banks Center for Race and Law at the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law is named as a statutory member of the Commission.
The Commission must submit an initial report by December 31, 2027, and a final report by December 31, 2029, directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to post a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates. Directs the Commissioner to publish the database on the Maryland Department of Labor's website. Mandates that the database allow users to search active certificates by street address, city, and county. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: owners and lessees of elevator units and members of the public seeking elevator inspection information
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Requirements can likely be implemented using existing budgeted resources. If existing online resources do not meet the bill's searchable database requirements, general fund expenditures may increase by an estimated $75,000 for a system module. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish and maintain a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates on the department's website, potentially requiring up to $75,000 in expenditures to upgrade existing database capabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates the membership of the Legislative Policy Committee and names of standing legislative committees in State law. Adds the Chair of the House Government, Labor, and Elections Committee to the Legislative Policy Committee. Decreases the number of additional Delegates appointed to the Legislative Policy Committee from four to three. Updates statutory references to reflect the House Health Committee and Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment. Redirects specified agency reports and regulatory notices to the updated legislative committees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly; Legislative Policy Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: members of the Maryland General Assembly, standing legislative committees, and State agencies required to submit reports or notices to legislative committees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or governmental operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 554 updates several sections of the Health - General Article governing reporting and notice requirements for the Maryland Department of Health (including tobacco and cancer grant allocations, Medicaid long-term care eligibility modifications, and regulatory notices) to reflect the renamed House Health Committee.

The bill updates statutory provisions in the Insurance Article requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Board to submit proposed regulations and active purchasing/contracting strategy plans to the renamed House Health Committee.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article to update the legislative committees (House Health Committee and Senate Finance Committee) to which the Commissioner of Labor and Industry must submit notices and recommendations regarding the federal Bloodborne Pathogen Standard.

The bill updates the committee titles under the State Government Article for the legislative chairs who may formally request the State Archivist to review, evaluate, and provide recommendations on official State designations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a predetermination review process to evaluate whether an individual's criminal history disqualifies them from occupational licensure. Makes the department's predetermination binding unless a subsequent direct and material adverse change occurs in the criminal history. Authorizes departments to charge a criminal history review fee up to $100, subject to an income waiver. Excludes mortgage loan originator applicants and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services from these provisions. Requires five State departments to report predetermination requests and associated implementation costs by October 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with criminal histories seeking State occupational licenses or certifications; applicants for mortgage loan originator licensure
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $50,800 in FY 2027, $22,500 in FY 2028, and $23,500 in FY 2029 for the Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Department of Agriculture. State special fund revenues experience an indeterminate but minimal net impact depending on review fee collections and application volumes. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is one of the primary departments required to establish the binding predetermination review process for occupational licenses and submit a report by October 1, 2028. The fiscal note identifies an increase in special fund expenditures for MD Labor to hire contractual staff to administer the process.

MDA is explicitly subject to the predetermination review requirements and reporting mandate under the bill, with the fiscal note noting an increase in special fund expenditures for programming updates for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

MDH is directly named as an implementing department that must offer the predetermination review process across its occupational licensing boards and submit an implementation report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

MDE is designated as an implementing department responsible for conducting predetermination reviews for occupational licenses or certificates under its jurisdiction and submitting a reporting update by October 1, 2028.

DHS is designated as an implementing department responsible for conducting predetermination reviews for applicable occupational certificates or licenses under its jurisdiction and reporting on its implementation by October 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly amends the law to exclude DPSCS from the statutory definition of 'department' subject to these occupational licensing review and non-denial requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the annual limit of one wine festival license that the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County may issue. Authorizes the Board to issue multiple wine festival licenses each year to eligible retail and winery license holders. Allows the Board to select multiple festival weekends, Friday through Sunday, each year. Removes the prohibition on holding a wine festival within the 24th legislative district. Requires the primary focus of each wine festival to remain the promotion of Maryland wine.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: holders of retail, Class 3 winery, and Class 4 limited winery licenses in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State operations or finances. Prince George's County local revenues increase minimally from issuing up to three additional wine festival licenses annually at a fee of $75 each.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates aspects of the alcohol industry and collects alcoholic beverage excise and sales taxes. Although this legislation specifically pertains to local wine festival licenses administered by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it touches upon alcoholic beverage distribution and sales involving state-licensed wineries and wholesalers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $5,687,000 annually for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program from fiscal 2028 through 2030. Reestablishes mandated state funding for the credentialing program. Supports awards for staff credentials, child development associate credentials, and administrator credentials. Authorizes the Office of Child Care to award achievement bonuses, training reimbursements, and training vouchers. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Office of Child Care
qa_results.stakeholders: child care providers, staff, and administrators pursuing or holding child care credentials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.7 million annually from fiscal 2028 through 2030 to fund the mandated appropriation for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Child Care Credential Program is administered by the Office of Child Care within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which oversees credentialing, achievement bonuses, training reimbursements, and vouchers for child care providers.

The Department of Budget and Management prepares and oversees the state budget, which must incorporate the bill's statutory mandated appropriation of $5,687,000 annually for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to include an appropriation of $5,687,000 for the program in the state budget bill for each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the felony offense of intentionally inflicting bodily harm, permanent disability, or death on a law enforcement animal. Prohibits intentionally harassing, interfering with, injuring, or killing an emergency response animal. Defines emergency response animals to include specified police dogs, police horses, and search and rescue dogs. Establishes misdemeanor penalties including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to $10,000. Allows the defense of necessity and an affirmative defense against unlawful police use of force.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State and local law enforcement units
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, emergency response animal handlers, search and rescue personnel, and individuals accused of offenses against emergency response animals.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not materially affected. Minor case-flow shifts may occur between the circuit courts and the District Court, but penalty adjustments will not significantly alter revenues or incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police utilizes trained law enforcement animals (such as K-9 units) in its daily policing, detection, and tracking duties, and investigates criminal violations involving interference with or injury to law enforcement animals.
The bill alters criminal penalties from a felony to specific misdemeanor offenses, impacting judicial caseload distribution between the District Court and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters sentencing, establishing misdemeanor terms of imprisonment ranging up to five years, which impacts state correctional and local detention operations and community supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new misdemeanor criminal offenses carrying potential terms of incarceration and sets specific affirmative defenses, directly affecting the representation of indigent defendants charged under this section.

The Department of Natural Resources Police employs trained K-9 units for conservation law enforcement and frequently participates in search and rescue efforts covered under the definition of emergency response animals.
The bill protects search and rescue dogs engaged in state-directed search and rescue operations, which fall under coordinated emergency response efforts managed and supported by MDEM.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on criminal law enforcement and handles any subsequent appellate litigation arising from convictions or legal challenges regarding the Maryland Use of Force Statute defense.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes consumer protection and disclosure requirements for registered cemetery operators and licensed crematories providing pet cremation services. Requires providers to distribute detailed written descriptions of available pet cremation services to owners, veterinarians, and the Department of Agriculture. Mandates written certification verifying the cremation date and identity of pet cremains returned to pet owners. Directs providers to maintain holding facilities that preserve dignity and to retain detailed cremation records for at least five years. Classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to civil enforcement and misdemeanor criminal penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors; Office of Cemetery Oversight; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Pet owners, licensed crematory operators, registered cemeterians, veterinarians, and pet shops
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are absorbable within existing budgeted resources, with revenues not materially affected. Imposes no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, housed within the Department of Health, is the primary regulatory and licensing body under the bill tasked with overseeing licensees offering pet cremation services, adopting regulations, investigating violations, and making enforcement referrals.

The Office of Cemetery Oversight within the Department of Labor regulates cemeterians, cemetery operators, and crematory permit holders under Title 5 of the Business Regulation Article, enforcing pet cremation and perpetual care requirements.

The bill designates violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act enforced by the OAG's Consumer Protection Division, and authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions for injunctive relief and civil penalties.

The bill statutorily mandates that each registrant, permit holder, and licensee offering pet cremation services distribute written descriptions of available pet cremation services to the Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Queen Anne's County to use development impact fee revenues for school replacement costs. Expands allowable fee expenditures beyond uses permitted under state law or local law. Permits fee revenues to finance any capital costs related to replacing public school facilities. Does not alter the imposition, assessment, or collection rates of existing county development impact fees. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Queen Anne's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Queen Anne's County public school system, property developers in Queen Anne's County, and Queen Anne's County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill does not alter development impact fee rates or collections in Queen Anne's County, but expands the authorized uses of collected fee revenue to include public school facility replacement capital costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands allowable uses of local development impact fee revenues in Queen Anne's County to finance capital costs for the replacement of public school facilities, which intersects with the Commission's oversight of public school construction and capital improvement funding across Maryland.

Under Maryland law, the Department of Planning collects required annual reports from counties on local laws authorizing development impact fees, surcharges, and excise taxes, as well as the collection and expenditure of those revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of nonprofit housing corporation for eligibility for real property tax and special assessment exemptions. Defines qualifying affordable housing based on federal low-income housing tax credits or local income and rent restrictions. Exempts certain real property owned through subsidiary entities of nonprofit housing corporations from State and political subdivision taxes. Excludes property in Baltimore City and projects that received local financial assistance before July 1, 2026. Authorizes nonprofit housing corporations to negotiate payments in lieu of taxes with political subdivisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit housing corporations, subsidiary entities developing affordable housing, low-income tenants, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate decrease in State and local property tax revenues beginning in FY 2027 depending on the number of nonprofit housing corporations that qualify for exemptions. State and local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 571 directly amends the Housing and Community Development Article (§ 12-104) regarding the definition of nonprofit housing corporations and affordable housing criteria (including Low-Income Housing Tax Credit covenants, which the Department oversees). The bill directly impacts affordable housing development, financing structures, and public-private housing partnerships in Maryland.

The bill broadens property tax exemptions for real property owned by nonprofit housing corporations and their subsidiaries. Any disputes over eligibility or qualification for these real property tax exemptions may be appealed through the local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards.

As the highest administrative review body for state and local tax disputes, the Maryland Tax Court has jurisdiction to hear appeals stemming from decisions regarding real property tax assessment exemptions for qualifying nonprofit housing corporations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from engaging in residential housing practices that have a discriminatory effect, regardless of intent. Defines discriminatory effect as having a disparate impact or perpetuating segregated housing patterns based on protected characteristics. Establishes that an action is not a violation if it is necessary for legitimate nondiscriminatory interests without less discriminatory alternatives. Authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations related to affirmatively furthering fair housing. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Landlords, residential property sellers and buyers, tenants, housing authorities, and political subdivisions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Civil Rights is the primary state agency responsible for administering and enforcing Maryland's fair housing laws. The bill expands prohibited discriminatory housing practices under Title 20 of the State Government Article to include acts with a discriminatory effect regardless of intent, directly governing MCCR's enforcement, investigation, conciliation, and litigation activities.

The bill directly amends the Housing and Community Development Article to authorize the Department of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations regarding its statutory obligations to affirmatively further fair housing.

The Office of the Attorney General has statutory authority under the re-enacted provisions of the State Government Article to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations, which include discriminatory housing practices defined under the bill.
Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings preside over administrative hearings on housing discrimination charges issued by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill references civil actions that aggrieved individuals or the Commission may bring in state courts to seek damages, injunctions, or other civil relief for alleged discriminatory housing practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the student attendance policy of each county board of education to allow excused or discretionary absences for civic engagement. Specifies civic engagement includes testifying before legislative bodies, meeting with legislative members, and participating in the legislative page program. Includes student advocacy on legislation and contributions to the consideration, development, or implementation of policy issues. Authorizes an appropriate representative to provide reasonable documentation if an attendance policy requires a note. Mandates that each county board of education adopt policies and procedures to carry out these requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: County boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students in Maryland and county boards of education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Local school boards can update attendance policies and track civic engagement using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 575 establishes standards for public school student attendance and lawful excused absences for civic engagement. The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public education policies and attendance regulations across Maryland's 24 local school systems, and the bill explicitly references the Department alongside county boards in deeming eligible civic engagement activities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies State endangered and threatened species conservation laws and the Irreplaceable Natural Areas Program. Defines "foreseeable future" and "harm" regarding protected fish, wildlife, and plants. Requires endangered and threatened species determinations to occur without reference to possible economic or other impacts. Requires the Secretary of Natural Resources to delist species substantiated as extinct, recovered, or misclassified. Authorizes the Secretary to designate essential habitats and adopt management protocols. Requires regulations authorizing the taking of black vultures if federal protections are removed or repealed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Secretary of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: agricultural producers dealing with black vultures, land developers, conservation organizations, and small businesses affected by habitat and wildlife regulations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 for the Department of Natural Resources to implement regulatory updates and for State agency capital programs to comply with enhanced protections, but specific figures cannot be reliably determined. Local government capital project expenditures may also increase. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with reviewing and updating regulations for the Irreplaceable Natural Areas Program, determining threatened and endangered species listings and delistings, designating essential habitats, and regulating the taking of species and migratory birds.

Under statutory provisions referenced in the bill, the Secretary of Natural Resources is required to consult with the Secretary of Agriculture regarding conservation programs for nongame, endangered, or threatened wildlife and plants. Additionally, the bill addresses depredation permits for black vultures, a species known to cause agricultural and livestock damage.

MDOT manages extensive state infrastructure and capital projects that may face regulatory delays, modifications, or increased compliance costs resulting from expanded definitions of harm and the designation of essential habitats for protected species.
DGS oversees the planning, construction, and management of state facilities and capital programs, which may be affected by strengthened protections for endangered and threatened species habitats.
The bill touches upon existing statutory provisions directing the Governor to review and utilize state programs in furtherance of endangered and threatened species conservation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates agency notification requirements for issuing a Class C per diem beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George's County. Requires the Board of License Commissioners to notify the director of the Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement. Removes the outdated notification requirement previously sent to the County Department of Environmental Resources. Maintains existing notices to the County Police Chief, County Fire Chief, and applicable municipal chief administrative officers. Mandates that each notice specify the time, place, and expected size of the event.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement; holders and applicants of Class C per diem beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. Prince George's County operations and finances are not materially affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county board of library trustees to provide for the selection of a student member. Requires the student to be a junior or senior in high school or a home instruction program. Mandates that the student demonstrate good character, good academic standing, and an interest in library matters. Establishes a one-year term of office for the student member. Authorizes the student member to vote on all policy matters before the board. Permits the board to adopt a policy or bylaw authorizing the student to vote on nonpolicy matters.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Boards of Library Trustees
qa_results.stakeholders: high school students enrolled in public, nonpublic, or home instruction programs, and county boards of library trustees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency provides leadership, coordination, and support for Maryland's 24 public library systems. This bill directly pertains to the governance and membership structure of county boards of library trustees by authorizing the addition of a student member.

The bill establishes eligibility requirements for high school students enrolled in public or nonpublic schools or home instruction to serve on county boards of library trustees; MSDE was consulted as an information source regarding student eligibility and status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority. Charges the workgroup with studying procurement approval structures for capital expenditures regarding State roads, bridges, or highways. Directs the workgroup to examine potential Board of Public Works oversight of new contracts and change orders. Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation and the Board of Public Works to jointly staff the workgroup. Mandates submission of final findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Board of Public Works; Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Transportation contractors, engineering and design firms, State transportation agencies, and labor organizations involved in Maryland road, bridge, and highway projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. Staffing and workgroup expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing Maryland Department of Transportation and Board of Public Works resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 587 establishes a workgroup focused on the procurement and contract approval authority for capital expenditures by the Department of Transportation (MDOT). The Secretary of Transportation serves on the workgroup, and MDOT is tasked with jointly providing staff for the workgroup.

The bill centers on studying whether and how the Board of Public Works (BPW) should exercise contract approval and oversight authority over transportation capital expenditures, and mandates that BPW jointly staff the workgroup alongside MDOT.

The workgroup is tasked specifically with reviewing and evaluating the approval authority structure, contract awards, change orders, and potential BPW oversight for capital expenditures made by the Maryland Transportation Authority.
The Comptroller of Maryland, or the Comptroller's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority.
The State Treasurer, or the State Treasurer's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority.
The Governor appoints four members to the workgroup, designates the chair, and receives the workgroup's final report and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary study body, the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority, to review transportation procurement procedures and report recommendations.

The workgroup's study scope specifically includes evaluating whether to expand delegated procurement authority to contracts and change orders supporting Maryland Transit Administration fixed guideway systems and associated transit facilities and vehicles.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Howard County Agricultural Land Preservation Fund to the Howard County Agricultural Preservation and Innovation Fund. Expands the authorized uses of certain transfer tax proceeds budgeted for the fund. Maintains funding to support the county's agricultural land preservation program. Authorizes funding for other programs, services, or initiatives that enhance the commercial viability or environmental sustainability of county agriculture. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Director of Finance; Howard County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Agricultural landowners, farmers, and agricultural businesses in Howard County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill modifies the allowable uses of dedicated transfer tax proceeds without changing county revenue or the amount allocated to the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the Public Local Laws of Howard County to expand the allowable use of local transfer tax proceeds in the renamed Howard County Agricultural Preservation and Innovation Fund to enhance the commercial viability and environmental sustainability of agriculture. While the bill has no state fiscal impact and is administered locally by Howard County, the policy area directly aligns with the Department of Agriculture's core mission of promoting agricultural land preservation and agribusiness viability.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person in Wicomico County from standing in a roadway, shoulder, median divider, or intersection determined to be inherently dangerous. Requires Wicomico County or municipal corporations to consult with the State Highway Administration before determining State roadways are inherently dangerous. Defines inherently dangerous as posing a serious risk of injury that cannot be mitigated with ordinary care. Prohibits a police officer from issuing a citation unless compliant warning signs are installed in the designated location. Requires State Highway Administration approval before the county or a municipality installs signs on a State highway. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Wicomico County; municipal corporations in Wicomico County
qa_results.stakeholders: pedestrians, motorists, municipal and county officials, and law enforcement officers in Wicomico County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances, as the State Highway Administration can handle duties with existing resources. No material effect expected on Wicomico County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires Wicomico County and its municipalities to consult with the State Highway Administration (SHA) to determine if state roadways are inherently dangerous and requires SHA approval before signage can be installed on state highways in accordance with SHA's traffic control standards.
As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the state highway network and standard traffic control specifications affected by the bill.

The bill sets legal conditions under which citations may be issued for standing in inherently dangerous roadways, which are processed through the District Court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill establishes restrictions and requirements on when police officers can issue citations for standing on specified roadways and highways within Wicomico County, which affects Maryland State Police troopers patrolling the area.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands an existing computer-related offense to include acts intended to interrupt or impair critical infrastructure. Subjects violators to existing felony penalties of up to five years of imprisonment, a $25,000 fine, or both. Prohibits unauthorized computer acts that deny authorized access to or interrupt critical infrastructure or a public safety answering point. Establishes a felony penalty of up to 10 years of imprisonment, a fine up to $50,000, or both. Defines critical infrastructure as physical or virtual systems vital to public safety, security, transportation, health, or utilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators and users of critical infrastructure, public safety answering points, and individuals accused of computer-related offenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and statewide emergency communications infrastructure. The bill specifically establishes felony penalties for unauthorized computer interference that impairs or interrupts public safety answering points (PSAPs), which are the 24/7 9-1-1 call centers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the custody and supervision of individuals sentenced to terms of incarceration. The bill expands criminal penalties and creates a new felony offense with sentences up to 10 years imprisonment.
The Judiciary and AOC are responsible for adjudicating criminal charges and civil actions arising under § 7-302 of the Criminal Law Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD provides legal representation to indigent defendants charged with criminal offenses, including the new and expanded felony offenses created by this bill.

MSP is the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for investigating criminal violations of state law, including cybercrimes and attacks targeting critical infrastructure or emergency communication centers.
DoIT manages cybersecurity, statewide IT networks, and digital infrastructure for state executive agencies, which are classified as critical virtual systems protected under the statute.
GOHS coordinates statewide strategy for disaster prevention, emergency readiness, and the protection and resilience of Maryland's critical infrastructure.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the State income tax credit for licensed physician preceptors in health care shortage areas. Repeals the requirement that preceptorship students be enrolled in an in-state medical school or training program. Reduces the required community-based clinical training per rotation from 100 hours to 90 hours. Caps the aggregate amount of unused tax credit certificates carried forward from prior fiscal years at $100,000. Applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Governor's Workforce Development Board; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed physicians serving as uncompensated preceptors, medical students, postgraduate medical trainees, and patients in health care workforce shortage areas
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 due to increased utilization of the tax credit, subject to the modified program cap; specific dollar estimates are unavailable. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary administrative agency responsible for identifying health care workforce shortage areas, receiving applications, issuing tax credit certificates to eligible physician preceptors, reporting annually on the credit's utilization, and adopting regulations.

As the state's tax collector, the Comptroller processes the State income tax credits claimed by physicians, receives annual certification reports from the Department of Health, and manages the associated impact on general fund revenues.

The bill statutorily requires the Department of Health to consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board to identify geographic areas with health care workforce shortages and to adopt regulations governing the credit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Conforms the Maryland Uniform Simultaneous Death Act to the uniform act adopted by the Uniform Law Commission. Deems an individual to have predeceased another if survivorship by at least 120 hours is not established. Divides survivorship property equally or proportionally among co-owners who do not survive each other by 120 hours. Establishes evidentiary rules for proving death and presumes death after five continuous years of unexplained absence. Shields third-party payors from liability for good-faith distributions made before receiving written notice of conflicting claims. Exempts distributions where application causes escheat to the State or contradicts express governing instrument terms.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Orphans' Courts; Registers of Wills
qa_results.stakeholders: heirs, estate beneficiaries, co-owners of property with right of survivorship, estate personal representatives, trustees, insurers, and financial institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is responsible for the administrative probate of decedents' estates and serving as clerk to the Orphans' Court. This bill substantively alters the legal rules governing survivorship (establishing a 120-hour survival requirement) which directly governs how estates are administered and how assets are distributed when related individuals die simultaneously or in close succession.

The bill establishes procedural and evidentiary standards for determining survivorship and death in judicial proceedings, and explicitly provides that payors may deposit disputed assets with the court having jurisdiction over probate proceedings, directly impacting court procedures and administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the timeframe for the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program in Montgomery County. Changes the alternative pilot program start date from April 1, 2024, to April 1, 2026. Extends the duration of the pilot program from seven years to nine years. Requires the Public Service Commission to submit an interim report in the program's seventh year. Postpones the deadline for the Commission's final study report to December 31, 2035.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County, residential and small commercial electric customers in Montgomery County, and electric companies serving Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and Montgomery County finances experience no significant fiscal impact during the initial five-year period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulator and implementing agency for the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program. The bill directly alters the program's statutory timeline, extending the duration of the pilot and shifting the deadlines for the commission's interim and final reports and studies.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in proceedings and matters concerning utility service and rates. As noted in the fiscal note, OPC monitors and participates in the pilot program's regulatory processes within existing budgeted resources.
The bill alters the statutory deadline (from December 31, 2031, to December 31, 2035) for the Public Service Commission to submit its final pilot program study report to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the required bond amount for the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer to $250,000. Authorizes the Metropolitan Commission to conduct studies, plans, and estimates for new facilities in specified unserved areas. Raises the maximum criminal fine from $100 to $1,000 for specified violations of county sanitary district laws. Establishes graduated civil fines between $250 and $1,000 for infractions, plus $250 for each continuing day. Alters civil fines for unauthorized water removal up to $1,000 for first violations and $2,000 for repeat violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission; Commissioners of St. Mary's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Treasurer and Deputy Treasurers of the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission, public water and sewer system users, and violators of St. Mary's County sanitary district laws
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Local revenues for St. Mary's County and the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 from higher fines and penalties. State operations and local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the required depository and fidelity bond given by the Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer of the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission must be in a form approved by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The bill modifies criminal penalty thresholds, civil infraction citation procedures, and judicial enforcement remedies handled by the District Court in St. Mary's County, which is supported administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones within the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville. Requires local authorization by local law enacted after reasonable notice and a public hearing before system deployment. Imposes a civil penalty of up to $40 on vehicle owners or drivers recorded failing to stop. Directs citation revenues toward program administration costs and local public safety programs. Requires each city to report program costs, revenues, and safety outcomes to state officials by December 1, 2028. Sunsets the pilot program on June 30, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers in the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville, pedestrians and students in local school zones, and municipal law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2030 from contested citations. Indeterminate increase in revenues and expenditures for the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville to the extent that each city elects to deploy stop sign monitoring systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Highway Administration to authorize the use of stop sign monitoring systems if placed on State highways in school zones, and mandates that SHA prominently place signage providing notice that the systems are in use on State highways.

The District Court (supported by AOC) is tasked with prescribing a uniform citation form, establishing civil penalty procedures, adjudicating contested citations, and coordinating citation processing and evidence sharing with local enforcement agencies.

The MVA is authorized to refuse vehicle registration or reregistration or suspend registration if penalties are unpaid and uncontested, and is prohibited from recording the violation as a moving violation or assessing points on driving records.

MDOT is the parent department overseeing both the State Highway Administration and the Motor Vehicle Administration, both of which have specific statutory roles and operational impacts under the bill.
The bill requires the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville to report comprehensive program implementation and evaluation data to the Governor by December 1, 2028.
Under statutory automated enforcement provisions referenced in the fiscal note, any citation revenues exceeding 10% of total local revenues must be remitted to the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution requiring the Governor to budget funds for all State employee memoranda of understanding. Establishes a binding arbitration process to resolve collective bargaining impasses for certain State employees. Requires bargaining parties to select a neutral arbitrator if negotiations do not conclude by September 15. Expands mandatory collective bargaining subjects to include health benefits and fringe benefits other than pension benefits. Makes statutory collective bargaining changes contingent on voter approval of the constitutional amendment in November 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees and exclusive employee bargaining representatives; State institutions of higher education; Maryland Environmental Service
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by at least $150,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2028 for arbitration services and personnel, with potentially significant impacts on personnel expenditures beginning in fiscal 2029 depending on arbitration awards. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the principal personnel and fiscal agency for Maryland state government. It leads collective bargaining on behalf of the State, oversees state employee compensation and health benefits (which are expanded under the bill), manages arbitration proceedings and costs, and prepares the annual state budget bill where funding for agreements must be included.

The bill proposes an amendment to Article III, Section 52 of the Maryland Constitution requiring the Governor to include appropriations in the annual budget bill to implement all terms of MOUs and binding arbitration awards for State and higher education employees.

MES is explicitly governed by the bill's collective bargaining and arbitration provisions. The proposed constitutional amendment and statutory changes require the Governor to fund MES memoranda of understanding in the state budget bill, which could fundamentally affect MES's nonbudgeted operational status.

USM and its Chancellor are explicitly subject to the bill's provisions regarding collective bargaining, memoranda of understanding, and the constitutional requirement that the Governor include appropriations in the budget bill to fund employee agreement terms.

Morgan State University's governing board is explicitly designated as a bargaining party under the statute, and its employee memoranda of understanding are subject to the required budget appropriations under the proposed constitutional amendment.

St. Mary's College of Maryland's governing board is explicitly named as a bargaining representative party, and its negotiated agreements are subject to the bill's collective bargaining provisions and mandated budget inclusion.

PERB administers collective bargaining laws for State and higher education employees and retains jurisdiction over unfair labor practice complaints that may arise during collective bargaining or the neutral arbitration process.
The State Board of Elections is responsible for administering the statewide general election ballot question in November 2026 for voter adoption or rejection of the proposed constitutional amendment.

MDOT oversees state transportation employees, including the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department and MDTA personnel covered under Title 3 collective bargaining, with specific carve-outs and arbitration procedures preserved in the bill.

The OAG provides legal advice to the Governor, DBM, and state agencies regarding the implementation of binding arbitration, collective bargaining statutory interpretations, and the ballot question language for the constitutional amendment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for residential property tax payment deferrals in Anne Arundel County. Applies the deferral to permanently and totally disabled homeowners who qualify for federal benefits as service members. Includes members of reserve components, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service. Requires qualifying homeowners to have resided in the dwelling for at least five consecutive years. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: permanently and totally disabled homeowners in Anne Arundel County who are service members, including members of reserve components, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County property tax revenues may experience a potential minimal decrease during deferral periods depending on participation, with revenues recouped upon repayment. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands property tax payment deferral eligibility in Anne Arundel County for disabled individuals by broadening the definition from United States armed forces to service members, including reserve components, NOAA, and the Public Health Service. DVMF is responsible for assisting and advocating for Maryland service members, veterans, and their families regarding benefits and resources.

The bill amends eligibility criteria related to permanent and total disability qualifications for residential property tax payment deferrals in Anne Arundel County, touching upon state policies and relief options available to individuals with disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes statutory annual salary schedules for the Comptroller, the Treasurer, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of State. Sets salaries for the Comptroller, Treasurer, and Attorney General at $175,000 for terms beginning in January 2027. Increases those three salaries to $180,000 in the second and third years and $185,000 in the fourth year. Sets the Secretary of State's salary at $120,000 in 2027, increasing to $128,000 by the fourth year. Applies salary adjustments to terms of office beginning January 2027 in accordance with constitutional requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer; Maryland Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: The Comptroller of Maryland, the Maryland State Treasurer, the Attorney General of Maryland, and the Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,800 in FY 2028, growing to $43,000 in FY 2031 to cover statutory salary and fringe benefit increases for the four constitutional officers. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the Comptroller for the term beginning in January 2027.
HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the State Treasurer for the term beginning in January 2027.
HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the Attorney General for the term beginning in January 2027.
HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the Secretary of State for the term of appointment beginning in January 2027.

As the State's principal budget and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for managing executive branch salary schedules, fringe benefits, and incorporating general fund expenditure increases into future state budgets.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill implements the formal recommendations submitted by the Governor's Salary Commission regarding constitutional officer compensation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland to receive an annual stipend in addition to annual salary.
