Permits a judge serving as an administrative judge for a circuit court or the District Court to receive the stipend. Alters the minimum annual salary of the Chairman of the State Workers' Compensation Commission. Requires the Chairman's salary to at least equal the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; State Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland, administrative judges of the circuit courts and District Court, and the Chairman of the State Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Workers' Compensation Commission special fund expenditures increase by $22,300 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to align the Chairman's salary with that of the Chief Judge of the District Court. Fiscal impacts of judicial administrative stipends are accounted for under separate enacted joint resolutions. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by authorizing annual stipends for the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland and judges serving as administrative judges for a circuit court or the District Court, whose administrative and financial operations are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill directly modifies the compensation structure for the Chairman of the State Workers' Compensation Commission to equal at least the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court, resulting in an annual increase in special fund expenditures of approximately $22,300 beginning in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a qualified organization to hold a gaming permit whenever operating a gaming device in St. Mary's County. Defines a gaming device as a mechanism for playing a game of chance, excluding slot machines. Requires the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to designate a person to administer gaming permit issuance. Authorizes the County Commissioners to adopt regulations in consultation with the designee to administer and enforce the permits. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified organizations operating gaming devices in St. Mary's County, including volunteer fire companies and bona fide religious, fraternal, civic, war veterans', and charitable organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. St. Mary's County can administer permits and enforce provisions with existing resources, and county revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's regulatory body for gaming operations, the Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency tracks gaming policy in the state, although the permitting and administration under this bill are delegated directly to St. Mary's County.

Under current law in this subtitle, Maryland State Police officers are authorized along with local law enforcement to inspect records of gaming devices and proceeds held by qualified organizations in the county.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires property improvements for shoreline erosion protection to consist of living shorelines or nonstructural measures unless demonstrated infeasible. Directs the Department of the Environment to adopt waiver regulations and develop a scoring system for evaluating waiver requests. Requires the Department to conduct site visits within 45 days upon owner request during waiver reviews. Requires the Department to notify local soil conservation districts and provide an opportunity for recommendations on waiver requests. Directs the Department to engage stakeholders on waiver alterations and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Riparian and waterfront property owners, local soil conservation districts, and marine contractors and businesses involved in shoreline stabilization projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MDE can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State and local expenditures for shoreline stabilization projects may increase beginning in fiscal 2027. MDE special fund revenues from application fees may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 if more structural projects are pursued. Specific dollar amounts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for administering the living shorelines and nonstructural shoreline stabilization regulations, developing and publishing a waiver evaluation scoring system, conducting site visits upon request, notifying local soil conservation districts, leading stakeholder engagement, and reporting progress to the General Assembly.
The bill amends and replaces provisions in the Natural Resources Article and requires MDE to consult with DNR in adopting regulations related to shoreline stabilization and waiver procedures.

The bill mandates that MDE provide local soil conservation districts with written notice and the opportunity to make recommendations on waiver requests. Local soil conservation districts coordinate closely with and are overseen through agricultural conservation programs under MDA.

The Board of Public Works possesses statutory authority over State wetlands licenses (often delegated to MDE), is referenced in the underlying tidal wetlands statute, and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of self-service storage rental agreements to include electronic agreements. Prohibits occupants from using a self-service storage facility beyond the lease term after receiving nonrenewal notice. Requires operators to give occupants at least 30 days and until term end to remove property. Authorizes operators to dispose of remaining personal property after providing at least 10 days' notice. Requires a second notice by verified mail when an emailed notice receives no confirmation within five days. Requires rental agreements to include a statement advising occupants to remove property upon nonrenewal.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of self-service storage facilities, and occupants renting space in self-service storage facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces Maryland's consumer protection laws under the Commercial Law Article and served as an information source regarding the bill's changes to self-service storage rental agreements, notices, and disposal procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact to create an expedited pathway for multistate podiatric licensure. Authorizes an eligible podiatrist to obtain an expedited license to practice podiatric medicine in member states. Requires applicants to meet specified examination, education, residency, certification, and criminal background check standards. Establishes the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission to administer compact operations and promulgate binding rules. Requires member boards to report disciplinary actions and share investigative information through a coordinated database. Conditions Maryland's participation on the enactment of substantially similar legislation in four other states.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners; Maryland Department of Health; Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Podiatrists seeking expedited multistate licensure, podiatric patients in Maryland and member states, and the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and revenues for the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners likely increase by an indeterminate amount upon entry into the compact due to annual commission assessments, coordinated database requirements, and expedited license application fees. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts an interstate licensure compact governing podiatrists, directly impacting the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners housed within MDH. The department is directly responsible for notifying the Department of Legislative Services once four states enact similar legislation, and BPME will handle the licensure requirements, database reporting, background checks, and associated special fund revenue/expenditures.

The bill creates Maryland's membership in a new multistate compact and interstate body, the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission, which falls directly under the collective classification of interstate compacts and commissions in which Maryland participates.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to MDH and its licensing boards. The bill specifically requires the approval of the Attorney General or appropriate legal counsel regarding the legal defense of Interstate Commission representatives in civil liability actions.

The Interstate Commission must submit annual reports and financial statements to the Governor, and the Governor receives official statutory notices regarding any member state defaults, terminations, or withdrawals from the compact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters voter registration qualifications for legal counsel appointed or retained by a local board of elections. Authorizes each local board of elections to appoint or retain counsel who is a registered voter of the State. Removes the requirement that board counsel must reside as a registered voter in the board's specific county. Maintains the requirement that counsel must be admitted to practice law in Maryland. Takes effect immediately upon enactment as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Local boards of elections and Maryland-admitted attorneys seeking appointment as board counsel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections oversees the administration of election laws and the activities of local boards of elections throughout the state. This bill alters the statutory qualifications required for counsel appointed or retained by local boards of elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum number of registered cannabis agents a micro dispensary may employ from 10 to 20. Extends the authorization for converted medical cannabis dispensaries to deliver medical cannabis until July 1, 2027. Renames the responsible vendor training program as the cannabis agent training program. Requires registered cannabis agents and on-site consumption employees to complete training within 90 days and every two years. Directs the Maryland Cannabis Administration to adopt regulations specifying core training curriculum elements. Requires the Administration to prioritize previously approved programs when reviewing cannabis agent training applications.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: micro dispensary licensees, converted medical cannabis dispensary licensees, registered cannabis agents, on-site consumption establishment employees, and cannabis training program providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 622 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA). It directly impacts MCA's regulatory operations by requiring the agency to adopt regulations for cannabis agent training programs, prioritize previously approved training programs, oversee updated employee caps for micro dispensaries, and manage the extension of delivery authorizations for medical cannabis dispensaries.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Purple Star Colleges Program to recognize colleges that provide strong services and support for military-connected students. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to administer the program and adopt implementing regulations. Requires participating colleges to designate a uniformed services liaison and establish a dedicated resource webpage. Requires qualifying colleges to maintain student-led transition programs and offer staff professional development. Alters the definition of military-connected student under the Purple Star Schools Program. Defines college to include institutions of higher education and private career schools.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Military-connected students (including active service members, veterans, and their spouses and dependents), public and private institutions of higher education, and private career schools.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $43,800 in FY 2027 and $46,400 in FY 2028 for the Maryland Higher Education Commission to hire a contractual half-time program manager. Public institutions of higher education, Baltimore City Community College, and local community colleges may incur voluntary, absorbable operational costs if seeking designation. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing and administering the Purple Star Colleges Program, adopting regulations, setting criteria, reviewing applications, and designating colleges.
Identical listing for MHEC, which serves as the primary agency responsible for administering and regulating the Purple Star Colleges Program.
MSDE oversees the Purple Star Schools Program, and the bill amends the statutory definition of 'military-connected student' under this existing program.
DVMF advocates for and supports veterans, active-duty service members, and their families, aligning closely with the bill's focus on military-connected students and collegiate support services.
USM member institutions are public higher education institutions eligible to voluntarily seek Purple Star College designation by meeting required support service and staffing criteria.
As a public university, Morgan State may elect to participate in the program and seek designation as a Purple Star College by providing the required military-connected student supports.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College is eligible to seek designation as a Purple Star College under the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that MHEC consult with the Maryland College Collaboration for Student Veterans Commission to adopt regulations carrying out the Purple Star Colleges Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires licensed hospitals, excluding State hospitals, to comply with certain staffing standards and establish a clinical staffing committee. Sets committee membership ratios of managers to employees based on whether a hospital has over 150 licensed beds. Requires each hospital's chief nurse executive to submit a draft clinical staffing plan to the committee. Directs the clinical staffing committee to finalize a clinical staffing plan that meets patient needs. Requires hospitals to implement the plan annually and assign patient care unit personnel starting July 1, 2028. Requires hospitals to provide the clinical staffing plan to staff upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Non-State licensed hospitals in Maryland, hospital administrators, hospital clinical staff, and hospital patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds staffing committee and staffing plan requirements to Title 19 of the Health - General Article for licensed Maryland hospitals, an industry regulated and licensed by the Maryland Department of Health. While State-operated hospitals are explicitly exempt from these requirements and there is no direct state fiscal impact, MDH oversees hospital licensing and regulatory compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers collection of annual Human–Relevant Research Fund contributions from the Maryland Department of Health to the Department of Agriculture. Requires Maryland research facilities submitting federal APHIS Form 7023 to pay annual contributions by January 15. Establishes tiered contribution amounts from $5,000 to $75,000 based on the reported number of animals. Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to distribute collected funds to the Human–Relevant Research Fund. Authorizes a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per day for noncompliance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Research facilities located in Maryland required to submit federal Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service Form 7023, higher education research institutions, and researchers seeking grants for animal testing alternatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Agriculture increase by $42,900 in FY 2027, rising to $54,200 by FY 2031, to hire one half-time administrative officer. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Technology Development Corporation continue and may increase with enhanced collection compliance. Local government and higher education finances have no material direct fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 625 designates the Department of Agriculture as the agency responsible for collecting annual contributions from qualifying animal research facilities, enforcing penalties for noncompliance, and distributing the collected funds to the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

The bill repeals the statutory provisions in the Health - General Article that tasked the Maryland Department of Health with collecting contributions from research facilities, thereby relieving MDH of this duty.

TEDCO administers the Human-Relevant Research Fund, which receives the contributions collected under the bill to fund research into alternatives to animal testing. Changes in collection effectiveness directly affect the fund's revenues and grant/loan expenditures.

Public higher education research institutions under USM that report animal research under USDA APHIS Form 7023 are subject to the required fee assessments, will submit payments to MDA instead of MDH, and are eligible to apply for grant and loan funding from the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to mandate specific police training curriculum across Maryland. Applies to entrance-level training and commission-determined in-service training at State, county, and municipal police training schools. Directs the curriculum to cover training regarding individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, and autism. Mandates instruction on locating wandering individuals, searching near water bodies, and using sensory-aware approaches. Includes training on reunification, documentation, and interagency coordination. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: State, county, and municipal police officers and trainees; State, county, and municipal police training schools; individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, or autism
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations. Local expenditures may experience a minimal increase to conduct additional training if local schools do not already provide it. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which establishes training standards and curriculums for law enforcement statewide, is housed within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency operating its own training academy, the Maryland State Police must incorporate the required curriculum on autism, dementia, and developmental disabilities into its entrance-level and in-service officer training programs.

The Department oversees the Maryland Natural Resources Police, whose sworn officers must complete police training programs that adhere to MPTSC standards, including the new training requirements for searching near water and locating missing individuals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires applicants seeking positions involving direct contact with children in certain child care facilities to undergo criminal history records checks. Mandates the Maryland State Department of Education to establish a centralized background check processing unit by June 30, 2027. Lowers the age threshold from three years to two years for probationary child care teacher qualification rules. Repeals the statutory cap on the number of Deputy State Superintendents of Schools. Requires the Department to review background check procedures and report findings by October 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants and volunteers seeking positions involving direct contact with children in child care facilities, child care center operators, and first-time child care teachers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education is anticipated to implement the bill's requirements with existing budgetary resources, resulting in minimal state fiscal impact. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency under the bill. It removes the statutory cap on Deputy State Superintendents, requires MSDE to establish a centralized unit by June 30, 2027 to manage child care background checks, alters probationary qualifications for child care teachers, and mandates a comprehensive review and report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references and relies upon DPSCS's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) to process and disseminate the criminal history records checks to MSDE's centralized unit, requiring ongoing operational coordination between the two agencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Secretary of Health to issue clinical recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services. Mandates a 30-day comment period and health commission analysis before adopting certain non-immunization preventive recommendations. Authorizes licensed pharmacists to administer Secretary-recommended vaccines to individuals at least seven years old. Requires health insurance carriers to cover recommended preventive services and child wellness immunizations without cost sharing. Applies insurance coverage mandates to policies, contracts, and plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Care Commission; State Board of Pharmacy
qa_results.stakeholders: Insured individuals and families in Maryland, licensed pharmacists, health insurance carriers, and health care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in fiscal 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Form reviews and Department of Health workload will be handled with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Health to issue, publish, and distribute recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services, and directly expands the scope of vaccines pharmacists may administer based on the Secretary's determinations.

The Insurance Commissioner and MIA are responsible for enforcing health insurance coverage mandates and cost-sharing prohibitions updated by the Secretary of Health's recommendations, and MIA will experience a minimal special fund revenue increase from rate and form filings.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Health to obtain an impact analysis from the Maryland Health Care Commission pursuant to § 15-1501 of the Insurance Article before adopting recommendations for certain preventive services.
This is an Administration priority bill ('The Vax Act') introduced by request of the Governor to protect public health standards and preventive care access in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals multiple obsolete or unnecessary state boards, commissions, and reporting requirements across various state agencies. Eliminates the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board, the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care. Transfers renewable fuels credit certification and payment responsibilities directly to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Authorizes reasonable compensation and expense reimbursement for Interagency Council on Homelessness members who have experienced homelessness. Replaces specialized intervention service reports with annual third-grade literacy proficiency reporting by local school boards. Alters membership compositions, reporting deadlines, and term lengths for various statutory advisory bodies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Housing and Community Development; Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of affected state boards and commissions; certified ethanol and biodiesel producers; public school students requiring literacy support; individuals experiencing homelessness serving on the Interagency Council on Homelessness; state and local government agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on state or local finances; the bill is largely procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM requested this departmental bill as part of its Government Modernization Initiative to streamline executive branch efficiency by repealing obsolete boards, commissions, and mandated reporting requirements.

The bill repeals the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board and transfers all authority for certifying, approving, and administering renewable fuel tax credits directly to the Department of Agriculture, and removes the Secretary from the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council.

The bill repeals several MDH reporting mandates (hepatitis C, cancer registry, mental health registry), consolidates youth camp epinephrine reporting, alters minority health disparities reporting, shifts health preceptor tax credit reporting deadlines, compiles Pre-K notification reports, and removes the Secretary from several oversight bodies.

The bill replaces the specialized intervention services report with a new Grade 3 literacy proficiency reporting mandate, repeals reports on youth suicide prevention and the Geographic Cost of Education Index adjustment, and removes MSDE from the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee.

The bill repeals the Two-Generation Family Economic Security Commission and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care within DHS, eliminates the Multidisciplinary Alternative Response Advisory Council, alters the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, and modifies Pre-K enrollment reporting requirements.

The bill repeals the Partnership for Workforce Quality Advisory Board, alters member terms and staggering for the Maryland Life Sciences Advisory Board, modifies the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission membership and strategic planning duties, and removes Commerce from the Customer Council and Green Purchasing Committee.

The bill designates the Secretary of Housing and Community Development as Chair of the Interagency Council on Homelessness, removes term limits on the chair, authorizes DHCD to administer a compensation policy for council members with lived experience of homelessness, and alters reporting dates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, requiring the Secretary of DPSCS to operate the CJIS Central Repository without the advisory board, and alters Customer Council membership.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly repeals, restructures membership for, or alters reporting requirements of numerous state boards, advisory councils, and commissions across state government.
The bill repeals the requirement for DNR to publish on its website a list of park maintenance projects costing over $25,000 and repeals the annual report on nutria eradication.
The bill repeals the annual reporting requirement on the Oil Contaminated Site Environmental Cleanup Fund and alters the membership of the Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Citizens Oversight Committee.
The bill modifies the membership of the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee housed within the Transportation Article and adjusts agency representation on other interagency bodies.
The bill repeals the annual statutory reporting requirement for the Maryland Department of Labor regarding voter registration efforts at one-stop career centers.

The bill directly implements efficiency recommendations spearheaded by the Government Modernization Initiative, an effort established in coordination with GOPI to eliminate government waste, redundancy, and unnecessary mandates.

The bill modifies gubernatorial appointment structures and terms (such as for the Maryland Life Sciences Advisory Board and Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Oversight Committee) and adjusts reporting requirements to the Governor.

The bill updates statutory citations and requires MHCC to continue analyzing information for the Health Care Disparities Policy Report Card published by MDH's Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership of the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board, which is established and housed within GOCPP.
The bill alters the statutory deadline from January 31 to March 1 for MDH to report to the Comptroller on tax credit certificates issued for medical preceptor programs.
The bill adjusts the membership and statutory references for the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council involving the MCA Director and social equity office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes alternative pathways to certified public accountant licensure based on educational attainment and practical work experience. Extends the maximum timeframe to obtain required practical work experience from three years to six years. Repeals the statutory 120-semester-hour examination requirement and the 150-semester-hour licensure requirement. Authorizes licensure with a master's degree or a bachelor's degree plus 30 semester credits and 2,000 hours of experience. Authorizes licensure with a bachelor's degree in accounting and 4,000 hours of practical work experience.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
qa_results.stakeholders: certified public accountant license applicants, certified public accountants, and accounting firms
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill with existing resources. Special fund revenues may increase minimally to the extent additional individuals apply for licensure. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, which oversees the occupational licensing and regulation of certified public accountants. The Department of Labor is responsible for implementing the bill's altered educational and experiential pathways for CPA licensure.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the qualifying age from 65 to 60 for the uniform redetermination process for energy assistance programs. Requires the Office of Home Energy Programs to update the redetermination process annually. Aligns state redetermination eligibility with federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program reporting standards for older adults. Streamlines the enrollment process for eligible energy customers aged 60 to 64. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Home Energy Programs; Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible energy assistance customers aged 60 and older, particularly those aged 60 to 64; local administering agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Human Services and local administering agencies can handle administrative changes using existing budgeted resources. Total program funding is not directly affected, though an increase in participating households could lead to downward adjustments in benefit amounts to remain within available funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS requested this departmental legislation and houses the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is directly responsible for administering energy assistance programs and implementing the uniform redetermination process for eligible older adults.

The bill expands streamlined enrollment and redetermination protections to individuals aged 60 to 64, directly aligning with the population of older adults served and advocated for by the Department of Aging.
MEA oversees state energy policy and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which partially funds the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) accessed through OHEP.
PSC regulates public electric and gas utilities whose low-income residential customers participate in the energy assistance programs affected by the redetermination process.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum Program Open Space funds transferable to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund to $9,000,000. Authorizes the Authority to award grants and loans for the management of certified heritage areas. Authorizes the Authority to require matching funds in whatever proportion the Authority considers appropriate. Repeals statutory 50% limits on project costs covered by certified heritage area grants. Alters the operating expense cap for transferred funds to up to 7% or $600,000, whichever is greater.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Heritage Areas Authority; Maryland Department of Planning; Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Local jurisdictions and entities managing certified heritage areas, Maryland Department of Planning personnel, and businesses supporting heritage area projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on overall State finances, but redirects up to $6.0 million annually from Program Open Space State land acquisition to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund beginning in FY 2027. Redirected funds cover two new Maryland Historical Trust positions totaling $202,318 in FY 2027. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase from additional grant and loan awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA) and the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) are housed within the Department of Planning, which directly administers the Maryland Heritage Areas Program, receives operating expense allowances under the fund, and requires additional personnel to manage the expanded grant funding.

Program Open Space (POS) is administered by DNR. The bill directly impacts DNR by increasing the transfer of POS State share funding to the MHAA Financing Fund by up to $6 million annually, redirecting funds away from State land acquisition and capital improvements on DNR land.

The bill redirects up to an additional $6 million from the State's share of Program Open Space funds designated under statute for recreation and open space purposes shared by DNR and the Historic St. Mary's City Commission.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to invest and reinvest moneys in the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund and credit investment earnings back to the fund.
DBM oversees the State budget and budget amendments authorizing the transfer of Program Open Space funds to the MHAA Financing Fund and reviewed the legislation as a contributing agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the per capita minimum funding calculation for the State Library Resource Center beginning in fiscal year 2028. Maintains the allocation at $2.07 per State resident through fiscal year 2027. Raises the allocation incrementally from $2.17 per resident in fiscal year 2028 to $2.64 per resident in fiscal year 2032 and thereafter. Requires the Center to use these funds for operating and capital expenses. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State Library Resource Center (Central Library of the Enoch Pratt Free Library System), local public library systems, and Maryland library patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $628,856 in FY 2028, rising to $2,817,159 in FY 2031 due to the mandated per-resident funding increase and projected population growth. State revenues are not affected. Local library systems benefit programmatically, but local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency coordinates the State Library Network and administers state funding for public library systems, including the State Library Resource Center and the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled, both of which are directly impacted by the bill's funding formula changes.

The bill creates an increased statutory mandated general fund appropriation starting in FY 2028, which the Department of Budget and Management must incorporate into state budget planning and execution.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor annually to proclaim the month of January as Muslim American Heritage Month. Requires the Governor annually to proclaim the month of May as Jewish American Heritage Month. Recognizes the contributions that Muslim Americans and Jewish Americans have made to the State. Requires both proclamations to urge educational and cultural organizations to observe the months properly. Specifies that observances include appropriate programs, ceremonies, and activities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Muslim Americans and Jewish Americans in Maryland; educational and cultural organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Governor to annually proclaim the month of January as Muslim American Heritage Month and the month of May as Jewish American Heritage Month.

The office oversees faith-based and ethnic/cultural commissions and community engagement, making it relevant to supporting and coordinating activities for the designated commemorative heritage months.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to report semiannually to the General Assembly starting July 1, 2026. Mandates reporting on changes in federal environmental policy deemed legally valid by final federal court decisions. Includes changes impacting motor vehicle or stationary source emissions, federally delegated authority, or nuclear power. Requires the Department to detail the steps the State is taking in response to each change. Mandates that the initial report cover changes occurring since January 1, 2024. Terminates the reporting requirement after three years on May 31, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of the Environment, the Maryland General Assembly, and entities subject to federal environmental and greenhouse gas emissions regulations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can fulfill the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 663 directly tasks the Department of the Environment (MDE) with monitoring and submitting semiannual reports to the General Assembly regarding legally valid changes in federal environmental policy and detailing the State's response to those changes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the alcoholic beverages license quota in Cecil County to apply exclusively to Class A licenses. Prohibits the Board from issuing more than one Class A license for every 2,000 registered voters or major fraction. Authorizes the Board to issue not fewer than two Class A licenses in each election district. Prohibits counting any other class of license in the computation of the aggregate quota. Requires the quota to be computed and applied separately for each election district.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Cecil County
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for and holders of Class A alcoholic beverages licenses in Cecil County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Cecil County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for the statewide regulation of the alcoholic beverages industry. While this bill specifically alters retail Class A license quotas administered locally by the Cecil County Board of License Commissioners, it touches the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person in St. Mary’s County from standing in certain roadways, shoulders, median dividers, or intersections. Applies to locations determined by the county or a municipal corporation to be inherently dangerous. Requires local authorities to consult with the State Highway Administration when evaluating State roadways. Prohibits police officers from issuing citations unless conforming warning signs are installed. Requires State Highway Administration approval before local authorities install signs on State highways.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: pedestrians in St. Mary’s County; drivers and vehicle passengers in St. Mary’s County; law enforcement officers in St. Mary’s County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or St. Mary’s County operations or finances. The State Highway Administration can implement the bill's consultation and sign-approval provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires St. Mary's County or its municipalities to consult with the State Highway Administration (SHA) to determine whether a State roadway is inherently dangerous, comply with SHA traffic control device manuals for signage, and obtain SHA approval before installing signs on State highways.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the State Highway Administration, which has direct statutory responsibilities for consultation, standard-setting, and sign approval under the bill.

The Maryland State Police enforce traffic and motor vehicle laws on State highways, including in St. Mary's County, and are directly subject to the bill's restrictions prohibiting police officers from issuing citations unless specified signage conditions are met.
The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for fiscal analysis as the judicial branch would process any contested traffic citations issued pursuant to this new prohibition.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates an annual budget appropriation of at least $2,000,000 for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman. Funding begins in fiscal year 2027. Draws this funding from money remitted by Medicaid managed care organizations in the second immediately preceding fiscal year. Requires a general fund appropriation for the difference if remitted funds total less than $2,000,000. Specifies that appropriated funds must supplement and not supplant funding otherwise provided for the office.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman; Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: residents of long-term care facilities; local area agencies on aging; Medicaid managed care organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2028 to fulfill the mandated appropriation or backfill Medicaid funding. In addition, up to $2.0 million in special fund expenditures shift annually from the Maryland Department of Health to the Maryland Department of Aging, resulting in no net change in special funds. Local area agencies on aging may experience increased revenues and expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman is established within the Department of Aging, and the bill mandates an annual appropriation of at least $2,000,000 to fund the office's operations.

The required funding is derived from medical loss ratio (MLR) remittances paid by Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs) to the Department of Health, shifting up to $2,000,000 in funds away from MDH Medicaid reimbursements.
DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and must incorporate the bill's mandated annual appropriation and manage the required general and special fund allocations.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include at least $2,000,000 in the annual state budget bill for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters eligibility requirements for grants awarded from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund. Limits grant recipients to nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations conducting pediatric cancer research. Removes grant eligibility for physicians, laboratories, and individual persons. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, nonprofit research organizations, and formerly eligible physicians, laboratories, and individuals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the change in grant eligibility is technical in nature and does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund is housed within and administered by the Secretary of the Maryland Department of Health, which adopts regulations and oversees the distribution of research grants under the amended eligibility criteria.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Pediatric Cancer Research Commission, established under § 20-121 of the Health - General Article, oversees the evaluation, ranking, and awarding of competitive pediatric cancer research grants and will have to align its grant application criteria with the altered eligibility standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands civil immunity protections regarding the transfer and receipt of certain unclaimed human remains. Protects licensed funeral establishments, registered reduction operators, and crematory permit holders acting in good faith from civil liability. Covers transferring unclaimed cremains, hydrolyzed remains, or soil remains of veterans or eligible dependents to veterans service organizations. Protects veterans service organizations acting in good faith from civil liability for receiving those unclaimed remains. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Office of Cemetery Oversight; State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors
qa_results.stakeholders: registered reduction operators, licensed funeral establishments, crematory permit holders, veterans service organizations, veterans, and eligible dependents of veterans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected, with no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which regulates crematories, reduction facilities, and registered reduction operators under the Business Regulation Article referenced in the bill.

The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which regulates licensed funeral establishments and jointly regulates reduction facilities and crematory permit holders.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families oversees veterans' cemeteries and receives unclaimed remains of eligible veterans or dependents when veterans service organizations do not take possession.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to provide civil immunity from liability for qualifying transfers and receipts of remains, which directly affects tort claims filed in state courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain employees at seven Maryland Department of Health facilities to join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System. Covers individuals serving as CAMH Specialist I – CI and CAMH Specialist II – CI on or after July 1, 2026. Permits affected members with 20 combined years of eligibility service to retire with normal service retirement benefits. Directs the Board of Trustees to transfer prior service credit from the Employees' Pension System or Employees' Retirement System. Allows members with pre-July 1, 2008 pension credit to opt out of the service transfer by June 1, 2027. Requires the board to grant the higher ordinary disability benefit calculated under either applicable retirement system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals employed as CAMH Specialist I – CI or CAMH Specialist II – CI at seven specified Maryland Department of Health facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the bill affects a very limited number of employees (approximately 12 positions). No effect on revenues, local finances, or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS). The bill requires the agency to manage the transfer of service credit, process election forms for affected members, and calculate retirement and disability benefits under the revised statutory provisions.

The bill directly modifies retirement system membership for specific Maryland Department of Health employees (CAMH Specialist I and II classifications at specified state health facilities), making their membership in CORS a mandatory condition of employment.

As the state's central personnel agency overseeing state employee job classifications, benefits, and fiscal planning, DBM is affected by changes governing retirement system enrollment and benefits for state positions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund to be the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund. Mandates annual budget appropriations for grants to eligible local management boards for fiscal years 2028 through 2031. Requires funding for fiscal years 2028 through 2030 to at least equal the fiscal year 2027 appropriation. Requires an additional $500,000 above the fiscal year 2030 funding level for fiscal year 2031. Specifies that grant money must supplement rather than supplant existing funding for eligible local management boards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office for Children; Children's Cabinet
qa_results.stakeholders: eligible local management boards; children, youth, and families receiving interagency services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in FY 2031 to fulfill the mandated appropriation to the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund. Local revenues and expenditures for local management boards increase by $500,000 in FY 2031 from additional grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office for Children serves as the fiscal agent for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and staffs the Children's Cabinet, which administers the fund and awards grants to Local Management Boards.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for developing the annual state budget and overseeing budget execution, which is directly impacted by the bill's statutory mandated appropriations to the fund for fiscal years 2028 through 2031.
The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2031.
The bill amends the Education Article to conform statutory cross-references to the newly renamed Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund, with which the department collaborates on rate-setting processes.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to conform statutory cross-references to the renamed Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund regarding funds used to provide services to children with disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil and criminal fine or penalty Baltimore City may establish from $1,000 to $5,000. Applies this cap to violations of any ordinance, rule, or regulation established by the city. Retains the provision specifying that imprisonment may not exceed 12 months. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and property owners who violate Baltimore City ordinances, rules, or regulations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent that higher civil or criminal fines and penalties are imposed and collected. City expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state court system, including the District Court and Circuit Court, which handle contested civil citations and criminal ordinance violations originating from Baltimore City. While the fiscal note indicates no material fiscal impact on state operations, the judiciary was consulted regarding potential court impacts resulting from altered penalty structures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes Class GC golf course licenses and sports activity venue alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue licenses to qualifying nine-hole golf courses and commercial sports facilities. Permits license holders to sell designated alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption Monday through Sunday without a Sunday permit. Sets the annual license fee at $1,200 for full-service licenses and $740 for beer and wine licenses. Requires sports venue licensees to serve prepared food, certify servers in alcohol awareness, and implement consumption monitoring policies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of qualifying golf courses and commercial sports activity venues in Anne Arundel County, their employees, and venue patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase beginning in FY 2027 to the extent new licenses are issued at annual fees of $740 or $1,200. Specific revenue totals are unavailable. State finances and Anne Arundel County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers state sales taxes. While the bill specifically establishes local alcoholic beverages licenses administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates generally to the state's alcoholic beverages statutory framework under the Comptroller's broader regulatory subject area.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers to notify enrollees when primary care or behavioral health providers are terminated. Extends transitional care rights to eligible behavioral health patients for up to 90 days after termination. Mandates that carriers notify the Insurance Commissioner at least 60 days before certain provider network terminations. Requires carriers and health systems to adhere to contract terms for 90 days following contract termination or nonrenewal. Establishes a 90-day special enrollment period for individual market enrollees whose regular treating provider is terminated.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health systems, hospitals, primary care and behavioral health providers, and individual health insurance enrollees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Additional workload for the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties of up to $5,000 per day for failure to timely file access plan updates. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary implementing agency for this departmental legislation. The bill establishes notification requirements to the Insurance Commissioner for material changes to provider networks, authorizes the Commissioner to assess daily fines for late updates, and requires the Commissioner to develop a uniform form for enrollee requests for transitional care.

MHBE operates the Individual Exchange (Maryland Health Connection) and is directly affected by the statutory requirement establishing a new 90-day special enrollment period for enrollees whose regular providers are terminated from their plan's network.

MDH oversees health care facilities, health systems, and Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs), which are subject to carrier provider panel notification and transitional care standards. The bill also adds a compliance section directly into the Health - General Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers regulatory oversight of crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors. Requires individuals and business entities operating crematories or reduction facilities to obtain registrations and permits from the Board. Increases maximum civil penalties to $10,000 per violation and $1,000 per day for continuing violations. Alters Board quorum standards, member removal grounds, and disciplinary appeal procedures. Mandates the Board to employ at least two inspectors and create a permanent inspector position by fiscal 2028. Directs the Board to convene a stakeholder workgroup and submit recommendations by December 31, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors; Office of Cemetery Oversight
qa_results.stakeholders: crematory operators, reduction facility operators, funeral directors, morticians, registered cemeterians, and consumers of death care services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors special fund expenditures increase by at least $101,200 in FY 2027 to hire an additional inspector, with ongoing personnel costs in future years. Board special fund fee revenues increase by an indeterminate amount, while Office of Cemetery Oversight special fund revenues decrease by approximately $6,000 biennially beginning in FY 2027. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors is a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill transfers full regulatory authority over crematories and reduction facilities to the Board, requires the Board to employ inspectors, establishes new registration and permit systems, and incurs operational and fiscal impacts on the Board's special fund.

The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill removes regulatory oversight of crematories and reduction facilities from OCO, transfers duties and records to the Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, alters the OCO Advisory Council composition, and results in a loss of special fund revenue for OCO.

The bill mandates the creation of a new state Position Identification Number (PIN) beginning in fiscal year 2028 for a full-time inspector position within the Board, requiring coordination with DBM regarding personnel and state budget allocations.
The bill amends statutory standards and grounds under which the Governor may remove appointed members of the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors.

The bill repeals Business Regulation Section 5-803 and updates statutory references concerning the transfer of unclaimed cremated and reduction remains of veterans to the Department of Veterans and Military Families.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits data controllers from knowingly selling consumer personal data to governmental units that recently engaged in civil immigration enforcement. Limits controller and processor compliance with subpoenas or law enforcement cooperation concerning immigration enforcement without a valid warrant. Requires public record custodians to take reasonable steps to determine whether persons seek records to enforce immigration law. Directs custodians to deny inspection of personal information, photographs, and facial recognition searches for immigration enforcement without a warrant. Extends law enforcement database access bans and verification requirements to message switching systems. Requires governmental entities to develop and publish procedures preventing the sale and redisclosure of sensitive data.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Department of State Police; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Information Technology; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents and consumers, commercial data controllers and processors, public records custodians, state and local law enforcement agencies, and government agencies seeking access to records or personal data.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase significantly for the Judiciary to implement operational procedures, additional staff, or programming changes to determine the purpose of data requests. Local government expenditures may increase for certain custodians to scrutinize public records requests, but specific figures are unavailable. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is explicitly mandated under Public Safety § 3-529 to adopt regulations governing access to message switching systems and law enforcement databases, and under General Provisions § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding immigration-related data and facial recognition requests.

MVA is explicitly required under General Provisions § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and procedures restricting access to personal information and facial recognition searches for immigration enforcement, and to submit an annual report to the General Assembly tracking such requests.

MSP is specifically mandated under General Provisions § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and procedures governing immigration-related data and facial recognition requests, and to report annually on these requests to the General Assembly.

The fiscal note specifically highlights that the Judiciary/AOC faces a significant operational and expenditure impact because court records are publicly accessible, necessitating new procedures, programming, and potential staffing to screen all public record requests to determine if they are sought for immigration enforcement.

Under State Government § 10-1702, DoIT is statutorily designated to consult with every governmental entity in the state as they develop and publish procedures to prevent the sale and redisclosure of personal records and sensitive data.

The bill amends the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act enforced by the OAG's Consumer Protection Division, specifically authorizing the Division to post consumer education materials and enforce prohibitions on selling or disclosing personal data for immigration enforcement.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), which is subject to extensive regulatory, procedural, and reporting mandates under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City organizations affiliated with a professional National Football League team to conduct raffles. Extends the termination date for raffles affiliated with professional Major League Baseball teams to May 31, 2031. Requires organizations to obtain an annual written permit from a designated Baltimore City agency. Restricts football raffle sales to between 4.5 hours before kickoff and the third quarter. Mandates age-verification measures and geofencing to limit electronic ticket sales to a specified geographic area.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City designated agency; Baltimore City Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: organizations affiliated with Major League Baseball and National Football League teams in Baltimore City; attendees and raffle ticket purchasers at Baltimore home games
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, though lottery revenues may see a minor substitution effect. Baltimore City finances are not materially affected, and the Baltimore City Police Department can issue permits using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency oversees gaming policy in the state. The bill expands allowable raffle operations at professional sporting events in Baltimore City, and the fiscal note evaluates the potential substitution effects of these raffles on State lottery revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that State and higher education employee email systems must support State business and cannot serve as a public forum. Requires State units and public higher education governing boards to protect employee email services from spam email. Mandates the implementation of systems that automatically filter spam email from employee email accounts. Excludes from spam email bulk emails related to State business from vendors, partners, and exclusive representatives. Requires information technology policies to permit incidental personal use with de minimis resource impact consistent with professional norms. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Secretary of Information Technology; governing boards of public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees; public higher education employees; units of State government; public institutions of higher education; State vendors, partners, and exclusive representatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances because the bill generally codifies existing practice. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT and the Secretary of Information Technology are the primary regulatory authorities responsible for setting IT guidelines, reviewing and approving IT policies, standards, and plans submitted by State agencies and higher education institutions, and overseeing statewide email security and IT master planning.

The bill explicitly amends State law to apply IT plan requirements to USM, requiring its governing board to develop and submit IT policies, standards, and plans regarding email spam filtering and acceptable State business use to the Secretary of Information Technology.

The bill explicitly amends State law to bring Morgan State University under the IT plan and email security requirements of § 3.5-305, requiring its governing board to submit IT policies and plans to the Secretary of Information Technology.

The bill explicitly amends State law to include St. Mary's College of Maryland under the IT plan and email security requirements of § 3.5-305, requiring its governing board to submit IT policies and standards regarding email spam filtering to the Secretary of Information Technology.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for State government, DBM is affected by statewide policies governing employee IT usage norms, allowable incidental personal use of State email, and standards for conducting State business.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the June 30, 2030 deadline for awarding initial Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans Scholarships. Eliminates the restriction limiting post-2030 scholarship renewals to individuals who received an initial scholarship earlier. Authorizes the Maryland Higher Education Commission to award new and renewal scholarships indefinitely. Preserves scholarship eligibility for qualifying veterans, active service members, reservists, and their spouses and children. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident veterans, active duty service members, and activated reservists of the Afghanistan and Iraq conflicts, as well as their spouses, children, and stepchildren
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $750,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2031 to maintain the scholarship program beyond its former sunset date. No effect on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship program and the associated scholarship fund, which will now continue awarding initial scholarships beyond June 30, 2030.
As the state's central higher education coordinating board that manages state financial aid programs, it oversees the administration and ongoing operation of the scholarship program and fund.
DVMF advocates for Maryland veterans, active-duty service members, and their families, assisting them in accessing state educational benefits including this scholarship.

USM institutions enroll eligible scholarship recipients, and the statutory formula capping the maximum scholarship award is directly tied to tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at USM institutions.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold and maintain the special, nonlapsing Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.
The Comptroller has a statutory duty to account for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands educational benefits, scholarship eligibility, and employment preferences to spouses of active service members and certain veterans. Requires public institutions of higher education to grant course priority registration to eligible spouses and certain veterans. Requires community colleges to include veterans' spouses in specialized advising services and campus resource centers. Authorizes senatorial and Delegate scholarships for out-of-state study to be awarded to spouses of active service members. Expands State personnel test credits and sanitary commission hiring preferences to include additional eligible veterans and spouses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public institutions of higher education; community colleges; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Department of Budget and Management; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Spouses of active service members; spouses of veterans; veterans with other than dishonorable discharges; students at Maryland public institutions of higher education and community colleges; applicants for State and local government employment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not materially affected and implementation costs can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM administers the State Personnel Management System and must update the JobAps system, testing guides, and administrative materials to implement the expanded definition of eligible veterans and military spouses for selection test credits.

MHEC coordinates statewide postsecondary education policies and administers state financial aid programs, including the senatorial and delegate scholarships whose eligibility criteria are expanded to include spouses of active service members domiciled in Maryland.
The bill amends the Public Utilities Article to authorize hiring and promotion preferences for spouses of active service members and adjusts the discharge criteria for eligible veterans.
USM institutions are public institutions of higher education that must adopt policies and grant priority course registration to eligible service members, qualifying veterans, and their spouses.
As an independent public university, Morgan State must adopt policies granting priority registration to eligible service members, qualifying veterans, and their spouses.
As an independent public honors college, St. Mary's must establish policies to grant priority course registration to eligible service members, veterans, and military spouses.

DVMF is the primary state agency responsible for assisting Maryland's veterans, active service members, and their families in securing benefits, higher education access, and support services impacted by this legislation.
The bill amends provisions in the Labor and Employment Article regarding hiring and promotion preferences for veterans and military spouses by private and local employers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters membership criteria for Class C veterans' organization alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. Requires eligible organizations to consist only of individuals who served in the uniformed services. Expands eligibility to veterans of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service. Repeals the requirement that members must have served during a war. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: veterans' organizations and clubs in Anne Arundel County and their members, including veterans of the uniformed services, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Local government finances and operations in Anne Arundel County are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers relevant provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, though local retail licenses in Anne Arundel County are handled by the local board of license commissioners.

The bill updates criteria for veterans' organizations to align with the broader definition of uniformed services (including NOAA and PHS) and removes wartime service restrictions, which touches on the community and advocacy scope of veterans' affairs in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the timeframe for the Securities Commissioner to bring franchise enforcement actions from three years to five years. Modifies the statute of limitations for franchisee civil liability claims against franchisors. Prohibits franchisors from restricting franchisees from joining trade associations or freely associating for lawful purposes. Authorizes franchisees to sue in circuit court for injunctive relief, damages, and attorney's fees for association violations. Establishes the Maryland Franchise Disclosure Document Renewal Fast-Track Review Pilot Program through September 30, 2032. Requires the Securities Commissioner to report on the pilot program by September 30, 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Securities Commissioner in the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Franchisees, franchisors, and prospective franchise buyers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $305,500 in FY 2027 to hire three staff positions in the Office of the Attorney General, rising to $413,400 by FY 2031; costs may potentially be mitigated by the Securities Act Registration Fund. Revenues are not materially affected. Local governments experience no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law is administered and enforced by the Securities Commissioner within the Office of the Attorney General. The bill expands the Commissioner's enforcement timeline, mandates the creation and administration of the Maryland Franchise Disclosure Document Renewal Fast-Track Review Pilot Program, imposes extensive reporting requirements on the office, and results in a direct fiscal impact requiring additional staff positions and general fund expenditures.

The bill modifies the statute of limitations for civil liability lawsuits and creates a new private right of action permitting franchisees to sue in circuit court for injunctive relief, damages, and attorney's fees if their rights of association are violated, directly impacting the operations and caseload of the Maryland Judicial Branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Legalizes the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and its supplements. Applies to the extent that the code or supplements contain laws enacted by the General Assembly. Requires all Maryland courts and public officials to recognize the code as evidence of enacted law. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Government
