qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore County officials, Maryland state and local courts, legal practitioners, and Baltimore County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Baltimore County can likely handle code publication costs with existing budgeted resources. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that the legalized 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and its supplements must be recognized in all courts of the State as evidence of the public local laws enacted by the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the approval deadline for community solar energy generating systems qualifying for agricultural use property tax assessments to December 31, 2030. Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to issue preconstruction determinations upon application. Directs the Department to review completed applications within 90 days. Qualifies land receiving a favorable determination for agricultural use assessment for the succeeding taxable year under specified conditions. Authorizes the Department to rescind a preconstruction determination under specified circumstances. Authorizes the Department to charge an application fee to recover administrative costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: community solar energy developers and operators, agricultural landowners hosting agrivoltaic projects, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease in State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 depending on the number of qualifying systems placed in service. Administrative costs incurred by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation are expected to be offset by application fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly conditions eligibility for the agricultural use property tax assessment on whether a community solar energy generating system has been approved by the Public Service Commission under § 7–306.2 of the Public Utilities Article, extending that approval deadline from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030.

The board adjudicates appeals of property tax assessments and exemptions following decisions by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Disputes regarding agrivoltaic agricultural use assessments or preconstruction determinations under the bill could be appealed to local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative review body for real property assessment disputes originating from SDAT or the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, potentially hearing appeals concerning denied or rescinded agricultural use assessments for community solar projects.

qa_results.bill_summary: Delays implementation of the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program for Low-Income Families until tax year 2030. Extends the program's annual reporting requirements and statutory termination date through December 31, 2035. Requires the Comptroller's Office to study outreach efforts that encourage eligible taxpayers to claim the credit. Requires the Department of Service and Civic Innovation to study how Maryland Corps participants might assist low-income residents. Mandates that both agencies submit their study findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller's Office; Department of Service and Civic Innovation
qa_results.stakeholders: low-income Maryland taxpayers eligible for the State earned income tax credit; employers subject to employee tax credit notification duties; Maryland Corps participants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Delays State general fund and local income tax revenue reductions associated with increased earned income tax credit claims under the program. The Comptroller's Office and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation can complete the required studies and reports using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program, which is delayed by five years under this bill. Additionally, the Comptroller's Office is mandated to conduct a comprehensive study on outreach efforts to eligible taxpayers and submit a report with recommendations by December 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Service and Civic Innovation to conduct a study and make recommendations regarding how Maryland Corps participants can assist low-income Marylanders in claiming the EITC and other family-serving credits, with a report due by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Transfer-on-Death Deed Act to authorize nontestamentary real property transfers effective at the transferor's death. Allows an owner to convey real property to designated beneficiaries through a recorded transfer-on-death deed without consideration. Authorizes the transferor to revoke a recorded transfer-on-death deed before death through subsequent recorded instruments or deeds. Exempts transfer-on-death deeds for a primary or secondary residence from recordation and State and county transfer taxes. Requires recording disclaimers of real property interests in the land records of the county where the property sits. Applies retroactively to deeds executed before October 1, 2026, if the transferor dies on or after that date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Administrative Office of the Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland real property owners, designated transfer-on-death deed beneficiaries, and estate planning attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $15,700 in FY 2027 for one-time Judiciary IT programming. General fund revenues may decrease minimally beginning in FY 2027 due to reduced probate fees and uncollected inheritance taxes. Special fund revenues for the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund may increase from recordation surcharges. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch and the clerks of the circuit court, who are responsible for recording transfer-on-death deeds, revocations, and notices of death, utilizing land record intake sheets provided by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC). The fiscal note identifies a direct expenditure increase of $15,700 for one-time judicial programming changes.

The bill allows real property to pass outside of the probate estate via transfer-on-death deeds, which directly impacts the administration of decedents' estates and is expected to decrease probate fee and inheritance tax revenues collected by the Registers of Wills.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $450,000 annually in the budget bill for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program. Mandates this appropriation for each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030. Directs the Governor to use federal funds to satisfy the requirement to the extent authorized under federal law. Requires county governing bodies and child care resource centers to jointly apply for and administer local program grants. Supports family child care providers with start-up assistance, technical support, and financial incentives.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: registered family child care providers, county governing bodies, child care resource centers, and families seeking child care
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Establishes a mandated appropriation of $450,000 annually for fiscal 2028 through 2030, to be funded with federal funds if authorized. State expenditures are not expected to be affected assuming historical level funding would have continued without the bill. Guarantees grant funding for participating local governments and child care resource centers in fiscal 2028 through 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program is housed within and administered by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which awards the grants and manages program implementation.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning, and the bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $450,000 for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
The bill explicitly requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of $450,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System for Dorchester County local detention center officers if the county participates. Grants affected officers eligibility and creditable service in the new system for previous Dorchester County employment. Terminates their membership and benefit rights in the Employees’ Pension System upon joining. Exempts these service credit transfers from standard statutory transfer rules and contribution rate differential payments. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Dorchester County
qa_results.stakeholders: Dorchester County local detention center officers and Dorchester County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. If Dorchester County elects to participate, its pension liabilities increase by $842,322. Due to an annual new entrant liability credit of $111,008 for 25 years, net local pension contributions increase by an estimated $36,748 annually beginning in FY 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency manages and administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes both the Employees' Pension System and the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS). The agency is directly responsible for executing the transfer of members, creditable service, and associated assets if Dorchester County participates in CORS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from imposing copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles for Collaborative Care Model services. Requires certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover Collaborative Care Model services. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study the impact of eliminating health insurance cost-sharing for these services. Requires the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2026. Applies the commercial coverage requirement to policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients; individuals enrolled in fully insured commercial health plans; primary care and behavioral health providers; health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. The Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from imposing copayment, coinsurance, or deductible requirements for services provided under the Collaborative Care Model to Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients.

Section 3 of the bill specifically mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct a study on the impact of eliminating health insurance cost-sharing for Collaborative Care Model services and submit a report with recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

The bill mandates coverage for Collaborative Care Model services across commercial health insurance carriers and HMOs, requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to regulate compliance and review policy rate and form filings.

As the administrator of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, the Department of Budget and Management was evaluated for fiscal impact regarding health coverage requirements for state employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities. Removes one Senate member and reduces House Health Committee representation from two members to one. Eliminates seats for the Health Facilities Association of Maryland and Voices for Quality Care. Adds one representative selected by LeadingAge Maryland. Requires the three assisted living industry representatives to represent specified facility sizes to the extent practicable.
qa_results.responsible_party: Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities, long-term care provider organizations, and health care advocacy groups
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory membership and composition of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees licensing and quality of care for nursing homes and assisted living facilities through the Office of Health Care Quality, and multiple MDH officials (Secretary, Director of OHCQ, and Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health) serve on the Oversight Committee.
The Secretary of Aging sits on the committee, and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (administered through the Department of Aging) is tasked with selecting local ombudsman and consumer members.
The Secretary of Disabilities or their designee serves as a designated statutory member on the Oversight Committee.
The Secretary of Human Services or their designee serves as a designated statutory member on the Oversight Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes new qualification pathways and ongoing timeframes for private prekindergarten educators on the career ladder. Allows teaching assistants holding high school diplomas to earn required credentials within three years or three months after hire. Removes the fixed 2024 cutoffs for educators qualifying through documented multi-year teaching experience. Requires lead teachers qualifying through experience by July 1, 2024, to earn an associate degree by July 1, 2030. Requires lead teachers qualifying through experience after July 1, 2024, to earn an associate degree within six months.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible private prekindergarten providers, early childhood teaching assistants, and prekindergarten lead teachers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact, as the Maryland State Department of Education oversees the career ladder within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary state agency responsible for establishing and overseeing the early childhood educator career ladder for eligible private prekindergarten providers, including setting credential and assessment criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from using force, threat of force, or physical obstruction to interfere with or physically injure another. Applies while the person lawfully exercises or attempts to exercise religious freedom at a place of religious worship. Grounds the protected exercise under the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution. Designates a violation of the prohibition as a misdemeanor. Subjects a convicted violator to imprisonment not exceeding 90 days, a fine not exceeding $1,000, or both.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals lawfully exercising religious freedom at places of religious worship; places of religious worship; individuals charged with criminal obstruction or interference
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal offense for obstructing or interfering with the exercise of religious beliefs at a place of worship, which will be filed, processed, and adjudicated within the Maryland District and Circuit Court systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the new misdemeanor offense carries a penalty of imprisonment of up to 90 days, the Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for providing legal representation to eligible indigent individuals charged under this statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages statewide correctional supervision, probation monitoring, and pretrial detention operations (such as in Baltimore City) for justice-involved individuals convicted of or charged with criminal offenses.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating violations of state criminal law and enforcing prohibitions against force or obstruction at places of religious worship.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's central coordinating body for public safety, crime reduction policies, and victim services, which encompasses strategies to address hate incidents and unlawful interference at places of worship.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from altering or tampering with a gift card or its packaging with the intent to defraud. Establishes the misdemeanor of gift card forgery, punishable by up to 18 months imprisonment, a $500 fine, or both. Applies provisions to open-loop gift cards and closed-loop gift cards, excluding credit cards, electronic funds transfers, and paper instruments. Establishes valuation rules for gift cards in theft crimes based on listed value, represented value, or incurred loss. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Consumers purchasing or using gift cards, retailers and payment card networks selling gift cards, and individuals charged with theft or fraud offenses involving gift cards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense of gift card forgery and alters the valuation standards for gift cards in theft prosecutions, impacting judicial caseloads and court proceedings administered by the Maryland Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new criminal misdemeanor punishable by up to 18 months imprisonment, which requires representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants charged with the offense.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is responsible for correctional facilities and community supervision (probation and parole) for justice-involved individuals sentenced under state criminal statutes, including the new misdemeanor penalties.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigates property crimes, fraud, and theft offenses, and will be tasked with enforcing the new criminal prohibition against gift card tampering and forgery.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals arising from convictions under Maryland theft and fraud statutes and oversees consumer protection initiatives related to retail fraud.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local governing bodies to withhold from tax sale dwellings of homeowners with a documented terminal illness or medical hardship. Directs county tax collectors to establish an application and biennial reapplication process for withholding these dwellings. Increases the maximum dwelling assessed value for Homeowner Protection Program eligibility from $300,000 to $450,000. Mandates priority enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program for homeowners experiencing a documented terminal illness or medical hardship. Requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to allow homeowners to designate a family member or representative to assist them.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners facing property tax sales, especially those with terminal illnesses or medical hardships, designated family representatives, county tax collectors, and private tax lien purchasers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and future repayment revenues from the Homeowner Protection Fund may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 due to expanded eligibility, though total appropriations remain unchanged. Local government revenues may be delayed or minimally reduced starting in fiscal 2027. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 753 explicitly requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to define 'terminal illness' and 'medical hardship' by regulation for the purposes of withholding qualifying homeowners' dwellings from tax sale.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the authorized hours of sale for Class B beer, wine, and liquor golf course licenses in Wicomico County. Authorizes license holders to sell alcoholic beverages starting at 7:00 a.m. instead of 10:00 a.m. daily. Permits sales on Monday through Saturday from 7:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. the following day. Permits sales on Sunday from 7:00 a.m. to midnight. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B beer, wine, and liquor golf course licensees in Wicomico County and golf course patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Wicomico County can handle any additional enforcement activities with existing resources, and county revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller has general regulatory oversight over the alcohol industry and taxation in Maryland. While this bill specifically alters the hours of sale for Class B golf course alcoholic beverage licenses in Wicomico County administered by the local board with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to the state's alcoholic beverages statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Social Work Examiners, beginning November 1, 2026, to issue provisional social work licenses. Authorizes initial applicants who meet education and experience requirements for bachelor or master social work to obtain provisional licensure. Requires provisional licensees to practice under the supervision of a Board-approved supervisor. Directs the Board to issue a full license when the licensee achieves a satisfactory examination score. Prohibits renewal of provisional licenses and sets expiration between 12 and 24 months after issuance.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: initial applicants for bachelor social work and master social work licenses; supervising social workers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Social Work Examiners special fund expenditures increase by $64,900 in FY 2027 for one administrator, with ongoing operating costs in future years. Special fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2027 from provisional licensing fees established to cover administrative costs. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health and its State Board of Social Work Examiners, requiring the Board to promulgate regulations, establish and issue provisional licenses for bachelor and master social workers, track supervisees, report annually to legislative committees, and hire additional staff funded via board special funds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each health occupations board to allow continuing education credits for completing an approved human trafficking awareness training program. Directs each board to conduct outreach regarding training options and adopt implementing regulations by January 1, 2027. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to approve the training program by July 1, 2026. Mandates that the training be readily accessible, free of charge, and at least one hour in duration. Outlines curriculum requirements, including sex and labor trafficking definitions, trauma-informed care, and reporting protocols.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; health occupations boards
qa_results.stakeholders: health care practitioners seeking license or certificate renewal; health occupations boards; human trafficking survivors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected. The Maryland Department of Health and health occupations boards can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to approve the human trafficking awareness training program by July 1, 2026, and its constituent health occupations boards must adopt regulations and conduct outreach to allow licensees to receive continuing education credits for completing the training.

The bill specifically references the University of Maryland SAFE Center for Human Trafficking Survivors as an example of a local university program that may collaborate with MDH to develop and approve the training curriculum.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires MDH to consult with the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force in approving the human trafficking awareness training program.

Morgan State University is a public institution with relevant qualifying programs (such as social work and public health) eligible to collaborate as a local university, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a rate-setting study for community-based behavioral health services by June 30, 2028. Establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization in the Maryland Health Care Commission. Directs the workgroup to develop cost-based reimbursement methodologies for certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide analytical support and technical assistance for the department's rate-setting study. Transfers annual behavioral health reporting duties on provider wages, turnover, and recruitment from the department to the commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, independent outpatient providers, direct care staff, licensed clinicians, and individuals receiving community-based behavioral health services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $391,974 in FY 2027 ($181,699 general funds for MDH and $210,275 special funds for MHCC) and $356,100 in FY 2028 for contractual staff and analytical vendor support. Indeterminate special fund expenditures continue in future years for ongoing annual reporting by MHCC. Local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (including the Behavioral Health Administration and the Medical Care Programs Administration) is required to conduct an independent rate-setting study for community behavioral health services, review and implement workgroup recommendations, administer cost-reporting tools, adopt implementing regulations, and designate a technical liaison.

The bill houses the newly created Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Maryland Health Care Commission, requires MHCC to provide staffing and analytical support, assists MDH with the rate-setting study, and mandates that MHCC submit interim and ongoing annual reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization, a temporary advisory body tasked with analyzing cost drivers, developing cost-based reimbursement methodologies, and reporting findings before terminating on June 30, 2028.
The bill requires multiple interim and annual reports detailing behavioral health rate methodologies, delivery systems, and implementation progress to be submitted to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires law enforcement officers to forward certain complaints to the Department of Juvenile Services. Applies when a child under age 13 allegedly commits an act resulting in a victim's death. Requires a juvenile intake officer to file a petition alleging the child is in need of supervision. Designates the legislation as the NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services; Law Enforcement Agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Children under age 13 alleged to have committed acts resulting in the death of a victim, their parents or guardians, and crime victims and their surviving families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 776 directly impacts the Department of Juvenile Services (DJS) by requiring DJS intake officers to file a petition alleging that a child is in need of supervision (CINS) if the child is under age 13 and alleged to have committed an act resulting in the death of a victim, removing intake discretion for informal adjustment or refusal in these cases.

The bill requires mandatory filing of CINS petitions in the juvenile court for specified cases involving children under 13, directly impacting juvenile court caseloads and judicial proceedings administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill establishes a statutory requirement under the Criminal Procedure Article that law enforcement officers, including Maryland State Police troopers, must forward complaints alleging an act by a child under 13 that resulted in the death of a victim to the Department of Juvenile Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Mandatory formal CINS petitions in juvenile court require legal representation for the children involved, which is routinely handled by the Office of the Public Defender in indigent juvenile proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the governing bodies of Washington County and municipal corporations in Washington County to grant a property tax credit. Sets the credit equal to 100% of the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on eligible real property. Applies the tax credit to real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated. Restricts eligibility to property used to provide housing to veterans. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington County; municipal corporations in Washington County
qa_results.stakeholders: Platoon 22, Incorporated; veterans housed by Platoon 22, Incorporated; Washington County; City of Hagerstown
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Local property tax revenues decrease annually beginning in fiscal 2027 by approximately $4,000 for Washington County and approximately $5,000 for the City of Hagerstown. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates a local property tax credit for property owned by Platoon 22, Inc. that is used to provide housing to veterans, aligning with the Department of Veterans & Military Families' mission to support and advocate for veterans' housing and welfare.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends authorization for aquaculture leaseholders to place shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation. Moves the statutory termination date from June 30, 2027, to June 30, 2030. Requires leaseholders to obtain prior written approval from the Department of Natural Resources before placement. Prohibits the Department from authorizing dredge harvesting in areas where submerged aquatic vegetation is present. Requires the Department to authorize harvest by diving on submerged land leases where submerged aquatic vegetation exists.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: shellfish aquaculture leaseholders and commercial shellfish businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of Natural Resources' authority to approve the placement of shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation by extending the statutory termination date of this regulatory program from June 30, 2027, to June 30, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes members and former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System assigned as helicopter pilots to receive military service credit. Applies this authorization to pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit receiving military credit from another retirement system. Prohibits an individual from receiving service credit under the section more than once. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who are or were assigned as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues because the bill applies to a very small number of individuals. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and is directly responsible for processing applications and granting military service credits under the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

The Maryland State Police operates the State's law enforcement Aviation Command, directly employing the helicopter pilots who are members of LEOPS eligible for the expanded military service credit under this bill.
The Department of Budget and Management serves as the central personnel and fiscal agency, monitoring state employee benefits, retirement plans, and state employer pension contribution rates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Commerce to allow eligible fund managers to receive loan management fees. Establishes that the fee must range between 1.5% and 3% of total loan principal. Requires management fees to be paid from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account. Authorizes eligible fund managers to retain fees for administrative purposes related to lending activities. Authorizes the Department to establish an annual cap on cumulative management fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: eligible fund managers (including county economic development corporations and private firms) and small, minority, and women-owned businesses in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Commerce can likely implement the bill with existing resources. Local economic development entities acting as eligible fund managers may receive new fee revenues, which would divert capital within the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account away from direct loans and grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA) and is directly responsible for authorizing eligible fund managers to receive management fees and setting annual caps under this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Although the program is directly administered by Commerce, this office coordinates policies and initiatives affecting small, minority, and women-owned business enterprises across Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Secretary of Aging. Directs fund resources to support the implementation of the Department of Aging's statutory mission. Authorizes expenditures for expenses aligning with that mission, including partnership development and departmental programs, services, or activities. Prohibits the Governor from reducing an appropriation for the fund approved by the General Assembly. Requires the Secretary to submit an annual fund administration report to specified legislative committees by January 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Secretary of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Older adults and seniors in Maryland, caregivers, families, and local area agencies on aging
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State special fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 from investment earnings, collected fees, and other accepted contributions. Potential increase in local area agency on aging revenues and expenditures to the extent funds become available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to support the Department of Aging's mission and requires the Secretary of Aging to administer the fund and report annually on its receipts and expenditures.

The bill statutorily tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Aging Resilience Fund separately, investing the money in the fund, and crediting interest earnings directly to the fund under an exemption to the General Fund interest sweep.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created Aging Resilience Fund.

The bill limits executive authority by explicitly prohibiting the Governor from reducing an appropriation for the Aging Resilience Fund in the State budget under Section 7-213 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

As the State's central agency responsible for budget development and execution, DBM is impacted by restrictions on budget reductions under Section 7-213 and the requirement that fund expenditures conform to the State budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant a property tax credit on qualifying dwellings. Applies to dwellings with a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity. Requires a covenant or legally binding agreement of at least 20 years enforcing income and equity or appreciation restrictions. Caps the credit at the difference between taxes on the full assessed value and the homeowner's first mortgage obligation. Allows local governing bodies to set credit duration, additional eligibility criteria, and application procedures. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners of qualifying affordable dwellings, nonprofit mortgage lenders, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent local jurisdictions enact the credit; specific figures are unavailable because revenue loss depends on local adoption and eligible property sales. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes an optional local property tax credit to incentivize and support affordable homeownership through nonprofit-provided mortgages and long-term affordability covenants. While the fiscal impact is local and the credit is administered by local governments, the policy directly aligns with DHCD's mission and initiatives to promote affordable homeownership and community stability.

qa_results.bill_summary: Specifies three intern fellowships in the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program. Includes the Governor's Summer Internship, Sondheim Maryland Nonprofit Leadership Internship, and Sondheim Public Service Law Fellows programs. Increases the maximum scholarship award under the program from $5,000 to $6,000. Requires the Governor to provide an annual budget appropriation starting in fiscal year 2028. Mandates funding for the University of Maryland, Baltimore County of at least 125% of fiscal 2026 levels.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Shriver Center; University of Maryland, Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: College and graduate students pursuing public service internships; public and nonprofit host entities; University of Maryland, Baltimore County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $87,500 annually beginning in fiscal year 2028 to satisfy the mandated 125% appropriation requirement for the University of Maryland, Baltimore County. No direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Shriver Center at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC), a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, administers the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program. The bill directly mandates funding for UMBC to support the program and its fellowships.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific statutory appropriation in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2028 equal to at least 125% of the program's FY 2026 appropriation.

As the principal budget agency for the State, DBM is responsible for preparing the Governor's budget and incorporating the mandated appropriation for the internship scholarship program beginning in FY 2028.
The program is codified under Title 18 (Student Financial Assistance) of the Education Article, which falls within MHEC's policy purview over higher education scholarships and financial aid programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is recognized in the bill's preamble as a cornerstone of the State's public service initiatives, aligning closely with the bill's objective of expanding public service pathways and internships for students.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to evaluate blockchain technology for property lease and title recordation. Directs the department to assess using blockchain to assist law enforcement and courts with squatting disputes. Defines squatting as unauthorized real property occupation without legal title, a lease, or possession rights. Requires reporting study results to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2026. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Maryland Judiciary; Maryland State Police; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: real property owners, tenants, alleged squatters, law enforcement agencies, and state courts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected; any potential costs associated with the study workgroup are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General is explicitly required by the bill to coordinate with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and other entities to conduct the study and submit the final report on blockchain-based real property title and lease recordation.

The Maryland State Police is specifically mandated to coordinate on the study and report, particularly evaluating how blockchain technology could assist law enforcement in resolving real property disputes involving squatting.

The Administrative Office of the Courts represents the Maryland Judiciary, which is explicitly named in the bill to coordinate on the study evaluating the potential use of blockchain technology by courts in resolving real property disputes.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the final study and recommendations required to be submitted by December 31, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of Aging to make grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging. Supports social connection for individuals in aging-in-place programs through events at multigenerational third places. Defines a multigenerational third place as a community space other than a home or workplace supporting connection. Authorizes grant funding for operational costs, including administrative and rental costs, for senior villages. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: nonprofit organizations, area agencies on aging, senior villages, and seniors participating in aging-in-place programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on state finances, as the bill alters the authorized uses of existing funds and the Maryland Department of Aging can implement changes with existing resources. Local governments operating area agencies on aging may receive grant revenues, with local expenditures increasing correspondingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA), authorizing the department to award aging-in-place grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging for multigenerational third places and related senior village operational costs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the cap on the Industry Automobile Insurance Association's assessment allocation percentage for private passenger auto from 3% to 1%. Authorizes the Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund to establish a private passenger auto insurance affordability program. Requires approval from the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and caps overall rate inadequacy at 20% of net written premium. Restricts program eligibility to qualified policyholders with household incomes not exceeding 250% of the federal poverty level. Prohibits the Commissioner from disapproving or modifying the program based on noncompliance with statutory capital requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; Maryland Insurance Administration; Industry Automobile Insurance Association
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund policyholders with household income not exceeding 250% of the federal poverty level, private passenger automobile insurers, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. Nonbudgeted Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund revenues likely decrease in fiscal 2028 and 2029 due to the continuation of discounted premium rates, but specific figures cannot be reliably predicted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs MAIF by authorizing its Executive Director to establish an automobile insurance affordability program for qualifying policyholders and reducing the cap on the assessment allocation percentage for its private passenger auto division from 3% to 1%.

The bill assigns regulatory and oversight responsibilities to the Insurance Commissioner and MIA to review, approve, and require modifications to MAIF's affordability program and ensure rates are not excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the maximum annual salary for clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills. Caps the maximum salary at Grade 26, Step 20 of the State Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale. Requires the Board of Public Works to set each official's salary within that statutory limit. Prohibits mid-term salary scale adjustments from applying to incumbent officials until their next term begins. Repeals an obsolete $12,000 minimum annual salary for the Baltimore City register of wills. Applies salary adjustments to terms of office beginning on or after October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Maryland Judiciary; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills across Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2027, State general fund expenditures increase by $403,800 for the Judiciary to cover clerk salary increases, rising to $692,300 annually thereafter. State general fund revenues decrease by $386,300 in FY 2027 due to increased register of wills compensation paid from fee and inheritance tax collections, decreasing by $662,100 annually thereafter. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the maximum annual statutory salary for the 24 elected registers of wills by tying it to Grade 26, Step 20 of the State salary scale, and repeals an obsolete salary provision for the Baltimore City register.

The bill increases the maximum salary for clerks of the circuit courts, directly impacting the Judiciary's operational budget with projected general fund expenditure increases of over $400,000 in FY 2027 and nearly $700,000 annually thereafter.

The Board of Public Works is the statutory body required to determine and fix the specific annual salaries for each circuit court clerk and register of wills within the newly established statutory cap.

The Comptroller oversees the remittance of taxes and fees from the registers of wills, authorizes transfers to cover expense or salary deficiencies in registers' offices, and manages the remittance of excess revenues that flow into the general fund.

DBM maintains the State of Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale (specifically Grade 26, Step 20) that establishes the salary ceiling under the bill and oversees state personnel compensation schedules and fiscal planning.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to appoint an employee of a county board of education to the State Board of Education. Limits the number of regular State Board members who are county board employees to two at any given time. Prohibits a county superintendent from serving as an employee member on the State Board. Restricts county board employee members from voting on specific personnel appeals and disciplinary actions. Requires an affirmative vote of a majority of authorized voting members to take action on restricted matters.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees of county boards of education and members of the Maryland State Board of Education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership eligibility, voting rules, and participation guidelines of the Maryland State Board of Education, which oversees the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).
The bill directly impacts the Governor's statutory appointment authority by permitting the Governor to appoint an employee of a county board of education to the State Board of Education.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, including the newly eligible county board employee seat on the State Board of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires applicants for for-hire and locally licensed taxicab driver licenses to verify completion of human trafficking awareness training. Mandates training on recognizing, responding to, and reporting suspected human trafficking to appropriate authorities. Requires transportation network operators to complete training within 30 days after first providing a prearranged ride. Bars transportation network companies from letting operators provide services if they fail to complete the training. Protects drivers, operators, and applicants from civil or criminal liability for good-faith reporting or responding to suspected human trafficking.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: taxicab drivers, for-hire drivers, transportation network operators, transportation network companies, and local taxicab licensing authorities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission increase by $10,000 in fiscal 2027 only for online application software modifications, offset by an equal increase in special fund assessment revenues on public service companies. Local governments can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory agency responsible for licensing passenger-for-hire drivers, taxicab drivers, and transportation network operators. The bill requires PSC to verify human trafficking awareness training documentation for applicants and entails a $10,000 IT modification expenditure in FY 2027.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents utility and passenger transportation consumers before the Public Service Commission and was consulted as an informational source regarding the regulatory impacts of the bill.

The bill provides civil and criminal immunity to for-hire drivers, taxicab drivers, and transportation network operators who report or respond to suspected human trafficking in good faith, which could marginally affect court proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes the Commission to Advance Lithium–Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with altered membership and an expanded mandate. Requires the Office of the State Fire Marshal to provide staff for the Commission. Requires the Commission to study battery fire safety, recycling practices, extended producer responsibility, and transportation risks. Requires an interim progress report to the Legislative Policy Committee by December 1, 2026. Requires a final report with recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal; Commission to Advance Lithium–Ion Battery Safety in Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Lithium-ion battery and vehicle propulsion battery manufacturers, battery recycling and solid waste facilities, first responders and firefighters, electric utilities, commercial and property casualty insurers, towing and recovery professionals, and the Maryland Port Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $70,700 in FY 2027 and $30,100 in FY 2028 for the Office of the State Fire Marshal to hire one contractual employee to staff the Commission. Revenues are unaffected. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal, an agency within the Department of State Police, is mandated to staff the Commission, which requires hiring a contractual employee resulting in a direct general fund fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reestablishes and sets the mandate and membership for the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland.
The bill designates a seat on the Commission for a representative of the Maryland Port Administration and specifically tasks the Commission with studying battery risks at the Port of Baltimore.

The Secretary of the Environment appoints multiple members to the Commission, including a representative of the Land and Materials Administration, and the Commission studies battery recycling, disposal, and solid waste issues.
The Director of MEA appoints a representative from MEA and battery industry representatives, and the Commission reviews grid-scale battery energy storage and safety standards.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner appoints members representing the property casualty and commercial insurance sectors, and the Commission is mandated to study the impacts of battery risk on insurance providers and coverage.
The Secretary of Transportation appoints members to the Commission, and the Commission evaluates lithium-ion battery risks on roads, rail, and tunnels throughout the state.
The Chair of the Public Service Commission appoints a representative to the Commission, which is tasked with studying safety standards for utility and grid-scale energy storage applications.
The Secretary of Natural Resources appoints a representative from the Power Plant Research Program to serve on the Commission.
The Commission is required to submit its final report with findings and legislative/regulatory recommendations directly to the Governor by December 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes pharmacists to enter into prescriber–pharmacist agreements to treat opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances drug therapy. Requires qualifying pharmacists to register with the federal Drug Enforcement Administration and the Maryland Office of Controlled Substances Administration. Requires treatment protocols to mandate pharmacist checks of the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program before initiating or modifying therapy. Adds licensed certified midwives to the definition of authorized prescribers, allowing them to enter therapy management contracts. Repeals the requirement that authorized prescribers submit prescriber–pharmacist agreements to their regulating health occupations boards.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health, Office of Controlled Substances Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed pharmacists, licensed certified midwives, authorized prescribers, and patients with opioid use disorders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $58,635 in FY 2027 for personnel and a one-time software update. General fund revenues increase by an estimated $72,000 in FY 2027 from controlled dangerous substances registration fees. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires pharmacists seeking to treat opioid use disorder with controlled dangerous substances (CDS) to individually register with the Office of Controlled Substances Administration (OCSA). OCSA will process the new registrations, update online portal software, and collect registration fee revenues.

MDH oversees health occupation licensing boards—including the State Board of Pharmacy—as well as the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) and OCSA. The bill regulates prescriber-pharmacist agreements, incorporates licensed certified midwives, impacts health occupations board submission requirements, and results in net fiscal impacts for MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each meeting of the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County to include public comment. Requires the Board to make a video or audio recording of each meeting. Requires the Board to post recordings online without charge, when practicable, within two business days. Requires the Board to maintain recordings and minutes in perpetuity. Authorizes transcribing video recordings maintained for at least five years if the transcription is kept in perpetuity. Requires board members to undergo governance, structure, responsibilities, and roles training at least every two years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County, Frederick Community College staff and students, and Frederick County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick Community College expenditures may increase minimally to record, post, and permanently maintain meeting recordings. Training requirements and public posting can be handled within existing resources. No state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's coordinating board for postsecondary education, MHEC oversees policies and standards relating to Maryland community colleges and provided information for the bill's fiscal analysis, though the direct requirements apply locally to Frederick Community College.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant a property tax credit against local property taxes. Applies the credit to dwelling houses of surviving spouses ineligible for the Section 7-208 property tax exemption. Authorizes local governing bodies to provide for the amount, duration, and additional eligibility requirements. Authorizes local governing bodies to provide regulations and procedures for uniformly processing credit applications. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; County Governing Bodies; Municipal Corporation Governing Bodies
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses of military service members ineligible for statutory property tax exemptions; Baltimore City; county governments; municipal corporation governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local property tax revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent jurisdictions grant the credit, with exact impacts depending on local adoption, property assessments, and local tax rates. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an optional local property tax credit for the surviving spouses of military service members who do not qualify for the existing state real property tax exemption. The Department of Veterans and Military Families assists service members, veterans, and their families in accessing state and local benefits, including housing and tax relief opportunities.

The bill authorizes local jurisdictions to establish a property tax credit on dwelling houses owned by surviving spouses of military service members. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is responsible for hearing appeals regarding property assessments, exemptions, and property tax credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for Maryland Community College Promise Scholarships to Delmar, Maryland residents graduating from Delmar High School in Delaware. Renames the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program to the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program. Extends scholarship eligibility to surviving transportation workers, their spouses, unmarried partners, and dependent children. Authorizes eligible siblings of fallen transportation workers without surviving partners or children to receive awards. Permits recipients to use scholarship awards for the total cost of attendance at any postsecondary institution.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; institutions of postsecondary education
qa_results.stakeholders: residents of Delmar, Maryland graduating from Delmar High School; surviving transportation workers; families, unmarried partners, and siblings of fallen or surviving transportation workers; Maryland institutions of postsecondary education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures beginning as early as fiscal 2027 for additional scholarship awards and increased award amounts covering total cost of attendance. Precise figures are unavailable due to unknown applicant counts. Expanding Promise Scholarship eligibility requires no additional state funding but may increase waitlists.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory and administrative agency for state financial aid programs, responsible for administering the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship and the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and its dedicated special fund.

MHEC is the primary agency responsible for administering state student financial assistance, overseeing program guidelines, and allocating funds for the Community College Promise Scholarship and the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program.

The bill explicitly requires MDOT, to the extent practicable, to provide contact information for the families of fallen or surviving transportation workers to the Commission following qualifying accidents.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the monies of the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund separately and receive gifts or grants deposited for the fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily directed to account for the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund.

USM institutions determine applicant eligibility and report recipient counts to the Commission; additionally, maximum scholarship amounts under the program are capped relative to undergraduate tuition and fees across USM institutions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts property owned by the City of Hagerstown from state, county, and municipal property taxes. Requires the property to be used primarily for public social, recreational, and entertainment purposes. Applies the property tax exemption retroactively to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023. Directs the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to grant retroactive exemptions upon request. Requires the State, Washington County, and the City of Hagerstown to refund any excess property tax paid.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Washington County; City of Hagerstown
qa_results.stakeholders: City of Hagerstown; Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc.; Washington County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease by $102,600 in FY 2027 ($80,300 for a retroactive refund and $22,300 for the ongoing exemption) and by $22,300 annually thereafter. Washington County and municipal property tax revenues decrease by approximately $1.3 million in FY 2027 for retroactive refunds ($575,700 county and $718,300 municipal) and by $160,000 annually beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for tracking State revenues, paying State bills, and administering tax refunds. The bill requires the State to pay refunds for excess property taxes paid due to the retroactive property tax exemption.

The bill reduces revenues to the Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) by approximately $80,300 in FY 2027 and $22,300 annually thereafter. The Treasurer's Office oversees the issuance of State general obligation bonds and the management of debt service funds paid through the ABF.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for setting the annual State property tax rate to ensure adequate revenues flow into the Annuity Bond Fund to cover debt service on State general obligation bonds, which are impacted by the exemption and refund in this bill.
The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is the administrative body that hears appeals regarding property tax valuations and disputes concerning eligibility for property tax exemptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Fire Prevention Commission to incorporate specified life safety provisions into the State Fire Prevention Code. Mandates the incorporation by reference of Sections 30.7.5 and 31.7.5 of the NFPA 101 Life Safety Code (2024 Edition). Permits trash and recycling materials awaiting scheduled collection to be placed in corridors and exits under those standards. Applies these collection standards to new and existing apartment buildings. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Fire Prevention Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Apartment building owners, apartment residents, valet trash and recycling collection services, and fire prevention officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Fire Prevention Commission can implement the bill using existing resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Fire Prevention Commission and the Office of the State Fire Marshal are established within the Department of State Police. The bill directly requires the Commission to amend its State Fire Prevention Code regulations regarding the placement of valet trash and recyclable materials in corridors and exits, and the State Fire Marshal is responsible for enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Fire Prevention Commission is a permanent regulatory commission mandated by the bill to adopt specific regulations incorporating sections of the NFPA 101 Life Safety Code into the State Fire Prevention Code.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an enrollment freeze in the Child Care Scholarship Program from applying to specified vulnerable children and families. Exempts recipients of Temporary Cash Assistance, federal TANF, Supplemental Security Income, siblings of enrolled children, and homeless children. Requires the State Department of Education to establish an enrollment waitlist when a freeze occurs. Prioritizes qualified applicants by financial need, child care employment, children under age three, and waitlist tenure. Requires the Department to develop an updated application and review job training eligibility standards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income families seeking child care assistance, children experiencing homelessness, recipients of TCA, TANF, or SSI, child care facility employees, and child care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $350,000 in FY 2027 to reprogram administrative tracking and portal systems. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE administers the Child Care Scholarship Program and is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to establish and manage a waitlist during enrollment freezes, exempt specific populations, develop a new application, review job training eligibility methodology, submit a report to the General Assembly, and reprogram tracking and portal systems at an estimated cost of $350,000.

DHS administers Maryland's Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) programs. The bill specifically exempts individuals and families enrolled in TCA and TANF from any enrollment freeze under the Child Care Scholarship Program, necessitating program alignment and data coordination for eligible recipients.

DBM is responsible for state budget oversight and fiscal planning. The bill impacts program funding mechanics, waitlist operationalization, and requires state general fund expenditures for IT modifications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a home builder holding a property open to the public to conspicuously display a disclosure notice. Mandates that the notice state the sales representative's duty of loyalty is solely to the builder. Informs prospective new home buyers of their right to obtain independent representation. Requires the displayed disclosure to use a clear, simple font unobstructed from view. Mandates that the lettering measure a minimum of one-half inch in height.
qa_results.responsible_party: Home Builder Registration Unit, Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: home builders holding properties open to the public, home builder sales representatives, and prospective new home buyers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly impact State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 4.5 of the Business Regulation Article concerning home builder disclosure requirements. The Home Builder Registration Unit, which administers and enforces the Maryland Home Builder Registration Act, is housed within the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The Maryland Department of Labor regulates real estate professionals and sales representatives. The disclosure requirements notify buyers of their right to independent representation in purchasing a home, which intersects with the department's oversight of real estate licensing and practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council is a tax-exempt body politic and corporate. Reaffirms that the Council serves as an instrumentality of the State. Maintains the Council's mandate to work with Centers for Independent Living on the State Plan. Requires the Council to carry out duties supporting State Plan implementation under the federal Rehabilitation Act. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council, Centers for Independent Living, and individuals with disabilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The change is technical in nature and does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC) coordinates independent living services and policies for Marylanders with disabilities, aligning directly with the Department of Disabilities' mission to improve community living and service delivery for individuals with disabilities. The Department was also consulted as an information source for the fiscal note.

The bill explicitly clarifies the tax-exempt legal status of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council as a body politic and corporate. As the state's chief tax administrator, the Comptroller oversees state tax-exempt statuses and was an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

MSILC works in conjunction with the Maryland State Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which is housed within the Maryland State Department of Education, to develop, monitor, and implement the State Plan for Independent Living.

The bill clarifies MSILC's corporate and tax-exempt legal status, which intersects with the Secretary of State's role in the registration and oversight of charitable and nonprofit organizations operating in the State.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program to include correctional officers and certificate programs. Renames the program the Maryland Police Officers, Probation Agents, and Correctional Officers Scholarship Program. Provides tuition assistance to eligible students enrolled in degree or certificate programs at public senior institutions or community colleges. Requires recipients to complete a five-year service obligation in the State within eight years after graduation. Mandates repayment of scholarship funds if a recipient fails to complete program requirements or perform the service obligation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
qa_results.stakeholders: Current correctional officers, individuals pursuing careers as correctional officers, and public higher education institutions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $20,000 in fiscal 2027 for Maryland Higher Education Commission system enhancements. Expanding scholarship eligibility has no direct effect on total mandated state appropriations or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (specifically through the Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the scholarship program, publicizing awards, selecting recipients, processing payments, and updating its Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at an estimated cost of $20,000.

MHEC is the primary state entity tasked with administering student financial aid programs, and this bill directly alters eligibility and requires system modifications to award scholarships to correctional officers and individuals in certificate programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs state correctional officers and parole and probation agents. The bill directly impacts DPSCS's workforce recruitment and retention by providing tuition assistance and scholarships for current correctional officers and individuals preparing to enter the field, tied to a five-year service obligation.
USM institutions constitute eligible public senior higher education institutions where scholarship recipients will enroll in eligible degree or certificate programs to fulfill their course of study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Nonpublic Special Education School Renovation Program administered by the Interagency Commission on School Construction. Authorizes the commission to provide grants to eligible nonpublic special education schools for renovations, upgrades, and necessary new construction. Limits eligibility to schools providing approved educational programs and serving students placed under State special education law. Authorizes the commission to prioritize projects addressing health and safety concerns, Department standards, or high resident enrollments. Expresses legislative intent that the Governor include an annual capital budget appropriation of at least $5,000,000. Requires the commission to adopt regulations to implement the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
