qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible nonpublic special education schools and students with disabilities placed in nonpublic educational programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $145,200 in FY 2027 for two full-time administrative staff positions, growing to $285,300 by FY 2031. Total capital budget expenditures are unaffected, though satisfying the $5.0 million annual legislative intent would divert capital funding from other projects or increase PAYGO general fund spending beginning in FY 2028. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Nonpublic Special Education School Renovation Program within the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) and requires the IAC to administer the program, evaluate applications, award grants, and adopt implementing regulations.

Grant eligibility and project prioritization are tied directly to MSDE-approved educational programs and standards. The fiscal note also identifies the need for one full-time school facilities engineer at MSDE to help develop standards and review applications.
The bill expresses legislative intent for the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $5,000,000 for the program in the annual capital budget bill.
DBM assists the Governor in developing the annual operating and capital budgets and oversees state budget planning, which will be implicated by the legislative intent to allocate $5,000,000 annually.

DGS provides support in reviewing design and construction documents for school construction projects, though the fiscal note anticipates minimal additional impact due to staffing additions at IAC and MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the time period during which common ownership communities may restrict candidate or proposition signs. Authorizes cooperative housing corporations, condominiums, and homeowners associations to set display limitations. Allows communities to restrict displays to not less than 45 days before early voting begins. Permits a limitation of not less than 45 days before the vote if no early voting occurs. Applies if the governing local jurisdiction does not specify a display time period. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Cooperative housing corporations; Condominium councils of unit owners; Homeowners associations
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, unit owners, and governing bodies of cooperative housing corporations, condominiums, and homeowners associations; candidates for public office
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General, specifically through its Consumer Protection Division, handles consumer disputes and statutory enforcement related to common ownership communities (HOAs, condominiums, and cooperative housing corporations), and was consulted as an information source on this legislation.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which hears civil disputes regarding covenant enforcement and property restrictions in common ownership communities; the Judiciary was consulted as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to register each local school system as an associate member of a national membership organization. Directs the department to pay all applicable fees and dues for access to the Educator Identification Clearinghouse. Requires local school systems to screen individuals offered licensed educator positions through the clearinghouse on or after August 1, 2026. Requires school systems to ensure each candidate applies for the appropriate license before employment begins. Mandates that individuals obtain the appropriate license before any interaction with children.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals receiving employment offers for licensed educator positions, local school systems, and public school students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $28,596 annually beginning in FY 2027 for MSDE to pay membership and subscription fees. Local school system expenditures decrease minimally ($2,400 or less per system) for school systems currently paying for clearinghouse access.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to register each local school system as an associate member of a national membership organization providing access to the Educator Identification Clearinghouse and to pay all associated annual membership dues and subscription fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to post the statewide Information Technology Master Plan publicly on its website. Requires submission of the plan to the General Assembly within one year after the Governor's inauguration in each term. Directs the Secretary of Information Technology to notify the Governor and specified legislative committees within 10 days if delayed. Limits any delayed publication date to no more than three months after the initial deadline. Requires the Secretary or a designee to provide an annual briefing to the General Assembly on plan implementation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Secretary of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive Branch state agencies and the Maryland General Assembly
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Information Technology can implement the reporting and briefing requirements using existing budgeted resources. No state revenue or local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) and the Secretary of Information Technology post the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan online, submit it to the General Assembly within specified deadlines, provide written notice if delayed, and conduct annual briefings to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes publication deadlines keyed to the Governor's inauguration in each gubernatorial term and requires the Secretary of Information Technology to provide written notification to the Governor if the master plan is delayed.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits operating certain freight trains in the State unless the train has a crew of at least two individuals. Applies to freight trains sharing a rail corridor with high-speed passenger or commuter trains. Excludes freight operations involving hostler service or utility employees in yard service. Establishes civil penalties up to $10,000, increasing to $25,000 for repeat willful violations within three years. Conditions implementation on New York, Pennsylvania, and Virginia enacting substantially similar legislation on or before October 1, 2056.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Railroad companies operating freight trains in Maryland, freight train crew members, and passenger rail operators sharing rail corridors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances under current federal rules. If federal two-person crew requirements are repealed or invalidated and multi-state legislative contingencies are met, Transportation Trust Fund expenditures could increase by up to $6.0 million annually to reimburse CSX under an existing track access agreement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the Railroad Safety and Health Program and its Commissioner is tasked with assessing civil penalties for violations of the freight train crew size requirements. The department is also required to monitor and notify the Department of Legislative Services when the multi-state contingency is satisfied.

The bill impacts freight rail operating in shared corridors with commuter rail. Under an Access Agreement with freight rail operator CSX, MDOT could face up to $6.0 million annually in State Transportation Trust Fund obligations if federal crew size rules are modified or invalidated.

The Maryland Transit Administration operates MARC passenger commuter trains that share tracks and infrastructure with CSX freight trains. An existing Access Agreement between MTA and CSX includes staffing reimbursement stipulations tied to state-mandated crew size laws.

The Public Service Commission possesses regulatory oversight over railroad carriers and by statute funds the Department of Labor's Railroad Safety and Health Program through annual assessments on public service companies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires contractors and subcontractors on covered public works projects to employ qualifying apprentices or journeyworkers for specified labor hours. Sets the initial apprenticeship utilization requirement at 20% for bids advertised on or after January 1, 2027. Requires the Secretary of Labor to set the applicable percentage every other December 31 beginning in 2028. Redefines covered projects to align with all projects subject to State prevailing wage law. Applies these public works apprenticeship standards to the University System of Maryland and Baltimore City Community College. Authorizes alternative payments to the State Apprenticeship Training Fund or qualified apprenticeship programs not exceeding 25 cents per hour.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors and subcontractors on public works projects subject to prevailing wage laws, registered apprentices and journeyworkers, qualified apprenticeship programs, the University System of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund increase starting in fiscal 2027 as contractors make payments in lieu of meeting apprentice utilization targets, though a reliable estimate is not feasible. State general fund revenues may increase minimally from penalties. State and local public works project costs could increase if contractor competition declines, or decrease if apprentice labor replaces higher-wage tradespeople. State agencies can implement the requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill. The Secretary of Labor is responsible for setting the applicable apprenticeship utilization percentage, administering and auditing the State Apprenticeship Training Fund (SATF), reviewing contractor waiver requests and monthly reporting, adopting implementing regulations, and assessing penalties.

The bill explicitly removes certain procurement exemptions to apply Title 17, Subtitle 6 (Apprenticeship Requirements for Public Works Contracts) directly to University System of Maryland procurements and capital projects.
The bill explicitly subjects public works procurements by Morgan State University to State apprenticeship utilization requirements and prevailing wage apprenticeship standards.
The bill's provisions amending procurement laws under § 11-203 apply the public works apprenticeship utilization requirements directly to Saint Mary's College of Maryland.

As the state's principal agency for public works, capital improvements, and facility construction, DGS will be required to ensure that contractors and subcontractors comply with the new apprentice and journeyworker utilization percentages and verification requirements.

MDOT awards and manages significant public works and infrastructure contracts that are subject to prevailing wage laws and will have to incorporate the revised apprentice and journeyworker utilization standards into contract administration.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves higher education capital improvement and service contracts exceeding statutory thresholds and approves procurement policies affected by the bill.
Under § 17-602(d), the Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
Under § 17-602(d), the State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees capital construction and maintenance of correctional facilities subject to public works procurement and prevailing wage requirements, directly impacting its contractor utilization standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The board retains dispute and contract claim authority over procurement contracts awarded by the universities and community colleges referenced under § 11-203.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to December 31, 2028. Alters the workgroup reporting deadline to December 1, 2028. Requires the workgroup to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly. Continues the workgroup study on specialized case management and support programs for affected individuals. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
qa_results.stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH) staffs and supports the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, whose operations, reporting deadline, and termination date are extended by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the lifespan, reporting deadline, and mandate of an active statutory body—the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing—through December 31, 2028.

The bill requires the Workgroup to submit its report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2028, and the staffing entity (ODHH) is a coordinating office within the Executive Department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a county or municipality to notify the Maryland Department of the Environment after accepting certain building permit applications. Requires notices to include the address, permit number, square footage, building type, planned energy sources, and owner contact information. Applies prospectively to construction with utility service requests, development applications, or permit applications filed after the effective date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: counties, municipalities, and owners and developers of proposed new buildings with a gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment and local governments can implement the notification requirement using existing resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires local governments (counties and municipalities) to provide notice to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) within 10 business days of accepting a permit application for any new building with a proposed gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more. MDE will receive and track these notices to support its Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for permanent full-time Seat Pleasant police officers. Applies only if the Seat Pleasant Police Department becomes a participating governmental unit in the system. Grants past eligibility and creditable service to qualifying officers employed before the participation effective date. Covers local law enforcement officers employed in permanent full-time positions before, on, or after the date. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System; Seat Pleasant Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: Permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department and the City of Seat Pleasant
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. If Seat Pleasant elects to participate, its municipal pension liabilities increase by $2,104,315. Net local employer pension contributions increase by an estimated $541,380 annually beginning as early as fiscal 2028, reflecting a $680,330 contribution offset by a $138,950 new entrant credit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). If the Seat Pleasant Police Department participates as a governmental unit, the agency will be responsible for administering member enrollment, crediting past service, and managing contribution accounts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the membership of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five. Requires the Governor to appoint members from lists recommended by the county General Assembly delegations. Authorizes the Governor to request a new list of recommendations at any time. Prohibits more than three members from the same political party and two from the same legislative district. Requires the Board to adopt and publish a written conflict of interest and recusal policy. Sets the initial terms for the two additional members to begin May 2, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and prospective appointees of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners, alcoholic beverage license holders and applicants in Anne Arundel County, and Anne Arundel County taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $39,995 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to fund salaries, fringe benefits, and incidental expenses for two new board members. State operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Governor to appoint members to the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from recommendations submitted by county legislative delegations, and grants the Governor authority to request new lists of recommendations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and executing appointments to state and local boards and commissions, directly encompassing the gubernatorial appointments altered by this bill.

The bill mandates that the Board adopt and publish a written policy concerning conflicts of interest and recusal, intersecting with the State Ethics Commission's role in ethics laws and standards for public officials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the workers' compensation occupational disease presumption for heart disease and hypertension to Carroll County correctional deputies. Conditions the presumption on heart disease or hypertension being more severe than pre-existing conditions. Requires correctional deputies employed on or before September 30, 2026, to submit medical reports by December 31, 2026. Classifies Carroll County correctional deputies as public safety employees for enhanced permanent partial disability benefits. Applies the public safety employee designation prospectively to claims arising on or after October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Sheriff's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County correctional deputies and Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Carroll County expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2027 due to enhanced permanent partial disability benefits and increased occupational disease claims; exact costs cannot be reliably estimated. State operations, finances, and revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission is the state agency responsible for administering Maryland's workers' compensation laws and adjudicating claims. It will oversee and adjudicate any workers' compensation claims filed by Carroll County correctional deputies under the newly established occupational disease presumption and enhanced permanent partial disability benefit provisions.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions that combine with workplace injuries or occupational diseases. Because the bill establishes specific requirements evaluating pre-existing heart disease and hypertension conditions, the Fund could be involved in contested claims involving pre-existing disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the June 30, 2026 termination date for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub. Repeals the requirement that the Governor include an annual $350,000 appropriation to the Hub. Requires the Hub to carry out its statutory health literacy duties to the extent funding is available. Continues the requirement that the Hub submit an annual implementation report to designated legislative committees by July 1. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy
qa_results.stakeholders: University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy, State and local government agencies, health systems, nonprofit and community-based organizations, and Maryland health care consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances or operations, as the $350,000 mandated annual appropriation was scheduled to sunset after fiscal 2026 and the Hub must operate to the extent funding is available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State's Consumer Health Information Hub is housed within the University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy (part of USM). The bill eliminates the Hub's June 30, 2026 termination date while repealing its $350,000 annual mandated appropriation, directing it to carry out its operations to the extent funding is available.

The bill amends the Health - General Article governing statewide consumer health information and health literacy, an area closely coordinated with the Maryland Department of Health, which collaborates with the Hub on evaluating health communication and literacy initiatives.
The bill explicitly repeals the statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include a $350,000 appropriation for the Hub in the annual state budget bill.
As the agency responsible for preparing the state budget and managing mandated appropriations on behalf of the Governor, DBM is impacted by the repeal of the annual $350,000 mandated appropriation.

The Hub's codified statutory duties specifically include supporting public reporting of vital public health information, including health care quality reports from the Maryland Health Care Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Wicomico County or a municipal corporation in Wicomico County to grant a property tax credit. Applies to property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc., for development, rehabilitation, and transfer to a private owner. Requires the organization to intend to relinquish ownership in the near future. Excludes property occupied by administrative or warehouse buildings owned by the organization. Requires an annual report documenting local property holdings and transactions if a jurisdiction grants the credit. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Body of Wicomico County; governing bodies of municipal corporations in Wicomico County
qa_results.stakeholders: Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.; Wicomico County; municipal corporations in Wicomico County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. Wicomico County and municipal property tax revenues decrease by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent credits are granted. Expenditures are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes qualifying transit-oriented developments served by frequent rail transit to receive enterprise zone designations. Requires the Maryland Economic Development Corporation to prioritize redeveloping government-owned land near qualifying rail stations. Prohibits local governments from imposing minimum off-street parking mandates within 0.25 miles of qualifying rail stations. Requires local zoning to allow mixed-use development within 0.5 miles of qualifying rail stations. Restricts local land use limitations on certain transportation land subject to an approved transit-oriented development plan.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Economic Development Corporation; Department of Commerce; Sustainable Growth Subcabinet
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments; residential and commercial real estate developers; businesses and residents near qualifying rail transit stations; Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate state and local impact. State general fund expenditures increase in future years to reimburse local governments for enterprise zone property tax credits. State income tax revenues to the general fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund decrease in future years. Local property tax revenues decrease from enterprise zone credits, and development impact fees and excise taxes are delayed if contingent provisions take effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is directly tasked with reviewing and concurring with local adequate parking studies within 45 days, approving transit-oriented development (TOD) plans that limit local zoning restrictions on contiguous transit land, and managing TOD joint developments and leases on transportation-owned properties.

The bill statutorily requires MEDCO to prioritize projects that redevelop land contiguous to rail transit stations owned by the State, Baltimore City, or WMATA when issuing loans under the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program.

Commerce oversees the Enterprise Zone program, and the bill expands the definition and process to automatically designate qualifying transit-oriented developments as enterprise zones outside the statutory cap on annual designations by the Secretary.

As the MDOT modal agency operating rail transit stations (including Light Rail, Metro Subway, and MARC), MTA's stations and surrounding state-owned properties are the core geographic focus of the bill's land use, parking, and transit-oriented development mandates.

The Comptroller administers state income tax collections and tax credits, which will experience future revenue reductions in the General Fund, TTF, and HEIF due to expanded enterprise zone tax credits created under the bill.

MDP guides state land use policies and plays a central administrative role with the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, which receives local enterprise zone election filings and coordinates state TOD designations.

DHCD is the primary agency for community revitalization and housing finance; the bill facilitates mixed-use and residential housing expansion around transit hubs to support statewide affordable housing goals.
The legislation was introduced as an Administration priority bill to implement the Moore-Miller State Plan and Executive Order 01.01.2025.19 targeting transit-oriented development and housing supply.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits food retailers and third-party delivery service providers from using dynamic pricing to set higher prices for tax-exempt food. Bans these entities from using personal data to increase tax-exempt food prices for a single consumer. Prohibits using protected class data to deny or withhold accommodations, advantages, or privileges from consumers. Requires the Consumer Protection Division to provide alleged violators a 45-day notice period to cure violations. Excludes violations from criminal penalties and prohibits private civil lawsuits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Food retailers operating establishments of at least 15,000 square feet, third-party delivery service providers, and Maryland consumers purchasing food
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General increase at least minimally beginning in FY 2027 to cover contractual training and technical expertise costs. The bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State revenues or local government finances and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of dynamic pricing and data protection restrictions as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General. The fiscal note anticipates an increase in general fund expenditures for the agency.
HB 895 is an Administration bill introduced at the request of the Governor to advance executive policy priorities regarding consumer protection and predatory pricing regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Military Department. Requires the Adjutant General to administer the fund. Restricts fund usage to personnel, equipment, and operational expenses of the National Guard during State active duty mobilization. Credits any investment earnings of the fund to the General Fund of the State. Mandates timely replenishment of expended money to maintain operational effectiveness for future mobilizations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Military Department; Office of the Adjutant General
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland National Guard personnel ordered to State active duty
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Accelerates general fund expenditures to capitalize the fund, likely with at least $1.0 million in fiscal 2027, with special fund revenues increasing correspondingly. Special fund expenditures increase starting in fiscal 2027 based on mobilizations. Ongoing general fund expenditures will accelerate as needed to replenish the fund. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund in the Office of the Adjutant General within the Military Department and designates the Adjutant General as the administrator of the fund.
The fund is specifically established to pay for the personnel, equipment, and operations of the Maryland National Guard during State active duty mobilizations.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the new special fund separately and invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill specifically mandates that the Comptroller shall account for the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund.
State active duty mobilization of the National Guard is ordered by the Governor as commander-in-chief, which triggers expenditures from the newly created fund.
The fund relies on State budget appropriations and replenishments managed through the executive budget process, which DBM oversees and coordinates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters, renames, and transfers multiple State economic development programs, financing funds, and tax credits. Redesignates the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account as the Strategic Closing Fund within the Department of Commerce. Transfers the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Zone and Build Our Future Grant programs to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation. Extends the Job Creation, Research and Development, and Employer Security Clearance Costs tax credits. Exempts sales of certain information technology services and digital products between affiliated group members from sales and use tax. Reallocates video lottery terminal proceeds and increases financing caps for small business development programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Maryland Economic Development Corporation; Comptroller of Maryland; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland business entities, small businesses, minority- and women-owned businesses, technology companies, film production entities, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State net fiscal impact is negative $37.3 million in FY 2027, with general fund revenues decreasing by $35.5 million and special fund revenues decreasing by $1.8 million due to sales and use tax exemptions. In FY 2028, general fund revenues decrease by $60.2 million and general fund expenditures increase by $10.6 million. Local highway user revenues decrease by an estimated $0.4 million annually beginning in FY 2028, and local property tax revenues are moderately affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Commerce is the primary state department impacted by the bill. It oversees the vast majority of altered economic development programs and tax credits, including the Strategic Closing Fund, MEDAAF, MSBDFA, SMWOBA, Job Creation Tax Credit, R&D Tax Credit, and Film Production Activity Tax Credit.

The bill directly transfers the administration and management of both the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program and the Build Our Future Grant Program from Commerce to MEDCO, expanding MEDCO's operational responsibilities, grant-making authority, and reporting requirements.

The Comptroller administers the state sales and use tax, which is amended to exempt certain affiliated group information technology and digital product sales (resulting in tens of millions in annual revenue reductions). The Comptroller also accounts for several established special funds, processes income and corporate tax credits, distributes VLT proceeds, and must submit a report on tracking tax credit carryforwards.

The Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold, invest, and report on the moneys of the newly restructured and consolidated special funds under the bill, including the Strategic Closing Fund, Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Fund, and Build Our Future Grant Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees video lottery terminal operations and prepares transmittals that govern the statutory distribution of VLT proceeds, which this bill alters by redirecting $5.0 million to the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund.

DBM oversees state budget execution and fiscal planning, which will be affected by major shifts in general and special fund expenditures, budget amendments for fund transfers, and backfilling lost education revenues.
Transportation Trust Fund revenues and local highway user revenue grants are reduced by the extension and alteration of corporate income tax credits included in the bill.

This is an Administration initiative establishing key statewide economic competitiveness policies. The Governor proposes funding for the Strategic Closing Fund, submits budget amendments, and receives multiple required program evaluation reports.

Higher education institutions serve as anchor qualified institutions for RISE zones and are eligible recipients for up to 50% of grant funds appropriated under the Build Our Future Grant Program; additionally, the Higher Education Investment Fund is fiscally affected by corporate tax credit extensions.

As a public research university, Morgan State can serve as a qualified institution under the RISE Zone Program and is eligible to receive infrastructure grants under the Build Our Future Grant Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits private home detention monitoring agencies and their agents from soliciting business on courthouse or correctional facility grounds. Extends this solicitation ban to courthouse employees and correctional facility employees. Bans distributing, displaying, or wearing items advertising private home detention monitoring agency services on those grounds. Establishes misdemeanor penalties with fines up to $2,500 for first offenses and $5,000 for subsequent offenses. Requires license suspensions of 30 days for first offenses and 90 days for subsequent offenses for licensed violators. Requires referral of convicted licensed offenders to the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: private home detention monitoring agencies and their agents; courthouse employees; correctional facility employees; criminal defendants seeking pretrial release monitoring
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal state and local fiscal impact. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the referral requirements with existing resources. Misdemeanor fine penalties are not anticipated to have a meaningful effect on State general fund or local revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the regulatory and licensing authority for private home detention monitoring agencies (PHDMAs). Under the bill, licensed individuals convicted of unlawful solicitation or promotion on courthouse or correctional facility grounds must be referred to DPSCS for disciplinary action, and the bill directly restricts the activities of correctional facility employees.

The bill was introduced at the request of the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly prohibits certain promotional activities and solicitation by courthouse employees or PHDMA agents on the grounds of courthouses, which are supported administratively by the AOC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a law enforcement agency from assigning an officer to non-administrative duties unless issued protective body armor. Requires issued armor to meet current National Institute of Justice ballistic standards and unexpired manufacturer dates. Requires agencies to replace protective body armor before the expiration or suggested replacement date indicated by the manufacturer. Directs agencies to notify the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission if armor is unreplaced 31 days past expiration. Requires the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to withhold available grant funds from noncompliant agencies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies and law enforcement officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $55,300 in fiscal 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to purchase protective body armor for its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit. No material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates GOCPP to withhold and manage grant disbursements to law enforcement agencies that fail to comply with protective body armor replacement and notification requirements, and GOCPP administers the State Protective Body Armor Fund.

The bill has a direct fiscal impact on MDH, requiring $55,305 in general fund expenditures in FY 2027 to purchase compliant protective body armor for 45 officers in its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit (STIU).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is tasked by the bill with receiving failure-to-replace notifications from law enforcement agencies and transmitting them to GOCPP. The department's Division of Parole and Probation also qualifies for body armor grant funding.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, MSP must ensure all active non-administrative officers are issued compliant, unexpired body armor and adhere to statutory replacement deadlines.
DNR employs the Maryland Natural Resources Police, which is subject to the bill's body armor issuance, compliance, and replacement standards for sworn officers.
MDTA operates a dedicated police force that must comply with the bill's body armor replacement timelines and standards.
MDOT oversees modal administrations that maintain sworn police forces (such as the Maryland Transit Administration Police), which must comply with the bill's body armor requirements.
The Comptroller's Office employs sworn enforcement officers who are subject to the bill's protective body armor equipment mandates.
Morgan State University maintains a campus police department subject to the bill's requirements governing body armor issuance, replacement, and reporting.
USM institutions operate campus police departments that employ sworn officers who must be equipped with compliant, unexpired protective body armor.
The Department of Labor has regulatory and enforcement personnel identified in state law enforcement surveys affected by protective equipment guidelines.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a licensee at Laurel Park to conduct live racing of Arabian breed horses. Limits Arabian breed racing to one race per day and three races per race meet. Requires Arabian races to run in addition to, not in place of, regular thoroughbred races. Prohibits funding purses from the thoroughbred purse account. Requires State Racing Commission approval and payment of standard racing taxes and fees. Takes effect immediately upon enactment as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Racing Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Laurel Park racing licensees, Arabian horse owners and breeders, and thoroughbred horse racing participants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Racing Commission, which regulates horse racing in the state and is statutorily required under this bill to approve the Arabian breed races conducted by the licensee at Laurel Park.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the membership of the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members. Requires the Governor to appoint the members with the advice and consent of the Senate. Retains requirements that members be county residents, registered voters, and individuals of high character and business capacity. Establishes that the initial terms for the two additional members begin July 1, 2026. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Senate; Worcester County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners; prospective board appointees; alcoholic beverage licensees in Worcester County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Worcester County expenditures increase by $4,200 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to pay salaries for two new board members. State revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the membership of the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five, requiring the Governor to appoint two additional members with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and managing the appointment process for state and local boards and commissions, which will include the two new seats on the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal Grant Program within the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Requires the Commission to administer the program. Directs the program to award grants to minorities residing in historically redlined neighborhoods and underrepresented communities. Supports recipients with the goal of pursuing Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal training. Aims to close appraisal gaps in those communities and diversify the appraisal field.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Minority residents in historically redlined neighborhoods and underrepresented communities seeking to become real estate appraisers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2027, including an estimated $50,000 in one-time computer programming costs in FY 2027 and an illustrative $88,000 annually for grant awards and licensing fees based on 10 recipients per year. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor may increase minimally beginning in FY 2028 from appraiser licensing fees. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program within the Maryland Higher Education Commission and requires the commission to administer the program and award grants.

The Department of Labor houses the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors, which licenses real estate appraisers and may see a minimal increase in special fund licensing revenues from grant recipients.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits applying sewage sludge with regulated PFAS concentrations of 50 parts per billion or more to agricultural or marginal land. Restricts applying sludge with regulated PFAS concentrations between 25 and 50 parts per billion starting October 1, 2028. Authorizes generators to commingle sewage sludge for up to two years to reduce PFAS levels below 25 parts per billion. Requires generators exceeding 25 parts per billion of PFAS to complete source tracking studies and develop five-year mitigation plans. Authorizes local jurisdictions and pretreatment authorities to establish pretreatment standards and set rates and fees for industrial users.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Sewage sludge generators, publicly owned treatment works, industrial wastewater dischargers, local pretreatment authorities, and owners and operators of agricultural or marginal land
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $248,100 in FY 2027 for three new positions, with ongoing personnel and operational costs increasing in subsequent years. Beginning in FY 2029, local government expenditures and nonbudgeted state expenditures may increase significantly for sewage sludge testing, mitigation, or alternative disposal. Local revenues may increase from rates and fees imposed on industrial users.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations, establishing monitoring protocols and reporting levels, providing technical assistance to sewage sludge generators and local jurisdictions, reviewing and approving mitigation plans, and evaluating pretreatment controls for industrial users.

MES is explicitly defined in statute as a sewage sludge generator and operates approximately 90 wastewater treatment plants across Maryland. The bill will impact MES operations by requiring compliance with PFAS testing, monitoring frequencies, and potential mitigation measures, leading to potential increases in nonbudgeted expenditures and contract revenues.

Under the Maryland Environment Article provisions governing sewage sludge, MDE cannot adopt regulations dealing with the land application of sewage sludge without the approval of MDA. Because the bill establishes strict new limits on applying sewage sludge to agricultural land, MDA has direct regulatory and policy oversight involvement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow up to $27,000,000 through general obligation bonds. Directs bond proceeds to public facility projects, water and sewer infrastructure, and volunteer fire department loans. Permits borrowing via installment purchase obligations to acquire agricultural land and woodland preservation easements. Prohibits any bond issue from maturing later than 30 years from its issuance date. Requires the County to levy annual ad valorem taxes sufficient to pay bond principal and interest. Exempts the bonds, interest, and derived income from all State, county, and municipal taxation.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County property owners and taxpayers, Carroll County volunteer fire departments, and Carroll County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Carroll County revenues increase by up to $27.0 million from bond proceeds. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $2.0 million annually over a 20-year period. There is no state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill exempts the Carroll County public facilities bonds, the interest payable on them, and any income derived from them from all State taxation. As the State's principal tax collection and revenue enforcement agency, the Comptroller oversees the administration of state tax exemptions, although the bill has no direct state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections to deny commercial licenses or permits for unpaid personal property taxes. Applies this authority to both initial permit issuances and renewals within Carroll County. Prohibits denial if the applicant submits satisfactory evidence disputing the unpaid tax amount. Authorizes the office to grant the license or permit once the applicant proves payment of the taxes. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial license and permit applicants in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Carroll County operations and finances are not materially affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes buyers to obtain Comptroller approval to issue multiple points of use certificates for digital codes, products, or taxable services. Requires participating buyers to maintain a sales and use tax account and pay all undisputed taxes. Establishes that buyer authorizations remain valid for at least two years unless revoked or suspended. Requires vendors to verify certificate authenticity and relieves compliant vendors of tax collection obligations. Directs authorized buyers to remit applicable taxes directly based on apportioned use.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and vendors of digital codes, digital products, and taxable data and information technology services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $183,400 in FY 2027 for two financial compliance auditors and one-time tax collection system programming, increasing to $207,000 by FY 2031. General fund revenues face a potential indeterminate decrease due to reduced audit access and compliance verification. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering the sales and use tax. Under the bill, the Comptroller must establish the registration and authorization process for buyers issuing multiple points of use (MPU) certificates, manage denials and revocations, publish the required forms and online application systems, and conduct audit and compliance reviews. The fiscal note identifies direct general fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office for personnel and system programming.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Washington County Salary Study Commission. Replaces the Cumberland Valley Associated Builders and Contractors, Inc. member with a Washington County Home Builders Association, Inc. member. Requires the County Commissioners of Washington County to appoint the individual recommended by the organization. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Washington County; Washington County Salary Study Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington County Home Builders Association, Inc.; Cumberland Valley Associated Builders and Contractors, Inc.; Washington County Salary Study Commission; Washington County public officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State operations or finances, and no material effect on Washington County operations or finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Montgomery County Public Schools to identify dollar amounts of school meal food procured in the 2026–2027 school year. Applies to food procured from certified local farms and certified Chesapeake invasive species providers. Mandates publishing that procurement data on the school system's website by September 1, 2027. Requires the school system to set target increases for five designated school years using the baseline data. Requires a plan to meet target increases in coordination with the Office of Food Systems Resilience and public input.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Public Schools; Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County Public Schools students and staff, certified local farms, and certified Chesapeake invasive species providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Montgomery County Public Schools expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 due to staffing, one-time information technology tracking costs, and potentially higher food procurement costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references and builds upon the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program and the Jane Lawton Farm-to-School Program administered by MDA, which is responsible for certifying the local farms and invasive species providers from which Montgomery County Public Schools must track and increase procurement.

MSDE oversees the state's 24 public school systems. While the bill specifically mandates reporting and procurement targets for Montgomery County Public Schools under the Education Article without direct state fiscal impact, MSDE holds broad oversight authority over local school systems.

The bill incorporates statutory definitions concerning certified Chesapeake invasive species harvested from Maryland waterways and licensed seafood dealers under the Natural Resources Article, connecting to DNR's fisheries management and aquatic nuisance species programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the deadline to prepare and file a certificate of birth from five to 12 calendar days. Requires attending clinicians to provide required medical information and the birth date within 12 calendar days. Applies the 12-day filing timeframe to births in institutions, out-of-institution births, and common carrier births. Authorizes filing within 10 days if a parent notifies the filer on the Secretary's form. Requires parental notification as soon as practicable, but not later than five days after the birth.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: parents of newborns, attending clinicians (physicians, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, and nurse midwives), and administrative heads of birth institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: None. The procedural changes do not directly affect State or local governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory timeframe for completing and filing birth certificates, which are submitted to and administered by the Maryland Department of Health's Division of Vital Records, and requires the Secretary of Health to provide related forms.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to notify local health departments within 24 hours after initiating nursing home complaint investigations. Requires the Department to consult and coordinate with local health departments on investigations to the extent practicable. Clarifies that local health departments are not required to assume nursing home oversight responsibilities. Establishes the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative and a task force to evaluate nursing homes and assisted living programs. Directs the task force to report preliminary findings by December 1, 2027, and final recommendations by December 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed nursing homes, assisted living programs, residents of long-term care facilities and their families, local health departments, and healthcare frontline workers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government operations can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, resulting in no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including notifying and coordinating with local health departments during nursing home investigations, staffing the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative task force, and serving on the task force through multiple leadership officials.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission is a statutory member of the task force, and the task force is specifically mandated to collaborate with MHCC on the use and sharing of available data and expertise for oversight and quality monitoring.

The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is designated as a member of the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative task force, addressing issues directly affecting care and quality of life for older adults in nursing homes and assisted living programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory task force under the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative to study quality standards, workforce issues, and oversight of nursing homes and assisted living facilities through June 2029.
The Attorney General (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative task force.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative task force.
The task force is required to report its interim and final findings and recommendations on nursing home and assisted living quality improvement to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2030. Adds the Blue Catfish Gill Net Program to the pilot program components. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to submit annual activity reports starting by December 1, 2026. Mandates reporting findings and recommendations to the Senate Education, Energy, and the Environment Committee and House Environment and Transportation Committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: commercial finfish harvesters and for-hire fishing operators targeting blue catfish in the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) with implementing, updating, and extending the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program, incorporating the Blue Catfish Gill Net Program, and submitting annual progress reports to legislative committees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires DNR to establish and coordinate the pilot program with the Invasive Catfish Advisory Committee, an advisory body within the executive branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals margin requirements for printed deeds and other instruments offered for recordation. Removes the requirement for a 3-inch top margin and 1-inch side margins on recorded documents. Requires each circuit court clerk to date every change or correction made to the general alphabetical index. Mandates that the clerk record the date on the horizontal line where the change or correction occurs. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals and entities filing deeds and land instruments for recordation; clerks of the circuit courts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters requirements for land records and instruments offered for recordation, specifically repealing margin requirements and mandating how clerks of the circuit court must date changes or corrections in the general alphabetical index. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, operational, and technological support to the circuit courts and clerks who maintain these records.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund. Requires approval from the Board of Public Works before any transfer occurs. Prohibits transfers that would reduce the Revenue Stabilization Account balance below 5% of estimated General Fund revenues. Adds transferred funds to the statutory composition of the State Disaster Recovery Fund. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Board of Public Works; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments and State agencies seeking or receiving disaster recovery assistance; disaster-affected communities in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct impact on State or local finances because the transfer authority is permissive. If transfers occur, special fund revenues for the State Disaster Recovery Fund increase while interest earnings in the Revenue Stabilization Account decrease minimally. General fund expenditures could increase in subsequent years to meet mandatory reserve replenishment targets if the account balance falls below 7.5% of estimated general fund revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account (Rainy Day Fund) to the State Disaster Recovery Fund, subject to approval from the Board of Public Works.
MDEM administers the State Disaster Recovery Fund (SDRF), which will directly receive potential transfers of funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account to finance disaster recovery operations.
The bill requires the approval of the Board of Public Works before any transfer of funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund can take place.

DBM is responsible for state budget development, fiscal planning, and monitoring the State Reserve Fund, including the Revenue Stabilization Account and subsequent required appropriations if fund levels decline.
The State Treasurer manages and invests state funds, including the Revenue Stabilization Account, and serves on the Board of Public Works, which must approve any fund transfer.
The Comptroller acts as the state's chief financial officer overseeing state accounts and is a member of the Board of Public Works tasked with approving the fund transfers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study Maryland buildings more than 40 years old containing condominiums. Mandates that the study determine the number of qualifying buildings and condominium units within each building. Directs the study to assess the average age and annual income of unit owners in each building. Requires the study to determine recent reserve study dates and reserve fund balances compared to required amounts. Requires the Department to report its findings to the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium unit owners and condominium councils of unit owners in buildings more than 40 years old
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2027 only for contractual services to complete the study. There is no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 956 directly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to conduct a comprehensive study on buildings in the State that are more than 40 years old and contain condominiums, and report its findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026. The fiscal note estimates a $75,000 general fund expenditure for DHCD in FY 2027 to procure contractual services to complete the study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each local school system to designate a point of contact for cybersecurity communications. Mandates local school systems to comply with State minimum cybersecurity standards beginning in 2027. Directs each local school system to conduct a cybersecurity maturity assessment every two years. Requires biennial compliance certification to the Office of Security Management starting June 30, 2027. Requires the Office of Security Management to annually review and update State minimum cybersecurity standards as necessary. Directs the Department of Information Technology, on request, to advise local school systems on compliance and remediation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Office of Security Management
qa_results.stakeholders: local school systems in Maryland, local school IT and cybersecurity personnel, and public school students and staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources with no revenue impact. Local school system expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2027 for technology upgrades, contracted services, and staff needed to achieve compliance, though total statewide costs are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT, through its Office of Security Management and the State Chief Information Security Officer, is the primary implementing agency. The bill requires DoIT to annually review and update State minimum cybersecurity standards, receive contact designations and biennial compliance certifications from local school systems, and advise local school systems on compliance, assessments, and remediation.

MSDE oversees the 24 local school systems across Maryland. The bill amends the Education Article to establish cybersecurity compliance, point-of-contact designation, and biennial assessment mandates across all local school systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters restrictions on appointing noncitizens as personal representatives in estate administration. Authorizes registers of wills and courts to grant letters of administration to lawful permanent residents of the United States. Permits individuals who are neither citizens nor permanent residents to receive letters under specified conditions. Requires those individuals to be domiciled in the United States. Requires those individuals to be the decedent's spouse, ancestor, descendant, or sibling. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Registers of Wills; Orphans' Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Noncitizens and lawful permanent residents seeking appointment as personal representatives, along with decedents' families and heirs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory qualifications under Estates and Trusts § 5-105 for individuals to whom a register of wills may grant letters of administration to serve as personal representatives of an estate.

The bill affects the granting of letters in judicial probate proceedings handled within Maryland's court system (specifically Orphans' Courts), which the Administrative Office of the Courts administratively and operationally supports.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires owners of weights and measures used for retail vehicle electricity sales to conspicuously display local contact information. Mandates that all electricity sold at retail as vehicle fuel be measured and sold in kilowatt-hours. Limits customer charges during a charging session strictly to the kilowatt-hours of electricity dispensed. Authorizes the owner or possessor to charge a fixed or time-based fee for related services. Requires any service fee to be applied at charging conclusion and itemized on the receipt.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Retail electric vehicle fuel sellers, electric vehicle charging station operators, and electric vehicle drivers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct, material impact on State finances or local government operations, as the bill largely codifies existing standards and regulatory requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 11 of the Agriculture Article governing weights and measures, which is directly administered and enforced by the Maryland Department of Agriculture's Weights and Measures Program.
The Public Service Commission regulates retail electric service and public utilities in Maryland and provided information regarding the regulation and sale of electricity as vehicle fuel.
The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state energy policy and electric vehicle infrastructure initiatives, and served as an information source for the legislation.
The Comptroller regulates motor fuel industries and tax collection, was considered in earlier versions of the bill regarding retail pricing, and was consulted for the fiscal note.
The Department of General Services manages state-owned facilities, vehicle fleets, and electric vehicle charging infrastructure across state properties, and was consulted for the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund to advance agricultural fairs and education. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $200,000 to the Fund in the State budget. Requires the Comptroller to pay an annual grant of $100,000 to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc. Requires the Comptroller to pay an annual grant of $100,000 to the Maryland FFA Association. Repeals a $75,000 annual grant to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc., from the horse racing Special Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc.; Maryland FFA Association; youth participating in agricultural education; horse racing special fund grantees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $200,000 annually beginning in FY 2028 due to the mandated appropriation, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures for grant distributions. Horse racing special fund revenues increase by $75,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to the repealed grant distribution, making those funds available for other existing statutory grantees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller to administer the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund, account for its monies, and disburse the annual statutory grants to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation and the Maryland FFA Association, as well as administer adjustments to the horse racing Special Fund distributions.

The bill codifies the new grant fund within the Agriculture Article of the Maryland Annotated Code to promote and advance agricultural education, youth agricultural programs, and agricultural fairs across the state.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established special fund separately, manage its investments, and exempt its interest earnings from accruing to the General Fund.
The bill creates a mandated annual General Fund appropriation of $200,000 beginning in fiscal year 2028, impacting state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning managed by DBM.
The bill imposes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $200,000 to the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund in the state budget bill.
The bill amends the Business Regulation Article concerning distributions from the horse racing Special Fund, which is regulated under the Maryland Racing Commission within the Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and acting third parties from advertising prostitution, escort, or sexual services. Bans massage therapy advertisements on websites known for sexual services and ads indicating sexual activity is included. Requires advertisements to display the provider's full licensed name and license or registration number. Exempts multi-practitioner businesses from listing each provider unless individual names are specified. Mandates removal of noncompliant physical signs or billboards visible to the public before May 1, 2027. Directs the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to adopt regulations defining prohibited language and reporting procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, massage therapy businesses, third-party advertisers, and massage therapy clients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill and adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates advertising for licensed massage therapists and registered massage practitioners, requiring the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners—an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health—to adopt regulations defining prohibited language and establish violation reporting procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of Human Services to establish and maintain a Guardianship Assistance Program providing monetary and medical assistance. Establishes eligibility criteria for guardians who execute voluntary assistance agreements following six months of foster care placement. Allows approved assistance to continue until age 21 for qualifying individuals participating in education, work, or job training. Authorizes local departments of social services to terminate assistance if certain violent or registered sex offenders reside in the home. Establishes the State Foster Youth Ombudsman within the Department of Human Services to advocate for youth in out-of-home care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Youth in foster care and out-of-home care, legal guardians of minor children, caregivers and adoptive parents, and local departments of social services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $37,500 in FY 2028 and by $50,000 annually thereafter to fund the State Foster Youth Ombudsman position, assuming a vacant position is repurposed; costs would rise to $120,000 in FY 2028 and $154,000 annually if a new position is created instead. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 980 directly tasks the Secretary of Human Services and DHS with establishing and maintaining the Guardianship Assistance Program, adopting implementing regulations, and creating and staffing the State Foster Youth Ombudsman position within the department.

The bill requires creating a new State Foster Youth Ombudsman position within the Management Service of the State Personnel Management System, which requires DBM approval for position classification and the repurposing of a vacant Position Identification Number (PIN).

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the hours of sale for Class HC beer and wine licenses in Harford County. Permits 6-day and 7-day license holders to sell beer and wine for on-premises consumption until 11 p.m. Replaces the prior closing time of 9 p.m. while maintaining the 1 p.m. opening time. Applies to qualifying health club facilities that feature swimming pools or pickleball courts. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of Class HC beer and wine licenses in Harford County and health club patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. The bill does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers related excise taxes. While local licensing and hours of sale are primarily overseen by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners, the bill touches on alcohol regulation within the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor. Requires sellers of travel and independent agents to annually file proof of professional liability and errors and omissions insurance. Mandates coverage of at least $1,000,000 and sets an initial $300 annual filing fee. Requires each seller of travel to annually file a list of affiliated independent agents. Prohibits receiving payment for travel services unless the provider meets all annual filing requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: sellers of travel; independent travel agents; consumers purchasing travel services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by at least $99,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 from filing fees. State expenditures increase by $106,513 in FY 2027 ($101,000 special funds and $5,513 general funds) for one executive director and start-up costs, with ongoing special fund expenditures averaging around $100,000 annually.
