Minimal increase in general fund revenues from interest earnings. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing and regulating agency under the bill. It is responsible for administering the newly established Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund, collecting annual filing fees, verifying insurance filings from sellers of travel and independent agents, establishing fee structures, adopting regulations, and conducting enforcement.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Labor to pay all collected registration fees to the Comptroller, who is statutorily directed to distribute those fees into the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund.

The bill specifies that the new special fund is subject to audit under § 2-1220 of the State Government Article, and the fiscal note notes that the Office of Legislative Audits can incorporate the fund into its regular audits of MD Labor using existing resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to notify a filer if a charter document is rejected. Mandates the Department record a corrected charter document as of the original filing date if refiled within 30 days. Authorizes boards of registered open-end investment companies to act without a meeting by majority consent under specified conditions. Authorizes corporate boards, bankruptcy trustees, and receivers to execute bankruptcy relief orders without stockholder approval. Repeals misdemeanor penalties for officers and agents of foreign corporations doing business in Maryland without registering or qualifying.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland corporations, registered open-end investment companies, foreign corporations doing business in Maryland and their officers, limited partnerships and general partnerships, and corporate charter document filers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Department of Assessments and Taxation operations can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal misdemeanor offense for officers and agents of unregistered foreign corporations and amends the standards under which a foreign corporation may maintain a civil suit in Maryland courts, directly touching judicial proceedings administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class 7 micro-brewery license in the 46th district. Authorizes the Board to transfer a Class B-D-7 license from the 40th district into the 46th district. Authorizes certain Class D license holders in the 46th district to apply for a seven-day sales privilege. Requires the Board to establish a standard template for neighborhood association memoranda of understanding by January 1, 2027. Requires the Board to adopt regulations establishing tiered penalties for license violations. Extends expiration dates for three specified alcoholic beverages licenses to July 1, 2027, for renewal or transfer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants in Baltimore City, local neighborhood associations in Baltimore City, and patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Baltimore City finances and operations are not materially affected; revenues collected from the $15,000 one-time fee for a seven-day Class D sales privilege are dedicated to enforcing required memoranda of understanding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters alcoholic beverages regulations and licensing in Baltimore City, including provisions regarding manufacturer/wholesaler donations and tax remittance. Although implementation is managed locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and there is no direct state fiscal effect, the Comptroller oversees state alcohol regulation and excise tax collection.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to produce more than one brand of alcoholic beverage. Repeals the requirement that a licensee maintain only one brand at any one time for each product. Allows the licensee to manufacture or rectify product for another brand or entity. Prohibits the licensee from manufacturing or rectifying more than 31,000 gallons of product each calendar year for another brand or entity. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of Class 9 limited distillery licenses and alcoholic beverage brands contracting for manufacturing or rectifying services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters regulations and production limits governing Class 9 limited distillery licenses for manufacturing and rectifying spirits. According to the agency summary, the Comptroller is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state excise taxes on alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Administrator, Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors to order arrests at polling places. Requires on-duty police officers at polling places to obey orders issued by these officials. Allows political committees and specified independent spenders to designate accredited challengers, watchers, and canvass observers. Expands the designation and presence of accredited challengers and watchers to early voting centers. Prohibits challengers and watchers from physically handling voting equipment. Requires designating persons to submit certificates of accredited challengers or watchers to local boards before entry.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections; State Administrator of Elections; local election directors
qa_results.stakeholders: Election judges, local election directors, police officers on duty at polling places, accredited and nonaccredited challengers and watchers, canvass observers, candidates, political parties, political committees, and independent spenders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Election Law Article to govern the authority of the State Administrator of Elections, Deputy State Administrator, and local election officials at polling places, early voting centers, and counting centers. It also tasks the State Board with prescribing forms for accredited challengers and watchers.

The bill explicitly requires police officers on duty at polling places to obey orders from the State Administrator, the Deputy State Administrator, or local election directors to maintain peace or effectuate arrests, providing statutory protection for officers executing such orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits nursing facilities from involuntarily transferring or discharging a resident to temporary housing or unconfirmed receiving facilities. Requires discharge notices to provide contact details for hearing requests, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, and Disability Rights Maryland. Repeals the shortened notice exception previously permitted when a resident resided in a facility for under 30 days. Establishes revised notice requirements and waiting periods ranging from seven to 30 days when transfer details change. Requires post-discharge care plans to identify the resident's post-discharge address and provide a safe, secure, and sustainable environment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of Maryland nursing facilities, nursing facility operators and staff, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, and Disability Rights Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates nursing facilities, prepares the standardized involuntary discharge notice form, receives copies of all involuntary discharge notices, and adopts regulations establishing requirements for post-discharge plans of care and hearing procedures.

The Department of Aging oversees the statewide Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, which is required under the bill to be provided with written notice of any proposed involuntary discharge or transfer and whose contact information must be provided to residents.
Administrative Law Judges within the Office of Administrative Hearings conduct hearings and issue binding orders regarding proposed involuntary transfers and discharges of nursing facility residents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a fiduciary institution to delay or deny disbursements from an account of an eligible adult if financial exploitation is suspected. Requires the institution to notify adult protective services, law enforcement, or a State's Attorney within four business days. Directs the institution to send written notice of delays to authorized account parties, excluding suspected exploiters. Authorizes institutions to extend disbursement delays and notify designated trusted contacts under specified conditions. Requires fiduciary institutions to provide relevant financial records to investigating authorities upon referral or request. Grants fiduciary institutions civil and administrative immunity when acting in good faith and exercising reasonable care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services; State's Attorneys; law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents at least 65 years old and vulnerable adults; fiduciary institutions including banks, credit unions, and savings associations; trusted contacts and authorized account parties; adult protective services staff and law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local social service agencies and law enforcement agencies can likely handle the bill's requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the Adult Protective Services (APS) program housed within local departments of social services overseen by DHS. Fiduciary institutions are required to report suspected financial exploitation to APS, provide relevant financial records, and APS may request or order extensions or terminations of disbursement delays.

The bill amends the Financial Institutions Article and governs fiduciary institutions, which fall under the regulatory and supervisory authority of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The bill authorizes fiduciary institutions to notify law enforcement agencies of suspected financial exploitation, provides law enforcement access to confidential financial records, and allows law enforcement to request extensions of disbursement delays.

The bill authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction within the Judicial Branch to issue orders terminating or extending disbursement delays related to suspected vulnerable adult financial exploitation.

The bill establishes statutory protections against the financial exploitation of adults aged 65 and older and vulnerable adults, aligning closely with the Department of Aging's mission to advocate for the rights and welfare of older Marylanders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county or municipality to establish a multidisciplinary and multiagency local suicide fatality review team. Permits two or more counties to establish a single multicounty local team under a memorandum of understanding. Requires local teams to meet at least quarterly, collect data, and coordinate with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee. Exempts team meetings discussing individual suicide cases from the Open Meetings Act. Designates team records and proceedings as confidential, privileged, and exempt from disclosure under the Maryland Public Information Act. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to a $500 fine and 90 days imprisonment for unauthorized disclosures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Suicide Fatality Review Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: County and municipal governments, local health departments, health care providers, law enforcement agencies, and individuals affected by suicide
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational impacts can likely be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Local government and local health department expenditures may increase indeterminately beginning in fiscal 2027, estimated at $30,000 to $50,000 per jurisdiction that chooses to establish a review team.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is authorized to adopt regulations establishing protocols, procedures, and data security standards for local suicide fatality review teams. Local health officers play a primary role in forming and appointing members to the teams, and the teams coordinate closely with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly integrates local teams with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee, requiring local teams to follow its guidance, establish operating protocols with it, and submit case reports, data, and policy recommendations.

The bill specifies that the director of the local department of social services (or their designee) must be included on local review teams, and local teams are authorized to request and receive confidential social services records.
The bill requires local suicide fatality review teams to include county superintendents of schools (or their designees), directly involving local public school leadership overseen by MSDE.
Local review team membership includes State law enforcement officers, and local teams are authorized to request and examine police investigative data regarding suicide fatalities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Local teams must include emergency medical services providers from the county and may request records or statements from first responders involved with decedents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide expedited Medicaid eligibility determinations for certain individuals relocating to Maryland. Applies to qualifying dependents whose caretaker died or became incapacitated after receiving out-of-state waiver services for ten years. Requires the dependent's Maryland family member to have resided in the State for at least two years. Mandates that the Department complete each expedited eligibility review within 60 business days after receiving a complete application. Places eligible individuals into the crisis resolution category for waiver services based on their prior out-of-state care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities who relocate to Maryland after losing an out-of-state caretaker, and their Maryland family members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can likely implement the expedited determinations with existing resources, though redirection of staff may delay other applications. If application volume expands, costs could increase by approximately $80,000 annually for one additional staff position split between general and federal funds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (specifically the Developmental Disabilities Administration) is directly responsible for administering the Community Pathways waiver and implementing the expedited eligibility determinations and priority placements required by the bill.

As the principal state agency responsible for coordinating and improving the delivery of services and policies for individuals with disabilities across Maryland, the bill aligns closely with the department's core advocacy and interagency policy focus.

qa_results.bill_summary: Voids noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in employment contracts concerning certain licensed architects. Applies to employers employing more than 30 qualifying workers on the architect's first day of employment. Requires a majority of those initial workers to report in Maryland or work remotely within the State. Invalidates provisions if the employer lacks an in-state principal place of business on the enforcement date. Also invalidates provisions if the employer lacks a majority Maryland workforce on that enforcement date. Applies only to employment contracts executed on or after October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed architects and employers of licensed architects with more than 30 employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1016 amends Title 3 of the Labor and Employment Article regarding noncompete and conflict of interest clauses, specifically applying protections to licensed architects whose employers relocate out of state. The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for enforcing state labor laws and regulating occupational licensing for professions, including architects.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State and local governments from approving the construction or operation of private detention facilities. Prohibits private entities from operating or occupying real property as a detention facility. Excludes licensed health care facilities, residential child care programs, and child placement agencies meeting specified treatment purposes. Authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil enforcement actions and seek injunctive relief. Subjects violating private entities to a civil penalty not exceeding $10,000 for each day of violation. Establishes contingent zoning and public notice requirements if a court invalidates the detention facility ban.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Private entities seeking to construct or operate detention facilities, local governments, and individuals held in civil or criminal custody
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government operations or finances. Indeterminate potential increase in State general fund revenues if civil penalties up to $10,000 per day are assessed against violating entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions in court to enforce the prohibition on private detention facilities and seek injunctive relief and civil penalties. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General is tasked with notifying the Department of Legislative Services if the primary provisions are declared unenforceable in court.

The bill provides for civil actions, injunctive relief, and daily civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation to be adjudicated in State courts, which could result in a minimal operational and caseload impact for the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly amends the Correctional Services Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland regarding the statutory definitions, approval, and operation of detention facilities within the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adopts the salary recommendations of the Governor's Salary Commission for the Governor and Lieutenant Governor. Establishes the Governor's annual salary at $195,000 in year one, $202,000 in years two and three, and $210,000 in year four. Sets the Lieutenant Governor's annual salary at $175,000 in year one, $180,000 in years two and three, and $185,000 in year four. Applies the new salaries to the four-year term of office beginning January 20, 2027. Directs the Department of Legislative Services to forward copies to the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, and Secretary of Budget and Management.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Governor and Lieutenant Governor
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $6,800 in FY 2028, $13,600 in FY 2029, $20,900 in FY 2030, and $28,300 in FY 2031 to cover salary increases and associated fringe benefits. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HJ 5 directly establishes the annual compensation and salary schedule for the Governor of Maryland for the 4-year term beginning January 20, 2027.
HJ 5 directly sets the annual salary schedule for the Lieutenant Governor of Maryland for the 4-year term beginning January 20, 2027.

As the state's principal budget and personnel agency, DBM must incorporate the adjusted executive salary figures and fringe benefits into future state budget planning, and the resolution explicitly directs that a copy be forwarded to the Secretary of Budget and Management.
The State Treasurer serves as a constitutional member of the Governor's Salary Commission which evaluated, determined, and submitted these salary recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases judicial salaries by $5,900 annually across fiscal years 2027 through 2030. Applies phased salary increases to judges of the Supreme Court, Appellate Court, Circuit Courts, and District Court. Grants an annual $7,500 stipend to the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland. Authorizes an annual $7,500 stipend for circuit court and District Court administrative judges.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Judges across the Supreme Court of Maryland, Appellate Court of Maryland, Circuit Courts, and District Court; administrative judges; retired recalled judges; magistrates; the State Prosecutor; the Public Defender; Workers' Compensation Commission members; and county officials whose salaries tie to judicial pay
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.3 million and special fund expenditures increase by $63,325 in FY 2027, with total annual State expenditure increases reaching $12.0 million by FY 2030. Local government expenditures increase minimally in counties that index local official salaries to judicial pay.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution directly sets the compensation, annual stipends, and salary schedules for all judges across the Maryland Judiciary, which the Administrative Office of the Courts administratively supports and funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: By statute, the salary of the Public Defender is tied to that of a circuit court judge, resulting in an automatic salary and expenditure increase for the agency.
By statute, the salary of the State Prosecutor is tied to that of a circuit court judge, resulting in an automatic salary and expenditure increase for the agency.
The salaries of the commissioners of the Workers' Compensation Commission are tied by statute to those of District Court judges, resulting in an increase in special fund expenditures for the agency.

The agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Judicial Retirement System, which experiences changes in actuarial assumptions and pension liabilities resulting from the revised judicial salary schedules.
DBM oversees the state budget and personnel allocations, which must account for the general and special fund expenditure increases across impacted state positions and agencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Highway Administration to approve, deny, or return speed monitoring system applications within 120 days of receipt. Deems an application approved if the Administration fails to act within the 120-day timeframe. Applies to county requests to operate speed monitoring systems on State highways within municipal corporations. Prohibits a program administrator or contractor from submitting more than 10 applications during any 30-day period. Requires contractors to consult with the program administrator before and after submitting an application.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland counties, municipal corporations, local program administrators, and speed monitoring system contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact. The State Highway Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources because internal processes already conform to the 120-day timeframe. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Highway Administration approve, deny, or return an application for the use of a speed monitoring system within 120 days of receipt, deems applications approved if the deadline is missed, and enforces application submission limits.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state highway network, capital projects, and modal administration operations impacted by the statutory application timelines.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for refunds of unearned alcoholic beverages license fees upon license surrender. Requires a refund when a license holder volunteers for or is called into the uniformed services. Replaces statutory references to the armed forces of the United States with the uniformed services. Extends refund eligibility to members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service. Applies the refund requirement to both State-issued and locally issued alcoholic beverages licenses. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; local alcoholic beverages licensing boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders who volunteer for or are called into the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller's office is responsible for collecting state revenues, administering fee payments and refunds, and historically oversees aspects of alcohol regulation and state revenue administration impacted by changes to license fee refund eligibility.

The bill expands eligibility for alcoholic beverage license fee refunds to individuals entering the uniformed services (including NOAA and the Public Health Service). The Department of Veterans & Military Families advocates for and assists service members and was an official information source on the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Entitles Maryland Golden Age Pass holders to free day-use entry at any State park charging service fees. Extends this free day-use entry to everyone in the vehicle when a per-vehicle fee applies. Authorizes pass holders to launch a boat at any State park without paying a boat launch fee. Expands half-price overnight camping privileges to apply Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Park Service
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Golden Age Pass holders age 62 or older and vehicle passengers visiting State parks with pass holders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies current regulations and Maryland Park Service practices into statute.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs fee exemptions and discounts at Maryland State parks, which are managed and operated by the Maryland Park Service under the Department of Natural Resources.

The bill enhances recreational access and fee discounts for Maryland residents aged 62 and older, which aligns with the department's mission to improve the quality of life for older adults, although the department has no direct administrative role.

qa_results.bill_summary: Aligns participant disqualification standards across the Maryland Children's, Disability, and Veterans Service Animal Programs. Defines "direct threat" across all three programs according to the federal Americans with Disabilities Act. Authorizes nonprofit training entities to disqualify participants who present a direct threat to others. Authorizes disqualification of participants who threaten an animal's mental or physical well-being. Authorizes disqualification if a participant does not meet entity training requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of Disabilities; Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: participants in state service animal programs including eligible children, individuals with disabilities, and veterans, as well as participating nonprofit training entities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances as the changes are technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 37 amends the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Children's Service Animal Program, which is established within the Maryland Department of Health, updating the definition of 'direct threat' and participant disqualification criteria.

SB 37 amends the Human Services Article governing the Maryland Disability Service Animal Program housed within the Department of Disabilities, revising statutory disqualification provisions and defining 'direct threat.'

SB 37 amends the State Government Article governing the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program administered by the Department of Veterans & Military Families, aligning participant disqualification standards with federal ADA definitions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an independent cost-driven rate-setting study by June 30, 2028. Directs the Department to review and implement recommendations from the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization. Establishes the Workgroup within the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop cost-based reimbursement methodologies. Covers certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers. Requires the Commission to submit an interim report by January 1, 2028, and annual impact reports thereafter.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Behavioral Health Administration; Medical Care Programs Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, independent outpatient providers, direct care staff, and individuals receiving community-based behavioral health services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $391,974 in FY 2027 ($181,699 in general funds for MDH and $210,275 in special funds for MHCC) and by $356,100 in FY 2028 for contractual staff, data analysis, and actuarial services. Workgroup and study expenses terminate at the end of FY 2028, though MHCC may incur indeterminate ongoing costs for required annual reporting. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department of Health (specifically through the Behavioral Health Administration and Medical Care Programs Administration) conduct an independent behavioral health rate-setting study, administer cost-reporting tools, develop and implement a payment system, and implement recommendations from the newly created workgroup, incurring significant general fund expenditures.

The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Commission, requires the Commission to staff the workgroup and assist MDH with the rate-setting study, and mandates that the Commission submit interim and annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly, resulting in notable special fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization, an advisory body tasked with analyzing outpatient behavioral health cost drivers and developing cost-based rate-setting methodologies.
The bill requires the Workgroup and the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit interim, final, and ongoing annual evaluation reports regarding behavioral health rate methodologies to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to include at least one question on motorcycle safety awareness on driver license examinations. Mandates that the examination question pool include at least five questions related to motorcycle safety awareness. Requires these questions to address motorcycle visibility, proper lane positioning, safe following distances, and crash prevention. Authorizes the Administration to include any other motorcycle safety topic it considers relevant. Applies to examinations administered for an original driver's license or a higher license class.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for Maryland driver's licenses; motorcyclists in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) include at least one question on motorcycle safety awareness on the driver skills examination and establish a question pool containing at least five motorcycle safety awareness questions.
As the parent department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT is directly impacted by changes to driver licensing requirements and statewide transportation safety education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters grounds for discipline across twelve health occupations boards. Authorizes boards to discipline a licensee or deny an application based on actions by specified external entities. Applies to disciplinary action by any branch of the uniformed services or the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Expands disciplinary grounds for naturopathic doctors to include court convictions or discipline from any state or country. Standardizes cross-references to each board's disciplinary statutes.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists; State Board of Dental Examiners; State Board of Dietetic Practice; State Board of Examiners in Optometry; State Board of Pharmacy; State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners; State Board of Physicians; State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners; State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists; State Board of Examiners of Psychologists; State Board of Social Work Examiners; State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants and licensed health professionals regulated by Maryland health occupations boards, including physicians, naturopathic doctors, dentists, dental hygienists, pharmacists, optometrists, physical therapists, podiatrists, psychologists, counselors, social workers, dietitians, and environmental health specialists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The changes are technical and do not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the health occupations licensing boards and committees whose statutory grounds for disciplinary action and license denial are directly amended by this bill.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and disciplinary prosecution support to the various health occupations licensing boards within the Department of Health.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts administrative hearings and adjudicates contested cases involving disciplinary actions and license denials initiated by state health occupations boards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters terminology in the Sheila E. Hixson Behavioral Health Services Matching Grant Program for Service Members and Veterans. Removes the limitation requiring service members to be on active duty. Broadens the definition of eligible individual to include any service member, spouse, child, or stepchild. Expands nonprofit grant eligibility to organizations serving all service members, veterans, or their families. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Service members, their spouses, children, and stepchildren, and local nonprofit organizations providing behavioral health services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected because overall funding for the matching grant program remains unchanged.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Sheila E. Hixson Behavioral Health Services Matching Grant Program for Service Members and Veterans codified under Title 7.5 of the Health - General Article, and will implement the broadened eligibility criteria for grant-funded programs.

The Department of Veterans & Military Families works to assist Maryland's veterans, active-duty service members, and their families in accessing services and benefits, and served as an informational agency for this legislation affecting service members and veterans.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends collective bargaining rights to certain police officers of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission. Applies specifically to officers authorized to make arrests in an official capacity. Excludes officers classified as supervisory, managerial, or confidential under regulations adopted by the Secretary. Allows eligible officers to obtain representation through the State Law Enforcement Officers Labor Alliance. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Police officers of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission authorized to make arrests; State Law Enforcement Officers Labor Alliance
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are minimal and can be absorbed within the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission's existing budget. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) administers collective bargaining for state employees and will be responsible for accrediting eligible Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission police officers into the appropriate bargaining unit.

The Department of Budget and Management serves as the state's central personnel agency, oversees state employee benefits, and represents the Executive Branch in collective bargaining negotiations with employee organizations such as SLEOLA.
The Office of Administrative Hearings is tasked with adjudicating any state employee grievances or contested cases that may stem from extending collective bargaining coverage to these officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of the Environment and the Department of General Services to include veteran notations on public profiles. Extends this profile notation authority to all licensing units within the Maryland Department of Labor. Permits applicants to request the notation and consent to contact from Executive Branch agencies regarding veterans' benefits. Requires applicants to submit acceptable certification of veteran status, including a DD Form 214. Mandates that participating entities transmit information about consenting applicants to requesting Executive Branch agencies. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of General Services; Maryland Department of Labor; health occupations boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Military veterans holding or applying for licenses, certificates, registrations, or State identification cards issued by the Maryland Department of the Environment, Department of General Services, or Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no impact on State revenues and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Department of the Environment to establish a process to include veteran status notations on public profiles for licensed individuals.
The bill directly authorizes the Department of General Services to include notations of veteran status on public profiles associated with state identification cards.
The bill directly authorizes units within the Maryland Department of Labor to include notations indicating veteran status on public profiles of licensees.

The bill references certifications of veteran status obtained from the Department of Veterans and Military Families to verify veteran status, and involves connecting consenting individuals to veterans' benefits.

The bill makes a technical amendment to the Health Occupations Article regarding health occupations boards (which operate under the Department of Health) and veteran status notations on licenses and public profiles.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Executive Director of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems to coordinate minimum emergency vehicle standards. Directs coordination with the Jurisdictional Emergency Medical Services Operating Program. Specifies that minimum equipment, supplies, and medications must include items needed for early childhood care, including neonatal care. Mandates that these supplies and medications be available on emergency medical services vehicles statewide. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Jurisdictional Emergency Medical Services Operating Programs, emergency medical services personnel, and pediatric and neonatal emergency patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources with no effect on revenues. Local governmental operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory duties of the Executive Director of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), requiring the agency to coordinate minimum equipment, supplies, and medications—specifically including those for early childhood and neonatal care—to be available on emergency medical services vehicles statewide.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands exemptions from State park day-use entry fees and per-vehicle fees to certain former Maryland National Guard members. Defines accepted entrance documents to include veteran ID cards, State-issued licenses, or department-approved identification. Requires former Maryland National Guard members to have been discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable. Authorizes qualifying individuals and vehicles carrying them to enter State parks fee-free upon presenting accepted entrance documents. Clarifies that the exemption does not apply to other park facility use service fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterans and former Maryland National Guard members discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the provisions align with current Department of Natural Resources practice. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources manages Maryland's state parks and is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering entry fee exemptions and determining acceptable identification documents.
The bill directly benefits honorably discharged or non-dishonorably released former members of the Maryland National Guard by granting them fee-free access to State parks.
The department is responsible for advocating for veterans and military service members and connecting them to state benefits and privileges, including park fee exemptions.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the Maryland National Guard, the Adjutant General's constituency of former service members is directly granted access privileges under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual reporting date for the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit from November 30 to October 1. Requires the Attorney General to submit the report annually to the Governor and the General Assembly. Specifies that the report must cover the Unit's activities during the previous fiscal year. Requires reporting on actions taken by the Department of the Environment or the Department of Natural Resources. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland Department of the Environment, and Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State operations or finances. There is no effect on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the annual reporting requirements and deadline for the Office of the Attorney General's Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit.

The report mandated by the bill must include actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations of the Unit, and aligns the reporting date with MDE's enforcement reporting.
The report mandated by the bill must include actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to findings and recommendations of the Unit.
The Governor is a statutory recipient of the altered annual report submitted by the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts sales of construction material and warehousing equipment used solely in a Washington County target redevelopment area from the sales and use tax. Defines the target redevelopment area as real property known as the Mount Aetna Technology Park. Requires buyers to present Comptroller-issued evidence of eligibility to vendors. Mandates that buyers maintain tax savings records for at least three years. Requires annual reporting by buyers to the Comptroller and by the Comptroller to the General Assembly. Sunsets the exemption on June 30, 2036, after a 10-year period.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Businesses and purchasers acquiring construction material or warehousing equipment for use in the Mount Aetna Technology Park in Washington County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount in fiscal 2027 through 2036 depending on the volume of eligible purchases. State expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the sales and use tax exemption, issuing evidence of eligibility certificates to buyers, collecting annual exemption reports from buyers, and submitting an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly detailing foregone tax revenue.
The bill requires the Comptroller to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing the aggregate amount of sales and use tax not paid as a result of the target redevelopment area exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of active service across State law to include active military, naval, air, or space service. Extends eligibility for property tax exemptions and credits to qualified Space Force members, disabled veterans, and surviving spouses. Includes qualified Space Force veterans within the definition of a qualified veteran employee for the Job Creation Tax Credit. Requires applicants to provide discharge certificates and federal disability certifications to receive specified property tax benefits. Applies the Job Creation Tax Credit provisions to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Applies property tax provisions to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Department of Commerce; Comptroller of Maryland; Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Active service members, disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of the U.S. Space Force, as well as businesses hiring qualified veterans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Section 9–901 of the State Government Article, which governs the Department of Veterans and Military Families, adding Space Force service to the uniform definition of active military service and updating definitions for veterans and military families.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article regarding the Job Creation Tax Credit administered by the Department of Commerce, updating the definition of 'qualified veteran employee' to encompass Space Force veterans.
The Comptroller administers state income taxes and processes the Job Creation Tax Credit claimed by employers hiring qualified veterans.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Prince George’s Community College to conduct a comprehensive feasibility study and program design assessment. The assessment evaluates establishing an aerospace systems technology workforce training program and an aviation systems technology workforce training program. Mandates consultation with private sector employers, the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission, the Maryland Department of Labor, and workforce entities. Requires Prince George’s Community College to report findings, recommended credential models, and implementation plans by December 1, 2027. Mandates a $100,000 state appropriation in fiscal year 2028 to complete the study.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's Community College
qa_results.stakeholders: Students at Prince George's Community College and private sector employers in aerospace, aviation, engineering, defense, and advanced manufacturing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in fiscal 2027 and $100,000 in fiscal 2028 due to funding in the fiscal 2027 budget and the bill's fiscal 2028 mandated appropriation. Prince George's Community College revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly across both fiscal years to conduct the study.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires Prince George's Community College to consult with the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission under the Department of Commerce in conducting the feasibility study and program design assessment.

The bill explicitly requires Prince George's Community College to consult with the Maryland Department of Labor regarding workforce demand, labor markets, and work-based learning opportunities like apprenticeships.

As noted in the fiscal and policy note, the Maryland Higher Education Commission is expected to consult on the feasibility study regarding degree, credit certificate, and noncredit credential structures.
The bill mandates a $100,000 general fund appropriation in the fiscal year 2028 budget bill, which impacts DBM's budget development and fiscal planning responsibilities.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include a $100,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2028 for the feasibility study.
The bill requires consultation with State and regional workforce development entities regarding regional and statewide aerospace and aviation workforce demand.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the purpose of the Individuals With Disabilities and Service–Disabled Veterans Boating Fund. Adds water-dependent recreational opportunities for eligible companions of individuals with disabilities or service-disabled veterans. Defines an eligible companion as an accompanying family member or direct support professional of a participant. Authorizes the Department of Disabilities to provide grants of up to $40,000 per fiscal year including companions. Maintains existing nonprofit eligibility requirements for organizations receiving fund grants.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with disabilities, service-disabled veterans, accompanying family members, direct support professionals, and qualified nonprofit boating organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The expansion is technical in nature and does not directly alter governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Disabilities is the primary administering agency of the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund, responsible for awarding grants and managing fund operations.

The bill directly impacts recreation and support services for service-disabled veterans and their family members or companions, an area aligned with the department's mission to support veterans and military families.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund separately.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily required to account for the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands certain state legal protections and benefits to apply to all members of the uniformed services. Exempts uniformed services members on official leave from trout stamp requirements while angling in Maryland. Extends expedited tenant holding over repossession remedies to landlords who are active service members. Alters the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to include fees from certain non-combat uniformed services license plates. Consolidates the statutory definition of a military protection order within the State Government Article.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families; Maryland Department of Transportation; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services, including the U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps and NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps; veterans; residential landlords and tenants; Maryland trout anglers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Department of Natural Resources may decrease by up to $4,400 annually due to newly eligible individuals qualifying for trout stamp exemptions. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the composition of the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund under the State Government Article, which is overseen and administered within the department to support veterans and military personnel.

The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to expand the trout stamp exemption to all uniformed services on leave, which has a direct operational and small fiscal impact on DNR's special fund licensing revenues.

The bill amends the Real Property Article regarding expedited District Court procedures for tenant holding over actions involving active service members, as well as cross-references relating to military protection orders under Courts and Judicial Proceedings and Family Law.
The bill amends the Transportation Article concerning federal facilities and references vehicle registration plate fees designated for the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund administered through MDOT/MVA.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding eligibility criteria for individuals who withdrew from high school to enlist in military service to apply for a high school diploma.
As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the agency is impacted by statutes standardizing definitions and provisions affecting service members and the National Guard.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals authorization for cigarette and other tobacco product licensees to manufacture, distribute, or sell electronic smoking devices under existing licenses. Requires these licensees to obtain a separate electronic smoking devices license to conduct those activities. Exempts certain cigarette and other tobacco product licensees applying as retailers or vape shop vendors from additional license fees. Allows existing licensees on September 30, 2026, to operate under their current licenses until expiration. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Clerks of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Cigarette and other tobacco products licensees, electronic smoking device manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, and vape shop vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by up to $25,100 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 from electronic smoking device license fees. Additional administrative duties can be absorbed with existing resources by the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission and local circuit court clerks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues and is statutorily involved in tobacco industry regulation and enforcement, making the changes to tobacco and electronic smoking device licensing requirements relevant to its administrative functions.

Clerks of the circuit courts, which are part of the Maryland Judicial Branch supported by the AOC, issue county retail licenses for tobacco products and electronic smoking devices and will absorb the administrative workload of issuing separate electronic smoking device retail licenses.

MDH oversees public health initiatives regarding tobacco and youth vaping prevention and is funded in part by retail tobacco licensing fees to enforce laws prohibiting the sale of tobacco products and electronic smoking devices to individuals under 21.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes certain payroll processing agents from the definition of money transmitter under the Maryland Money Transmission Act. Applies to a designated agent operating under a written agreement directing payroll processing on a payor's behalf. Requires the payor to hold the agent out to employees and other payees as providing payroll processing services. Mandates that the payor's obligation to payees is not extinguished if the agent fails to remit funds. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Payroll processing service providers, employers utilizing third-party payroll processors, and employees receiving payroll disbursements
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor decrease by $6,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to lost money transmitter licensing fees. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Maryland Money Transmission Act regulated by the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department experiences a reduction in special fund licensing revenues of $6,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 as certain payroll processors will no longer require a money transmitter license.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes civil liability immunity for persons who donate or dispense pet items, including commercial feed. Protects acts or omissions affecting the nature, age, condition, or packaging of good-faith donations. Excludes acts or omissions amounting to gross negligence or willful and wanton misconduct. Covers donations made for use or distribution by nonprofits or units of state or local government. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture to inspect donated commercial feed and establish handling procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Donors of pet items and commercial feed, nonprofit organizations and government units that distribute pet supplies, pet owners, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $84,600 in fiscal 2027 to fund one agricultural inspector position, vehicle purchase, and operating expenses to inspect donated commercial feed. Expenditures range from $69,700 to $80,000 in subsequent fiscal years. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) to inspect donated commercial feed for wholesomeness and establish procedures for handling donated commercial feed. The fiscal note indicates general fund expenditures for MDA to hire an agricultural inspector to handle inspections.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish a statutory civil liability immunity defense for individuals and entities donating or dispensing pet items, directly affecting civil tort actions filed in the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters certification renewal requirements for security guards in the State. Establishes that a security guard certification expires on the last day of the holder's birth month. Requires the Secretary of State Police to email renewal notices 90, 60, and 30 days before expiration. Requires applicants to submit a renewal application and renewal fee before the certification expires. Repeals the five-dollar daily late fee for renewal applications.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Secretary of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: certified security guards, licensed security guard agencies, and security guard employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2027 for one-time IT system updates to the online application portal. General fund revenues decrease annually beginning in FY 2027 due to the repeal of certification renewal late fees, though the exact amount is indeterminate. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (under the Secretary of State Police) is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for the licensing and certification renewal of security guards. The bill alters renewal timelines to the holder's birth month, mandates electronic notification schedules, repeals late renewal fees, and requires $100,000 in FY 2027 IT modifications to the department's licensing portal, along with causing an ongoing decrease in fee revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends through fiscal year 2030 the required annual budget appropriation of $500,000 for the Recovery Residence Grant Program. Administered by the Maryland Department of Health, the program awards competitive grants to certified nonprofit recovery residences. Grant recipients use awarded funds to support operations, recovery housing, peer support, and transportation services. The extended funding requirement takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified nonprofit recovery residences and individuals with substance-related disorders or addictive disorders receiving recovery housing and support services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2030 to fund the mandated appropriation. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Recovery Residence Grant Program is established and administered within the Maryland Department of Health, which awards competitive grants to certified recovery residences and submits annual reports on the program.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state budget preparation and execution, and the bill extends a mandated general fund appropriation of $500,000 annually from fiscal year 2028 through 2030.

The Governor is responsible for submitting the annual state budget bill, which must incorporate the extended statutory mandated appropriation of $500,000 per year for the grant program through fiscal year 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a consumption-only nonprofit swim club license in Anne Arundel County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue the license to a nonprofit swim club. Authorizes license holders to allow members and guests to bring beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption. Restricts consumption to designated club areas during designated events from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. Limits events to five days per year unless the Board authorizes up to three additional days. Establishes an annual license fee of $100 and a fee of $50 for each additional day.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit swim clubs in Anne Arundel County and their members and guests
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 from license fees ($100 annually plus $50 per additional day). County expenditures are unaffected. State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation specifically authorizes the local Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners to issue local consumption-only nonprofit swim club licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article under the Comptroller's general regulatory domain.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain alcoholic beverages license applications from the population ratio quota in Anne Arundel County. Applies to Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) license applications filed on or after January 1, 2023. Limits the exemption to applications approved by the Board of License Commissioners before July 1, 2025. Permits license issuance even if an assessment district exceeds one off-sale license for every 3,500 individuals. Takes effect July 1, 2026, and abrogates December 31, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County whose applications were filed on or after January 1, 2023, and approved before July 1, 2025; Anne Arundel County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase by $5,160 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to the collection of license fees from three newly issued licenses. County expenditures are not affected, and there is no State fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study household exclusions from the Heat and Eat Program. Examines exclusions from automatic standard utility allowance eligibility under the federal One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025. Directs the Department to compile historical participation data and calculate benefit reductions across each county. Mandates an evaluation of administrative costs and logistics for verifying individual energy expenses. Requires the Department to report its findings and recommendations to designated legislative committees by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Households participating in or eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and the Heat and Eat Program, particularly households without an elderly or disabled member
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Human Services can complete the required study and report using existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 461 directly mandates that the Department of Human Services (DHS) conduct a study and report recommendations on households affected by changes to the Heat and Eat Program and standard utility allowance eligibility within the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands an exception to the hearsay rule to include criminal cases charging assault in the second degree. Permits out-of-court statements when a defendant intentionally procured the declarant's unavailability through wrongdoing. Requires the court to hold a hearing outside the jury's presence before admitting the statement. Requires the court to find by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant procured the unavailability. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Defendants charged with second-degree assault, victims and witnesses in criminal assault proceedings, State's Attorneys, and criminal defense attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands an exception to the hearsay rule to criminal trials involving assault in the second degree, requiring state court judges to hold evidentiary hearings outside the presence of the jury to determine admissibility.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts criminal defense practice by allowing certain out-of-court statements to be admitted against defendants charged with second-degree assault, affecting cases handled by public defenders.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals, which may involve defending trial court rulings on the admissibility of hearsay statements under this expanded statutory exception.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board to advise the Secretary of Natural Resources. Directs the Board to advise on the operation, acquisition, regulation, and general oversight of recreational vehicle trails. Specifies the Governor appoints five State residents representing vehicle drivers and motorcycle organizations to staggered terms. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to provide staff and operational support for the Board. Mandates that the Board elect a chair annually and meet at least quarterly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Off-highway recreational vehicle drivers, motorcycle and off-highway vehicle dealers, recreational riding associations, and counties containing state-maintained off-highway vehicle trails
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Natural Resources can provide staff and support using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board to advise the Secretary of Natural Resources on trail operations, acquisitions, regulations, and oversight. The Department of Natural Resources is required to provide staff and support services to the board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent statutory advisory and oversight body within the state executive structure.
The Governor is responsible for appointing all voting members of the newly established board and appointing successors in the event of vacancies.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor by recruiting, vetting, and recommending qualified candidates to fill the newly created gubernatorially appointed positions on the board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Highway Administration to establish a speed monitoring system program in designated highway safety corridors. Permits local jurisdictions to deploy speed cameras on State highways within safety corridors under an Administration permit. Applies to vehicles traveling at least 12 miles per hour above the posted speed limit. Establishes escalating civil penalties from $40 up to $425 depending on vehicle speed. Requires citation revenues to cover system administrative costs before distribution to the Transportation Trust Fund. Mandates warning notices instead of citations during the first 30 days of camera operation at new locations.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Comptroller of Maryland; District Court of Maryland; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers; vulnerable road users, including pedestrians, bicyclists, and highway work zone personnel; local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase potentially by millions of dollars annually beginning in FY 2027 to cover camera implementation and administration. Remaining revenues distribute to the Transportation Trust Fund for highway safety and system preservation. Local government revenues and expenditures increase if local safety corridor camera programs are established under permit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SHA is the primary agency authorized to establish, operate, and regulate the safety corridor speed monitoring system program, permit local jurisdictions to operate cameras on State highways, and receive special fund disbursements to cover program costs and system preservation.
MDOT is the parent department of SHA and MVA. Remaining revenues from civil penalties are distributed to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) for highway safety and system preservation purposes.

MVA is responsible for enforcing vehicle registration suspensions or refusals to register/transfer registration when violators fail to pay safety corridor speed citations or appear for trial, and places administrative flags on vehicle records.

The District Court of Maryland has exclusive original civil jurisdiction over contested citations, with the Chief Judge tasked with adopting procedures and prescribing uniform citation forms for safety corridor violations.
The Comptroller is statutorily mandated to collect and distribute civil fine revenues generated by State-operated safety corridor speed monitoring systems into a dedicated special fund.

The bill amends the Insurance Article to prohibit insurers from considering safety corridor speed citations for auto insurance reclassification or premium increases, which falls under MIA's regulatory oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: Implements the federal Workforce Pell Grant Program for short-term programs in the State. Requires the Governor, after consulting with the Governor's Workforce Development Board, to approve eligible short-term programs. Prohibits institutions of postsecondary education from disbursing program funds without state and federal approvals. Mandates minimum completion and job placement rates of 70% for short-term program approval. Prohibits institutions from charging tuition and fees exceeding the maximum available Pell Grant funds. Authorizes application evaluation fees and requires annual reporting to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor; Governor's Workforce Development Board; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Students in short-term workforce programs, public and private institutions of postsecondary education, and employers in high-skill or in-demand industry sectors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $300,000 in FY 2027 to cover administrative and staffing costs for the Governor's Workforce Development Board and the Maryland Higher Education Commission, with ongoing staffing costs in subsequent years. Indeterminate increase in general fund revenues beginning in FY 2027 from application fees. Indeterminate impact on revenues and expenditures for public institutions of higher education and community colleges that voluntarily seek program approval.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Board to consult with the Governor on program approvals, collect compliance and outcome data from postsecondary institutions, establish application fees, adopt regulations, and submit an annual report to the General Assembly.

The Commission is authorized to collect application fees, verify program compliance, adopt regulations jointly with the Governor's Workforce Development Board, and submit an annual report on the program to the General Assembly.

The Commission is authorized to collect application fees, verify program compliance, adopt regulations jointly with the Governor's Workforce Development Board, and submit an annual report on the program to the General Assembly.

The bill tasks the Governor directly with determining whether short-term educational programs meet statutory and federal criteria for Workforce Pell Grants and requires the Governor to revoke program approvals under certain conditions.

The Department staffs the Governor's Workforce Development Board and oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council, which approves registered apprenticeships referenced in the bill. Additionally, the department receives the contingent general fund appropriation associated with the bill's implementation.

Constituent institutions of the University System that choose to offer short-term workforce training programs will be directly impacted by the application requirements, data reporting mandates, tuition caps, and credit transfer regulations established by the bill.

The bill explicitly provides that a finding by the Attorney General under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act regarding unfair, deceptive, or abusive trade practices related to the program triggers mandatory revocation of an institution's program approval.

As an independent public postsecondary institution, the university is impacted if it seeks Workforce Pell Grant eligibility for short-term workforce programs and must comply with the bill's tuition, transferability, and reporting standards.
