qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain health insurance policies to reimburse for services rendered by graduate-level clinical interns under specified circumstances. Covers graduate-level counseling, social work, and psychology clinical interns enrolled in graduate programs. Mandates that covered services be provided at outpatient health care facilities under direct clinical supervision. Specifies that supervising clinicians must bill for the services provided by the interns. Applies to health benefit policies and contracts issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Insured individuals receiving mental health services, graduate-level counseling, social work, and psychology clinical interns, supervising licensed mental health professionals, outpatient behavioral health clinics, and health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 only from $125 rate and form filing fees. Expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing health insurers in Maryland. The bill amends the Insurance Article to mandate reimbursement for services rendered by graduate-level clinical interns, requiring MIA to review and approve updated policy forms and rate filings from health insurance carriers.

MDH oversees health professional licensing boards (including the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, whose supervisor regulations are specifically cross-referenced in the bill) and regulates outpatient health care facilities where reimbursable services will be provided.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Calvert County to grant a property tax credit on certain former tobacco barns. Qualifying property must be located on land subject to a tobacco buyout agreement. Alternatively, qualifying property must qualify for an agricultural use assessment and support an approved agricultural activity. Authorizes the county to provide by law for the amount, duration, and administration of the credit. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: governing body of Calvert County; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: owners of real property formerly used solely as tobacco barns in Calvert County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County property tax revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent the tax credit is granted, but specific figures are unavailable because the county lacks an inventory of eligible properties. State finances and county expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes Calvert County to establish a property tax credit for real property formerly used solely as a tobacco barn. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is tasked with hearing disputes concerning real property valuations, exemptions, and property tax credits, making it potentially relevant in the event of administrative appeals regarding credit eligibility, though any operational or fiscal impact is minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the tax collector for each county to include specific digital resources with property tax bills. Mandates inclusion of a website address or quick-response code in written materials sent with each bill. Directs the link or code to connect to a county government webpage. Requires the webpage to list each property tax credit available to taxpayers in the county. Mandates that the webpage provide a brief explanation of how to apply for the tax credits.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Tax Collectors
qa_results.stakeholders: property taxpayers in Maryland; county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. County expenditures are not expected to be significantly impacted by the requirement to include a webpage address or QR code, and county revenues are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from recklessly or willfully and maliciously defacing, damaging, or destroying telecommunications infrastructure. Establishes a misdemeanor penalty of imprisonment up to 6 months, a fine up to $500, or both. Exempts telecommunications company employees, authorized agents, and political subdivisions exercising supervision and control. Expands the definition of junk or scrap metal to include specified telecommunications equipment and infrastructure. Prohibits junk dealers and scrap metal processors from purchasing telecommunications equipment without documentary proof of lawful selling authority.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: junk dealers; scrap metal processors; telecommunications companies; individuals selling telecommunications scrap metal
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. Minimal small business effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense for defacing, damaging, or destroying telecommunications infrastructure, which directly affects the judicial branch through the adjudication and processing of new criminal charges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense carrying penalties of up to six months of imprisonment, the Office of the Public Defender would be responsible for providing legal defense to eligible indigent defendants charged under the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees pretrial detention facilities in Baltimore City and community supervision through the Division of Parole and Probation, which may be impacted by individuals sentenced or detained under the newly created misdemeanor.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating crimes involving property destruction, infrastructure damage, and monitoring compliance with scrap metal and stolen property laws.

The Public Service Commission regulates public utilities and telecommunications providers in Maryland, whose critical network equipment and infrastructure are protected under the provisions of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a temporary to-go event permit and a Class C per diem municipal to-go license in Worcester County. Authorizes the Board to issue the license to the Town of Berlin, Pocomoke City, or the Town of Snow Hill. Restricts permit eligibility to Class B and Class D establishments located within or immediately adjacent to designated event areas. Authorizes permit holders to sell alcoholic beverages in approved to-go cups carried into the event area. Sets daily fees of $45 for the municipal license and $20 for the temporary event permit. Requires the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to adopt implementing regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages licensees in Worcester County, the Town of Berlin, Pocomoke City, and the Town of Snow Hill
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in Worcester County revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 from the $45 per day Class C municipal license fee and $20 per day temporary permit fee; local monitoring can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland and oversees alcoholic beverage taxation. While the bill's provisions are administered locally by the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates directly to the regulation and retail sale of alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for Allegany County local detention center officers if the county participates. Grants eligibility service and creditable service in the retirement system for past employment with the county. Terminates membership and benefit rights in the Employees' Pension System upon joining the retirement system. Exempts transferring officers from standard statutory requirements to pay contribution rate differences for prior service. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Allegany County
qa_results.stakeholders: Allegany County local detention center officers and Allegany County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. If Allegany County elects to participate in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, local pension liabilities increase by approximately $2.4 million, and net annual local employer pension contributions increase by $164,546 beginning in FY 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). SRA is responsible for administering the transfer of membership, creditable service, and pension assets and liabilities for the Allegany County detention center officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reorganizes Maryland's public health governance and extends the Commission on Public Health through June 30, 2028. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps for statewide emergency volunteer coordination. Establishes the Public Health Workforce Development Fund administered by the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission. Authorizes county health officers to enter into certain health care service agreements if the Secretary does not respond within seven days. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to develop a process to assess health equity impacts of relevant legislation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Commission on Public Health; Maryland Community Health Resources Commission; Department of Legislative Services; Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: county health officers; local health departments; public health workforce; clinical and nonclinical emergency volunteers; Maryland hospital boards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the Public Health Workforce Development Fund, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures. State expenditures increase minimally in fiscal 2027 and 2028 to maintain staffing for the extended Commission on Public Health. Local health department revenues may increase to the extent they receive workforce development funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for significant portions of the bill. It is required to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps, maintain its volunteer tracking system, designate a surge coordinator, consult with local health departments on EHR procurements, submit quarterly updates to the Commission on Public Health, co-manage transfers to the new Public Health Workforce Development Fund, and convene a workgroup on local health department recruiting and classification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the governance, membership, staffing, reporting duties, and sunset date of the Commission on Public Health; establishes a joint workgroup on local health department recruitment; and alters the composition of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Health Services Cost Review Commission, in conjunction with MDH, to transfer money from the Population Health Improvement Fund to the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund under the AHEAD Model State Agreement.

The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is added as a member of the Commission on Public Health, and DBM must participate in a newly mandated workgroup convened by MDH to examine local health department recruiting and classification efficiencies.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission on Public Health to advise on public health IT and data systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI oversees the Maryland Corps Program, and the bill alters the statutory membership of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board by adding a county health officer appointed by the Governor.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the moneys of the newly created Public Health Workforce Development Fund, with interest earnings credited back to the fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund.

The bill modifies the Governor's appointment authority for public members of the Commission on Public Health, adds a gubernatorial appointee (a local health officer) to the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board, and mandates annual report submissions to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters notice requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosures on certain vacant and abandoned property. Requires a county or municipal corporation to serve the foreclosure complaint on each interested party under the Maryland Rules. Repeals the mandate to send notice by first-class and certified mail within five days after filing. Applies when filing an in rem foreclosure complaint in the appropriate circuit court. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Circuit Courts; Maryland Counties and Municipal Corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, mortgagees, and other interested parties in vacant and abandoned real property subject to tax foreclosure; Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1110 alters the notice and service procedure for judicial in rem tax foreclosure complaints filed in Maryland circuit courts, requiring service to be made in accordance with the Maryland Rules rather than specific statutory mailing requirements. As the administrative support entity for the state court system, the Administrative Office of the Courts is directly affected by changes governing circuit court filings and procedural service rules.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health care providers who evaluate and manage pregnancy or postpartum care to screen for perinatal behavioral health conditions. Mandates health insurance carriers and Medicaid to cover perinatal behavioral health screenings at well visits. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to identify screening tools, resource networks, and provider training programs. Requires health occupations boards to grant two continuing education credits for each hour of approved training. Requires carriers to provide members standing referrals to behavioral health care providers during pregnancy and postpartum. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study coverage impacts and report by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum patients; infants; health care providers evaluating perinatal care; hospitals; health insurance carriers; Medicaid recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. The Maryland Department of Health, Medicaid, the Maryland Health Care Commission, and relevant health occupations boards can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no likely expenditure increase for local governments purchasing fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with identifying approved screening tools for perinatal behavioral health conditions, identifying and developing provider training programs with health occupations boards, disseminating educational materials to local WIC agencies, and ensuring Medicaid coverage for required screenings.

The bill mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct a formal study and analysis on the impact of requiring coverage and prohibiting cost-sharing for perinatal behavioral health condition screenings, reporting findings to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating health insurance carriers subject to the coverage mandate, reviewing amended rate and form filings, and collecting filing fee revenues.

The bill text includes provisions establishing a refundable state income tax credit of $1,000 for parents of a stillborn child, which falls directly under the Comptroller's jurisdiction for tax administration, processing, and refund issuance.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and assesses whether mandated health insurance coverage requirements impact the State plan.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Foreign Service members and their spouses relocating to Maryland on assignment to practice under an out-of-state professional license. Requires individuals to submit assignment notices, maintain good standing, and have actively used the license within the preceding two years. Limits authorized practice strictly to the discipline and scope permitted by the out-of-state license. Prohibits State licensing authorities from requiring a Maryland license unless an individual practices outside that authorized scope. Excludes the practice of law and professions practicing under interstate compacts from these provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Insurance Administration; Public Service Commission; State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission; Department of State Police; Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the U.S. Foreign Service and their spouses relocating to Maryland on assignment or detail, regulated occupational and professional practitioners, and Maryland employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $45,000 in FY 2027 ($30,000 in general funds for the Maryland State Department of Education and $15,000 in special funds for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners) for one-time software modifications. State general and special fund licensing fee revenues decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2027. Local finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts numerous occupational and professional licensing boards housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (including architects, accountants, cosmetologists, electricians, engineers, real estate appraisers, and home improvement contractors), as well as financial and labor regulatory divisions.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees dozens of health occupations licensing boards (such as nursing, physicians, pharmacy, dentistry, and social work) and laboratories, all of which are required to permit practice under the bill's portability provisions.

The bill applies to licensing programs administered by the Department of Agriculture, including the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners, pesticide applicators, and fertilizer applicators. The fiscal note estimates a $15,000 software modification expense and lost licensing fee revenue.

The bill exempts qualifying Foreign Service members and spouses from certain certification requirements to teach or provide school counseling. MSDE anticipates general fund expenditures of up to $30,000 in FY 2027 to update its teacher licensure platform.

The bill alters licensing and certification provisions for programs under MDE's jurisdiction, such as waterworks and waste systems operators, well drillers, marine contractors, on-site wastewater professionals, and radiation machine inspectors.

MSP licenses security guards, private detectives, and security systems technicians, administers vehicle inspection mechanic licensing via the Automotive Safety Enforcement Division, and oversees explosives and electrical inspector certifications via the State Fire Marshal.

MVA is the licensing authority for vehicle salespersons, automotive dismantlers and recyclers, title service agents, drivers' schools, and driving instructors, which are subject to the bill's portability exemptions.
MIA is the licensing authority for insurance producers, advisers, bail bondsmen, public adjusters, and motor club service providers, all of which are impacted by the license portability mandate.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees the licensing and certification of emergency medical services (EMS) providers under Education Article § 13-516, which is amended to recognize authorization under the bill.
The PSC licenses energy salespersons and vendors, as well as master plumbers/gasfitters under its utility jurisdiction, which are subject to reciprocal authorization under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes qualified Foreign Service members and spouses holding out-of-state licenses to work as video lottery employees and sports wagering employees without separate State licensure.

The bill exempts qualified individuals authorized under the bill from certain registration and administrative supervision requirements for rehabilitation counselors and vocational evaluators registered with the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services licenses private home detention monitoring agencies, which are amended to recognize authorizations under the bill.

Clerks of the Circuit Court issue various commercial and trader licenses under Business Regulation Article Title 17 that are amended by the bill; the fiscal note notes that the Judiciary anticipates potential minimal reductions in license fee collections.
The Comptroller administers and issues licenses for transient vendors under Business Regulation Article § 17-20A-02, which is amended by the bill.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, whose professional licenses (vehicle sales, driving schools, etc.) are directly impacted by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes licensed pharmacists to order specified vaccines for individuals at least three years old without personally administering them. Limits eligible orders to influenza vaccines, COVID-19 vaccines, or vaccines used during a public health emergency. Requires pharmacists ordering vaccines for minors to inform adult caregivers about pediatric primary care visits. Mandates that pharmacists report all ordered vaccinations to the state ImmuNet Program. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed pharmacists, adult caregivers, and vaccine recipients aged three and older
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state or local government finances. The changes are technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Pharmacy, the State Board of Physicians, and the State Board of Nursing, which regulate health occupations and establish vaccination protocols. MDH also maintains the ImmuNet statewide immunization registry where pharmacists must report ordered vaccinations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study residential-in-commercial-zone laws. Defines these laws as legislation requiring local jurisdictions to allow multifamily residential or mixed-use developments in commercial zones. Directs the Department to assess impacts on infrastructure, local economic goals, housing production, and existing mixed-use communities. Mandates recommendations on development standards, including parking, density limits, building heights, and urban, suburban, and rural considerations. Requires the Department to report its findings to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: local governments, commercial property owners, multifamily and mixed-use housing developers, and housing advocates
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in fiscal 2027 only for contractual services to assist with the study. Local government finances and State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Housing and Community Development conduct a study of residential-in-commercial-zone (RICZ) laws, develop recommendations, and submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026, resulting in an estimated $75,000 fiscal impact for contractual services.

The Department of Housing and Community Development is required to submit its completed study findings and policy recommendations regarding residential-in-commercial-zone laws to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

The study directly evaluates statewide land use planning, commercial zoning overrides, infrastructure impacts, and local economic development, which fall within the Department of Planning's advisory and policy domain.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the missing October 2025 Consumer Price Index value for State Retirement and Pension System calculations. Sets the October 2025 value as the average of the September 2025 and November 2025 values. Applies this calculated value to determine cost-of-living adjustments effective July 1, 2026, and July 1, 2027. Addresses the lack of an official federal report caused by the federal government shutdown. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System and participating governmental units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Likely has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities and contribution rates, with no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1138 directly governs the calculation of cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) for retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary entity responsible for administering these retirement allowances and implementing the revised Consumer Price Index formula.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters administrative procedures and participation requirements for participating governmental units in the State Retirement and Pension System. Sets a 7.75% annual interest rate on delinquent payments owed by county governments. Requires eligible governmental units to make pension enrollment available to all eligible employees. Deems eligible employees who fail to submit election documentation as enrolled in the applicable pension system. Shifts the third quarterly payment deadline for certified local employer charges from April 1 to April 16. Repeals immediate vesting rights for the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: county governments; local employers; participating governmental units; eligible employees of participating governmental units including law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, and local detention center officers; and the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Local government expenditures increase if a county government fails to make timely pension payments and incurs the 7.75% annual interest penalty on delinquent amounts. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill directly amends the administration of SRPS plans, including rules for participating governmental units (PGUs), enrollment deadlines, default election mechanisms, prior service credit determinations, and receipt of local payments.

The bill explicitly directs the State Comptroller to exercise setoff and withhold delinquent amounts plus a clarified 7.75% annual interest penalty from funds due to delinquent counties or local employers and remit those payments to the SRPS Board of Trustees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals Section 29-304(19) of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, removing the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs from the list of state officials entitled to immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures. Requires the Task Force to evaluate county and municipal government revenue structures across Maryland. Directs the evaluation of current and optional revenue sources, interstate practices, and cost-of-living impacts. Requires recommendations regarding local government authority to increase revenue sources. Mandates a final report to the Governor and specified General Assembly committees by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: county and municipal governments in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal State expenditure impact, as the Department of Legislative Services can likely provide staff support within existing budgeted resources and member expense reimbursements are absorbable. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, is explicitly designated as a member of the newly created Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures.
The Secretary of Budget and Management, or the Secretary's designee, is explicitly designated as a member of the Task Force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures, a temporary advisory body established to evaluate county and municipal revenue structures and report recommendations.
The Task Force is required to submit a final report of its findings and recommendations regarding local revenue modernization to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Legacy Protection Program in the State Department of Assessments and Taxation under the State Tax Sale Ombudsman. Requires the Ombudsman to provide grants to qualified legal services organizations and eligible heirs for probate costs. Requires the Governor to appropriate $250,000 annually and counties to collectively pay $500,000 annually to the program fund. Grants the homeowners' and homestead property tax credits to certain eligible heirs for up to three taxable years. Expands State Tax Sale Ombudsman assistance to estates, personal representatives, and heirs of deceased homeowners.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; State Tax Sale Ombudsman
qa_results.stakeholders: Heirs and legatees inheriting residential dwellings, estates and personal representatives of deceased homeowners, county governments, and legal services organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2028, State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually, and Legacy Protection Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $750,000 annually. County expenditures collectively increase by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2028. Indeterminate potential decreases in State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local property tax revenues begin in FY 2027 due to expanded eligibility for the homeowners' and homestead property tax credits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to collaborate with the Registers of Wills to develop a step-by-step guide to probating an estate and becoming the record title holder of a dwelling. Furthermore, the newly created program provides direct grants to heirs to pay probate fees and inheritance taxes administered and collected by the Registers of Wills.

The bill establishes the Legacy Protection Fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately, invest its moneys, and credit interest earnings to the fund pursuant to an exemption from standard interest accrual to the General Fund.

The bill specifies that the Comptroller must account for the newly created Legacy Protection Fund and process interest earnings allocations under Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The bill establishes a statutory mandated annual appropriation of $250,000 to the Legacy Protection Fund starting in FY 2028, impacting state budget preparation and fiscal management.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $250,000 from the interest on overdue State property tax to the Legacy Protection Fund in the annual state budget bill.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for the bill's fiscal note regarding impacts on the judicial system, as county land records maintained by the circuit court clerks determine record title holder status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to settle State claims in arrears against businesses that permanently ceased operations regardless of elapsed time. Eliminates the two-year waiting period previously required before settling claims against these defunct businesses. Requires the Comptroller to verify that the State cannot collect the claim through legal process before settling. Authorizes the Comptroller to abate all or part of the principal or interest due. Requires discharging the debtor and surety once the agreed settlement sum is paid into the State Treasury.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: business entities that have permanently ceased operations, their sureties, and taxpayers with unresolved State liabilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State tax revenues (general funds and special funds) increase by potentially $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 from earlier settlement of claims. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office increase by $74,124 in FY 2027 and by $98,500 in FY 2031 to hire one revenue administrator. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures and local income tax and highway user revenues may increase by indeterminate amounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency for HB 1149. The bill authorizes the Comptroller to settle delinquent State claims against business entities that have permanently ceased operations without waiting for the claims to be two years in arrears, and requires additional personnel expenditures to process the anticipated increase in settlements.

The Department of Transportation is fiscally impacted because a portion of corporate income tax revenues flows into the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will experience expenditure increases for local highway user revenue grants as claims are settled sooner.
Under the statute amended by the bill, agreed-upon settlement sums from resolved claims are paid directly into the State Treasury, which is managed and safeguarded by the Treasurer's Office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of State Police to study and recommend policies on employing and using special police officers. Mandates that the study examine commissioning, employment requirements, operations, training, equipment, jurisdiction, and regulatory oversight. Directs the Department to survey requirements in surrounding states and analyze public and private employer best practices. Requires consultation with special police officers, employers, law enforcement associations, prosecutors, state officials, and training academies. Directs the Department to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Special police officers, public and private employers of special police officers (including county and municipal governments), security training academies, and law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Department of State Police can implement the study using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1152 directly tasks the Department of State Police (including its Licensing Division) with conducting a comprehensive study on the employment, commissioning, training, and regulatory oversight of special police officers, and submitting a final report with recommendations by December 1, 2026.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with a representative of the Office of the Secretary of State in carrying out the study regarding special police officers.

The bill requires the Department of State Police to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2026, relevant to the Governor's statutory authority to appoint and deputize special police officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Calvert County to enter into contracts for infrastructure or asset management programs. Requires covered infrastructure or assets to have a life cycle of not less than 15 years. Limits the initial contract term to not more than 20 years. Includes water towers, flow meters, and other water and sewer assets as eligible infrastructure. Permits contracts to include planning, design, construction, operation, maintenance, modification, revitalization, and decommissioning.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County Government and contractors providing infrastructure and asset management services in Calvert County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Calvert County government finances, though it may generate operational efficiencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases death and burial benefits under the Calvert County Length of Service Award Program. Raises the maximum benefit to $14,000 for qualified volunteers who complete 25 certified service years. Increases the benefit to up to $560 per certified service year for volunteers receiving specified service benefits. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Volunteer fire, rescue, and emergency medical services personnel in Calvert County and their beneficiaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County expenditures may increase by approximately $16,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 due to higher death and burial benefit payments. State operations and local revenues are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory reference to Calvert Memorial Hospital in the Public Local Laws of Calvert County. Replaces the obsolete name with CalvertHealth Medical Center, Inc., and its successors. Authorizes the Calvert County Commissioners to appropriate an amount determined by them to the medical center. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: CalvertHealth Medical Center, Inc. and Calvert County Commissioners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. The bill is procedural in nature and does not affect Calvert County finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to study limited-income mechanisms for eligible limited-income customers. Evaluates water companies, sewage disposal companies, and water and sewage disposal companies in the required study. Requires the Commission to report study findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026. Authorizes the Commission, effective July 1, 2027, to require these companies to adopt approved limited-income mechanisms. Permits mechanisms to take the form of programs, tariff provisions, credits, rates, or riders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Water companies, sewage disposal companies, water and sewage disposal companies, eligible limited-income residential utility customers, and other rate-paying utility customers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State expenditures are likely not materially affected because most State agencies are not served by the affected companies, and there is no effect on State revenues. Local government expenditures could be affected if rates increase as early as fiscal 2028 to fund adopted limited-income mechanisms, but specific figures cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing regulatory agency under the bill. The bill requires the Commission to study the feasibility of requiring water and sewage disposal companies to adopt limited-income mechanisms, submit a report by December 1, 2026, and authorizes the Commission to require such companies to implement limited-income mechanisms starting July 1, 2027.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers, including water utility customers, in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding utility rate structures, consumer affordability, and limited-income assistance mechanisms.

The Department of Human Services administers the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is referenced in the statute to certify eligible limited-income customer qualifications if required by an approved mechanism.
The Public Service Commission is required to report its findings on the feasibility of limited-income mechanisms for water and sewage disposal companies to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires specified apprenticeship programs used in State procurement to have a completion rate of at least 25%. Applies the completion rate standard to apprenticeship programs that have graduated at least one apprenticeship cohort. Directs contractors awarded covered procurements valued at $1,000,000 or more to utilize registered apprenticeships or eligible internship programs. Requires public work and capital construction contractors choosing apprenticeship payments to fund only programs meeting the standard. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Labor to determine and verify program completion rates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors and subcontractors on State procurements and public works, registered apprenticeship program sponsors, and apprentices.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in State Apprenticeship Training Fund special fund revenues beginning in FY 2027 if more contractors choose fund contributions over program participation. State and local project procurement costs may increase if fewer eligible contractors bid, though payment alternatives mitigate this effect. State agencies and local governments can implement requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing and enforcing agency under the bill. It is responsible for verifying that registered apprenticeship programs meet the new 25% completion rate requirement, overseeing prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance, and administering the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.

DGS houses the Chief Procurement Officer, who is statutorily directed to establish criteria and adopt regulations defining 'covered procurements' that require the use of registered apprenticeship or eligible internship programs.

The Secretary of Information Technology is explicitly required to be consulted by the Chief Procurement Officer in adopting regulations and defining covered procurements for state information technology contracts under Title 3.5.

The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily designated under § 17-602 to account for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, which receives contractor payments and penalty revenues affected by the bill.
The State Treasurer's Office is statutorily designated under § 17-602 to hold the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the voting rights of the student member of the Howard County Board of Education. Authorizes the student member to vote on budgetary matters, school consolidation, student transportation, and student suspensions and expulsions. Permits the student member to vote on geographical attendance areas, donations, condemnation, and real property acquisition and disposition. Prohibits the student member from voting on architect employment, superintendent appointment and salary, and staff appointments. Prohibits the student member from voting on staff discipline, employee appeals, and collective bargaining. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: the student member and students of the Howard County Public School System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the changes are procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public education system and the 24 local school systems. Although this legislation specifically affects the local governance and voting authority of the student member on the Howard County Board of Education with no state fiscal impact, MSDE holds broad administrative and policy oversight over local school boards in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters governance provisions for the Board of Directors of the Howard County Economic Development Authority. Repeals the designation of an ex officio nonvoting member by the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council chair. Decreases required board meeting frequency from monthly to at least once every other month. Designates the Executive Director of the Authority as Chief Executive Officer instead of Chief Administrative Officer. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Economic Development Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Board of Directors and staff of the Howard County Economic Development Authority, Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council, and Howard County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Howard County operations or finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Howard County Executive to indicate the percentage of county general fund revenue allocated to public school operating costs. Applies this reporting requirement to the annual budget submission to the Howard County Council. Requires the approved county school budget to include the percentage of general fund revenue appropriated. Excludes one-time expenses from the general fund revenue calculation. Mandates reporting on pensions, employee and retiree benefits, debt service, school safety, and transportation costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Executive; Howard County Council; Howard County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Public School System, Howard County Board of Education, and Howard County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Howard County can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, and county revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1176 amends Section 5-102 of the Education Article regarding the submission and contents of local school board budgets. Under this section, copies of the approved local school board budget containing the newly required percentage allocations must be submitted to the State Superintendent of Schools, who leads the Maryland State Department of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a municipality seeking to annex certain land to notify specified members of the General Assembly. Applies when the land is located in a different legislative district than the municipality. Requires written notice after the municipality introduces an annexation resolution. Mandates notice delivery by electronic communication and United States Postal Service to affected legislators. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Municipalities
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities seeking to annex land, and members of the General Assembly representing legislative districts affected by municipal annexations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning oversees state land use policy, coordinates with local governments on comprehensive planning and growth management, and monitors municipal boundary changes and annexations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Architects to deny, reprimand, suspend, or revoke a license under specified circumstances. Expands disciplinary grounds to include misrepresenting that an individual holds an architecture license or permit. Directs the Board to notify each county code official when a license is suspended or revoked. Requires county code officials to verify an architect's seal and license before processing building permits. Authorizes the Board to establish an electronic portal for anonymous and confidential violation reporting.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Architects
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed architects, applicants for architecture licensure, architecture firms, and county building code officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations can absorb requirements using existing resources. Discretionary special fund expenditures may increase minimally if the State Board of Architects elects to build an electronic reporting portal. State and local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing). The bill alters disciplinary standards, requires notifications to county code officials, and authorizes the board to establish an electronic reporting portal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters procedures for placing children in out-of-home care under voluntary placement agreements. Requires local departments of social services to schedule assessment meetings within five business days of receiving requests. Mandates written eligibility determinations within five business days following the assessment meeting. Prohibits requiring parents to relinquish legal custody or guardianship of a child to access services. Prohibits referring families entering voluntary placement agreements to child support enforcement. Declares previous child support balances owed to the State under voluntary placement agreements unenforceable and uncollectable.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses, their parents and legal guardians, local departments of social services, and behavioral health providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $94,700 in FY 2027, growing to $127,700 by FY 2031, for the Department of Human Services to hire one program manager. Special fund revenues from child support foster care offsets may decrease. Montgomery County expenditures increase by approximately $162,000 annually for personnel and technology upgrades.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary state agency responsible for child welfare and out-of-home placements. The bill establishes new assessment and determination timelines for local departments of social services regarding voluntary placement agreements (VPAs), alters child support enforcement referral policies and order modifications via the Child Support Administration, mandates staff training, requires data collection and website publishing, and requires a joint report with MDH.

MDH is required to consult with the Social Services Administration on annual training for local department staff regarding VPAs for children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses, coordinates with local behavioral health authorities receiving direct referrals for Medicaid-eligible children seeking psychiatric residential treatment, and must co-author a joint report evaluating hospital discharge delays and VPA reform implementation.

The bill impacts juvenile and family court proceedings by restricting the court from ordering child support in certain VPA cases, mandating filings of motions to modify existing child support orders, and requiring judicial best-interest findings for children remaining in VPA placements beyond 180 days.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission employee suspended for disciplinary purposes to appeal to the Office of Administrative Hearings. Requires the Office of Administrative Hearings to dispose of a case or conduct a hearing and issue a final decision. Applies these appeal rights to disciplinary suspensions without pay of up to 30 days. Prohibits the Commission from suspending an employee for disciplinary purposes for more than 30 days in a calendar year. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Administrative Hearings; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission employees suspended for disciplinary purposes
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not materially affected, as both the Office of Administrative Hearings and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission can implement the bill with existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1185 directly tasks the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) with hearing appeals and issuing final decisions regarding disciplinary suspensions of Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) employees, amending § 4–401 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters motor vehicle liability insurance requirements and liability standards for peer-to-peer car sharing programs. Authorizes shared vehicle drivers to maintain required liability coverage during a car sharing period. Repeals the prohibition on insurers canceling or nonrenewing a personal policy solely because a vehicle is shared. Exempts the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund from covering shared vehicle drivers unless the vehicle is a replacement vehicle. Authorizes car sharing programs to transfer liability to drivers for tolls, fees, and traffic control camera fines.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: peer-to-peer car sharing programs, shared vehicle owners, shared vehicle drivers, private passenger motor vehicle insurers, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in fiscal 2027 only from rate and form filing fees. Implementation and enforcement will use existing budgeted resources with no material effect on local governments or the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes significant changes to insurance requirements, coverage priorities, policy exclusions, and disclosures governing peer-to-peer car sharing programs. The Maryland Insurance Administration oversees compliance and will review required rate and form filings.

The bill explicitly amends statute to provide that the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is not required to provide coverage to a shared vehicle driver for the use of a shared vehicle that is not a replacement vehicle, directly affecting MAIF's statutory coverage obligations.

The bill amends multiple sections of the Transportation Article governing peer-to-peer car sharing programs, required vehicle security under Title 17, and exclusions from red light camera citation liability.

The MVA administers Maryland's vehicle security requirements under § 17-103 of the Transportation Article and driver/vehicle compliance frameworks directly referenced in the bill's insurance provisions.

The bill authorizes peer-to-peer car sharing programs to transfer monetary liability and charge drivers for any tolls or fees incurred during the car sharing period, which impacts the collection and enforcement of MDTA toll facilities.

The bill alters the definition of 'owner' for traffic control signal monitoring system (red light camera) violations to exclude peer-to-peer car sharing programs, affecting liability and adjudication of citations processed through the District Court.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the membership of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters from seven to 11 members. Delays the deadline for the Board to establish and publish interpreter licensing requirements to July 1, 2027. Extends the general interpreter licensure mandate to January 1, 2028, and to July 1, 2028 for educational settings. Requires the Board to consult specified stakeholders and submit a report before adopting regulations on specialist areas. Requires public entities to provide reasonable accommodations supporting an individual's indicated preference for in-person or video remote interpretation.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Sign Language Interpreters; Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
qa_results.stakeholders: sign language interpreters, deaf and hard of hearing individuals, deafblind individuals, interpreter agencies, and public entities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund licensing fee revenues and minimal general fund penalty revenues are delayed until fiscal 2028 due to postponed licensure deadlines. Special fund expenditures are unaffected, and affected State agencies can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Sign Language Interpreters is housed within the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH). The bill establishes nomination procedures handled by ODHH, mandates ODHH staff support the board's study and reporting, and requires ODHH's Director to include specific interpreter licensing metrics in annual reports.

The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as an ex officio nonvoting member of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters, and the Department must be consulted by the Board before regulations regarding specialist areas are established.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is added as an ex officio nonvoting member of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters.

The Governor appoints all 11 members of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters, holds statutory authority to remove members for attendance and performance reasons, and receives required reports regarding specialist areas and interpreter licensing.

The Maryland Judiciary (supported administratively by the AOC) is designated as a stakeholder that must be consulted by the Board prior to establishing specialist area licensing regulations for legal settings.

The Maryland State Department of Education is explicitly named as a stakeholder that the Board must consult when preparing the report and evaluating specialist licensing standards for educational settings.
The Maryland Department of Health is explicitly required to be consulted by the Board regarding specialist area licensing requirements for medical and behavioral health settings.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and processing of appointees to state boards, which is impacted by the expansion and altered qualification requirements of the 11-member Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts retirees of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System from an earnings offset if reemployed as bailiffs in a State court. Excludes these reemployed retirees from earning creditable service or eligibility service during reemployment. Prohibits pension deductions or employer pickup contributions from their reemployment compensation. Requires Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services officials to include reemployed bailiffs in an annual report to the Joint Committee on Pensions. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System reemployed as bailiffs in Maryland State courts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Likely no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or employer contribution rates due to the limited number of qualifying positions. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System. It is responsible for tracking retiree reemployment notifications and administering the earnings offset exemption provided by the bill.

The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary by exempting retirees of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System who are reemployed as bailiffs in State courts from an earnings offset penalty against their retirement allowances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the correctional officers who retire under CORS. The bill amends annual reporting requirements under § 25-403(j), requiring leadership within DPSCS (the Commissioner of Correction, Commissioner of Pretrial Detention and Services, and Director of the Patuxent Institution) to track and report on rehired retirees under the new exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to develop an action plan for enforcing secondary maximum contaminant levels. Directs the plan to address water discoloring, taste, and odor at community water systems and nontransient, noncommunity water systems. Mandates that the plan include contaminant presence listings, a draft enforcement approach, interstate regulatory comparisons, and cost evaluations. Requires the Department to consult with water system owners, operators, serviced residents, and the Maryland Rural Water Association. Mandates reporting of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, operators, and residents serviced by community water systems and nontransient, noncommunity water systems, and the Maryland Rural Water Association
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can develop the action plan, consult with stakeholders, and submit the required report using existing budgeted resources, with no material impact on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of the Environment (MDE) develop an action plan for enforcing standards for secondary maximum contaminant levels in community and nontransient, noncommunity water systems, consult with stakeholders, and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds a substitute member appointed by the Governor to the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners. Establishes a special event permit for Class 3 wineries and Class 4 limited wineries. Authorizes holders of specified alcoholic beverages licenses with catering options to cater events anywhere in the county. Requires caterers to supply continuous service personnel and certified alcohol awareness staff at events. Mandates that food sales represent at least 70% of total catered event costs. Requires license applicants to submit documentation verifying U.S. citizenship or lawful immigration status.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners; Garrett County Board of County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders, winery operators, caterers, and license applicants in Garrett County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Garrett County expenditures increase by $3,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 to salary the substitute board member. Garrett County revenues increase beginning in FY 2027 from special event permit fees ($1,750 annual fee plus a $1,750 one-time issuing fee), but the total increase cannot be reliably estimated. There is no state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily requires the Governor to appoint an additional substitute member to the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners, subject to legislative confirmation.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and processing gubernatorial appointees, and will be responsible for administering the appointment process for the newly created substitute member position on the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes all Maryland counties to honor certificates of guarantee to satisfy county bond requirements. Expands permissive authority previously limited to nine specified counties and Baltimore City. Permits approved nonprofit contractor associations or their wholly owned subsidiaries to issue these instruments. Applies certificates to county bond requirements for public improvements and other county bond requirements. Clarifies that counties are not required under the Insurance Article to honor certificates of guarantee. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland county governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors bidding on or performing county construction and maintenance projects, nonprofit associations of contractors and their wholly owned subsidiaries, and all Maryland county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect; the Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce requirements using existing budgeted resources. County fiscal impact is expected to be minimal because honoring certificates of guarantee remains permissive.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1216 amends Section 1–203 of the Insurance Article regarding certificates of guarantee used to satisfy county bond requirements. As the regulatory agency tasked with administering and enforcing state insurance laws, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees the article affected by the bill, though the fiscal note indicates the agency can handle any oversight using existing budgeted resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs to develop a plan addressing severe health and safety risk properties. Limits the plan's application specifically to multi-unit rental properties containing 50 or more units. Directs the Office to collaborate with the Attorney General and coordinate with local governments and housing stakeholders. Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to publish the list of identified properties on its website. Mandates submission of the plan by August 31, 2027, followed by a final report by December 31, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Tenants and landlords of multi-unit rental properties with 50 or more units in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $248,500 in FY 2027 and $84,700 in FY 2028 for contractual staff and services until the Act sunsets on December 31, 2027. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs within the Department of Housing and Community Development develop a plan to identify and intervene in severe health and safety risk multi-unit rental properties, publish a public list of these properties, and submit reports, resulting in direct fiscal impacts for additional personnel and contractual services.
The bill explicitly requires the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs to develop the intervention plan and related legal strategies in formal collaboration with the Attorney General.
The bill requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to submit the required intervention plan, statutory recommendations, and final report on identified properties to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the University System of Maryland to study the relationship between climate change, homeowner's insurance, and disaster preparedness. Directs the study to proceed with oversight from designated state agencies, legislators, and emergency management officials. Evaluates insurance costs and availability, federal disaster funding streams, and local recovery resources. Authorizes up to $100,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to conduct the evaluation. Mandates submission of findings and policy recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: University System of Maryland; Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners; property and casualty insurers and insurance agents; local and municipal emergency managers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund increase by $100,000 in FY 2027 to fund the study. Higher education expenditures may increase by up to an additional $200,000 in FY 2027 for the University System of Maryland to complete the study, which would be offset by general funds if reimbursed. Coordinating state and local agencies can carry out oversight using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the University System of Maryland as the primary entity responsible for conducting the study on climate change, homeowner's insurance, and emergency management, and submitting findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027.

The Maryland Department of Emergency Management is explicitly mandated to coordinate and oversee the study, which focuses on emergency capabilities, disaster preparedness, and potential modifications to the State Disaster Recovery Fund.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is required to coordinate and provide oversight for the study, which directly examines homeowner's insurance availability, pricing, flood insurance markets, and potential modifications to the Insurance Article.
The Department of the Environment is explicitly required to coordinate with and provide oversight for the study, providing expertise related to climate change and state flood hazard management.
The Department of Natural Resources is explicitly named in the bill to coordinate with and provide oversight for the study conducted by the University System of Maryland.
The bill authorizes up to $100,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is administered by the Maryland Energy Administration, to fund the required study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires short-term rental hosts to conspicuously post evacuation diagrams and emergency telephone numbers in short-term rental units. Mandates that hosts provide working fire extinguishers, carbon monoxide alarms, and interconnected smoke alarms in each unit. Requires booking services to notify hosts of fire safety requirements and collect compliance documentation. Directs counties and Baltimore City to require annual inspections of short-term rental units by July 1, 2028. Authorizes local jurisdictions to establish inspection fees and delegate inspections to qualified third-party inspectors. Requires the State Fire Marshal to report local inspection data to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal; State Fire Prevention Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: short-term rental hosts, booking services, short-term rental guests, third-party fire safety inspectors, and county governments and Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Office of the State Fire Marshal can likely be absorbed with existing resources unless a formal licensure program is required. Local expenditures increase for counties and Baltimore City to conduct annual inspections and hire staff, which may be offset by authorized local inspection fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission are housed within the Department of State Police. The bill assigns direct responsibilities to the State Fire Marshal, including establishing minimum qualifications, certifications, and procedures for third-party inspectors of short-term rentals, authorizing alternative smoke alarm interconnectivity standards, receiving local compliance reports, and reporting findings to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires the State Fire Marshal to consult with the State Fire Prevention Commission regarding authorization of alternative requirements for interconnected smoke alarms in short-term rental units.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual salary of the Prince George's County State's Attorney from $199,000 to $250,000. Requires the salary and expenses to be paid in equal semimonthly installments. Applies the salary increase beginning at the start of the next term of office. Excludes an incumbent State's Attorney serving in a term beginning before October 1, 2026. Exempts an individual appointed or elected after the effective date to fill an expired term.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County State's Attorney; Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County State's Attorney and Prince George's County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County expenditures increase by $40,371 in fiscal 2027 and by $69,207 annually thereafter to reflect higher salary and fringe benefit costs. State finances and operations are not materially affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters procurement programs and governance within the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission. Repeals the statutory name of the Office of Supplier Diversity and Inclusion and requires the Commission to rename it by regulation. Transforms the local small business enterprise program into a business participation program. Expands eligibility to local, small, local small, Maryland-based, and qualified veteran-owned and disabled veteran-owned businesses. Authorizes the Commission to accept registered vendors from other jurisdictions or through self-certification. Authorizes regulations promoting workforce engagement and local economic benefits in Commission contracts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Businesses contracting or seeking to contract with the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, including local, small, Maryland-based, veteran-owned, and disabled veteran-owned businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. Changes are procedural in nature and do not directly impact local government finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an exemption or partial exemption from Baltimore City real property taxes for qualifying economic development projects in the Downtown RISE District. Covers newly constructed or rehabilitated hotels, office buildings, retail facilities, multifamily residential facilities, or mixed-use facilities. Requires owners to demonstrate financial necessity and execute a payment in lieu of taxes agreement with the Board of Estimates. Requires owners to apply, obtain building permits, and satisfy financing requirements on or before June 30, 2036. Requires the City of Baltimore to report annually on qualifying projects and job creation by January 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of Estimates; City of Baltimore
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and multifamily residential property developers and owners in the Baltimore City Downtown RISE District; City of Baltimore
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 depending on the number and assessed value of participating projects, though revenue losses will be mitigated by negotiated payment in lieu of taxes agreements. State finances are unaffected. Specific dollar amounts are indeterminate.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Critical Infrastructure Protection Branch in the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center. Requires the Center's Executive Director to appoint a Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer. Directs the branch to identify threats and prioritize critical infrastructure assets across the State. Requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to coordinate consequence management efforts following attacks.
