Directs the Department of Information Technology to provide cybersecurity reporting standards to infrastructure operators. Allows owners and operators of critical infrastructure to join the Maryland Information Sharing and Analysis Center.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center; Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of critical infrastructure in Maryland, including hospitals and healthcare facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances or revenues because the bill codifies an existing branch within the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center, and agencies can implement requirements with existing resources. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates MDEM, in consultation with the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center, to coordinate consequence management efforts and respond to cascading impacts resulting from an attack on the State's critical infrastructure.

The bill assigns direct statutory responsibilities to DoIT, including allowing critical infrastructure owners/operators to join the Maryland Information Sharing and Analysis Center, providing cybersecurity reporting standards, directing critical infrastructure cybersecurity efforts across State government, and coordinating threat assessments.

The Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), where the new Critical Infrastructure Protection Branch is created and whose Executive Director appoints the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer, is housed within the Department of State Police.
The bill requires the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer to coordinate with and advise the Director of the Governor's Office of Homeland Security on critical infrastructure security issues.
The bill explicitly requires the Critical Infrastructure Protection Branch to coordinate with the Public Service Commission to determine threat levels to the State's critical infrastructure.
The bill specifically directs the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer to coordinate with the National Guard regarding statewide critical infrastructure security efforts.
The bill establishes that the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer must directly advise the Governor on critical infrastructure security issues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts specified personal property of certain small alcohol manufacturers in Prince George's County from municipal corporation property tax. Applies to manufacturing businesses that hold a State alcoholic beverages manufacturer's license and have 50 or fewer employees. Covers manufacturing stock in business, tools, implements, machinery, apparatus, raw materials, and manufactured products. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed alcoholic beverages manufacturers with 50 or fewer employees in Prince George's County and municipal corporations in Prince George's County, including the Town of Riverdale Park
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Property tax revenues for the Town of Riverdale Park decrease by approximately $12,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 due to an exemption for one qualifying brewery. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding the valuation and exemption status of personal property following determinations by assessment authorities. This bill creates a specific municipal personal property tax exemption in Prince George's County for small alcoholic beverage manufacturers.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals regarding state and local property tax matters, including potential disputes over personal property assessment and exemption qualifications under the Tax - Property Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of extraordinary development district to include the site of a qualifying immersive entertainment venue. Authorizes Prince George's County or its revenue authority to use bond proceeds to acquire, construct, or rehabilitate the venue. Authorizes the Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission to pledge specified taxes as bond security upon adopting required resolutions. Establishes that exterior visual effects displayed on an immersive entertainment venue are not considered signs under county zoning ordinances. Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to grant waivers or exceptions to provisions requiring State approval for the venue.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County; Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County; Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission; private developers and operators of immersive entertainment venues
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Prince George's County revenues and expenditures increase beginning as early as fiscal 2026 from bond proceeds, tax revenues, and subsequent debt service payments. A portion of Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission property tax revenues within the district may be redirected, though specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1247 adds § 8-706 to the Transportation Article, granting the Secretary of Transportation specific statutory authority to issue waivers or exceptions to state outdoor advertising approval requirements for an immersive entertainment venue.

The State Highway Administration oversees and enforces outdoor advertising regulations along state highways under Title 8, Subtitle 7 of the Transportation Article, which the bill makes eligible for Secretary-granted waivers for qualifying venues.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article regarding tax increment financing mechanisms intended to facilitate major private tourism, arts, and entertainment infrastructure investments, and the Department was consulted as an information source.
The bill amends provisions within the Land Use Article concerning zoning classification and tax increment agreements, and the Department of Planning provided information for the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace to study and recommend expanding part-time State employment opportunities. Requires the workgroup to focus on removing employment obstacles for individuals challenged by full-time employment. Directs the Department of Budget and Management to provide staff for the workgroup. Requires the workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by September 15, 2027. Requires the department to distribute guidance to State agencies on expanding part-time employment by December 31, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace; Maryland Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, State personnel, and individuals challenged by traditional full-time employment structures, including caregivers, individuals with disabilities, and older adults
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected. The Department of Budget and Management can staff the workgroup and issue guidance using existing budgeted resources, and any member travel reimbursements are minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary agency tasked with staffing the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace. The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves on the workgroup, and DBM is required to develop and distribute guidance to State agencies on expanding part-time employment opportunities based on the workgroup's findings.

The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is a designated member of the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically tasked with outlining steps to encourage the expansion of part-time employment within the Department of Transportation.

The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland (or designee) serves on the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically tasked with outlining steps to encourage the expansion of part-time employment within USM.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary study entity, the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace, charged with evaluating policies, studying economic and operational effects, and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace to examine inclusive employment opportunities.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as a member of the workgroup to assist in studying state employment barriers and opportunities for individuals with disabilities.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.
The Comptroller of Maryland (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.

The Governor is tasked with designating the chair of the workgroup and appointing a representative from a State employees union, with discretionary authority to appoint additional community representatives and a labor economist.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and coordinating appointments to state task forces and workgroups, including the appointments authorized under this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certification standards established by a credentialing entity to prohibit certified recovery residences from refusing services. Applies this protection specifically to individuals receiving medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder. Prohibits certified recovery residences from requiring individuals to cease or modify treatment before receiving services. Authorizes credentialing entities to revoke certificates of compliance from noncompliant recovery residences. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals receiving medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder and operators of certified recovery residences
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local revenues or expenditures because the bill codifies existing Behavioral Health Administration nondiscrimination policies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), primarily through its Behavioral Health Administration (BHA), oversees and approves the credentialing entity that establishes certification standards, inspects, and certifies recovery residences under Title 19, Subtitle 25 of the Health - General Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study housing availability and affordability in Montgomery County. Requires the Department to make recommendations to increase housing availability and affordability in the county. Mandates that the study identify housing makeup by unit type, development prospects, and regulatory and market impacts. Requires the Department to confer with specified Montgomery County agencies regarding data collection and analysis. Requires interim reports by February 1, 2027, and February 1, 2028, and a final report by February 1, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, housing developers, and local government agencies in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 for the Department of Housing and Community Development to hire an external consultant to conduct the study. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to conduct a multi-year study on housing availability and affordability in Montgomery County, consult with local agencies, and submit annual interim and final reports. The fiscal note indicates an increase in general fund expenditures of $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 to hire a consultant.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local zoning authorities to maintain Patuxent Research Refuge and Beltsville Agricultural Research Center lands in open space zoning classifications. Continues non-commercial, non-industrial, and non-residential zoning restrictions if the federal government sells, leases, licenses, or encumbers these properties. Prohibits converting central natural areas within either property to agriculture, active recreation, forestry, or other plant harvesting. Requires local authorities to hold a public hearing prior to any development on refuge or center property. Mandates a final determination in consultation with state environmental and natural resources departments that development will not substantially impact central natural areas.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Council; District Council for Prince George's County; Maryland Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County and Prince George's County zoning authorities, federal land managers for the Patuxent Research Refuge and Beltsville Agricultural Research Center, and prospective land developers or purchasers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that local zoning authorities and the district council must consult with the Department of Natural Resources prior to approving any development on Patuxent Research Refuge or Beltsville Agricultural Research Center lands to ensure there is no substantial impact on central natural areas.

The bill explicitly requires local zoning authorities and the district council to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment before rendering a final decision on any proposed development on Patuxent Research Refuge or Beltsville Agricultural Research Center land.

The Department of Planning serves as the state's primary agency for land use planning and policy guidance; while not given direct regulatory mandates under the bill, it monitors state and local land use and zoning legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Neighborhood Social Connection and Development Program within the West North Avenue Development Authority. Authorizes the Authority to annually set aside up to $150,000 in existing funds for program grants. Requires participating organizations to collaborate with West North Avenue Corridor residents on planned events and projects. Expands the purpose of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund to include assisting the Authority with blight removal. Requires the Authority to submit annual comprehensive grant-awarding reports beginning December 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, community development corporations, neighborhood associations, volunteer groups, and nonprofit organizations within the West North Avenue Corridor in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures in total are not expected to change, though the West North Avenue Development Authority may redirect up to $150,000 annually from existing funds to award grants. State revenues, the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, and Baltimore City operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the statutory purpose of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development, to assist the West North Avenue Development Authority in expeditiously removing blighted property in Baltimore City.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is a statutory partner named alongside the Department of Housing and Community Development, Baltimore City, and the West North Avenue Development Authority in utilizing the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund for blight removal.
The bill requires the West North Avenue Development Authority to submit an annual report to the Governor on its comprehensive grant-awarding activities under the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires regulations governing the catalytic revitalization project tax credit application process to emphasize applications that promote workforce housing. Defines workforce housing to include rental housing affordable to households earning between 50% and 100% of area median income. Includes homeownership housing affordable to households earning between 60% and 120% of area median income. Expands the homeownership income threshold up to 150% of area median income in designated Maryland Mortgage Program target areas. Directs the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt implementing regulations in consultation with the Department of Commerce.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Developers and property owners applying for catalytic revitalization project tax credits, and households seeking workforce housing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on overall State or local revenues or expenditures. The Department of Housing and Community Development can update regulations using existing budgeted resources, though the allocation of tax credit awards among projects may shift.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency administering the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit and is responsible for updating its program regulations to emphasize applications that promote workforce housing.
Section 6-904 of the Housing and Community Development Article requires the Secretary of DHCD to consult with the Department of Commerce when adopting regulations for the tax credit program.
As the State's tax collection and enforcement authority, the Comptroller administers the claiming of the catalytic revitalization project tax credit against the State income tax.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the University of Maryland, College Park to study establishing a universal monthly payment program for caregivers. Directs the Department of Human Services to assist by identifying potential funding sources and operating costs. Requires the university to examine economic impacts, tax revenues, and appropriate stipend amounts in consultation with the Comptroller. Directs the Department of Human Services to consult with the Maryland Department of Aging, Maryland Department of Health, and local agencies. Requires the university to submit a final report to specified General Assembly committees by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland, College Park; Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Caregivers supporting qualified family members who are elderly, have Alzheimer's disease, or have developmental or functional disabilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures increase by $490,000 in FY 2027 only for the University of Maryland, College Park to conduct the study and complete the report. Revenues are unaffected. The Department of Human Services and the Office of the Comptroller can perform required tasks using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the University of Maryland, College Park (a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland) as the lead entity responsible for conducting the feasibility study, exploring caregiver stipend amounts, and submitting the final report, resulting in an estimated $490,000 fiscal impact in FY 2027.

The Department of Human Services is explicitly tasked with assisting the University of Maryland, College Park with the study by identifying funding sources, determining administrative and operating costs, and conducting interagency consultations.

The study must be conducted in consultation with the Office of the Comptroller to examine the economic impact of caregiver stipends on state and local economies, tax revenues, and public benefits participation.
The Department of Human Services is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Aging in conducting the feasibility study for the caregiver infrastructure program.
The Department of Human Services is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Health as part of the feasibility study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations authorizing a residential service agency to train licensed nurses after hire. Authorizes a residential service agency providing private duty nursing to employ licensed nurses who lack department-established clinical experience. Requires the agency to implement an approved training program and assign a preceptor until competency is demonstrated. Mandates clinical supervision by a qualified registered nurse and competency evaluations documented in the nurse's personnel file. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: residential service agencies providing private duty nursing services, licensed nurses, and patients receiving private duty nursing care
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $204,800 in FY 2027 ($152,300 general funds and $52,600 federal funds) for two staff positions within the Maryland Department of Health and Medicaid, offset by $52,600 in federal fund revenues. No effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with adopting regulations for on-site nurse training programs at residential service agencies (RSAs), approving training programs and competency evaluations via the Office of Health Care Quality, and conducting provider audits through Medicaid, which incurs direct fiscal and staffing impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners to issue barbershop and beauty salon beer, wine, and liquor licenses. Expands the existing beer and wine license to include liquor. Authorizes license holders to provide up to 1.7 ounces of liquor to a customer during one visit. Restricts service to customers receiving barbering or cosmetology services or attending a fund-raising event. Permits service during normal business hours until 9 p.m., including Sundays without a separate Sunday license.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: barbershop and beauty salon owners, permit holders, and customers in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County revenues and expenditures are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes barbershop and beauty salon alcoholic beverage licenses for holders of barbershop and beauty salon permits issued under the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which are regulated and licensed by boards within the Maryland Department of Labor.
The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers excise and sales taxes related to alcoholic beverage sales and consumption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the African American Heritage Preservation Program to be the Speaker Adrienne A. Jones African American Heritage Preservation Program. Repeals the authority of the Secretary of Human Services to appoint the executive director of the Maryland Commission for Women. Designates the executive director as a skilled service employee rather than a special appointee. Expands the Commission's statutory duties regarding research on disparities, legislative advocacy, and partner organization programs. Authorizes the Commission to appoint advisory committees in all fields affecting women in the State. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Commission for Women; Maryland Historical Trust; Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture
qa_results.stakeholders: Women in Maryland, statewide women's organizations, local commissions for women, and the executive director of the Maryland Commission for Women
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Negligible impact on the Department of Human Services to reclassify the executive director position. The Maryland Commission for Women can implement requirements within existing budgeted resources, and renaming the preservation program has no state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission for Women is housed within the Department of Human Services. The bill alters the commission's statutory duties and modifies personnel provisions governing its executive director, specifying that the position is in the skilled service rather than a special appointment.

The Maryland Historical Trust, which is overseen by the Department of Planning, administers the African American Heritage Preservation Program that the bill renames to the Speaker Adrienne A. Jones African American Heritage Preservation Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory powers, duties, research mandates, and leadership appointment provisions of the Maryland Commission for Women.
The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article (§ 6-212) to update the name of the program prioritized for funding within sustainable communities.

As the central personnel and human resources agency administering the State Personnel Management System, DBM oversees job classifications and changes affecting positions transitioned into the skilled service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Education to include college enrollment and six-year graduation rates in an annual child welfare report. Mandates the department include, where appropriate, comparison data for students not in the child welfare system. Directs the department and the Department of Human Services to submit an educational outcomes report by December 1, 2026. Requires the report to identify service gaps and provide recommendations to improve foster youth outcomes. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: children and foster youth in the State child welfare system
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Department of Human Services can implement the reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland State Department of Education to include new college enrollment and six-year graduation metrics for foster youth in its annual child welfare report, provide comparison data, and collaborate with the Department of Human Services to submit a comprehensive report on improving educational outcomes for students in foster care.

As the state's child welfare agency, DHS is a joint recipient of the annual reporting data under Family Law § 5-1312 and is statutorily required to cooperate with MSDE in developing and submitting the 2026 report to the General Assembly regarding services and educational outcomes for foster youth.

MLDSC is the state entity responsible for linking student records between K-12 and postsecondary education. Reporting on the number of foster youth who enroll in college and graduate within six years relies directly on longitudinal data matching systems maintained by MLDSC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Department of Education to establish a sliding fee copayment scale for the Child Care Scholarship Program. Exempts families with household incomes at or below the federal poverty line from paying child care copayments. Repeals the statutory process and special fund for granting presumptive eligibility under the program. Requires the department to identify, inform, and assist applicants qualifying for publicly funded prekindergarten or Head Start. Mandates at least 90 days of notice before the department implements the new copayment system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Child Care Scholarship Program applicants and recipients, low-income families with young children, and participating child care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $749,700 in FY 2027 for one staff position and one-time IT system modifications, with ongoing expenditures between $118,200 and $134,800 annually through FY 2031. Copayment revenue and presumptive eligibility repeals may offset costs to serve more families without increasing net program spending. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) directly administers the Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program. The bill authorizes MSDE to implement a sliding fee scale and partial scholarships, alters copayment requirements, repeals presumptive eligibility provisions, requires MSDE to coordinate Pre-K and Head Start options for applicants during enrollment freezes, and imposes reporting requirements, resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of $749,700 in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Decreases the archery hunting safety zone in Baltimore City from 150 yards to 50 yards. Excludes areas within Legislative District 43A from this reduced archery safety zone. Prohibits archery hunters within 50 yards of occupied buildings without advance permission from the owner or occupant. Applies the safety zone to dwelling houses, residences, churches, and other buildings or camps occupied by human beings. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: archery hunters and property owners or occupants in Baltimore City (excluding Legislative District 43A)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to decrease the archery hunting safety zone from 150 yards to 50 yards in parts of Baltimore City. The Department of Natural Resources oversees wildlife management, regulates hunting, and enforces hunting safety zones statewide.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Human Services to disclose child abuse or neglect records after a finalized indicated finding. Permits disclosure to administrators of government-operated child care centers or centers in State-occupied buildings. Allows disclosure to coaches, team administrators, or managers of youth sports programs for minors. Authorizes disclosure to personnel of organizations with temporary care, custody, or supervision of a child. Restricts these disclosures to evaluating an individual's suitability for employment or voluntary service. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants and volunteers for youth-serving positions, youth sports programs, government child care centers, organizations caring for or supervising children, and individuals with indicated findings of child abuse or neglect
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Department of Legislative Services projects the Department of Human Services can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency responsible for maintaining child abuse and neglect records and the centralized confidential database. The bill directly expands DHS's authority to disclose reports and records of indicated child abuse or neglect to certain child care administrators, youth sports organizations, and child supervision entities for employment and volunteer suitability determinations.

MSDE regulates and oversees child care centers and programs referenced in the bill under Title 9.5 of the Education Article, and the agency was consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note regarding personnel screening and child care facility administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the homeowners' property tax credit application cycle to operate year-round for each taxable year. Extends the standard application filing deadline from October 1 to February 14 of the taxable year. Repeals the provision authorizing late applications for good cause through October 31. Establishes property tax payment due dates for credits granted on applications received after October 1 but on or before February 14. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners eligible for the property tax credit and local governments providing local supplemental credits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $168,200 annually beginning in fiscal 2028 due to additional credits granted. Local revenues decrease in counties and municipalities that provide local supplemental property tax credits to the extent that more homeowners become eligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board adjudicates appeals of property tax determinations made by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), including disputes regarding property tax credits and exemptions. Altering the application cycle and deadlines for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit may impact the volume or timing of taxpayer eligibility appeals.

As the State's principal fiscal agency responsible for budget development and supervision, DBM is impacted by the projected ongoing increase of approximately $168,200 in annual General Fund expenditures starting in FY 2028 to fund additional homeowners' property tax credits.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative review body for tax disputes, hearing appeals from final decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board regarding property tax assessments and credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to procure a third-party entity to conduct an independent staffing study. Mandates an assessment of information technology and cybersecurity staffing needs across Executive Branch principal departments. Directs the study to analyze capability gaps, evaluate department technology environments, and recommend updated staffing models. Requires recommendations for updated job classifications and pay scales informed by State and local government compensation data. Requires the department to submit the completed study to the Governor and General Assembly by November 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Information technology and cybersecurity professionals in Maryland State government and principal departments of the Executive Branch
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $250,000 in each of fiscal 2027 and 2028, totaling $500,000 across the two-year period, to procure the study. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency responsible for procuring the third-party study, assessing IT and cybersecurity staffing needs, managing the $500,000 fiscal expenditure, and reporting findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee compensation, salary structures, and job classifications, which the mandated study directly evaluates for IT and cybersecurity positions.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments subject to the IT staffing assessment and is a designated recipient of the final study and recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Voids any trust provision purporting to penalize an interested person for contesting the trust if probable cause exists. Invalidates trust provisions that penalize an interested person for instituting other proceedings relating to the estate. Aligns trust penalty enforceability with existing Maryland law governing no-contest clauses in wills. Applies prospectively only to causes of action arising on or after July 1, 2026. Prohibits retroactive application to any cause of action arising before the effective date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: settlors, trustees, and beneficiaries or interested persons involved in Maryland trusts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill voids in terrorem clauses in trusts if probable cause exists for instituting proceedings, directly impacting trust litigation, estate disputes, and judicial proceedings heard within the Maryland court system.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court, which frequently interacts with estate and testamentary trust proceedings affected by in terrorem provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a 1-hour expedited processing tier and a $1,000 fee for specified documents filed with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Requires the Department to process eligible documents within 1 hour after receipt. Applies this timeframe to documents filed at least 1 hour before the Department's close of business. Requires filed documents to first receive preclearance acceptance from the Department. Takes effect January 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Business entities and law firms filing corporate and organizational documents with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation on an expedited basis
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues likely increase beginning in fiscal 2028 from expedited filing and preclearance fees, but the exact increase is indeterminate. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill with existing resources. No local government fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a regulatory framework for payment stablecoin services institutions and State issuers under the Maryland Stablecoin Act. Designates the Office of Financial Regulation as the State payment stablecoin regulator. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to issue operating certificates to qualifying nondepository trust companies and credit union service organizations. Prohibits certificate holders from extending credit, accepting consumer deposits, or accepting insured deposits. Lowers the examination fee for a new commercial bank charter from $15,000 to $7,000. Requires commercial banks and credit unions to notify the Commissioner before offering stablecoin-related services or seeking federal issuer authorization.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: nondepository trust companies, credit union service organizations, commercial banks, credit unions, and stablecoin users
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. The Office of Financial Regulation can implement the regulatory framework using existing budgeted resources. Revenue reductions resulting from lowering the commercial bank charter examination fee from $15,000 to $7,000 are expected to be minimal and recuperated through annual regulatory assessments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), a principal regulatory division within the Maryland Department of Labor, with serving as the State Payment Stablecoin Regulator under the federal GENIUS Act of 2025. OFR is responsible for evaluating applications, issuing certificates, establishing assessments, conducting oversight, and enforcing compliance for payment stablecoin service institutions and state issuers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires manufacturers of menstrual hygiene products to list all ingredients on each consumer-facing package sold in Maryland starting April 1, 2028. Mandates that ingredients appear in order of predominance and be displayed prominently in conspicuous type. Authorizes manufacturers to list a confidential substance by its common name to protect confidentiality. Defines menstrual hygiene products as disposable or reusable products used to absorb or contain menstruation or vaginal discharge. Designates a violation as an unfair or deceptive trade practice subject to Consumer Protection Division enforcement and penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Manufacturers and consumers of menstrual hygiene products sold in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties, and the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can handle enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that a failure to comply with menstrual hygiene product ingredient labeling requirements is an unfair or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires centers performing mammography testing to include a notice regarding breast arterial calcification in screening results letters. Mandates specific language explaining that breast arterial calcification may indicate an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Advises patients with breast arterial calcifications to discuss cardiovascular risks and potential additional testing with their physician. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations modifying the notice if medical evidence changes. Prohibits construing the notice requirement to create a standard of care or basis for a cause of action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients receiving mammography screening, mammography testing centers, and physicians
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local government finances and operations are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1364 amends the Health - General Article regarding mammography result notices and grants the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) discretionary authority to adopt regulations modifying the required notice language if medical evidence changes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover evaluation and management of menopause. Mandates that health occupations boards grant at least two hours of continuing education credit for each hour completed on menopause. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to identify an approved menopause training program in consultation with professional associations. Alters the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness by adding menopause expertise and women's representation. Requires the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Commission for Women to submit policy and access reports by October 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Commission for Women; Maryland Insurance Administration; State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals experiencing perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal symptoms; licensed health care providers who evaluate and manage menopause; commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; health occupations licensing boards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,300 in FY 2027 and $30,200 in FY 2028 for the Maryland Department of Health to retain contractual staff and vendor support for required evaluations and reports. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2027 from filing fees. Local government expenditures may increase minimally for fully insured employee health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency. MDH is tasked with identifying approved menopause training programs for health professional licensees, overseeing health occupations boards updating continuing education rules, administering the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, and conducting two comprehensive studies and reports to the General Assembly regarding community health worker outreach and clinical education.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates commercial health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans subject to the bill's new insurance coverage mandate for the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated symptoms, requiring policy form reviews and complaint handling.

The Maryland Commission for Women is administratively housed within the Department of Human Services. The bill adds the Commission's Executive Director to the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness and tasks the Commission with evaluating state policy initiatives and submitting a report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory membership and composition of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness and assigns formal evaluation and reporting duties to the Maryland Commission for Women.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate compliance and fiscal impacts associated with state-mandated health insurance coverage expansions.
MDH must consult with institutions of higher education to evaluate methods for increasing clinical and postgraduate education opportunities regarding menopausal evaluation and treatment.
MHEC oversees postsecondary education standards and contributed to the fiscal note analysis regarding MDH's consultation with higher education institutions on clinical training programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care to envision a comprehensive health care system for Maryland. Requires the Commission to study delivery models, provider reimbursement rates, coverage scope, and network barriers. Directs the Commission to submit preliminary reports in 2027 and 2028 and a final report by December 1, 2029. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide staff for the Commission. Conditions the Commission's implementation on securing private funding before June 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland health care consumers, health care practitioners, health insurers, hospitals, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in special fund revenues and expenditures from fiscal 2027 through 2030 if the Maryland Health Care Commission secures sufficient private funding to support commission operations; no effect in fiscal 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC is the primary implementing agency tasked with providing staff support for the Commission, determining required funding levels, and securing the private funding upon which the bill is contingent.

The Secretary of Health and the Deputy Secretary of Health Care Financing (Medicaid) serve as statutory members on the Commission, which focuses on reforming the statewide health care delivery system.
The Executive Director of the Health Services Cost Review Commission serves as a designated member of the Commission to advise on hospital financing, cost containment, and system reform.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is a statutory member of the Commission, which is tasked with studying coverage, health benefit designs, and health insurance access.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a designated member of the Commission, which will examine health insurance regulation, network adequacy, and high-deductible plans.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Commission.
The Governor jointly designates the Commission chair with legislative presiding officers, appoints several key members to the body, and receives the required preliminary and final reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a multi-year temporary advisory body (the Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care in Maryland) scheduled to operate through May 31, 2030.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting the numerous gubernatorial appointees specified in the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Audit and Finance Compliance Unit in the Department of Budget and Management to monitor Executive Branch audit compliance. Requires the Governor to implement systems and processes to monitor Executive departmental units correcting Office of Legislative Audits findings. Directs the unit to assist Executive departmental units with four or more repeat audit findings or unsatisfactory audits. Requires the unit to establish a specialized team to review resolution timelines, perform sample tests, and monitor progress. Mandates that the unit submit an annual report on audit findings to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by October 1. Authorizes specified legislators, executive officials, and the unit to view unredacted cybersecurity audit findings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive Branch departmental units subject to Office of Legislative Audits reviews, state internal auditors and compliance personnel, and legislative oversight committees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $216,971 in FY 2026 and $2,288,120 in FY 2027 to support nine new regular positions and contractual services under contingent budget appropriations. Out-year expenditures range from $2.14 million to $2.35 million annually through FY 2031. There is no effect on revenues or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1369 establishes the Audit and Finance Compliance Unit within the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). DBM is the primary implementing agency, responsible for staffing the unit, providing technical assistance to other executive units, and producing annual compliance reports, with an expenditure impact of approximately $2.29 million and nine new positions.

The entire statutory framework created by the bill centers on monitoring, remediating, and reporting on audit findings and recommendations issued by the Office of Legislative Audits (OLA), including handling unredacted cybersecurity findings.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor implement systems and processes to monitor executive departmental units' efforts to resolve audit findings, and authorizes the Governor, Chief of Staff, and Deputy Chiefs of Staff to review unredacted cybersecurity audit findings.

DoIT, through the State Chief Information Security Officer, plays a key role in tracking and remediating cybersecurity and repeat audit findings across state agencies, and manages the information technology tracking tools used to monitor audit compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Health Centralization Commission to recommend ways to increase collaboration between the Department of Health and health occupations boards. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission and the Office of Health Care Quality to publish facility inspection dates and quality metrics online. Directs each health occupations board to annually certify compliance with State minimum cybersecurity requirements to the Secretary of Information Technology. Mandates each health occupations board to designate a liaison and provide requested information to the commission within 10 business days. Requires the commission to convene by July 1, 2026, and submit annual findings and recommendations beginning December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Centralization Commission; Maryland Health Care Commission; Office of Health Care Quality; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Information Technology; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State health occupations boards, licensed health care practitioners, health care facilities inspected by the Office of Health Care Quality, and Maryland health care consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources, with no impact on State revenues. The bill has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission, in collaboration with the Office of Health Care Quality, establish a process to receive inspection dates and quality metrics and publish them on its Maryland Quality Reporting website.

The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), and its affiliated health occupations boards. MDH leadership sits on the newly created Maryland Health Centralization Commission to improve departmental collaboration and oversight of the boards.
The bill requires each health occupations board to annually certify to the Secretary of Information Technology that their IT systems comply with State minimum cybersecurity requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates an advisory entity, the Maryland Health Centralization Commission, to advise the General Assembly and develop recommendations regarding health occupations boards.

The bill directly responds to recent OLA audit findings concerning regulatory services and health occupations boards, and the newly established commission is tasked with ensuring boards remedy audit findings.
The bill requires annual reports detailing findings, recommendations, and draft legislation from the Maryland Health Centralization Commission to be submitted to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Maryland Children’s Health Program to issue prior authorization determinations for transfers to special pediatric hospitals. Mandates delivery of the determination within three business days after receiving a request from a special pediatric hospital. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing a retrospective review process by December 31, 2026. Requires the regulations to include peer-to-peer reconsideration of medical necessity determinations requested by a pediatric specialty hospital. Mandates retrospective reviews for denials of hospital admissions or reimbursements issued on or after January 1, 2025. Specifies that the retrospective review process must be conducted by a licensed physician.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: special pediatric hospitals and pediatric patients enrolled in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program or Maryland Children's Health Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to modify utilization control agent contracts and conduct retrospective reviews, funded 50% from general funds and 50% from federal fund revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP). HB 1376 directly mandates that MDH provide prior authorization determinations for transfers to special pediatric hospitals within three business days upon request and adopt regulations by December 31, 2026, establishing a retrospective review process.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Redirecting Safe Prescription Drugs Pilot Program to expand medication access for underserved populations. Requires the Secretary of Health to collaborate with the federal Drug Enforcement Agency and four registered drop-off sites. Directs participating drop-off sites to separate eligible, unopened, noncontrolled prescription medications collected during National Prescription Drug Take Back Day. Requires participating sites to transfer eligible medications to a State repository and provide collected controlled substances to the DEA. Requires the Secretary of Health to report collection data to the State Board of Pharmacy and the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Pharmacy
qa_results.stakeholders: Underserved patients needing prescription medications, participating drop-off sites, and licensed drug repositories in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Pharmacy can handle oversight and reporting responsibilities with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Secretary of Health to administer the Redirecting Safe Prescription Drugs Pilot Program, collaborate with the federal Drug Enforcement Administration and participating drop-off sites, and report findings to the Maryland State Board of Pharmacy (housed within MDH) and the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Lowers the statutory minimum commission rate paid by the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund from 10% to 5%. Applies this reduced minimum commission rate to private passenger auto insurance policies issued by the Fund. Maintains the existing maximum commission cap of 15% of the total premium. Prohibits the Fund from paying a commission on policies written directly without producer involvement. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
qa_results.stakeholders: fund producers licensed to sell Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund policies, small business insurance agencies, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MAIF nonbudgeted expenditures decrease beginning in FY 2027, potentially by several hundred thousand dollars annually, to the extent MAIF lowers commission rates paid to producers. State operations, state revenues, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1387 directly governs the operations and statutory obligations of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF). It alters the minimum commission rate MAIF must pay to producers for private passenger auto insurance policies from 10% to 5% and prohibits commissions on direct-written policies, leading to a notable decrease in MAIF's nonbudgeted operating expenditures.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's insurance industry, licenses insurance producers, and enforces provisions under the Insurance Article, making the regulatory framework regarding producer commissions relevant to its oversight authority.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of child abuse to include female genital mutilation for mandatory reporting provisions. Prohibits knowingly performing, attempting, conspiring, or transporting an individual under age 18 for female genital mutilation. Increases maximum criminal penalties for violations to 10 years imprisonment and a $10,000 fine. Requires health occupations licensing boards to revoke the license of an individual convicted of violations. Authorizes victims of female genital mutilation to file civil actions for actual, compensatory, and punitive damages. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to publish annual reports and distribute culturally appropriate educational materials.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; health occupations licensing boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors at risk of female genital mutilation, victims of female genital mutilation, licensed health care practitioners, mandatory child abuse reporters, and parents or legal guardians of minors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $39,500 in FY 2027, $40,900 in FY 2028, and $17,900 in FY 2029 for a part-time contractual health policy analyst at the Maryland Department of Health to establish data collection, publish educational materials, and prepare annual reports. The position terminates on December 1, 2028. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill's provisions, including collaborating to develop, publish, and distribute educational materials, coordinating with health occupations boards to enforce mandatory license revocations, submitting an annual report to the General Assembly, and incurring direct fiscal expenditures for personnel.

The bill alters the definition of child abuse to include female genital mutilation under Family Law provisions, directly impacting local departments of social services that receive and investigate mandatory abuse reports. In addition, the Social Services Administration within DHS is explicitly required to consult with MDH on the annual report.

The bill creates a specific civil cause of action for victims in the circuit courts with an extended statute of limitations, and also alters felony criminal provisions, impacting court caseloads and judicial administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill increases the maximum criminal penalty for female genital mutilation from 5 to 10 years of imprisonment, potentially increasing the length of stay for individuals committed to State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings and will be responsible for defending individuals charged under the expanded criminal prohibitions and increased felony penalties.

MSP is a primary law enforcement agency responsible for investigating felony violations, receiving mandatory reports of child abuse involving female genital mutilation, and consulting on data collection for MDH's annual report.

The bill explicitly mandates that educational materials on female genital mutilation be distributed to schools, and educators are designated mandatory reporters of child abuse under the impacted reporting statutes.
OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and health occupations licensing boards regarding license revocations, regulatory actions, and defense of state actions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes warranty protections and repair procedures for consumers purchasing or holding warranties on new agricultural equipment. Requires consumers to report nonconformities by written notice via certified mail during the warranty period. Mandates manufacturers, factory branches, or authorized dealers to repair reported nonconformities free of charge within 30 days. Requires manufacturers to provide replacement equipment or a full refund if repairs fail after a reasonable number of attempts. Authorizes civil actions and bad-faith damages up to $5,000 against noncompliant manufacturers or distributors. Designates violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Purchasers, owners, and operators of agricultural equipment, as well as manufacturers, factory branches, distributors, and authorized dealers of agricultural equipment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can handle enforcement and complaint investigations using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of the Agricultural Equipment Warranty Enforcement Act as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
The bill creates a private civil right of action allowing consumers to sue equipment manufacturers or authorized dealers in Maryland courts, with provisions for bad-faith damages up to $5,000.

The bill establishes warranty protections and remedy procedures for purchasers of agricultural equipment used in the business of farming, directly affecting the economic viability and operations of the agricultural community that the department supports.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to suspend or revoke shellfish aquaculture harvester permits or registration cards for specified violations. Authorizes permit or registration card suspension for up to five years for a first violation and revocation for subsequent violations. Prohibits an individual whose permit or registration card is suspended or revoked from working in any aquaculture activity. Establishes a process and deadlines for certain sole leaseholders to remove gear or transfer their lease before termination. Authorizes the State to seize and forfeit gear and equipment if a leaseholder fails to complete the process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: shellfish aquaculture harvester permit and registration card holders and shellfish aquaculture leaseholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general and special fund expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 to cover Office of Administrative Hearings costs for permit or registration card suspension or revocation proceedings. Revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating shellfish aquaculture leases, issuing harvester permits and registration cards, conducting administrative proceedings, and executing lease transfers or gear forfeitures.
OAH conducts the required administrative hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act prior to the suspension or revocation of shellfish aquaculture permits or registration cards.
The bill penalizes violations of delivery timeframes established by the Maryland Department of Health's Vibrio Parahaemolyticus Control Plan (COMAR 10.15.07.06).
The circuit courts under AOC may receive and adjudicate petitions for judicial review filed by individuals aggrieved by DNR's final administrative decisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes and alters criminal history records check requirements for multiple health occupations licensing boards. Requires initial applicants, certain renewal applicants, and reinstatement applicants to submit fingerprints and fees to the Central Repository. Directs the Central Repository to forward criminal history record information and any subsequent updates to boards and applicants. Prohibits specified boards from issuing, renewing, or reinstating credentials before receiving required record information. qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants, licensees, and certificate holders across regulated health occupations (including acupuncturists, dentists, dental hygienists, dental radiation technologists, dietitian-nutritionists, environmental health specialists, forensic nurse examiners, medication technicians, optometrists, pharmacists, and physical therapists)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: DPSCS general fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2028 from conducting additional criminal history records checks, with potential revenues up to $946,512 depending on renewal timing. agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that applicants submit fingerprints and fees to the department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) to conduct state and national criminal history checks and report subsequent arrest information to licensing boards, resulting in notable operational and revenue impacts beginning in FY 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Budget and Management to set pay scales for certain chief financial and chief information officers. Excludes the University System of Maryland from these executive pay and qualification requirements. Requires the Department of Budget and Management to adopt minimum qualification regulations for chief financial officers by November 1, 2026. Requires qualifying chief financial officers to provide annual financial reports and an attestation letter to the Comptroller's Office. Requires units waiving liquidated damages to submit documentation to the Board of Public Works. Mandates sending the same liquidated damages documentation to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Board of Public Works; Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee; Office of the Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: chief financial officers and chief information officers in Executive Branch units; State procurement units; State contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase from general and special funds beginning in fiscal 2027 if higher pay scales are established for chief financial officers and chief information officers. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing minimum qualifications for Chief Financial Officers by regulation and setting the pay scales for both CFO and Chief Information Officer positions across qualifying executive branch units.

State units that decide not to pursue liquidated damages on procurement contracts must provide written documentation explaining the rationale for their decision directly to the Board of Public Works.

As an executive branch department receiving over $1.75 billion annually, MDH is directly subject to the bill's requirements regarding CFO qualifications, reporting to the Comptroller, and adjusted CFO/CIO pay scales.

As a major agency exceeding the $1.75 billion funding threshold, MSDE is directly impacted by the CFO minimum qualification mandates, financial reporting and attestation requirements to the Comptroller, and potential pay scale adjustments for its fiscal and IT leadership.

MDOT exceeds the $1.75 billion threshold and conducts significant procurement contracting; it is directly impacted by the CFO/CIO provisions as well as the broadened liquidated damages reporting requirements.

DHS meets the $1.75 billion annual funding threshold and will be subject to new CFO qualification standards, reporting and attestation obligations to the Comptroller, and altered executive salary scales.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Identified as one of the state agencies meeting the fiscal threshold, DPSCS is directly impacted by the revised CFO qualifications, financial reporting requirements, and executive compensation provisions.

DoIT coordinates IT strategy and leadership across the executive branch, making it relevant to the bill's establishment of statutory standards and pay scale authorizations for Chief Information Officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the September 30 deadline for Class A alcoholic beverages license holders in Baltimore City to pay supplementary Sunday sales fees. qa_results.bill_summary: Adds one nonvoting student member from each public high school to the Somerset County Board of Education. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the Governor's statutory authority to appoint qualified individuals to fill vacancies on the Somerset County Board of Education, transferring this appointment power to the County Commissioners of Somerset County.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction to distribute funds directly to eligible public charter schools. Restricts eligibility to public charter schools that had an unqualified audit in the prior fiscal year. Requires recipient charter schools to report project status to the Commission before receiving subsequent annual funds. qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public charter schools, charter school students and operators, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $116,835 in FY 2027 for administrative staff, rising to approximately $5.2 million in FY 2028 due to the mandated $200 per pupil facilities appropriation ($5.0 million) and administrative expenses. Out-year expenditures grow with inflation and projected charter school enrollment. Federal fund revenues may increase if the State obtains competitive federal charter facility grants. Direct local fiscal impact is minimal because disbursements go directly to charter schools.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) is the primary implementing agency responsible for adopting regulations, distributing funds directly to eligible public charter schools for capital improvements, debt service, or lease payments, and monitoring project reporting and compliance.

MSDE oversees the state's public education system, including the Maryland Public Charter School Program, and tracks the student enrollment data used to calculate the annual per-pupil facilities appropriation.

DBM oversees state budget preparation and execution, which is directly affected by the bill's statutory mandated General Fund appropriation of approximately $5.0 million or more annually starting in fiscal 2028.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill equal to $200 multiplied by aggregate public charter school enrollment beginning in fiscal year 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and maintain a centralized caregiver resource webpage. Mandates plain-language resources covering children, adults, and older adults with functional limitations or special health needs. Requires information on respite, financial assistance programs, safety planning, and technology data privacy considerations. Requires coordination with the State Department of Education, Department of Aging, and Developmental Disabilities Administration. Directs the department to review and update the webpage at least annually.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Caregivers in Maryland providing care or assistance due to an individual's age, disability, chronic illness, cognitive impairment, or other functional limitation, as well as the individuals receiving care.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local governmental finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health (and its Developmental Disabilities Administration) to develop, host, review, and maintain a centralized caregiver resource webpage on its website.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to coordinate with the Department of Aging to develop the webpage, which must include resources for older adults and individuals with dementia or cognitive impairments.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to coordinate with the Maryland State Department of Education to include resources and school-based supports for children with disabilities and special health care needs.
The Department of Human Services staffs the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which oversees family caregiver support services and was consulted as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires municipalities to submit candidate qualifications for each municipal office to the State Board of Elections before filing deadlines. Requires municipalities using ranked-choice voting to submit their ballot tabulation regulations to the State Board. qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, municipal election candidates, and municipal voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact as the State Board of Elections can implement the bill with existing resources. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1448 directly mandates that the Maryland State Board of Elections receive municipal election candidate qualifications, candidate lists, voting procedures/locations, and ranked-choice voting regulations from municipalities and publish this information immediately on its website.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Suitland Development Authority in Prince George's County as an instrumentality of the State.
