Authorizes the Authority to acquire property, issue grants, manage funds, and modify target area boundaries. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $500,000 to the Authority, which must become self-sustaining by fiscal 2036. Creates the Suitland Development Authority Fund to finance administrative costs, consulting fees, and employee salaries. Exempts the Authority from general state procurement law and specified state and local taxes on projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Suitland Development Authority; State Treasurer; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, commercial property owners, and businesses along the Suitland Road and Silver Hill Road corridor in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $10.0 million annually from FY 2027 through FY 2035 to capitalize the authority, with corresponding special fund revenues and expenditures. The statutory $500,000 mandated appropriation begins in FY 2028 and continues in perpetuity after the authority becomes self-sustaining in FY 2036. Prince George's County expenditures increase if local funding is provided, while local revenues may shift due to tax exemptions and future property development.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the newly established Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair. The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair, as the revitalization plan specifically addresses transportation along the Suitland Road and Silver Hill Road corridor.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair.
The bill establishes the Suitland Development Authority Fund and statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Suitland Development Authority Fund and administers state tax exemptions provided to the authority.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $500,000 for the authority in the state budget bill and requires the authority to submit its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report to the Governor by December 15, 2027.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, which includes administering the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $500,000 to the authority.

Because the authority is subject to Title 12, Subtitle 4 of the State Finance and Procurement Article as a procurement-exempt unit, it must submit its written procurement policies and procedures to the Board of Public Works for review.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland's Future Board in the Department of Commerce to develop, annually evaluate, and revise a visionary plan. qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Calvert County to borrow up to $80,957,080. qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County expenditures increase by approximately $52,300 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $100,900 annually thereafter due to increased salaries and benefits. State revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC coordinates higher education policy, receives annual reporting on Dream Act tuition exemptions, and administers state-supported financial aid programs whose eligibility is directly linked to in-state tuition status.

MHEC coordinates higher education policy, receives annual reporting on Dream Act tuition exemptions, and administers state-supported financial aid programs whose eligibility is directly linked to in-state tuition status.
USM institutions are required to implement the altered documentation and residency requirements for out-of-state tuition exemptions and may experience tuition revenue and enrollment impacts.
As an independent public university, Morgan State must implement the revised Dream Act exemption rules and could see an impact on student tuition revenues and admissions.
As an independent public four-year institution, St. Mary's College is subject to the bill's changes regarding out-of-state tuition exemption eligibility and documentation standards.
The bill bases tuition exemption eligibility on Maryland income tax return filings, which are administered and verified through records held by the Comptroller's Office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Restructures State energy assistance programs, utility ratemaking standards, and clean energy initiatives to reduce ratepayer costs. Modifies the EmPOWER Maryland Program by removing gas companies and lowering electric greenhouse gas reduction targets. Lowers the large load customer demand threshold from 100 megawatts to 25 megawatts. Mandates that high-voltage transmission line owners participate in a regional transmission organization. Directs the Public Service Commission to implement a successor net energy metering program capped at 6,000 megawatts. Authorizes residential customers to install one portable solar energy generating system per electric meter.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Maryland Energy Administration; Department of Natural Resources; Department of Human Services; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: residential electric and gas ratepayers, electric and gas utility companies, data center operators, solar energy developers, and energy efficiency contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $201.4 million in FY 2027, including $100.0 million for PSC rate relief grants and $100.0 million for MEA renewable energy auctions funded by the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. Special fund spending increases by $198.2 million in FY 2028 due to ongoing auctions and mandated appropriations, while general fund expenditures increase by at least $10.0 million annually from FY 2029 through FY 2031 for the Urban Trees Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places extensive regulatory, administrative, and reporting mandates on the PSC, including establishing utility rate-setting restrictions, developing and implementing a successor net energy metering program, regulating large load customers/data centers, expanding CPCN requirements to underground transmission lines, restructuring EmPOWER Maryland, and publishing new online dashboards and annual rate reports.

The bill significantly impacts MEA by mandating two annual competitive low-bid renewable energy auctions ($100 million each in FY 2027 and FY 2028) using SEIF alternative compliance payment revenues, transferring primary administration of DRIVE Act on-site clean energy incentives/rebates to MEA, reallocating RGGI proceeds within SEIF, and requiring consultation on multiple studies and dashboards.

As the independent advocate for residential utility customers, OPC is tasked with participating in rate proceedings, consulting on annual utility rate reports, bringing actions before PSC for inaccurate rate information, and participating in the stakeholder proceeding regarding the successor net metering program.

The bill directly impacts DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), which must evaluate additional CPCN applications resulting from expanded transmission line reviews and altered definitions of large capacity energy resources, conduct a study on streamlined energy permitting and priority sites, and receive an altered allocation of SEIF funding.

The bill formally transfers statutory administration of the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) from the PSC to the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) within DHS and requires DHS consultation on an automatic community solar enrollment study.

The bill authorizes BPW, upon the recommendation of the Secretary of General Services, to waive the mandatory termination for convenience clause in multi-year State procurement contracts for renewable energy generation projects.

As the State's lead procurement agency, DGS is empowered to recommend waivers to BPW for termination for convenience clauses in multi-year renewable power purchase contracts to facilitate project financing and reduce State energy costs.

The bill's restructuring of SEIF clean energy program accounts affects the dedicated funding stream currently supporting the Trust's Urban Trees Program and Climate Corps program, necessitating $10 million annually in replacement general funds starting in FY 2029.

DHCD administers low-income energy efficiency programs under the EmPOWER Maryland Program; while its targets and funding allocations remain intact, the broader restructuring of EmPOWER surcharges and goals directly intersects with its energy efficiency portfolio.
MDE is required to consult with DNR on the energy development streamlined permitting study and is operationally affected by adjustments to greenhouse gas reduction goals and EmPOWER program targets.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to seek judicial enforcement against local governments that fail to comply with residential solar permitting software implementation and inspection timeline requirements.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations of unencumbered RGGI proceeds from SEIF in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2028 and authorizes budget amendments to transfer funds for residential customer rate relief.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds lead to the statutory list of prohibited intentionally added cosmetic ingredients. Classifies violations of cosmetic ingredient prohibitions as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices. Establishes civil liability for violators causing actual harm, allowing treble damages, punitive damages, and attorney's fees. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to investigate complaints, inspect premises, and test product samples. Requires the department and the Office of the Attorney General to report a fund plan by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and sellers of cosmetic products, and consumers harmed by prohibited cosmetic ingredients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State revenues from penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act beginning in fiscal 2027. State general fund expenditures increase minimally for the Office of the Attorney General to enforce violations and for the Maryland Department of Health to conduct inspections and develop the required plan.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) with investigatory and inspection authorities under § 21-259.2, including entering premises and sampling cosmetic products to ensure compliance with prohibited ingredient standards. MDH is also required, in conjunction with the Office of the Attorney General, to develop and report a plan for a special fund to support research and treatment for conditions caused by harmful hair chemicals.

The bill classifies violations of the prohibited cosmetic ingredient statute as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). In addition, OAG is jointly tasked with MDH to develop a plan for the administration and use of a special fund derived from enforcement recoveries.

The bill creates an explicit civil cause of action and establishes specific statutory liability, statutes of limitations, and authorization for courts to award treble damages, punitive damages, and attorney's fees for actual harm sustained from prohibited cosmetic ingredients, directly affecting judicial branch proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the June 30, 2028 termination date for State operating grants to the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center. Requires the Governor to include a $10,000,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for each fiscal year thereafter. Makes permanent the mandated annual operating support for the medical center. Alters legislative findings to emphasize the ongoing need for State investment in Prince George's County healthcare. Restricts grant funding to increasing access to critical health care services and facilitating cost containment measures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center, University of Maryland Medical System Corporation, and patients and healthcare consumers in Prince George's County and southern Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2029 to maintain the mandated operating grant. Revenues are unaffected, and local government finances are not directly impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily mandates that the Governor include a $10,000,000 operating grant appropriation in the annual state budget bill for the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center for each fiscal year beyond fiscal 2028 into perpetuity.

As the principal agency responsible for preparing the state budget and managing fiscal planning, DBM is responsible for accommodating the ongoing $10,000,000 mandated general fund appropriation starting in fiscal 2029.

The bill amends the Health - General Article regarding state support and health care delivery goals for the regional medical center, impacting state health system financing and healthcare access in the region.

USM partners closely with the University of Maryland Medical System in academic and clinical programming, and was consulted on the operational and policy impacts of the medical center's ongoing state operating grant.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Office of the Comptroller to study exempting electricity purchased for agricultural purposes from sales and use tax. Requires consultation with the Public Service Commission and PJM Interconnection, LLC. Evaluates electricity purchased by farmers to raise livestock or poultry, tend soil, or handle crops. Directs electric companies to provide aggregate usage and billing information upon request. Mandates submission of the report and fiscal impact estimate to the General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller; Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland farmers and electric companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Comptroller may increase in fiscal 2027 to conduct the required study. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Office of the Comptroller to conduct a study, estimate the fiscal impact, and report to the General Assembly regarding a potential sales and use tax exemption for electricity used for agricultural purposes.

The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller's Office to consult with the Public Service Commission in studying the proposed tax exemption and examining electric utility usage and billing information.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Real Estate Advisory Committee in the Department of General Services to advise on commercial real estate matters. Requires the committee to review State long-term real estate plans annually and meet at least three times each year. Mandates an annual committee report to the Governor, Board of Public Works, and General Assembly. Expands oversight requirements for State real property acquisitions and high-value State leases. Prohibits disposing of specified Guilford Avenue property in Baltimore City without demonstrated community engagement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Board of Public Works; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies leasing or acquiring real estate, commercial property owners and landlords leasing to the State, and Baltimore City residents near Guilford Avenue
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,008 in FY 2027 for one administrative staff position in the Department of General Services, rising to $121,000 by FY 2031 due to annualization and operating costs. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency; the bill establishes the Real Estate Advisory Committee within DGS, requires DGS to provide staff and support, and requires DGS to submit cost-benefit analyses and justifications for high-value real estate leases and acquisitions, incurring direct fiscal costs for staffing.

The bill places new requirements on real property acquisitions and leases approved by BPW, requiring reporting and justifications to the Legislative Policy Committee, and establishes the advisory committee in part to advise BPW.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent advisory entity, the Real Estate Advisory Committee, charged with reviewing state real estate plans and advising on commercial real estate trends and best practices.

As an agency that manages state property, facilities, and leases, MDOT is responsible for producing and disseminating required information and justification to the Legislative Policy Committee for qualifying real estate transactions.

As an entity managing significant real property and facility leases, USM is identified in the fiscal analysis as responsible for compiling and submitting required property lease and acquisition justifications under the expanded reporting requirements.
The Governor sits on the Board of Public Works which is subject to the bill's property approval provisions, and receives the advisory committee's mandatory annual reports.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is directly advised by the new committee and subject to expanded oversight and submission requirements before approving certain high-value leases and property transactions.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is directly advised by the new committee and subject to expanded reporting and approval conditions for high-value state real estate leases.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the use of unlicensed settings for children in out-of-home placement programs. Expands the definition of unlicensed settings to include pediatric hospital overstay patients. Establishes the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel within the Governor's Office for Children. Requires pediatric overstay coordinators to convene Rapid Response Placement Teams to locate appropriate placements. Authorizes the Department of Human Services to execute emergency procurements for in-state or out-of-state placements. Establishes the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office for Children; Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: children and youth in out-of-home placements, pediatric hospital overstay patients, foster parents, hospitals, child welfare service providers, and local departments of social services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Governor's Office for Children special fund expenditures increase by $204,600 in fiscal 2027 for new staff, reflecting the phase-in of one contractual position and one permanent position. Costs annualize in subsequent years through fiscal 2031, with the contractual position terminating in fiscal 2030. The Maryland Department of Health and the Department of Human Services can absorb operational requirements within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly houses the newly established Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, creates the Senior Advisor for Children and Families within the office to oversee the panel and placement teams, and requires the office to provide administrative and staff support for both the panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families, resulting in a direct fiscal and operational impact.

The bill directly regulates DHS's out-of-home placement program by prohibiting placements in unlicensed settings and pediatric overstays, alters the duties and reporting of DHS's pediatric overstay coordinator, authorizes DHS to execute emergency procurements for youth placements, and mandates joint reporting with the Department of Health.

The bill alters requirements and data collection for MDH's pediatric overstay coordinator, designates MDH's notification system for hospitals, requires joint capacity-building reporting with DHS, and places the Secretary of Health on the review panel and advisory council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes multiple new state entities, including the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, Rapid Response Placement Teams, and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families, and its working subgroup.

The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is mandated to serve as a member of both the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.

The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is named as a statutory member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its specialized assessment and data subgroup.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (or designee) is designated to serve on the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its subgroup, which examines insurance parity and rate reform barriers.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission (or designee) is mandated to serve on the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its working subgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its working subgroup.

The Governor appoints the Senior Advisor for Children and Families (who serves at the Governor's pleasure), appoints various stakeholder members to the Review Panel and Advisory Council, and receives annual reports and recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to examine carriers issuing patterns of adverse decisions on emergency department claims. Authorizes the Commissioner to obtain independent review of carrier decisions at the carrier's expense. Requires the Commissioner to include post-acute care data in the annual appeals and grievances summary report. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission and Health Services Cost Review Commission to conduct two studies by January 1, 2027. Requires the commissions to quantify hospital and post-acute bed capacity and evaluate transitions from acute to post-acute care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Health Care Commission; Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: health insurance carriers, private review agents, hospitals, post-acute care facilities, and patients receiving emergency or post-acute services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal state fiscal impact. Studies by the Maryland Health Care Commission and Health Services Cost Review Commission, as well as additional workload for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA), can likely be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. MIA special fund revenues may increase minimally to recoup carrier examination costs. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1563 authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to conduct market examinations of carriers demonstrating a pattern of adverse decisions or grievances regarding emergency department claims/authorizations, mandate independent external reviews at the carrier's expense, and incorporate post-acute care adverse decision and grievance data into the annual appeals and grievances summary report.

The bill directly mandates that MHCC, in conjunction with HSCRC and industry representatives, conduct two major studies due January 1, 2027: one quantifying bed capacity in hospitals and post-acute settings and recommending a standardized bed reporting and auditing process, and another analyzing options to facilitate clinically appropriate transitions from acute to post-acute care.

HSCRC is mandated to partner with MHCC to conduct both required studies regarding hospital and post-acute care bed capacity, annual bed collection and auditing mechanisms, and acute to post-acute patient care transitions, submitting joint reports to the Governor and legislative committees.

MHCC is an independent regulatory agency housed within the Maryland Department of Health, and MDH was consulted as an information source regarding state health facility oversight and regulations implicated by the emergency department and post-acute care study requirements.

The Governor is designated as a recipient of the mandated study findings and recommendations from MHCC and HSCRC regarding hospital bed capacity auditing and acute to post-acute transitions due by January 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the Minority Business Enterprise Program and its related procurement requirements to July 1, 2031. Establishes new legislative findings based on the 2025 disparity study to support the program. Requires State procurement units to submit quarterly reports on minority business participation and small business awards. Directs the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to establish a small business certification review process. Expands the definition of small business to include qualifying joint ventures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Department of Social and Economic Mobility; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: certified minority business enterprises; small businesses; veteran-owned small business enterprises; State procurement units; prime contractors; applicants and licensees for cannabis, offshore wind, video lottery terminal, and sports wagering operations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal effect. State procurement agencies can implement the altered reporting deadlines and new quarterly reporting mandates using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reauthorizes the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program, requires OSBA to establish a small business certification review process, modifies OSBA's reporting schedules and mandates new quarterly tracking, and adjusts OSBA's duties regarding cannabis, offshore wind, and gaming licensees.

The bill requires annual procurement reports to be submitted to BPW, involves BPW in criteria adoption and approval of reporting forms, regulates public-private partnership approvals under MBE guidelines, and oversees the designated MBE certification agency.

OAG is statutorily required to consult on MBE plans and disparity evaluations for cannabis, offshore wind, sports wagering, and public-private partnerships, participate in criteria development for noncompliant prime contractors, and handle contractor debarment referrals.

DGS houses the Office of State Procurement, which must jointly adopt criteria for contractor debarment with OSBA, assist in developing small business reserve exemption procedures, and serve on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

The bill extends the MBE requirements applicable to cannabis licensees through July 1, 2031, and requires the Administration and its Office of Social Equity to consult on disparity evaluations and licensee MBE participation plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reauthorizes and extends MBE participation compliance requirements through 2031 for video lottery terminal (VLT) and sports wagering licensees, which the Commission is tasked with enforcing.

The bill extends the MBE requirements for approved offshore wind projects through July 1, 2031, and requires offshore wind renewable energy credit (OREC) holders to submit biannual MBE progress reports to the Commission.

MDOT serves as a designated certification agency in procurement regulations, the Secretary must be consulted regarding capital project subgoal guidelines, and the Secretary serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

Uncodified language in the bill requires the State Retirement and Pension System to provide information necessary to assess the need for remedial measures in the brokerage and investment management services industry.
The bill amends the composition of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation to specifically add the Secretary of Labor or the Secretary's designee as a member.
The Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation is required to report to the Governor annually, and OSBA operates within the Executive Department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership, chair, meeting mandates, and duties of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is a designated member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department must adhere to the new quarterly and annual procurement reporting schedules.
The Secretary of Commerce is a designated member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the agency must comply with the altered MBE/SBR reporting deadlines.
The Secretary of Health serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department is subject to the accelerated procurement reporting requirements.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the agency must submit quarterly and annual MBE/SBR data.
The Secretary of Human Services serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department is subject to the updated procurement reporting timelines.

The Secretary of Information Technology is a member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department is impacted by the modified procurement preference reporting deadlines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and must comply with revised quarterly procurement preference reporting.

The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is a statutory member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation, and the bill amends reporting rules for the Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers operational authority and project responsibilities for horse racing redevelopment projects to the Maryland Stadium Authority. Increases Maryland Stadium Authority bond authorization for Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor facilities from $400,000,000 to $425,000,000. Designates Montgomery County and Howard County as grantees under the Bus Rapid Transit Fund. Mandates a $5,000,000 appropriation in fiscal year 2028 for backstretch housing facilities at Laurel Park. Alters annual distributions from the State Lottery Fund and the Purse Dedication Account for racing facilities and debt service.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Transportation; State Racing Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Thoroughbred horse racing operators, backstretch workers at Laurel Park, transit riders, Prince George's County, Montgomery County, and Howard County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million annually beginning in FY 2027 due to increased statutory lottery distributions. General fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2028 only for Laurel Park backstretch housing. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028, and Purse Dedication Account expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028. Montgomery County continues to receive $27.0 million annually and Howard County receives $2.0 million annually in local bus rapid transit grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Requested the bill and serves as the primary implementing agency; designated as the successor entity to MTROA for racing and community development projects, given oversight over Pimlico operations and financial statements, authorized up to $425 million in bonds for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor, and administers project funds.

Administers the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Grant Program, which is altered to mandate multi-year grant agreements with Montgomery and Howard counties, expands authorized uses of grant funds, and increases mandated appropriations from the Transportation Trust Fund to the BRT Fund.

Responsible for executing altered statutory distributions from the State Lottery Fund to the Racing and Community Development Financing Fund, the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund, and issuing warrants from the Purse Dedication Account.

Transfers MEDCO's operational responsibilities for the Pimlico racing project to the Maryland Stadium Authority, while MEDCO is allocated $2 million annually from the Purse Dedication Account for debt service on a training facility site.

Directly designated under the bill to receive 10% of the thoroughbred racetrack operator's annual net income as local impact grants for community development projects under the Pimlico Area Joint Plan.
Houses the Maryland State Racing Commission, whose statutory authority regarding licensing, race-day allocations, Preakness Stakes transfers, and the Purse Dedication Account is altered.

Invests and manages proceeds in the Purse Dedication Account, and evaluates the fiscal impact of increased lottery fund distributions and transportation debt on state debt affordability and bond ratings.

Approves bond issuances by the Maryland Stadium Authority for Blue Line Corridor facilities and receives formal 180-day notification and alternative use plans if racing operations at Pimlico are no longer viable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Regulates and manages the State Lottery Fund from which increased statutory distributions are mandated for racing facilities and Blue Line Corridor debt service, directly affecting lottery coverage ratios.
Authorized to receive delegated adjudications as contested cases from the Maryland Stadium Authority regarding disputes over commercial viability or alternative use plans for the Pimlico site.
Mandated to include specific appropriations in the annual state budget bill, including $5 million in FY 2028 for Laurel Park backstretch housing and increased funding for the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

The bill repeals Section 10-612 of the Economic Development Article, removing provisions that required MSA to notify and report to the State Ethics Commission regarding employee service on affiliated sports foundation boards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters statutory parameters governing how public school performance is measured under the State's educational accountability program. Increases the maximum combined weight of academic indicators from 65% to 70% of the composite score. Prohibits any academic indicator of proficiency from being weighted at more than 20% of the composite score. Prohibits accountability indicators established by the State Board of Education from incorporating, referencing, or relying on teacher evaluations. Authorizes school staffing measures and completion of well-rounded curriculum measures as school quality indicators. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to submit annual reports on accountability indicators and poverty correlations through 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public schools, public school students, public school educators, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No impact on State revenues or expenditures. Any implementation costs for the Maryland State Department of Education are expected to be absorbable within existing resources, and local school system finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1582 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) that alters the statutory parameters governing the State's public school educational accountability program and school quality indicators. MSDE and the State Board of Education are directly responsible for administering the accountability system, calculating composite scores, and producing the required annual reports on accountability indicators and correlation with poverty levels.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of "slot machine" to increase allowable handheld bingo cards from 54 to 100. Specifies that an electronic instant bingo machine need not print a paper ticket unless the player chooses. Exempts authorized electronic instant bingo machines from statutory prohibitions governing illegal gaming devices. Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to adopt implementing regulations. Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to submit an independent gaming expansion study by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency; State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial electronic instant bingo licensees, qualified nonprofit gaming organizations, electronic bingo players, satellite simulcast facility operators, and gaming industry labor unions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in fiscal 2027 for the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to retain an independent consultant. State revenues and local finances in Anne Arundel and Calvert counties are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission with adopting regulations to implement changes to electronic instant bingo operations, and mandates that the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency hire an independent consultant to conduct a study and report on the impacts of potential gaming expansions by December 1, 2026, incurring up to $100,000 in general fund expenditures.

The bill explicitly requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to submit a comprehensive report detailing the potential expansion and economic impacts of electronic instant bingo, historical horse racing machines, and satellite simulcast facilities to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a racing licensee to receive a Racetrack Facility Renewal Account grant without providing a matching fund. Requires a licensee receiving grants without matching funds to conduct live racing for at least 10 years after construction completion. Directs the State Racing Commission to recapture grant funds on a pro rata basis if racing requirements fail. Requires the Commission and Department of General Services to certify completion of capital construction plans upon written request. Alters to 75% the unencumbered balance transferred between Rosecroft Raceway and Ocean Downs Race Course if either facility closes.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Racing Commission; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Horse racing licensees, particularly standardbred racing licensees operating at Rosecroft Raceway and Ocean Downs Race Course
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill allows standardbred racing licensees to access Racetrack Facility Renewal Account grant funds without matching funds but does not alter total fund revenues or distributions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Racing Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, and the bill amends provisions governing the Commission's oversight and administration of the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account, including capital plan approvals, grant requirements, regulations, and grant recapture.

The bill requires multiyear capital improvement plans to be provided to the Department of General Services and requires the State Racing Commission to consult with the Department of General Services when monitoring plan implementation and certifying capital construction completion.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program to fund oyster propagation and replenishment projects. Establishes the Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund to assist commercial watermen and seafood industry small businesses. Authorizes the temporary transfer of up to $337,500 each from two existing loan programs to the fund. Requires notification to the Department of Natural Resources when a tidal fish licensee is delinquent on a loan. Prohibits the department from approving tidal fish license transfers until the delinquent borrower becomes compliant. Mandates an annual $2,000,000 Transportation Trust Fund appropriation for the enhancement program starting in fiscal year 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial watermen; seafood industry small businesses; tidal fish license holders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2,000,000 in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the new fund under a contingent budget appropriation. Nonbudgeted revenues increase by $2,000,000 and nonbudgeted expenditures increase by $2,700,000 in fiscal 2027 to provide loans and cover administrative costs, reflecting the contingent appropriation and $675,000 transferred from other loan programs. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures increase by indeterminate amounts in future years from loan repayments and reissuance. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is the primary implementing agency for the newly created Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund. It is tasked with administering the fund, setting loan terms and eligibility criteria, executing temporary fund transfers from existing programs, and notifying DNR of delinquent borrowers.

DNR houses and administers the newly codified Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program for oyster propagation and replenishment projects, receives program funding, and is prohibited from approving transfers of tidal fish licenses for borrowers delinquent on MARBIDCO loans.

The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $2,000,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) administered by MDOT to support DNR's oyster replenishment efforts, codifying a long-standing interagency mitigation agreement between MDOT and DNR.

The bill's Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program specifically funds oyster propagation and replenishment projects that mitigate the ecological impacts of transportation, dredging, and maintenance projects at the Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore, which MPA operates.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal planning, including the implementation of the statutory mandated annual TTF appropriation of $2,000,000 starting in FY 2028 and the FY 2027 contingent general fund appropriation.
The bill requires the Governor to include a mandated annual appropriation of $2,000,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund in the state budget bill beginning in FY 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue certain Class B restaurant licenses in the 40th district. Permits new Class B licenses on West Baltimore Street and North Charles Street, subject to community agreements. Authorizes the Board to waive member-only sales restrictions for a Class C license on Eutaw Place. Alters geographic boundaries establishing restricted 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. sales hours in the district. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and restaurant owners in the 40th alcoholic beverages district of Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. Baltimore City finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article concerning alcoholic beverages licenses and hours of sale in Baltimore City. While local licensing and enforcement are administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller is the state agency responsible for overseeing alcohol regulation and administering alcoholic beverage taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters income eligibility limits for an optional local property tax credit on dwelling houses of disabled veterans. Limits eligible federal adjusted gross income to $150,000 for individual filers and $300,000 for joint filers. Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or county and municipal governing bodies to set additional eligibility criteria. Permits those governing bodies to base additional criteria on income and disability ratings. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Honorably discharged disabled veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities, their surviving spouses, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Potential decrease in local property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent local jurisdictions grant the credit and higher income limits expand eligibility. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies eligibility thresholds, including income caps and disability ratings, for local property tax credits available to disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. As the primary state agency tasked with assisting veterans and their families in accessing benefits, housing resources, and tax relief information, this legislation directly pertains to their advocacy and constituent service mission.

The bill establishes eligibility caps based on federal adjusted gross income from individual and joint income tax returns. While the tax credit is applied at the local property tax level with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller administers Maryland income tax reporting and was consulted on the fiscal and policy note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a mutual insurance holding company owning 100% of a reorganized stock insurer's capital stock to convert into a mutual insurer. Requires approval of a conversion plan by a majority of the board and at least 75% of voting members. Mandates submitting the plan and a 5-year operation plan to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner at least 60 days before conversion. Requires the Commissioner to approve the plan if it complies with statutory standards and is equitable to members. Directs the holding company and intermediate holding companies to dissolve upon conversion.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Mutual insurance holding companies, reorganized stock insurers, and their policyholders and members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net state fiscal impact. Special fund expenditures and revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration may increase correspondingly if the agency retains an outside expert to review a conversion plan at the holding company's expense; exact amounts are unavailable. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1616 directly regulates the conversion of mutual insurance holding companies to mutual insurers, requiring approval, review, and potential hearings by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner. The Maryland Insurance Administration is also authorized to retain experts to assist in reviewing plans of conversion and adopt implementing regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Designates the Village Council of Drummond as the governing body of the Village of Drummond special taxing district in Montgomery County. Establishes a three-member Village Council elected annually by village residents who are at least 18 years old. Requires the Village Council to appoint a mayor, a treasurer, a secretary, and necessary employees. Alters eligible uses of special tax levy funds and establishes an annual budget adoption process with public hearing requirements. Raises the competitive bidding threshold for material or work contracts to $15,000 and defines specific bidding exemptions. Authorizes the Village Council to establish, operate, maintain, and control non-State public ways in the village.
qa_results.responsible_party: Village Council of Drummond; Montgomery County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: residents and property owners in the Village of Drummond special taxing district in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Village of Drummond expenditures increase minimally to purchase fidelity bonds for required officers, estimated at $1,000 to $5,000 per bond for approximately two individuals, which does not materially affect village finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual salaries of the Sheriff of Howard County and the State's Attorney for Howard County. Sets each official's annual salary at $220,601 for calendar year 2027. Increases both salaries to $227,230 for 2028, $234,079 for 2029, and $241,149 for 2030 and subsequent years. Applies the salary modifications beginning with the next term of office for each position.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Government; Sheriff of Howard County; State's Attorney for Howard County
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Howard County, State's Attorney for Howard County, and Howard County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Howard County expenditures increase by approximately $48,000 in fiscal 2027, $96,000 in fiscal 2028, and at least $104,000 annually thereafter to cover higher salary costs. State operations, State finances, and county revenues are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies prior authorizations of State debt across multiple previous capital budget acts. Alters authorized uses and scopes of work for specified capital grants. Changes designated grantee names and reallocates certain grant funds among projects. Extends termination deadlines to allow grantees additional time to expend or encumber funds. Removes matching fund requirements for select local capital improvement projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of Budget and Management; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Grant recipients of prior State capital debt authorizations, including local governments, cultural institutions, community development organizations, and healthcare facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances. Modifies the conditions, purposes, and deadlines under which existing State capital grant funds may be expended, with potential impact only on local governments that receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works oversees and certifies matching funds for state debt authorizations and approves capital grants, state contracts, and expenditures modified by this omnibus bill.
DGS administers state capital grants and local legislative initiatives on behalf of the State and the Board of Public Works, and was consulted as an information source for this bill.
DBM is responsible for the state's capital budget planning, supervising budget execution, and monitoring state debt authorizations, and provided information for the fiscal note.
The bill explicitly strikes the requirement that a $10,000,000 grant to Park Heights Renaissance be used in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development.
The State Treasurer oversees the issuance of State general obligation bonds, manages debt authorizations, and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works.
The Comptroller serves as a key member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees and approves disbursements and contract terms for state-funded capital grant projects.

qa_results.bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution governing legislative and congressional election districts. Clarifies that constitutional compactness, contiguity, and equal population standards apply exclusively to General Assembly legislative districts. Establishes that no provision in the Maryland Constitution provides criteria for congressional districting boundaries. Authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional districting plans. Submits the proposed constitutional amendment and specific ballot question text to voters at the November 2026 general election.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; Maryland General Assembly; Supreme Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters and candidates for the Maryland General Assembly and the U.S. House of Representatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The proposed constitutional amendment is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the submission of a constitutional amendment to Maryland voters at the November 2026 general election, setting specific ballot language and modifying standard statutory requirements for the ballot question administered by the State Board of Elections.

The Secretary of State is responsible for the certification of statewide ballot questions and constitutional amendments, as well as serving as the custodian of state official records and constitutional changes.

The proposed constitutional amendment authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional districting plans, directly impacting judicial proceedings and appellate caseload.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides demographic and mapping support, maintains official legislative and congressional redistricting maps, and is listed as an informational source on redistricting data.

Pursuant to the bill and Article XIV of the Maryland Constitution, the official election returns regarding the proposed constitutional amendment must be transmitted to the Governor to make the official proclamation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Withdraws and repeals a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment regarding collective bargaining for State employees. Repeals Sections 2 through 4 of Chapter 156 of the Acts of 2026. Alters the contingency clause of Chapter 156 to depend on voter ratification of Chapter 155 of 2026. Prevents identical constitutional amendment questions from appearing on the November 2026 general election ballot. Takes effect immediately upon enactment as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters and State employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the change is technical and merely prevents duplicate language from appearing on the general election ballot.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 2101 directly impacts the ballot preparation responsibilities of the State Board of Elections by withdrawing and repealing duplicate constitutional amendment language from Chapter 156 of 2026, ensuring that the referendum on binding arbitration for State employee collective bargaining appears only once on the November 2026 general election ballot.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to develop uniform policies on law enforcement face coverings and identification. Prohibits law enforcement officers from wearing face coverings on duty, except as authorized by policy or during undercover operations. Mandates that uniformed officers display identification on outermost clothing and verbally disclose identifying information upon request. Bars local jurisdictions and agencies from adopting differing policies regarding officer face coverings or identification. Classifies violations as civil offenses punishable by fines up to $1,500 and as police misconduct.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: law enforcement officers and law enforcement agencies in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from District Court civil penalties. Potential minimal increase in State and local expenditures to update law enforcement officer uniforms and training programs. The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can implement the policies with existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), housed within DPSCS, is required to develop two statewide uniform policies prohibiting face coverings and mandating worn identification for law enforcement officers.
The District Court must prescribe a statewide uniform citation form, establish a schedule for fine prepayments, and schedule and adjudicate civil citation trials for violations of the bill.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, its sworn troopers are subject to the face covering prohibitions and identification display mandates, and must update uniform and training protocols accordingly.
DNR employs the Natural Resources Police, whose sworn officers are subject to the uniform policies regarding face coverings, visible outerwear identification, and associated training requirements.
MDOT oversees modal administrations that employ sworn law enforcement personnel who must adhere to the new identification and face covering mandates and adjust uniforms or training as needed.
MDTA operates its own dedicated police force, whose sworn officers must comply with the uniform policies on identification and face coverings.
MTA maintains a sworn transit police force that must comply with the MPTSC uniform policies regarding face coverings and outer uniform identification.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, whose sworn officers are directly subject to the uniform policies prohibiting face coverings and requiring visible identification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund, which is specified in the bill to receive court-ordered penalty payments from individuals adjudicated of civil violations under this Act.
USM institutions employ sworn campus police officers who are subject to MPTSC standards, requiring compliance with the uniform face covering and identification policies.
Morgan State University maintains an independent campus police department with sworn law enforcement officers who must comply with the bill's uniform identification and face covering requirements.
As a public institution maintaining campus public safety personnel, it is potentially affected by the statewide law enforcement uniform and identification policies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends collective bargaining rights to eligible nontenure track faculty at public institutions of higher education. Covers instructional nontenure track faculty at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland. Establishes a separate collective bargaining unit for nontenure track faculty at each institution. Excludes faculty at fully online institutions and faculty funded through grants, contracts, or clinical revenues. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Nontenure track instructional faculty and administrations at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for the Public Employee Relations Board increase minimally from institutional fees. Expenditures for the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland increase minimally to reimburse the board, with potentially significant but indeterminate administrative and personnel cost increases contingent on union election results and collective bargaining negotiations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PERB is responsible for administering union elections, certifying exclusive representatives, investigating unfair labor practice charges, and resolving collective bargaining disputes for the newly created nontenure track faculty bargaining units.

USM institutions are directly required to establish a separate collective bargaining unit for eligible nontenure track faculty, negotiate terms and conditions of employment, and reimburse PERB for collective bargaining election expenses.

MSU is an affected public institution of higher education directly required to recognize collective bargaining rights for its eligible nontenure track instructional faculty and handle associated negotiation and administrative costs.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the bill's provisions, requiring it to establish collective bargaining for eligible nontenure track faculty and incur potential administrative and reimbursable costs with PERB.

OAH has delegated authority from institutions to hear employee grievances and disciplinary appeals; it will experience an operational impact from training administrative law judges on the new law and potential increases in case hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands identity fraud prohibitions to include unauthorized use of personal identifying information to cause harm. Prohibits assuming another person's identity with fraudulent intent to harm, harass, intimidate, threaten, or coerce them. Prohibits using artificial intelligence or deepfake representations with fraudulent intent to cause harm or create false records. Establishes felony penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment for artificial intelligence or deepfake identity fraud violations. Authorizes victims of artificial intelligence or deepfake violations to bring civil actions for injunctive or other relief.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Office of the Attorney General; State's Attorneys
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of identity fraud, deepfake depictions, or artificial intelligence impersonation; law enforcement agencies; individuals accused of identity fraud offenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations, with any additional caseloads accommodated within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 8-301(p) of the Criminal Law Article, the Attorney General is explicitly granted authority to investigate and prosecute identity fraud violations under this section, possessing all powers of a State's Attorney including the use of a grand jury.

The Department of State Police is statutorily empowered to initiate investigations and enforce this identity fraud section statewide without jurisdictional limitations and adopts regulations governing investigative authority for other law enforcement entities under § 8-301(l) and (m).

The bill creates a new private right of action permitting victims to bring civil suits for injunctions and appropriate relief in the courts, and expands criminal identity fraud offenses handled by the state court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands identity fraud crimes and penalties (including new felony classifications for deepfake and AI fraud), impacting the caseload and representation duties of the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new and expanded misdemeanor and felony offenses carrying terms of imprisonment ranging up to 10 years, which impacts state correctional and pretrial intake and supervision operations.

The Maryland Transportation Authority Police are specifically authorized by § 8-301(m) and (n) to investigate identity fraud violations throughout the State and receive notifications of investigations occurring on MDTA property.

The Maryland Port Administration Police are explicitly authorized under § 8-301(m) and (n) to investigate identity fraud offenses throughout the State and receive investigative notifications for incidents on MPA property.

Section 8-301(n) specifically requires notification to the chief of police of the Maryland Aviation Administration when an identity fraud investigation occurs on property owned, leased, or operated by the administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires landlords of residential rental apartment buildings with 10 or more dwelling units to provide air-conditioning. Mandates landlords maintain unit temperatures at or below 80 degrees Fahrenheit from June 1 through September 30. Applies starting June 1, 2026, to newly constructed units and units previously equipped or leased with air-conditioning. Requires compliance beginning October 1, 2026, for units undergoing substantial electrical or heating system renovations. Exempts National Register historic properties and specified Housing Authority of Baltimore City developments. Preempts local laws and regulations that impose inconsistent air-conditioning requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; local code enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Tenants and landlords of residential rental apartment buildings with 10 or more dwelling units, including public housing authorities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Local government expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, for jurisdictions and local housing authorities that own or operate residential rental apartment buildings or experience increased code enforcement demand.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development is the state's principal agency for housing policy, standards, and rental housing programs. While the bill establishes statutory requirements under the Real Property Article enforced largely at the local level or through court proceedings, the department was consulted as an information source and monitors statewide rental housing standards.

The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the judicial branch administration. Landlord-tenant disputes, lease breaches, and habitability issues arising under Real Property Article statutory requirements are adjudicated within the state court system (primarily the District Court).

The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection and fair housing laws, provides legal guidance regarding tenant-landlord regulations, and served as an information source during the evaluation of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits the amount an employer may deduct from an obligor's earnings under a child support earnings withholding order or notice. Caps deductions at 35 percent of the obligor's disposable earnings under specified individual income conditions. Applies this limit when the obligor's individual income does not exceed 250 percent of federal poverty guidelines for a family of one. Excludes obligors determined to be voluntarily impoverished at the time of the most recent court order. Authorizes employees to administratively contest an earnings withholding that exceeds these statutory limits. Directs the Child Support Administration to investigate timely contest requests within 15 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Child Support Administration, Department of Human Services; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income child support obligors, employers subject to earnings withholding orders, and child support recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Human Services increase by $618,840 in FY 2029 ($210,406 general funds and $408,434 federal funds) for system programming enhancements, offset by $408,434 in federal matching revenues. Ongoing operational expenditures increase by $59,520 annually thereafter ($20,237 general funds and $39,283 federal funds). A potential reduction in overall child support collections may impact federal performance incentive payments by an indeterminate amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Child Support Administration is a division of the Department of Human Services. DHS is the primary agency responsible for administering child support services, updating the Child Support Management System (CSMS) to reflect withholding limits, investigating employee contests, and issuing relevant notices.

The bill explicitly designates the Office of Administrative Hearings as the appeals body for obligor employees contesting child support earnings withholding determinations made by the Child Support Administration.
Child support earnings withholding orders stem from court orders, and the judiciary handles underlying child support cases, voluntary impoverishment findings, and judicial contests.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and representation to the Department of Human Services' Child Support Administration and represents the agency in administrative challenges and enforcement actions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires petition signature pages and ballot questions to include plain language summaries and statements explaining voting outcomes. Prohibits the use of passive voice, legal jargon, and double negatives in required petition and ballot statements. Advances the deadline for officials to prepare and certify ballot questions to July 1 before a general election. Requires the State Board of Elections to hold a 15-day public comment period for submitted ballot question information. Mandates that election boards publicly post the full text of specified ballot questions 90 days before the election.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections; Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, petition sponsors, petition circulators, and local election officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Elections can implement the requirements using existing resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections (SBE) is the primary state entity tasked with implementing the bill. SBE must establish plain language guidelines prohibiting passive voice and legal jargon for petition summaries, administer a 15-day public comment period for submitted ballot questions, and post complete texts and links to applicable legislation online for at least 90 days before the general election.

The bill directly alters statutory deadlines and responsibilities for the Secretary of State, requiring the office to prepare and certify statewide ballot questions and petitioned referenda by July 1 prior to the general election, adhere to new plain language standards, review public comments received during the 15-day comment window, and submit the certified plain text to SBE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Designates the megalodon as the State shark. Designates The Natural History Society of Maryland as the State natural sciences museum. Requires the Governor to annually proclaim October 1 as Purple Lights Night. Establishes the annual observance to honor victims and survivors of domestic violence. Expresses Maryland's support for the elimination of domestic violence statewide. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: The Natural History Society of Maryland; victims and survivors of domestic violence in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate Bill 35 directly mandates that the Governor annually proclaim October 1 as Purple Lights Night to honor victims and survivors of domestic violence and express support for eliminating domestic violence in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters approval thresholds and oversight procedures for public school construction and systemic renovation projects. Increases the change order threshold requiring State Superintendent approval from $50,000 to $350,000. Repeals the requirement for the Interagency Commission on School Construction to approve 75% preliminary allocations annually. Requires the Interagency Commission to establish an appeal process for projects omitted from 90% budget recommendations. Mandates periodic status reports to each county board and local governing body on requested school projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Superintendent of Schools; Interagency Commission on School Construction; Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: local boards of education; local governing bodies; Maryland public school students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is largely procedural and has no direct State or local fiscal impact, though administrative changes may allow the Interagency Commission on School Construction to utilize existing resources more efficiently.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill requested by and primarily governing the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC). It alters the approval timeline for school construction allocations, establishes a new appeals process, modifies reporting deadlines for the Statewide Facilities Assessment and Maintenance Effectiveness Assessment, and updates funding review thresholds.

The bill directly amends statutory requirements governing the State Superintendent of Schools (who heads the Maryland State Department of Education), altering the thresholds and criteria for Superintendent review and approval of county school site acquisitions, facility additions, renovations, and construction change orders.

The bill amends provisions in Education Article § 5-314 governing the Department of General Services' review of public school design and construction documents, exempts change orders from DGS review, and requires DGS to coordinate with the IAC to establish timelines for project review and approval.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Port Administration to provide written notices regarding proposed land acquisitions in Anne Arundel County. Mandates notice to the Anne Arundel County Delegation at least two weeks before announcing a required public hearing. Requires written notice to the delegation when the Administration requests county approval to acquire property interests. Specifies that county approval is deemed given unless denied in writing within 90 days. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Port Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Delegation to the General Assembly and Anne Arundel County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Port Administration can handle notifications using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local finances and operations in Anne Arundel County are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends laws governing the Maryland Port Administration's procedures, requiring it to provide written notice to the Anne Arundel County Delegation when requesting approval or holding a hearing to acquire land or improvements in Anne Arundel County.
The Maryland Port Administration is a modal administration under the Department of Transportation, which oversees its operational policies and land acquisition activities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits counterfeiting a lease of real property or rental agreement relating to real property with intent to defraud. Prohibits knowingly possessing a counterfeit lease of real property or rental agreement relating to real property with fraudulent intent. Punishes counterfeiting these documents as a felony subject to 10 years imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both. Punishes possessing these counterfeit documents as a misdemeanor subject to three years imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both. Authorizes prosecution where an element occurred, instruments were recorded, or the victim resides or conducts business.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Landlords, tenants, property owners, and individuals involved in residential or commercial real property transactions
