qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State and local revenues from fines and minimal increase in State and local expenditures for incarceration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal counterfeiting laws to include real property leases and rental agreements, subjecting violators to felony penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment and misdemeanor penalties of up to 3 years. This creates a fiscal and operational impact on DPSCS through potential increases in inmate commitments and incarceration costs in State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new felony and misdemeanor offenses carrying significant terms of incarceration, which may impact OPD's caseload as it is responsible for providing legal defense representation to indigent defendants charged with incarcerable offenses.
The bill expands criminal offenses adjudicated in the State's District Court and circuit courts, which are operationally supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits consumer loan lenders, commercial loan lenders, and earned wage access providers from soliciting or accepting tips from consumers. Requires lenders to return any tip received within seven days after receipt to avoid a statutory violation. Mandates that lenders and earned wage access providers prominently disclose the prohibition on accepting or soliciting tips. Prohibits earned wage access providers from publishing false, misleading, or deceptive statements regarding fees, rates, or terms. Prohibits earned wage access licensees from discriminating against consumers based on race, color, creed, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, marital status, or age.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Earned wage access providers, consumer loan lenders, commercial loan lenders, and Maryland consumers obtaining earned wage access or consumer loans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected. Specific expenditure and revenue figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This was introduced as a departmental bill on behalf of the Department of Labor. Its Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) regulates earned wage access providers and consumer lenders, enforcing licensing, tipping prohibitions, advertising standards, and consumer protections.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces consumer protection laws related to credit and lending. Additionally, the bill specifically references written opinions and form approvals issued by the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for state loan assistance repayment and higher education scholarships to include correctional officers. Renames both programs to include police officers, probation agents, and correctional officers. Authorizes loan assistance repayment for correctional officers who complete at least two years of eligible service. Provides tuition assistance for students preparing to become correctional officers or current officers advancing their careers. Requires scholarship recipients to complete a five-year service obligation within eight years after graduation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
qa_results.stakeholders: Correctional officers, individuals studying to become correctional officers, and public higher education institutions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $20,000 in FY 2027 for one-time software enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System. Program award spending is not directly affected, and local finances experience no impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (specifically through the Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering both the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program and the Scholarship Program, including processing applications, tracking service obligations, and implementing a $20,000 system enhancement to MDCAPS in FY 2027.

MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the loan assistance repayment and scholarship programs expanded by this bill, including managing application processing, eligibility verification, and system updates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is directly impacted as the primary state employer of correctional officers. The bill expands higher education tuition scholarships and loan repayment assistance to correctional officers, serving as a workforce recruitment and retention incentive for the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an enforcement process for Maryland residents whose motor vehicles are improperly registered in another jurisdiction. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a warning allowing owners 60 days to register or show an exemption. Assesses a civil fine of $7 per day for up to 60 days against noncompliant motor vehicles. Authorizes county attorneys to initiate civil actions in rem to immobilize persistently noncompliant vehicles through impoundment or booting. Prohibits title service agents from selling, offering, advertising, or facilitating out-of-state vehicle registrations to State residents. Authorizes reciprocal enforcement agreements with other jurisdictions for automated traffic enforcement systems.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents with out-of-state registered vehicles, title service agents, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $379,400 in FY 2027 to hire five customer service agents and cover operating costs, rising to $481,700 by FY 2031. Special fund revenues increase significantly beginning in FY 2027, including an estimated $15.4 million initially from registration fees, titling fees, emissions testing, and civil fines, with ongoing annual revenues around $6.2 million. Local government revenues increase from higher highway user revenue distributions and improved collection of unpaid automated traffic citations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with issuing compliance warnings and civil fines, taking possession of improper out-of-state plates, negotiating reciprocal automated enforcement agreements, administering titling tax exemptions, and licensing title service agents.

As the parent department of MVA and SHA, MDOT is significantly impacted fiscally, with the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) incurring hundreds of thousands in operating expenditures and realizing millions of dollars in increased registration and fee revenues.
SHA operates automated traffic speed and enforcement systems on state roadways and stands to benefit from reciprocal enforcement agreements with other jurisdictions to collect outstanding citations.
MDTA operates automated enforcement systems on toll facilities and may receive nonbudgeted citation revenues collected through the new reciprocal enforcement agreements.
The District Court adjudicates contested automated traffic citations and county attorneys may bring civil in rem actions in court against noncompliant vehicles.
MSP enforces vehicle and traffic laws statewide, coordinates on automated enforcement, and was consulted on the implementation of vehicle registration enforcement measures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS receives a notable indirect fiscal impact, as additional vehicle registrations generate significant dedicated EMS surcharge revenue for the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF).

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board in the Maryland Information Network to implement the 3-1-1 Program. Requires the board to designate four initial counties—two with existing 3-1-1 systems and two without—to participate. Directs the deployment of artificial intelligence chatbots by June 30, 2027, and voicebots by December 1, 2027. Requires the board to submit an implementation plan to expand the program statewide by July 1, 2028. Permits each county to determine the scope and manner of its participation after the final report. Establishes the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee to provide technical guidance through September 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board; Maryland Information Network
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland county governments, Maryland residents seeking nonemergency municipal and government services, 9-1-1 public safety answering points, and communications technology vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $1.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to reimburse the Maryland Information Network for personnel, technology procurement, media campaigns, and administration. Local expenditures may decrease in counties that reduce or replace existing local 3-1-1 systems. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT has a designated representative on the newly created Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board, and the Secretary of Information Technology is tasked with appointing a geographic information systems (GIS) expert to the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee. The agency also plays a central role in statewide AI governance and previously conducted the virtual 3-1-1 feasibility study.

MDEM has a designated seat on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board, oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board (which also has a representative on the Oversight Board), and the Secretary of Emergency Management designates two 9-1-1 Public Safety Answering Point Directors to the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee to ensure system interoperability.

The Maryland Department of Disabilities has a designated seat on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board, directly aligning with the bill's requirements to ensure 3-1-1 chatbot and voicebot systems adhere to best practices for accessibility and equity.
The Maryland Department of Aging has a designated seat on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board to ensure nonemergency community referral and automated 3-1-1 systems adequately serve older adults.

The Governor appoints the Board chair and technical experts in AI and GIS to the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board, appoints members to the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee, and receives required progress and evaluation reports on the 3-1-1 Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates two new advisory and governing bodies: the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and the temporary 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and administering appointments for the newly created Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits creating, using, or disseminating deepfakes knowingly or with reckless disregard to produce materially false election-related information. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to a $5,000 fine, five years imprisonment, or both for violations. Requires the State Administrator of Elections to distribute accurate information upon receiving credible reports of election misinformation or disinformation. Authorizes the State Administrator to seek injunctions against online platforms and issue subpoenas for dissemination records. Authorizes the State Board of Elections to file civil actions to recover correction costs, damages, and attorney's fees. Exempts satire, parody, bona fide news broadcasts, and interactive computer services protected under federal law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; State Administrator of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: voters; political candidates; political action committees; individuals and entities communicating election information; online platforms and broadcasters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund and State general fund revenues may increase annually beginning in fiscal 2027 from criminal penalties and civil damages, but the amounts cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Administrator of Elections and the State Board of Elections with receiving reports, issuing corrective information, seeking court injunctions against online platforms, issuing subpoenas, and initiating civil actions to recover costs.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes election law violations in Maryland, receives referrals of election misinformation/disinformation from the State Board of Elections portal, and enforces criminal election fraud provisions.
The Maryland Judiciary will handle civil actions, injunction requests, subpoena processes, and criminal proceedings authorized and created under the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Board of Elections, and may represent the State in legal actions, court injunctions, and constitutional defenses of the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal misdemeanor penalty with up to 5 years imprisonment for the unlawful creation, use, or dissemination of deepfakes, which may require representation of indigent defendants by the Public Defender.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a misdemeanor offense subject to imprisonment of up to 5 years, potentially impacting state correctional facilities and parole and probation supervision.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a State income tax credit for retired 9-1-1 specialists for taxable years 2026 through 2028. Sets the credit at 4.75% of the first $15,000 of qualifying retirement income, up to $700. Caps total tax credit certificates approved by the Department of Emergency Management at $250,000 per year. Requires certificates to be issued on a pro rata basis if qualifying applications exceed the cap. Requires the Department of Emergency Management to report program metrics to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: retired 9-1-1 specialists in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by up to $250,000 annually in FY 2027 through FY 2029. State general fund expenditures increase by $41,506 in FY 2027, $43,400 in FY 2028, and $45,300 in FY 2029 for the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to administer the program. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing and administering the application, approval, and certification process for the 9-1-1 specialist income tax credit, managing the $250,000 annual cap, and submitting a required report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Comptroller is responsible for administering the state income tax system, receiving tax credit certificates from qualifying taxpayers claiming the credit, and coordinating with MDEM regarding issued certificates.
MDEM is statutorily required to submit a report on the tax credit's usage and vesting of 9-1-1 specialists to the Governor by December 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters governance, oversight, and disbursement procedures for campaign finance entities and authorized candidate campaign committees. Establishes the treasurer as the financial steward of a campaign finance entity. Requires a candidate to appoint the chair and treasurer of an authorized candidate campaign committee. Authorizes candidates or responsible officers to designate authorized agents to carry out duties for the entity. Prohibits candidates from making disbursements from designated campaign accounts while requiring knowledge of all disbursements. Repeals the requirement that a campaign manager be a registered voter of the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: candidates, campaign finance entities, campaign chairs, campaign treasurers, and campaign managers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Elections and the Department of Legislative Services anticipate no direct, material impact on State finances and no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill proposed by the State Board of Elections (SBE). SBE is the primary regulatory body responsible for administering and enforcing Maryland election laws, prescribing campaign finance forms, receiving committee filings and agent designations, and imposing civil penalties for campaign finance violations.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for investigating and prosecuting offenses relating to state election laws and campaign finance integrity, which are directly governed by the statutory standards altered under this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the sentencing date limitation for individuals seeking a reduction in the duration of their sentence. Applies to individuals convicted as adults for offenses committed when they were minors. Retains the requirement that the individual must be imprisoned for at least 20 years for the offense. Requires the court to conduct a hearing on each motion to reduce sentence duration. Permits the victim or victim's representative to submit a victim impact statement regarding the proposed reduction.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals convicted as adults for offenses committed as minors who have served at least 20 years, crime victims and their representatives, and State's Attorneys' offices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impacts are unlikely to occur until out-years beyond the five-year projection period because individuals sentenced after October 1, 2021, must serve at least 20 years before becoming eligible to file a motion.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for individuals to file motions to reduce the duration of their sentences under the Juvenile Restoration Act. Circuit courts, administratively supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, are required to process these motions, conduct hearings, and issue written decisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent incarcerated individuals who become eligible to file motions for sentence reduction and require legal representation during court hearings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services houses individuals serving adult sentences who may be granted sentence reductions or release under the expanded provisions of the Juvenile Restoration Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Office of the Comptroller to study and report on issues relating to foreign earned income. Mandates submission of the report to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026. Directs the study to determine the number of residents with foreign earned income under federal tax law. Requires reporting the number of residents exceeding federal income limitations and the aggregate amount of that income. Mandates identification of the countries from which those residents earned the foreign income.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents with foreign earned income
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The Office of the Comptroller can conduct the study and complete the report using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Office of the Comptroller to conduct a study and submit a report on Maryland residents claiming the federal foreign earned income exclusion under IRC § 911 by December 1, 2026.
The bill requires the Comptroller to submit the required study and findings on foreign earned income tax modifications to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters specifications, capacity, and construction timelines for a comprehensive rehabilitative prerelease facility for female incarcerated individuals. Defines eligible individuals as incarcerated women with prerelease or minimum security status within 36 months of anticipated release. Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to site the facility on at least three acres in Baltimore City. Mandates completion of facility construction by March 1, 2031, and operation by September 1, 2031. Expands required rehabilitative prerelease services to include screening and application assistance for public benefits prior to release. Directs the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman to monitor and verify annual progress beginning June 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of General Services; Office of the Correctional Ombudsman
qa_results.stakeholders: Female incarcerated individuals with prerelease or minimum security status within 36 months of release
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $51,800 in FY 2027 and $86,200 in FY 2028 for the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman to hire one assistant ombudsman to monitor compliance. Capital design, construction, and future operating costs for the facility will increase significantly, which may reduce or delay funding for other State capital projects. Local revenues and expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, which requires the Commissioner of Correction to operate a comprehensive rehabilitative prerelease facility for eligible female incarcerated individuals, acquire property, meet construction and operation timelines, provide gender-responsive and trauma-informed services, and submit progress reports.

DGS is directly tasked with submitting a timeline of deliverables for planning, design, and construction, potentially reviewing proposals and issuing requests for proposals, and submitting progress reports on the facility's design and construction to legislative committees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires municipalities to inventory all publicly owned and privately owned existing open drainage inlets by July 1, 2027. Directs municipalities to adopt a safety prioritization plan and notify affected private property owners by April 1, 2028. Mandates municipalities complete safety improvements on prioritized existing inlets by April 1, 2031, covering all installation costs. Requires any new open drainage inlet installed in a municipality to feature an approved grating system. Authorizes municipal personnel to enter private property to conduct inventories and install approved grating systems. Directs the Department of the Environment to allocate $250,000 annually in matching grants from fiscal 2029 through 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, private property owners with open drainage inlets, and municipal residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on State finances, as $250,000 is annually reallocated within the existing Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program from fiscal 2029 through 2031. Local expenditures may increase significantly beginning in fiscal 2027 for municipal governments to inventory inlets and install improvements, potentially offset in part by State matching grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Environment Article governing the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program administered by MDE, requiring the department to award matching grants to municipalities and mandating that $250,000 of program funds be allocated annually in fiscal years 2029 through 2031 for drainage inlet improvements.

The fiscal note highlights significant operational and potential fiscal impacts raised by SHA regarding whether new open drainage inlet requirements would apply to state highway drainage infrastructure located within or adjacent to municipal boundaries.

MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration and served as an information source for the fiscal analysis regarding potential impacts on state-maintained transportation infrastructure within municipal borders.

The bill amends section 5-803 of the Environment Article, which requires the Department of Planning to consult on grant program regulations and review subdivision applications and flood management compliance via the State Clearinghouse.

Under the statutory framework governing the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program in Section 5-803, the Board of Public Works holds general oversight and approval authority over certain grant awards and state debt allocations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes felony penalties for child pornography offenses involving 100 or more images or children under age 13. Defines each still visual representation as one image and each video depiction as 20 images. Prohibits possessing, distributing, or viewing qualifying depictions of a child younger than age 13. Prohibits possessing with intent to distribute, distributing, or possessing 100 or more qualifying depictions. Subjects violators to imprisonment not exceeding 10 years. Authorizes courts to impose sentences consecutive to or concurrent with other convictions based on the same act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals prosecuted for child pornography offenses, state and local law enforcement agencies, state prosecutors, and victims of child sexual abuse
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to the bill's incarceration penalties. Local revenues and expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new felony offenses for child pornography violations involving 100 or more images or depictions of minors under age 13, carrying sentences of up to 10 years imprisonment, which directly impacts DPSCS correctional facility intake, bed days, and expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new felony prohibitions and severe penalties for certain child pornography offenses, requiring legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent individuals charged under these provisions.
The bill creates new statutory felony charges and sentencing structures, impacting trial court caseloads, hearings, and judicial administration across the state court system.

As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for criminal investigations, MSP investigates internet crimes against children, computer-facilitated crimes, and violations of state child pornography statutes.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals resulting from convictions under Maryland's criminal code, including appeals stemming from these new felony offenses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and Fund from the Maryland Energy Administration to the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Requires the Center to manage the Program, hold the Fund, and invest its money. Repeals the authority of the Maryland Energy Administration to adopt regulations implementing the Program. Limits annual reporting on Strategic Energy Investment Fund receipts and disbursements to amounts exceeding $10,000. Alters reporting to require estimates of greenhouse gas emissions reductions instead of electricity savings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Clean Energy Center; Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible businesses, nonprofit organizations, local jurisdictions, and State agencies seeking energy conservation loans, as well as participating financial institutions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Net State fiscal impact is $0. In fiscal 2027, the transfer of the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund balance and operations increases Maryland Energy Administration special fund expenditures by $9.0 million and decreases special fund revenues by $947,700, while Maryland Clean Energy Center nonbudgeted revenues increase by $12.3 million and nonbudgeted expenditures increase by $2.4 million. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund to MCEC, requiring the Center to manage the program, hold and invest the fund, and provide loans.

This departmental bill transfers MEA's Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and associated special fund to MCEC, repeals MEA's regulatory authority over the program, and alters MEA's annual reporting requirements for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF).

The bill removes the statutory responsibility of the State Treasurer to hold, invest, and reinvest the moneys of the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund, shifting custody and investment responsibilities to MCEC.
The bill repeals the requirement that the Comptroller account for the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund as the fund is transferred out of the State Treasury to MCEC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes nonconsensual sexual contact committed in connection with a first-, second-, or third-degree burglary as third-degree sexual offense. Subjects convicted individuals to felony penalties including imprisonment for up to 10 years. Classifies convicted individuals as Tier I sex offenders if the victim is not a minor. Designates offenders as Tier II sex offenders if the victim is a minor at least 13 years old. Classifies offenders as Tier III sex offenders if the victim is a minor under 13 years old. Applies these provisions prospectively to offenses committed on or after October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals convicted of sexual offenses in connection with first-, second-, or third-degree burglaries; victims of nonconsensual sexual offenses; state correctional facilities; local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State expenditures from enhanced incarceration penalties and sex offender registration classifications. Potential minimal decrease in local revenues from fewer fines imposed in circuit court cases. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands third-degree sexual offense (a felony carrying up to 10 years imprisonment) and alters sex offender registry tiers. DPSCS operates the state correctional facilities housing individuals serving sentences over 18 months and oversees supervision and the sex offender registry.
Circuit courts across the state will hear cases involving the reclassified felony offenses, sex offender designations, and sentencing under the bill's amended statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency provides legal defense for indigent individuals charged with newly expanded felony third-degree sexual offenses and subject to sex offender registry tier enhancements.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP investigates felony sexual offenses and burglaries, and serves as the registering law enforcement entity for sex offenders in many Maryland jurisdictions.
The OAG represents the State of Maryland in all criminal appeals resulting from convictions under the revised third-degree sexual offense and sex offender registration statutes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits cemetery owners from selling or transferring a cemetery without approval from the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight. Requires owners seeking approval to submit an application, complete a preservation plan, and provide specified public notice. Grants standing to descendants, descendant community organizations, and other interested parties to challenge sale decisions in court. Directs courts reviewing disputes to allow, prohibit, or order alternative dispositions for proposed cemetery sales or transfers. Authorizes the State, counties, and municipalities to acquire abandoned cemeteries for transfer to qualifying descendant, veterans, or nonprofit organizations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight
qa_results.stakeholders: cemetery owners, registered cemeterians, permit holders, descendants of interred individuals, descendant community organizations, veterans organizations, and nonprofit cemetery preservation organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations are not materially affected; the Office of Cemetery Oversight and the Judiciary can likely implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight is the primary official tasked with approving cemetery sales and transfers, reviewing preservation plans, considering public comments, and facilitating reinterments.

The bill establishes legal standing and detailed procedures for circuit courts to adjudicate actions regarding cemetery sales, transfers, alternative uses, and disposition of abandoned cemeteries within a mandatory six-month timeframe.
The bill explicitly exempts property acquired by the Department of Transportation that is necessary for a public project from the bill's cemetery sale and transfer approval requirements.

The Maryland Historical Trust, a division within the Department of Planning, is referenced in statutory provisions determining interested persons for burial sites when local advisory boards are absent, and the department contributed to the fiscal review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes active service members and their spouses relocating to Maryland under military orders to practice under out-of-state licenses. Requires qualifying applicants to submit proof of orders, an affidavit of good standing, and a marriage certificate if applicable. Allows licensing authorities to issue temporary licenses if applications cannot be processed within 30 days. Prohibits licensing authorities from requiring a separate State license within the same discipline and scope of practice. Repeals the one-year post-discharge time limit defining an eligible veteran for expedited occupational licensing. Authorizes each licensing authority to adopt implementing regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Insurance Administration; Public Service Commission; Department of State Police; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Active service members and military spouses relocating to Maryland; military veterans seeking expedited occupational licensing; State occupational and professional licensing boards; Maryland employers in licensed professions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $107,900 in FY 2027 ($80,100 general funds, $27,800 special funds) for software programming updates and personnel across multiple agencies. Future annual general fund expenditures range between $43,600 and $50,300 through FY 2031. General and special fund revenues decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2027 due to reduced licensing fee collections. Local government revenues from clerk-issued business licenses experience an indeterminate minimal decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends licensing requirements across dozens of occupational and professional boards housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, including electricians, plumbers, accountants, architects, cosmetologists, home improvement contractors, and financial regulators. MD Labor expects IT programming costs and potential special fund revenue losses.

The bill directly impacts the numerous health occupations licensing boards and MDH departmental licensing (such as medical laboratories and tissue banks), requiring them to authorize qualifying active service members and spouses to practice and adjust expedited licensing procedures.

MSDE is directly required to alter its teacher and school counselor licensure processes and expand expedited licensing for military service members and spouses, incurring fiscal impacts for system modifications and administrative staffing.

The bill alters licensing and certification requirements for veterinarians, pesticide applicators, nutrient management consultants, and milk haulers, requiring software updates and causing minimal revenue reductions for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

MDE and its affiliated boards (such as well drillers, waterworks operators, marine contractors, and on-site wastewater professionals) must authorize qualifying military personnel and spouses to operate under out-of-state credentials.

Clerks of the Circuit Court issue several business licenses affected by the bill (such as peddlers and traders), and the Judiciary requires general fund expenditures in FY 2027 to update its e-licensing software.

MSP certifies private detectives, security guards, security systems technicians, and vehicle inspection mechanics, all of which are subject to the bill's military license recognition and examination exemption provisions.
MVA issues professional licenses for vehicle salesmen, automotive dismantlers, title service agents, and driving instructors, which are subject to the bill's military license recognition exemptions.
MIA licenses insurance producers, advisers, public adjusters, and bail bondsmen, which are subject to the bill's authorization framework for military service members and spouses.
The PSC licenses energy salespersons and vendors and recognizes master plumber/gasfitter reciprocity, all of which are amended by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates sports wagering and video lottery terminal personnel and operators, which are amended to accommodate the bill's out-of-state license recognition for service members and spouses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS and the EMS Board oversee the licensing and certification of EMS providers, which are specifically amended under the bill.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which regulates several commercial and vehicle-related professions impacted by the bill.
DNR licenses taxidermists and tree experts, both of which are amended to accommodate military personnel and spouses licensed in other states.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS licenses private home detention monitoring agencies, which are subject to the out-of-state licensing recognition provisions in the bill.
WCC oversees the registration of rehabilitation counselors and vocational evaluators under the Labor and Employment Article, which is amended to exempt authorized military personnel and spouses.
The Comptroller issues transient vendor licenses under the Business Regulation Article, which are exempted for eligible military service members and spouses.
The bill requires service providers to provide notice of rights that are posted on the Maryland National Guard's website in connection with military contract termination protections under the SCRA.
DVMF advocates for active-duty service members, veterans, and military spouses in navigating state benefits and services, aligning directly with the bill's civil relief and licensing protections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits county and municipal governing body election methods that impair protected classes from electing candidates of their choice. Applies to protected classes defined by race, color, or language minority groups. Authorizes the Office of the Attorney General and any person to file civil enforcement actions. Empowers courts to order tailored remedies, grant preliminary relief, and award reasonable attorney's fees to prevailing plaintiffs. Excludes statewide elections from its requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Voters belonging to race, color, or language minority groups; county and municipal governing bodies; local election candidates in Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase to the extent the Office of the Attorney General pursues enforcement actions; the office estimated costs of $242,704 in fiscal 2027 for legal personnel and expert witness fees, though the overall extent of enforcement is indeterminate. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) to bring civil enforcement actions against counties or municipal corporations for voting rights violations, and the fiscal note outlines potential general fund expenditures for OAG personnel and expert witness fees.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action for voting rights violations in local elections, establishing specific evidentiary standards, preliminary relief procedures, and remedial powers for the Maryland court system.

The bill amends the Election Law Article to regulate local election systems and standards for county and municipal governing bodies, which interacts with the State Board of Elections' oversight of election laws and administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a special enforcement officer in Baltimore City to enforce laws regulating cigarettes, other tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices. Authorizes the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to reprimand licensees or suspend or revoke licenses. Requires applicants for initial or renewal county licenses in Baltimore City to obtain a local licensure authorization. Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City to establish an authorization process and charge a fee. Requires Baltimore City to remit 50% of authorization fees to the Comptroller for the Family League of Baltimore City, Inc. Prohibits issuing licensure authorizations to initial applicants between October 1, 2026, and October 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: retailers and vendors of cigarettes, other tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices in Baltimore City; Family League of Baltimore City, Inc.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in state special fund and general fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 from licensure authorization request fees. Indeterminate increase in Baltimore City expenditures for local enforcement and administering licensure authorizations. Minimal one-time general fund expenditure increase in fiscal 2027 for Judiciary programming.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller of Maryland to receive 50% of the licensure authorization request fees collected by Baltimore City and distribute those funds to the Family League of Baltimore City, Inc. The fiscal note also evaluates the Comptroller's administrative capacity and special fund impacts associated with managing these disbursements.

Circuit court clerks, supported administratively and technologically by the Administrative Office of the Courts, issue retail tobacco and electronic smoking device licenses. The bill requires clerks in Baltimore City to verify licensure authorizations before issuing licenses, resulting in required system programming changes and minor general fund expenditure impacts for the Judiciary.

The bill references and amends provisions governing retail tobacco licensing fees, which partially fund Maryland Department of Health enforcement activities prohibiting sales to individuals under 21. It also interfaces with Baltimore City Health Department enforcement officers carrying out tobacco use prevention and cessation oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: Appropriates State funds for the conduct of State government for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. Establishes operating and capital appropriations across executive departments, independent agencies, the General Assembly, and the Judiciary. Authorizes fiscal 2026 deficiency appropriations for specified state agencies and programs. Sets executive pay plan salary schedules and positions for designated officials and judicial officers. qa_results.bill_summary: Adjusts State appropriations, revenue distributions, and statutory funding mandates to balance the State budget. Caps annual State aid growth to community colleges under the Cade funding formula at 3% for fiscal 2027 through 2029. Decouples State income tax from federal production property depreciation and limits manufacturing bonus depreciation to 20%. Increases county retirement contributions for local educators and librarians by $39.3 million annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Authorizes fund transfers to the General Fund, including $380 million from the Local Income Tax Reserve Account. Requires motor vehicles to be at least 25 years old to register as historic vehicles beginning in fiscal 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits courts and case parties from disclosing court records to nonparties without redacting identifying information of sexual assault or stalking victims. Requires a court to redact identifying information from existing records upon written request of a victim. Permits disclosure of unredacted records if a court finds good cause by clear and convincing evidence. Authorizes health occupations boards to petition for unredacted records to investigate or discipline a defendant for sexual misconduct. Requires the State's Attorney to notify victims of board petitions and explain objection procedures. Prohibits health occupations boards from publicly disclosing records obtained under the petition process.

Requires recipient organizations to submit annual expenditure reports, service numbers, and outcome-based performance measures. Extends the termination date of the grant program to June 30, 2029.

qa_results.stakeholders: Qualifying nonprofit organizations providing automotive repair training, and incarcerated or formerly incarcerated individuals receiving training and reentry assistance.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $1.0 million in FY 2029 if discretionary funds are included in the annual budget bill. Revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary administering agency responsible for distributing the grant funds to qualifying nonprofit organizations, establishing data sharing and reporting requirements, and receiving required annual performance and expenditure reports.
The bill explicitly extends discretionary authority to the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $1,000,000 in the state budget bill through fiscal year 2029.

DBM assists in developing the annual state budget and supervising expenditures, and would oversee the inclusion and execution of the potential $1.0 million general fund appropriation in fiscal year 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the current compensatory education enrollment funding calculation method through fiscal year 2028. Repeals the sunset on using Concentration of Poverty School Grant funds for certain required regulatory programs. Alters initial teacher certification requirements by adding state-approved portfolios and apprenticeship certificate options. Delays the National Board Certification requirement for new licensed principals from July 1, 2029, to July 1, 2034. Repeals the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Skills Standards Advisory Committee while modifying CTE Committee responsibilities. Suspends operation of the Expert Review Team Program for the 2026–2027 school year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board; Career and Technical Education Committee; Governor's Workforce Development Board; State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: public school students (including low-income and dual enrollment students), public school teachers and teacher candidates, prospective and current school principals, local boards of education, county governments, and career and technical education providers and employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $228.5 million in FY 2027, $311.5 million in FY 2028, $170.4 million in FY 2029, $75.5 million in FY 2030, and $23.7 million in FY 2031, driven primarily by formula aid increases for compensatory education and concentration of poverty grants. Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund special fund interest revenues decrease by $4.7 million in FY 2027 and $3.0 million in FY 2028 due to lower fund balances. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase statewide, and county government appropriations increase by $6.8 million in FY 2027 and $14.5 million in FY 2028 to meet local share requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency impacted by this bill. The legislation alters school finance formulas (compensatory education enrollment calculations and Concentration of Poverty grants), modifies teacher certification and principal career ladder criteria, suspends the Expert Review Team Program for the 2026–2027 school year, redirects associated budget funding, and directs MSDE to collaborate on low-income student counting methodology.

The bill directly modifies the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee, which is an explicit unit within the Governor's Workforce Development Board (GWDB). GWDB collaborates with and approves the CTE Committee's list of priority occupations and comprehensive career pathway information.

The Secretary of Labor is a designated member of the CTE Committee, and the Department staffs the committee. The bill also requires all relevant workforce development programs, including registered apprenticeships approved by MD Labor, to align with the newly established priority occupations list and career pathways.

The Secretary of Higher Education serves on the CTE Committee, and the commission is directly impacted fiscally (requiring an additional education policy analyst position per the fiscal note) to ensure postsecondary CTE and academic programs align with the priority occupations list and career pathway frameworks.

The Secretary of Higher Education serves on the CTE Committee, and the commission is directly impacted fiscally (requiring an additional education policy analyst position per the fiscal note) to ensure postsecondary CTE and academic programs align with the priority occupations list and career pathway frameworks.

DBM is statutorily mandated to be consulted by MSDE and the Accountability and Implementation Board regarding the methodology for counting students from low-income households. The bill also carries massive fiscal ramifications across the state budget and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.

The Secretary of Commerce is designated as an ex officio member of the CTE Committee to align statewide career and technical education frameworks with Maryland's economic development goals and priority workforce needs.

The Governor jointly appoints the chair and industry representatives to the CTE Committee with legislative leaders, receives mandated annual reports on CTE and Expert Review Teams, and receives the final low-income student counting methodology report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the purpose, duties, and membership structure of the CTE Committee and repeals the CTE Skills Standards Advisory Committee.
USM institutions are affected by provisions modifying teacher preparation accreditation and certification pathways, post-CCR dual enrollment limitations, and higher education CTE alignment.

As a public university offering teacher preparation and postsecondary pathways, Morgan State University is affected by altered teacher candidate assessment standards and postsecondary career pathway alignments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the circumstances under which an individual convicted of a crime is disqualified from jury service. Disqualifies individuals convicted of crimes punishable by imprisonment exceeding one year who are currently serving their sentence. Specifies that disqualification includes time spent serving a term of parole or probation. Disqualifies individuals convicted of perjury, witness intimidation, jury intimidation, or crimes under Title 8 of the Criminal Law Article. Repeals the provision qualifying individuals with a disqualifying conviction who have received a pardon. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: prospective jurors with criminal convictions, individuals currently serving criminal sentences or on probation/parole, and Maryland circuit courts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,100 in FY 2027 only for one-time programming costs incurred by the Judiciary to update juror qualification forms. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the operational, administrative, and technological functions of Maryland's judicial branch, which includes managing jury selection and qualification. The agency incurs a direct fiscal impact of $28,100 in FY 2027 to update and reprogram online and printed juror qualification forms to reflect the altered disqualification criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the exclusive original jurisdiction of the juvenile court over children at least 16 years old. Repeals statutory exclusions for certain handgun violations, firearm violations, and first-degree assault. Requires an intake officer to authorize prehearing detention for specified violent or handgun offenses. Prohibits holding or transporting juveniles within sight or sound of incarcerated adults, effective October 1, 2029. Establishes annual juvenile justice reporting requirements for state agencies and commissions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy; Administrative Office of the Courts; Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices
qa_results.stakeholders: juveniles accused of delinquent acts or criminal offenses, juvenile intake officers, State's Attorneys, public defenders, and state and local correctional facility staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant operational cost savings for the Department of Juvenile Services beginning in fiscal 2027. Local State's Attorneys' offices face potentially significant expenditure increases due to increased juvenile caseloads and shortened timelines. Local detention facility expenditures decrease beginning in fiscal 2030 or earlier. Maryland may avoid the loss of approximately $173,000 annually in federal grant funding by meeting sight-and-sound compliance standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DJS is the primary state department impacted by the bill. The legislation alters juvenile court jurisdiction to keep certain serious charges initially in the juvenile system, mandates that intake officers authorize pre-hearing detention for specified offenses, requires secure juvenile facility placement instead of adult jails, and establishes ongoing statutory reporting requirements for DJS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is explicitly mandated by the bill to submit an annual report detailing youth housed with adult offenders, sight and sound violations, and charges under adult jurisdiction. Additionally, GOCPP administers federal Title II Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act (JJDPA) grant funds, which are directly tied to the sight-and-sound separation and adult jail removal provisions in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is impacted by provisions restricting the detention, confinement, and transport of youth in adult correctional facilities, requiring strict sight and sound separation from incarcerated adults, and potentially seeing minor expenditure reductions due to fewer youth placed in adult state facilities.

The bill directly alters the statutory boundaries between juvenile court and criminal court jurisdiction, waiver procedures, and pre-hearing detention determinations. AOC is also explicitly required to consult with DJS on annual statutory reporting regarding juvenile court petitions, waivers, and transfers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent juveniles facing delinquency and adult criminal charges. The bill alters where cases originate and how waiver hearings proceed, which directly impacts OPD caseload distribution and contractual expenditures for psychological evaluations in transfer/waiver hearings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices is statutorily designated to receive annual reporting from DJS and GOCPP, and is mandated under Section 3 to submit an evaluation report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2027 regarding bill implementation, behavioral incidents, and DJS staffing capacity.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an optional direct admission program at participating public senior higher education institutions beginning in the 2028–2029 academic year. Requires eligible students to meet college and career readiness standards and a minimum grade point average. Requires participating institutions to waive application fees and offer conditional direct admission to eligible applicants. Authorizes participating institutions to establish additional criteria and revoke admission offers under specified circumstances. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the State Department of Education to study program implementation by July 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland State Department of Education; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public high school seniors; participating public senior higher education institutions (constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland, University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $100,000 in FY 2027 for MHEC and MSDE to conduct the required study and report. Future implementation costs beginning in FY 2028 are indeterminate but potentially significant, possibly reaching millions of dollars for IT system integration and data sharing. Institutional costs and tuition revenue impacts will depend on voluntary participation by public senior higher education institutions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is a primary implementing agency tasked with administering the direct admission program, establishing eligibility requirements through an MOU with educational partners, receiving eligible student data, generating customized admission lists, and conducting a comprehensive implementation and feasibility study in collaboration with MSDE.

MHEC is a primary implementing agency tasked with administering the direct admission program, establishing eligibility requirements through an MOU with educational partners, receiving eligible student data, generating customized admission lists, and conducting a comprehensive implementation and feasibility study in collaboration with MSDE.

MSDE is a primary implementing partner required to collaborate with MHEC on establishing direct admission eligibility criteria and executing an MOU, establishing a process to annually identify and report eligible students meeting CCR standards and GPA thresholds, and collaborating on the implementation study.

USM is specifically named as a required partner to establish direct admission eligibility standards and enter into the MOU, and its constituent institutions may participate in the direct admission program, waive application fees, and offer conditional admission to qualifying students.

MSU is explicitly mandated to collaborate with MHEC, MSDE, and other public senior institutions to establish eligibility criteria and enter into the program MOU, with the option to participate in offering direct admission and fee waivers to eligible students.

Saint Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly required to participate in establishing eligibility requirements and executing the MOU for the direct admission program, with the option to enroll direct-admission students and waive application fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits manufacturing, selling, offering for sale, purchasing, receiving, or transferring a machine gun convertible pistol beginning January 1, 2027. Expands the definition of rapid fire activators to include pistol converters. Authorizes lawful owners to sell or transfer a machine gun convertible pistol to eligible immediate family members. Requires the Department of State Police to adopt regulations and publish a list of prohibited pistols. Exempts law enforcement personnel, servicing by licensed dealers or gunsmiths, firearm surrenders, and temporary gratuitous exchanges.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: firearm owners, licensed firearms dealers, gunsmiths, firearm manufacturers, and law enforcement personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $220,200 in FY 2027 for the Department of State Police to hire staff to evaluate handguns and publish regulations and lists, with ongoing costs in future years. Potential minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures from expanded misdemeanor penalty enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of State Police adopt regulations to implement the law, including reviewing firearm models and compiling and publishing the official list of prohibited machine gun convertible pistols, resulting in direct operational impacts and ongoing general fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates and expands criminal misdemeanor and felony penalties involving machine gun convertible pistols and pistol converters, which can lead to incarceration and supervision within State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation and expanded scope of criminal firearm offenses and associated incarceration penalties increases caseloads for public defenders representing indigent defendants charged under these provisions.
The bill establishes new prohibitions and penalties regarding firearm crimes, impacting judicial proceedings and caseload processing within the State court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes vehicle dealer associations and vehicle manufacturer associations to request an administrative hearing with the Motor Vehicle Administration. Allows associations to request hearings on behalf of themselves, an individual entity, or a group of members. Permits hearings to resolve statutory disputes or seek clarification or interpretation of vehicle licensing and franchise provisions. Restricts dealer association dispute requests to matters germane to their purpose not requiring individual member participation. Excludes disputes involving any manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch lacking at least one franchised dealer in Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: Vehicle dealers, vehicle manufacturers, dealer associations, manufacturer associations, vehicle distributors, and factory branches in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected; any increase in caseload for the Motor Vehicle Administration, Office of Administrative Hearings, or Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates vehicle dealers and manufacturers in Maryland and is the agency before which dealer and manufacturer associations may request administrative hearings to resolve disputes or seek statutory clarifications.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which oversees vehicle dealer licensing, franchise relations, and the administrative dispute resolution process altered by this bill.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested administrative hearings referred by state agencies, including hearings requested under Title 12 of the Transportation Article involving vehicle dealer and manufacturer disputes.

Decisions and orders resulting from these administrative hearings may be appealed to the Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County within the state judicial system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an aggrieved party or the Office of the Attorney General to sue a covered officer for federal rights deprivations. Defines a covered officer as an armed officer authorized to make arrests for federal code violations. Excludes Maryland law enforcement officers acting under a joint task force primarily enforcing federal law. Permits plaintiffs to seek damages along with declaratory and injunctive relief. Authorizes courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and expert witness fees to a prevailing plaintiff. Requires plaintiffs to file an action within five years after the cause of action accrues.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Covered officers with federal arrest authority, individuals deprived of federal constitutional or statutory rights, and civil litigation attorneys.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not anticipated to be affected, though general fund revenues may increase if the Office of the Attorney General is awarded damages, fees, or costs. Local government finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to initiate civil actions against covered officers who deprive individuals of constitutional rights, seeking damages, declaratory, and injunctive relief.

The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund and handles Maryland Tort Claims Act claims; the agency anticipates an operational impact investigating claims and filing motions regarding alleged state officer liability.
The bill establishes a new civil cause of action, standard of relief, and fee-shifting provisions within the state court system, directly affecting judicial administration and caseloads.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases per capita State funding for regional resource centers and county public library systems beginning in fiscal 2028. Renames the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Young Readers Grant Program and repeals local matching requirements. Increases the mandatory annual State budget appropriation for the Young Readers Grant Program to $450,000. Requires grant applicants to include specific measures for serving children residing in low-income zip codes. Updates the qualifying categories of educational and community services that each public library must offer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency; State Librarian; State Library Board; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: County public library systems, regional resource centers, children and families in low-income zip codes, and nonprofit book-gifting organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.3 million in FY 2028, rising to $5.2 million in FY 2031 due to phased-in per capita formula increases and a $100,000 annual boost for the Young Readers Grant Program. State aid to local library systems and regional resource centers increases by $1.2 million in FY 2028 and $5.1 million in FY 2031. Local expenditures are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is the primary implementing agency; the bill renames and modifies the Young Readers Grant Program administered by the State Librarian, updates funding formulas for regional resource centers and county library systems, and updates service requirements for public libraries.

The bill mandates significant increases in general fund appropriations for the Young Readers Grant Program and per capita aid formulas for public library systems and regional resource centers beginning in FY 2028.

Statutory provisions in the bill explicitly require the Comptroller to withhold State funds from any county library system certified by the State Library Board as failing to meet state standards for libraries.
The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 for the Young Readers Grant Program in the annual State budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the pay schedule for the full-time chief inspector employed by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County. Increases the position's compensation range from non-represented pay schedule NR-05 to pay schedule NR-12. Requires the Board to fix the chief inspector's annual salary within the updated schedule. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: full-time chief inspector employed by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Anne Arundel County finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected, as the board funds operations from license fees and retains discretion over specific salary amounts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Community Forensic Aftercare Program within the Maryland Department of Health to monitor individuals on conditional release. Requires the program to establish a community monitoring board to review conditional release and out-of-state travel requests. Prohibits courts from ordering the program to make clinical decisions regarding a committed person's treatment. Authorizes an authorized agent to attend forensic review board and community monitoring board meetings virtually. Repeals the requirement that forensic review boards notify committed persons within ten days of recommending court action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Committed persons on conditional release, criminal defendants found incompetent to stand trial, behavioral health providers, and public defenders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $97,000 in fiscal 2028 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire two part-time personnel, with annualized costs in future years. The Office of the Public Defender may incur future costs if advocacy demand exceeds existing capacity. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, which establishes and codifies the Community Forensic Aftercare Program (CFAP) and Community Monitoring Boards within the department, alters requirements for facility forensic review boards, and incurs direct general fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes specific statutory requirements for CFAP and treatment providers to disclose medical and legal records directly to public defenders representing committed individuals within 24 hours without client authorization, permits nonlegal defense staff to serve as authorized agents at board proceedings, and may affect defense social worker staffing and caseloads.

The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by prohibiting courts from issuing orders requiring CFAP to make clinical treatment decisions and establishes specific procedures regarding the receipt of release recommendations and reports of conditional release violations.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to provide legal representation and counsel to MDH during CFAP Community Monitoring Board meetings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits employers from disciplining employees or refusing to hire applicants who decline employer-sponsored religious or political meetings. Authorizes employees to file written complaints with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within 180 days of an alleged violation. Requires the Commissioner to investigate complaints and attempt informal resolution through mediation. Authorizes civil penalties up to $10,000 for initial violations and up to $25,000 for subsequent violations. Requires employers to post and provide new hires with a model notice developed by the Commissioner. Exempts specified religious organizations, political organizations, educational institutions, nonprofit training programs, and mandatory legal compliance trainings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers, employees, and job applicants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $131,588 in FY 2027 for 1.5 enforcement and legal positions within the Maryland Department of Labor, rising to $173,100 by FY 2031. Civil penalty revenues are not expected to materially affect general fund revenues. State and local government employer expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor is the primary entity charged with implementing and enforcing the Maryland Worker Freedom Act. MD Labor is responsible for receiving complaints, conducting investigations, facilitating mediations, assessing civil penalties, issuing orders, petitioning circuit courts, and publishing required informational posters and notices. The agency requires additional general fund expenditures and staffing to handle this new workload.

The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for providing legal counsel and representation to the Commissioner of Labor and Industry for enforcement actions, orders, and circuit court petitions. The fiscal note explicitly accounts for funding a half-time assistant attorney general position to assist MD Labor in enforcing the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits research facilities and testing facilities from performing devocalization surgeries on dogs or cats or using devocalized dogs or cats. Restricts testing facilities from using traditional animal test methods when regulatory agencies approve alternative methods or grant waivers. Excludes medical research from restrictions on traditional animal testing methods. Requires euthanasia of dogs and cats at covered facilities to follow American Veterinary Medical Association guidelines. Extends adoption placement mandates for dogs and cats no longer needed for research to testing facilities. Mandates annual reporting to the Secretary of Agriculture on animal use and rescue releases beginning in 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Secretary of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: research facilities, testing facilities using live vertebrate animals, animal rescue organizations, and licensed veterinarians
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement and enforce the requirements using existing resources. State revenues are not expected to be materially affected by penalty fines of up to $1,000 for a first offense and $5,000 for subsequent offenses. Local government finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing and regulatory agency for the bill, which amends Title 15 of the Agriculture Article. The Secretary of Agriculture is responsible for collecting annual data reports from research and testing facilities, compiling an anonymized annual report, posting it to the department's website, and enforcing the title's provisions and fines.
