agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within MD Labor with assessing civil penalties for child labor violations and indexing those penalties to inflation. It also directs MD Labor to monitor federal actions regarding the National Labor Relations Act and notify the Department of Legislative Services if statutory contingencies are triggered.

The bill expands PERB's jurisdiction to include private sector employees under specified federal contingencies, authorizing PERB to process representation petitions, conduct elections, certify exclusive representatives, adjudicate unfair labor practices, and assess civil penalties.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees executive branch employee standards and policies. The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to prohibit any Executive Branch unit from applying to the federal government for a waiver of any applicable provision of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act.

The bill provides that orders issued by the Public Employee Relations Board regarding private employees are subject to judicial review by the circuit courts, which are supported administratively by the AOC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of foster care recipient to expand eligibility for tuition exemptions at Maryland public institutions of higher education. Lowers the qualifying out-of-home placement age threshold from an individual's thirteenth birthday to their eighth birthday. Applies to individuals in out-of-home placements for at least one year who enter guardianship, adoption, or parental reunification. Exempts eligible students from tuition if enrolled before age 25 for a vocational certificate, associate's degree, or bachelor's degree. Requires eligible students to file for federal and State financial aid. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Department of Human Services; public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Foster care alumni placed in out-of-home placement on or after age eight who exited through adoption, guardianship, or reunification; Maryland public four-year universities and community colleges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education tuition revenues decrease, potentially significantly, beginning in fiscal 2027 due to additional tuition waivers granted. Local community college tuition revenues also decrease, potentially significantly. State and community college expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount annually due to additional student enrollment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters eligibility for foster care recipients placed in out-of-home care by the Department of Human Services, requiring DHS foster care placement and exit records to determine student eligibility.

MHEC oversees higher education policies and financial assistance in the state and receives mandatory annual reporting from public higher education institutions regarding foster care tuition waivers and forms used.

The commission is responsible for establishing statewide higher education policies and receives required annual reporting from public institutions regarding students receiving foster care tuition waivers.

USM institutions are public institutions of higher education that must provide tuition waivers and on-campus housing priority to newly eligible foster care recipients, experiencing decreases in tuition revenue and increases in educational expenditures.

As a public four-year university, Morgan State must grant tuition exemptions to newly eligible foster care students, resulting in a direct reduction in tuition revenue and potential expenditure impacts.

As an independent public four-year institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is required to waive tuition and mandatory fees for eligible foster care recipients, impacting tuition revenue.
MLDSC connects foster care data with postsecondary education outcome data and tracks college-going rates and waiver eligibility for foster youth.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of rental dwelling unit under the State's lead risk reduction in housing law. Repeals the requirement that a habitable rental unit must be independent. Includes units that have living facilities with, or access to, permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation. Maintains exclusions for unfinished basements, hotel and motel units, secured inaccessible areas, and units not offered for rent. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and landlords of residential rental properties (including single-room occupancy and shared-housing facilities), tenants, local public housing authorities, and lead paint inspection and abatement contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund increase by an estimated $1,406,300 in FY 2027 and future odd fiscal years ($281,300 in even years) from biennial registration fees. Special fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $369,600 in FY 2027 and between $255,000 and $291,400 annually thereafter for three positions, outreach, and database upgrades. Local expenditures may increase for local housing entities required to pay fees and perform inspections or remediation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment administers the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program and enforces the Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing law under Title 6, Subtitle 8 of the Environment Article. The bill directly expands the definition of rental dwelling units subject to MDE registration and regulation, requiring MDE to add staff, upgrade its database, and process substantial registration fee revenues.

The Maryland Department of Health coordinates on statewide public health initiatives to prevent childhood lead poisoning and works in conjunction with lead surveillance and local health department case management for elevated blood lead levels.

The Department of Housing and Community Development oversees affordable rental housing programs, single-room occupancy (SRO) units, and residential property standards that are directly affected by expanded lead risk reduction compliance mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to study captive insurance use, regulation, and taxation. Directs the study to examine utilization by nonprofit and for-profit entities and interstate regulatory and tax frameworks. Evaluates the feasibility and structure of establishing a State registry for out-of-state captive insurers. Protects information submitted by nonprofit health systems and hospitals from disclosure under the Public Information Act. Requires submission of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly committees by January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Captive insurance companies, nonprofit and for-profit entities utilizing captive insurance (including nonprofit hospitals and health systems), and Maryland insurance regulators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Insurance Administration can conduct the study using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the comprehensive study on the use, regulation, and taxation of captive insurance companies in Maryland and reporting findings and recommendations.
The bill requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to submit its final study report and policy recommendations on captive insurance to the Governor by January 1, 2027.

As the state's principal revenue and tax administrator, the Comptroller has an interest in the study's examination of tax frameworks, capital contributions, and premium receipts taxation for captive insurers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover menopause and menopause-associated symptoms. Requires health occupations boards to grant qualifying licensees at least two continuing education credits per hour of menopause training. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to identify at least one qualifying menopause training program. Alters the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness. Requires the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Commission for Women to evaluate policy initiatives and report findings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Commission for Women; State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; licensed and certified health care providers who manage menopause; individuals experiencing perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal symptoms.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,300 in FY 2027 and $30,200 in FY 2028 for Maryland Department of Health contractual staff, vendors, and reporting requirements. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. Local government health care expenditures may increase for fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is directly responsible for identifying approved training programs for health occupations licensees regarding menopause, overseeing health occupations boards implementing continuing education requirements, and conducting evaluations and reporting action plans regarding community health workers and clinical education.

MIA regulates the private health insurance market in Maryland and will be responsible for enforcing the bill's mandate requiring health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans to cover the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated symptoms, as well as processing rate and form filings.

The Maryland Commission for Women is housed within DHS; under the bill, the Commission's Executive Director is added to the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, and the Commission is mandated to evaluate state policy initiatives and report findings to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory membership and composition of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, places reporting requirements on the Maryland Commission for Women, and requires consultation with the State Community Health Worker Advisory Committee.
DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate compliance and coverage standards with respect to state-mandated health insurance benefits.

MHEC serves as an informational source and coordinates higher education policy, relevant to the bill's requirement that MDH consult with institutions of higher education to evaluate methods for expanding clinical education on menopause.

USM institutions, including the University of Maryland School of Medicine, are consulted regarding clinical and postgraduate medical education opportunities related to menopausal evaluation and treatment.
Morgan State University is an institution of higher education consulted on opportunities for clinical and professional education in menopausal care.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Maryland bankruptcy exemption for owner-occupied residential real property to include residential property held in a revocable trust. Sets the maximum bankruptcy exemption amount for eligible residential real property at $125,000 for an individual. Caps the combined exemption at $125,000 if multiple individuals claim the exemption for the same property in the same proceeding. Requires the exemption amounts to adjust annually based on the Consumer Price Index beginning in fiscal year 2028. Repeals provisions that prohibit repeat exemption claims on the same property within eight years. Applies prospectively to bankruptcy proceedings filed on or after June 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individual debtors domiciled in Maryland filing for bankruptcy, settlors of revocable trusts, and creditors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding statutory debtor exemptions for residential real property in bankruptcy proceedings. While bankruptcy cases are adjudicated in federal courts, state courts interact with judgment execution and exemption laws, and the Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for operational review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes statutory standards governing when an absentee ballot is considered timely and may be counted. Prohibits counting absentee ballots that do not meet these timeliness requirements. Requires election boards to refer to Internet-delivered absentee ballots as "print-at-home ballots" in public communications. Requires votes in nonfederal contests on timely ballots to be counted if federal timeliness requirements differ. Requires the State Board of Elections to adopt conforming regulations and provide voter notices under differing federal rules.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters casting absentee ballots and local boards of elections
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026, by at least $317,000 in FY 2027, and by $182,000 in each future general election fiscal year if federal absentee ballot timeliness requirements differ from State law. Local expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026, by at least $392,000 in FY 2027, and by $182,000 in each future general election fiscal year. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 949 directly amends the Election Law Article and mandates that the State Board of Elections (SBE) establish public communication terminology ('print-at-home ballots'), adopt regulations for absentee ballot canvassing under potential federal conflicts, and execute voter outreach and notification campaigns. SBE also incurs significant fiscal and operational impacts for acquiring additional ballot scanners, modifying the statewide voter registration system, and printing voter notices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts the driver's seat of a school bus from seat upholstery fire block test requirements. Relieves driver's seats from specifications adopted by the most recent National Congress on School Transportation. Maintains required fire block materials for school bus passenger seating. Directs the Motor Vehicle Administration to adopt regulations promoting school bus fire safety standards. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: local school systems, school bus drivers, and school bus manufacturers and contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal decrease in local school system expenditures for school bus procurement beginning in FY 2027. The Motor Vehicle Administration can update safety inspection procedures with existing resources. No effect on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is statutorily tasked under § 7-808 of the Education Article with adopting regulations to promote fire safety standards for school buses and will need to update its vehicle safety inspection procedures to reflect the driver's seat upholstery exemption.

The Department of Education is statutorily designated to advise the Motor Vehicle Administration on the adoption of school bus fire safety standards and oversees public education transportation requirements across Maryland's school districts.

The Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which regulates school bus safety specifications and inspections, and was consulted on the fiscal and operational impact of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Specifies that the inspector for the Caroline County Board of License Commissioners is the county codes administrator or an appointed individual. Authorizes the Board to appoint an individual as inspector. Requires the Board to specify the inspector's duties, including administering and enforcing county alcoholic beverages laws. Requires the inspector's salary to be provided in the county budget. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Caroline County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Caroline County Board of License Commissioners, the Caroline County codes administrator, and appointed alcoholic beverages inspectors in Caroline County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state finances. Does not materially affect Caroline County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry. While this bill specifically addresses the local appointment of the alcoholic beverages inspector for the Caroline County Board of License Commissioners, it pertains to the broader enforcement of alcoholic beverage laws in Maryland.
